body.translated_text: [1.1] The traditional collection (<s>samāmnāya</s>) has been handed down; it is to be explained. They call this traditional collection '<s>Nighaṇṭavas</s>' (glossaries). Why are they called <s>Nighaṇṭavas</s>? Because they are <s>nigamas</s> (traditional texts). Having been gathered together from the Vedic hymns (<s>chandas</s>), they were handed down. Being <s>nigantavas</s> (things gathered), they are called <s>Nighaṇṭavas</s> because of their being gathered (<s>nigamana</s>) — so say the followers of <s>Aupamanyava</s>. Or else they may be so called from 'striking' (<s>hanana</s>), meaning they are 'struck together' (compiled). Or [they are so called] because they are 'collected' (<s>samāhṛta</s>). Now, the four classes of words — <s>nāman</s> (nouns), <s>ākhyāta</s> (verbs), <s>upasargas</s> (verbal prefixes), and <s>nipātas</s> (particles) — these are [what the collection contains]. Regarding these, the following characteristic of <s>nāman</s> and <s>ākhyāta</s> is prescribed: The <s>ākhyāta</s> (verb) is that in which <s>bhāva</s> (becoming, action) predominates; <s>nāmāni</s> (nouns) are those in which <s>sattva</s> (being, entity) predominates. Now, where both have <s>bhāva</s> as predominant: one expresses by the <s>ākhyāta</s> a becoming that is prior or subsequent — '<s>vrajati</s>' (he goes), '<s>pacati</s>' (he cooks). From the beginning up to the completion, the concrete, entity-like being [is expressed] by <s>sattva</s>-names — '<s>vrajyā</s>' (going), '<s>paktiḥ</s>' (cooking). '<s>Adaḥ</s>' (that) is the designation of entities — '<s>gauḥ</s>' (cow), '<s>aśvaḥ</s>' (horse), '<s>puruṣaḥ</s>' (man), '<s>hastī</s>' (elephant). '<s>Bhavati</s>' (becomes) designates becoming — '<s>āste</s>' (sits), '<s>śete</s>' (lies), '<s>vrajati</s>' (goes), '<s>tiṣṭhati</s>' (stands). Speech is perpetually connected with the senses — so says <s>Audumbarāyaṇa</s>.

[1.2] Therein, the fourfold [classification] is not fully adequate. For words that are not simultaneously arisen, there is mutual designation made by the framers of the science, and there is etymological connection (<s>yoga</s>). Because of the pervasiveness of language and because of [its] subtlety, designation by word is made for the purpose of practical usage in the world. Of these [words], the designation of deities is like that of humans. Because human knowledge is impermanent, the efficacy of the ritual action [depends on] the <s>mantra</s> in the <s>Veda</s>. There are six modifications of being (<s>bhāva-vikāra</s>) — so says <s>Vārṣyāyaṇi</s>: it is born, it exists, it transforms, it grows, it declines, it perishes. 'It is born' — this denotes the beginning of a prior state of being; it does not denote, nor does it negate, a subsequent state. 'It exists' — this is the ascertainment of an entity that has come into being. 'It transforms' — this is the modification of something that has not departed from its essence. 'It grows' — this means the increase of its own parts, or of associated things; 'it grows in victory' or 'it grows in body.' 'It declines' — this is explained by the same [analysis] in reverse. 'It perishes' — this denotes the beginning of a subsequent state of being; it does not denote, nor does it negate, a prior state.

[1.3] Other modifications of being beyond these are [merely] modifications of these same [six] — so he used to say; they should be inferred according to the [specific] expression. The <s>upasargas</s> (verbal prefixes) do not, when unconnected, express meanings independently — so says <s>Śākaṭāyana</s>. But in connection with <s>nāman</s> and <s>ākhyāta</s>, they serve to illuminate the connection with the action. The meanings of words are of various degrees — so says <s>Gārgya</s>. Thus, the meaning that [the upasargas] express in these words is a modification of the meaning of the noun or verb. '<s>Ā</s>' denotes [movement] hither; '<s>pra</s>' and '<s>parā</s>' are its opposites. '<s>Abhi</s>' denotes [facing] toward; '<s>prati</s>' is its opposite. '<s>Ati</s>' and '<s>su</s>' are in the sense of exaltation; '<s>nir</s>' and '<s>dur</s>' are their opposites. '<s>Ni</s>' and '<s>ava</s>' are in the sense of restraint; '<s>ud</s>' is their opposite. '<s>Sam</s>' denotes unification; '<s>vi</s>' and '<s>apa</s>' are its opposites. '<s>Anu</s>' denotes similarity and succession. '<s>Api</s>' denotes conjunction. '<s>Upa</s>' denotes proximity. '<s>Pari</s>' denotes totality. '<s>Adhi</s>' denotes being above, or sovereignty. Thus, they express meanings of various degrees; these should be considered.

body.translated_text: [1.4] Now, <s>nipātas</s> (particles) fall among meanings of various kinds. Some are in the sense of comparison, some serve to aggregate action, and some are fillers of the verse (<s>padapūraṇa</s>). Of these, four are in the sense of comparison: '<s>Iva</s>' (like) — in both common speech and in the hymn texts. [As in:] '<s>agnir iva</s>' (like fire) (ṚV X.84.2; 106.3), '<s>indra iva</s>' (like <s>Indra</s>) (ṚV X.84.5; 166.2; 173.2). '<s>Na</s>' — in the sense of prohibition, in common speech; in both [senses] in the hymn texts. '<s>Na indram devam amaṃsata</s>' (they did not regard <s>Indra</s> as a god) (ṚV X.86.1) — here in the prohibitive sense. That which it negates stands before it. '<s>Durmadāso na surāyām</s>' (like those intoxicated with liquor) (ṚV VII.2.12) — here in the sense of comparison. That with which it compares stands after it. '<s>Cid</s>' — this has multiple functions. 'The teacher indeed (<s>cid</s>) would say this' — in the sense of veneration. A teacher — why [called] <s>ācārya</s>? Because he imparts conduct (<s>ācāra</s>), or because he gathers meanings, or because he gathers understanding. '<s>Dadhi cid</s>' (like curds) — in the sense of comparison. '<s>Kulmāṣāṃś cid āhara</s>' (bring even porridge) — in the sense of contempt. <s>Kulmāṣas</s> (porridge) — [so called because] they settle (<s>sīdanti</s>) in the families (<s>kula</s>). '<s>Nu</s>' — this has multiple functions. '<s>Idam nu kariṣyati</s>' (he will indeed do this) — in the sense of indicating a reason. '<s>Katham nu kariṣyati</s>' (how will he do [it]?) — in a question. '<s>Nanv etad akārṣīt</s>' (did he not do this?) — also [in a question]. And sometimes it is in the sense of comparison: '<s>vṛkṣasya nu te puruhūta vayāḥ</s>' (your branches, O much-invoked one, are like those of a tree) (ṚV VI.24.3). [That is:] '<s>Vṛkṣasya iva te puruhūta śākhāḥ</s>' — like the branches of a tree, O much-invoked one. <s>Vayāḥ</s> means branches; they are [so called because they are] paths of the wind (<s>vāta-ayana</s>). <s>Śākhāḥ</s> (branches) — [so called because they] hang in the sky (<s>kha-śaya</s>), or from the root <s>śak</s> (to be able). Now, [a word] whose separate meaning is known from [its syntactic] context, but not from its analytical separation as if it were a primary word — that serves the aggregation of action. '<s>Ca</s>' — in the sense of conjunction, it connects with both [terms]. '<s>Ahaṃś ca tvaṃś ca vṛtrahan</s>' (both I and you, O slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>) (ṚV VII.62.11) — in this very sense. '<s>Devebhyaś ca pitṛbhya ā</s>' (to both the gods and the ancestors) (ṚV X.16.11) — the <s>ā</s>-syllable [is a variant of <s>ca</s>]. '<s>Vā</s>' — in the sense of alternative. '<s>Hanta aham pṛthivīm imām ni dadhāni iha vā iha vā</s>' (Come, let me place this earth here or here) (ṚV X.119.9). But sometimes it is also in the sense of conjunction.

body.translated_text: [1.5] '<s>Vāyur vā tvā manur vā tvā</s>' (whether <s>Vāyu</s> or <s>Manu</s>) (TS 1.7.7.2; KS 13.14). '<s>Aha</s>' and '<s>ha</s>' — these are in the restrictive sense and connect with what precedes. 'Let this one do this' — 'This he will indeed do,' 'This he will not do.' And the '<s>u</s>'-syllable is in this very sense, connecting with what follows: 'These speak falsely; they indeed (<s>u</s>) speak the truth.' And also as a verse-filler: '<s>idam u</s>' (ṚV IV.51.1), '<s>tad u</s>' (ṚV I.62.6). '<s>Hi</s>' — this has multiple functions. '<s>Idam hi kariṣyati</s>' (he will do this, for...) — in indicating a reason. '<s>Katham hi kariṣyati</s>' (how indeed will he do [it]?) — in a question. '<s>Katham hi vyākariṣyati</s>' (how indeed will he explain [it]?) — in censure. '<s>Kila</s>' — indicates [certainty based on] received knowledge: '<s>evam kila</s>' (so indeed). And also it connects with '<s>na</s>' and '<s>nanu</s>' in questions: '<s>Na kila evam</s>' (is it not so?), '<s>Nanu kila evam</s>' (is it not indeed so?). '<s>Mā</s>' — in prohibition: '<s>mā kārṣīḥ</s>' (do not do), '<s>mā hārṣīḥ</s>' (do not take). '<s>Khalu</s>' — '<s>khalu kṛtvā</s>' (having done indeed), '<s>khalu kṛtam</s>' (done indeed). And also as a verse-filler: '<s>evam khalu tad babhūva</s>' (thus indeed it happened). '<s>Śaśvat</s>' — in the sense of doubt in common speech. '<s>Śaśvad evam</s>' (is it always so?) — in a question. '<s>Evam śaśvat</s>' (it is always so) — when not asked by oneself. '<s>Nūnam</s>' — in the sense of doubt in common speech. In both [senses] in the hymn texts — both in the sense of doubt and as a verse-filler. [Story:] <s>Agastya</s>, having prepared an oblation for <s>Indra</s>, wished to give it to the <s>Maruts</s>. <s>Indra</s> came and lamented:

body.translated_text: [1.6] '<s>Na nūnam asti no śvaḥ kas tad veda yad adbhutam</s>' (There is neither today nor tomorrow; who knows that which is wondrous?) (ṚV I.170.1). '<s>Anyasya cittam abhisañcareṇyam uta adhītam vi naśyati</s>' (The mind of another is hard to penetrate, and even what has been learned perishes) (ṚV I.170.1). '<s>Na nūnam asti</s>' — there is neither [anything belonging to] today, nor indeed [anything of] tomorrow. '<s>Adya</s>' (today) — in this day. '<s>Dyuḥ</s>' is the name of the day — [so called] because it shines (<s>dyotate</s>); that is well known. '<s>Śvaḥ</s>' (tomorrow) — the anticipated time; '<s>hyaḥ</s>' (yesterday) — the elapsed time. '<s>Kas tad veda yad adbhutam</s>' — who knows that which is <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous)? [The word <s>adbhuta</s> means] that which has not been (<s>abhūta</s>). This other too is <s>adbhuta</s> — as if it had not been. '<s>Anyasya cittam abhisañcareṇyam</s>' — the mind of another is [hard] to penetrate (<s>abhisañcārya</s>); another should not be led [astray]. <s>Citta</s> (mind) is from the root <s>cet</s> (to perceive). '<s>Uta adhītam vinaśyati</s>' — even what has been learned (<s>adhyāta</s>) perishes; <s>adhyāta</s> [means] that which has been intended. And also [<s>nūnam</s> is used] as a verse-filler.

body.translated_text: 1.7: "Surely that bountiful gift shall be milked forth for you, your worshipping singer, O <s>Indra</s>, O Munificent One" (<s>ṚV</s> 2.11.21). "Bestow upon the praisers; do not burn us past. May we speak greatly at the assembly, blessed with heroes" (<s>ṚV</s> 2.11.21). That [gift] is milked forth for you as a boon for the singer. <s>Vara</s> (boon) means that which is to be chosen. <s>Jaritā</s> (worshipper) means 'singer' (<s>garitā</s>). <s>Dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial gift) is <s>maghonī</s> (bountiful), meaning possessed of <s>magha</s> (wealth). <s>Magha</s> is a name for wealth, from the root <s>maṃh</s> meaning 'to give.' <s>Dakṣiṇā</s> is from the root <s>dakṣ</s> meaning 'to make capable'; it makes the ritual efficacious and prosperous — thus [it is explained]. Or alternatively, because of its going around in the clockwise direction (<s>pradakṣiṇa āgamanāt</s>). With reference to the direction, the original form is <s>dik-hasta</s> (hand of direction); the right hand is <s>dākṣiṇa hasta</s>. [<s>Dakṣiṇā</s>] may be from <s>dakṣ</s> meaning 'to be active, vigorous,' or from <s>dāś</s> [meaning 'to worship, give']. <s>Hasta</s> (hand) is from <s>han</s> meaning 'to strike,' swift in striking. 'Give desires to the praisers.' 'Do not oppress us' (<s>mā asmān atidaṃhīḥ</s>). 'Do not give [to others] passing us by.' 'May fortune (<s>bhaga</s>) be ours.' 'May we speak greatly at our own assembly.' <s>Bhaga</s> (fortune) is from <s>bhaj</s> (to share, distribute). <s>Bṛhat</s> (great) is a name for what is great; it becomes exalted (<s>parivṛḍha</s>). [<s>Suvīrāḥ</s> means] possessing heroes, or having excellent heroes. <s>Vīra</s> (hero) vanquishes (<s>vīrayati</s>) enemies; or it may be from <s>vī</s> meaning 'to go,' or from <s>vīray</s> [causative]. <s>Sīm</s> is either a comprehensive particle or a verse-filler. "<s>Āditya</s> sent them forth" (<s>ṚV</s> 2.28.4). This means either 'he released [them]' or '[he released them] in all directions.' "The <s>Vena</s> of beautiful light separated them from here" (<s>AV</s> 4.1.1) — and so on. <s>Āditya</s> uncovered [them] on all sides. <s>Surucaḥ</s> (of beautiful light) refers to the rays of <s>Āditya</s>, from 'shining beautifully' (<s>surocanāt</s>). Or alternatively, one should take <s>sīmā</s> as a meaningless appendage, adopting the fifth [interpretation]. <s>Sīmnaḥ</s>, <s>sīmataḥ</s>, <s>sīmātaḥ</s> — from the boundary (<s>maryādātaḥ</s>). <s>Sīmā</s> (boundary) is <s>maryādā</s> (limit); it separates (<s>viṣīvyati</s>) two regions. <s>Tva</s> is a pronoun with a separative meaning, <s>anudātta</s> (grave-accented) — some call it a half-name (<s>ardhanāma</s>).

body.translated_text: 1.8: "One, having flourished, enjoys the nourishment of the <s>ṛcs</s> (hymns); one sings the <s>gāyatra</s> among the <s>śakvarīs</s>" (<s>ṚV</s> 10.71.11). "The <s>Brahman</s> priest speaks the knowledge as each [ritual act] is born; one measures out the form of the sacrifice" (<s>ṚV</s> 10.71.11). This describes the assignment of the priestly functions. One, having flourished, enjoys the nourishment of the <s>ṛcs</s> — [this is] the <s>Hotā</s> (invoking priest); <s>ṛc</s> is from <s>arc</s> (to praise). One sings the <s>gāyatra</s> among the <s>śakvarīs</s> — [this is] the <s>Udgātā</s> (chanting priest). <s>Gāyatra</s> is from <s>gā</s> meaning 'to praise.' <s>Śakvaryas</s> are <s>ṛcs</s> (verses), from <s>śak</s> (to be able). It is traditionally known: "Because with these [verses] they were able to slay <s>Vṛtra</s>, that is the <s>śakvarī</s>-nature of the <s>śakvarīs</s>" (<s>KB</s> 23.2). The <s>Brahman</s> priest speaks the knowledge as each [ritual act] is born. The <s>Brahman</s> is all-knowing; he is qualified to know everything. The <s>Brahman</s> is exalted (<s>parivṛḍha</s>) through learning; <s>brahman</s> is exalted in every way. One measures out the form of the sacrifice — [this is] the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. <s>Adhvaryu</s>: he who yokes (<s>yunakti</s>) the sacrifice (<s>adhvara</s>), or the leader of the sacrifice, or one who desires the sacrifice. Or alternatively, <s>yu</s> is an appendage [suffix] added to <s>adhīyāna</s> (one who studies). <s>Adhvara</s> is a name for sacrifice; <s>dhvarati</s> means 'to harm' — [<s>adhvara</s> is] the negation of that [i.e., non-violence]. Some [say it is] a <s>nipāta</s> (particle). How then could it be of <s>anudātta</s> (grave-accented) base form? But it is observed to lose [its accent]. "And they call you one of firm drinking among friends" (<s>ṚV</s> 10.71.5) — in the second [case]. "And she spread her body for him" (<s>ṚV</s> 10.71.4) — in the fourth [case]. Now also [<s>tva</s> appears] in the nominative plural.

1.9: "Those friends who have eyes and ears have become unequal in the swiftness of minds" (<s>ṚV</s> 10.71.7). "Some are up to the mouth, some up to the armpits; and some, having bathed as in lakes, appeared" (<s>ṚV</s> 10.71.7). [They are] possessing eyes and possessing ears, [these] friends. <s>Akṣi</s> (eye) is from <s>cas</s> (to see) or <s>añj</s> (to anoint) — according to <s>Āgrāyaṇa</s>. "Therefore these two [eyes] become, as it were, more manifest" — thus it is traditionally known. <s>Karṇa</s> (ear) is from <s>kṛnt</s> (to cut); [the ear] has a cut-open passage — or from <s>ṛcch</s> (to reach), according to <s>Āgrāyaṇa</s>. "They reach upward, as it were, into the sky" — thus it is traditionally known. They became unequal in the swiftness of minds; some [are immersed] up to the mouth, others up to the armpits. <s>Āsya</s> (mouth) is from <s>as</s> (to throw); or 'food flows into it' [<s>āsyandata enad annam</s>]. <s>Daghna</s> (reaching up to) is from <s>dagh</s> (to flow) or may be from <s>das</s> (to be exhausted) — it means 'reaching further.' Some [who have bathed] in lakes worthy of bathing appeared. <s>Hrada</s> (lake) is from <s>hrād</s> (to sound) or may be from <s>hlād</s> (to refresh) — denoting the action of becoming cool. Now also [<s>ca</s>] occurs in a cumulative sense. "Turn by turn, like you, O <s>Aśvins</s>" (<s>MB</s> 17.4) — both the <s>Aśvins</s> and the turns [are meant]. Now, those [particles] which come as sentence-fillers in passages of clear meaning in texts of unlimited syllables, they are meaningless [word-fillers] in texts of limited syllables — such as <s>kam</s>, <s>īm</s>, <s>id</s>, <s>u</s>.

1.10: "Those who have lips and ears, O men, those many children, like [birds] from a tree" (untraced). "Trembling, they cried aloud, [desiring] the cool for the sake of life" (untraced). '<s>Śiśira</s>' (cool) [is sought] for the sake of life. <s>Śiśira</s> is from <s>śṛ</s> (to injure) or from <s>śam</s> (to be calm). "Release him to the pressed [<s>Soma</s>]" (<s>ṚV</s> 1.9.2) — [means] 'release him at the pressing.' "May our songs increase him" (<s>ṚV</s> 5.21.92.21; 9.61.14) — [means] 'may our hymns, our praises, increase him.' <s>Giraḥ</s> (songs) is from <s>gṛ</s> (to praise). "This one is equal to you" (<s>ṚV</s> 1.30.4) — [means] 'this one is equal to you.' <s>Iva</s> (like) also appears as <s>su</s> — 'they knew well' [<s>su viduḥ</s>], 'they are well-known' [<s>su vijñāyete</s>]; [and] as <s>iva</s>. Now also, <s>na</s> (not) is joined with <s>id</s> in the sense of apprehension [or fear].

1.11: "Some, who are inspired, worship with <s>havis</s> (oblations); some press <s>Soma</s> at the pressings" (<s>ṚVKh</s> 10.106.1). "Rejoicing in powers and with <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial fees) — may we not fall crookedly into <s>naraka</s> (hell)" (<s>ṚVKh</s> 10.106.1). <s>Naraka</s> (hell) means <s>nyaraka</s> — going downward (<s>nīcair gamanam</s>); or [a place where] there is not even the slightest abode of pleasure. Now also, <s>na ca</s> (and not) is joined with <s>id</s> in the sense of a subsequent question — [as in] 'they do not drink <s>surā</s> (liquor).' <s>Surā</s> (liquor) is from <s>su</s> (to press). Thus [these particles] fall in contexts of both high and low meaning — they should be disregarded [as semantically empty].

1.12: Thus these four classes of words have been enumerated: <s>nāma</s> (noun), <s>ākhyāta</s> (verb), <s>upasarga</s> (preverb), and <s>nipāta</s> (particle). Among these, nouns are derived from verbs — [this is the view of] <s>Śākaṭāyana</s> and the convention of the <s>Nairuktas</s> (etymologists). Not all [nouns are so derived] — [this is the view of] <s>Gārgya</s> and some of the <s>Vaiyākaraṇas</s> (grammarians). [That is,] where accent and morphological formation, both being meaningful, are accompanied by a derivational modification. Those [nouns whose derivation] is recognized are such as <s>gauḥ</s> (cow), <s>aśvaḥ</s> (horse), <s>puruṣaḥ</s> (man), <s>hastī</s> (elephant). Now, if all nouns were derived from verbs, then whatever being performs that action, all those beings would be called by that [name]. Whatever traverses (<s>aśnuvīta</s>) a path would be called <s>aśva</s> (horse). Whatever is cut (<s>tṛndyāt</s>) would be <s>tṛṇa</s> (grass). Moreover, if all nouns were derived from verbs, one would obtain names corresponding to as many states as [the thing] is associated with. In that case, a pillar (<s>sthūṇā</s>) could also be [called] <s>daraśayā</s> (a place for splitting) or <s>sañjanī</s> (a place of birth).

1.13: Moreover, there is the regular action-based etymological formation of these [nouns]. And one should designate them as their meanings are understood — [for example,] one would call a man <s>puriśaya</s> (dweller in a city), a horse <s>aṣṭā</s> (the swift one), grass <s>tardana</s> (that which pierces). Moreover, when the utterance is complete, they [still] investigate [further]. They say '<s>pṛthivī</s>' (earth) is from <s>prathana</s> (spreading). [But the objection is:] who would have spread it? And what would be its support? Now, when the meaning is not connected, when the modification is not derivational, <s>Śākaṭāyana</s> derived [the etymological formation] from words to half-words. From <s>e</s> he [derived] causatives and those beginning with <s>ya</s>, and the final element from <s>as</s> (to be); pure [forms] and those beginning with <s>sa</s> [he also derived]. Moreover, they say that being (<s>sattva</s>) precedes becoming (<s>bhāva</s>) [i.e., the noun precedes the verb]. [The reply is:] The derivation of the prior [noun] from the subsequent state [verb] is not possible. This [position] is not tenable.

1.14: As to the further objection — that wherever accent and grammatical form (<s>svara-saṃskāra</s>) are capable [of conveying meaning], when accompanied by a provincial modification (or quality, acc. to <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>) — if everything is merely provincial, then this becomes an objection without basis. As to the objection that whoever performs that action, they would call every such being by that name — we observe that among those performing the same action, some obtain the designation and some do not, just as [the words] <s>takṣā</s> (carpenter), <s>parivrājaka</s> (wandering mendicant), <s>jīvana</s> (livelihood), <s>bhūmija</s> (earth-born) — by this very [reasoning] the further objection is answered. As to the objection that they would name them according to their understood meanings — there are words of rare usage, single-word compounds, such as <s>vratatir</s>, <s>damūnā</s>, <s>jāṭya</s>, <s>āṭṇāra</s>, <s>jāgarūka</s>, <s>darvihomī</s>. As to the objection that people analyze after the expression is complete — indeed, when an expression is complete, etymological investigation (<s>yoga-parīṣṭi</s>) does take place. They say '<s>pṛthivī</s>' (earth) is from <s>prathana</s> (spreading) — [but the objection is:] who would have spread it? And what was its support? But indeed, by perception <s>pṛthu</s> (wide) [is established] — even if not spread by others. Moreover, thus all explanations based on observation are subject to criticism. As to the objection that someone composed a half-verse from [individual] words — whoever composed meaning from unconnected [words], he is blameworthy for that; this is blame of the person, not blame of the science (<s>śāstra</s>). As to the objection that the designation of the former [thing] is not established from a later state — we observe that among beings born earlier, some obtain designations from a later state and some do not, just as <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple), <s>ada</s>, <s>lamba</s>, <s>cūḍaka</s>. <s>Bilva</s> is from <s>bharaṇa</s> (nourishing) or <s>bhedana</s> (splitting).

body.translated_text: 1.15: Moreover, without this [etymological analysis], there is no understanding of meaning in the mantras. Without understanding the meaning, the teaching of accent and grammatical form is not of ultimate [value]. This [<s>Nirukta</s>] is a branch of knowledge, a supplement to grammar (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>), and it accomplishes its own purpose. If [one says] it is purposeless for understanding the meaning of mantras — <s>Kautsa</s> [says]: 'The mantras are indeed meaningless.' This should be examined. Fixed utterances have fixed sequences. Moreover, [meanings] complete with form are prescribed by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> texts. 'Spread wide' (<s>uru prasthasva</s>) — this spreads. '<s>Prohāṇi</s>' — this drives forth. But some have impossible meanings: 'O herb, save him!' (<s>oṣadhe trāyasva enam</s>); 'O axe, do not harm him!' (<s>svadhite mā enam hiṃsīḥ</s>) — this is said while harming. Moreover, some have contradictory meanings: '<s>Rudra</s> alone stood, no second' (<s>eka eva Rudro avatasthe na dvitīyaḥ</s>); [but also] 'Innumerable thousands of <s>Rudra</s>s upon the earth' (<s>asaṃkhyātā sahasrāṇi ye Rudrā adhi bhūmyām</s>). '<s>Indra</s> was born without enemies' (<s>aśatrur Indra jajñiṣe</s>); [but also] '<s>Indra</s> conquered a hundred armies at once' (<s>śatam senā ajayat sākam Indraḥ</s>). Moreover, one commands someone who already knows: 'Bring firewood for <s>Agni</s>, recite' (<s>Agnaye samidhyam ānāya anu brūhi</s>). Moreover, it says '<s>Aditi</s> is everything': '<s>Aditi</s> is the sky, <s>Aditi</s> is the atmosphere' (<s>Aditir dyaur Aditir antarikṣam</s>) — we shall explain that further on. Moreover, some have unclear meanings: '<s>amyak</s>', '<s>yādṛśmin</s>', '<s>jārayāyi</s>', '<s>kāṇukā</s>'.

1.16: [The mantras] are meaningful, because of the general nature of words. And the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [states]: 'This indeed is the perfection of the sacrifice — that which is perfect in form, when an <s>Ṛc</s> or <s>Yajus</s> accompanies the ritual act being performed.' [The verse] 'Playing with sons and grandsons' (<s>krīḍantau putrair naptṛbhiḥ</s>) [is meaningful]. As to the [argument] that fixed utterances have fixed sequences — this applies in everyday language too, as in '<s>Indrāgnī</s>' [always in this order], '<s>pitāputrau</s>' (father and son). As to the [argument] that meanings complete with form are prescribed by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — that is a restatement of what has been said. As to the [argument] that some have impossible meanings — from the Vedic injunction, non-harm is to be understood. As to the [argument] that some have contradictory meanings — this occurs in everyday language too, as in 'This <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is without rivals, this king is without enemies.' As to the [argument] that one commands someone who already knows — one also greets the knowing one, one offers <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture) to the knowing one. As to the [argument] that '<s>Aditi</s> is everything' — this occurs in everyday language too, as in 'Water is endowed with all flavors.' As to the [argument] that some have unclear meanings — 'This is not the fault of the post that the blind man does not see it; it is the fault of the person.' Just as among countrymen, distinction comes through knowledge, so among those versed in the various recensions, the more learned one is praiseworthy.

1.17: Moreover, without this [analysis], word-division (<s>pada-vibhāga</s>) is not possible. '<s>Avasāya padvate Rudra mṛḍe</s>' — 'Having pastured, for the one with feet, O <s>Rudra</s>, be gracious' — <s>padvat</s>: the cows have feet; <s>pathyā adana</s>: [from] <s>ava</s> + <s>ati</s> with the sense of going, <s>asa</s> is the agent — therefore they do not separate [the words]. [Alternatively:] 'Unharness the horses' — <s>syati</s> with the preverb means 'loosening,' therefore they do separate [the words]. '<s>Dūto Nirṛtyā idam ā jagāma</s>' (The messenger of <s>Nirṛti</s> came here) — the consideration is whether it is an ablative or genitive ending. '<s>Paro Nirṛtyā ā cakṣva</s>' (Declare beyond <s>Nirṛti</s>) — the consideration is a dative meaning, ending in <s>ai</s>. The closest connection is <s>saṃhitā</s> (continuous text). <s>Saṃhitā</s> has the word (<s>pada</s>) as its basis. The recension texts (<s>pārṣadāni</s>) of all schools have the word as their basis. Moreover, in sacrificial [mantras], many passages are determined by deity — this should be examined. If they were to say, 'We know [the deity] by the characteristic mark (<s>liṅga</s>)' — [consider:] '<s>Indram na tvā śavasā devatā Vāyum pṛṇanti</s>' — [this has] characteristics of both <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Indra</s> in an <s>Āgneya</s> (fire-related) mantra. '<s>Agnir iva Manyo tviṣitaḥ sahasva</s>' (O <s>Manyu</s>, blazing like <s>Agni</s>, conquer) — likewise <s>Agni</s> [appears] in a mantra to <s>Manyu</s>. <s>Tviṣita</s> means 'blazing'; <s>tviṣi</s> is also a name for splendor. Moreover, there is praise of knowledge and censure of ignorance:

1.18: 'This one became a mere post, a burden-bearer, who having studied the <s>Veda</s> does not understand its meaning.' 'One who knows the meaning enjoys complete well-being, goes to heaven (<s>nāka</s>), with sins destroyed by knowledge.' 'What is grasped but not understood is merely repeated by rote (<s>nigada</s>).' 'Like dry firewood without fire, it never blazes.' <s>Sthāṇu</s> (post) is from <s>sthā</s> (to stand); <s>artha</s> (meaning) is from <s>ṛ</s> (to go); or [<s>sthāṇu</s> means] one who stands in the wilderness (<s>araṇa-stha</s>).

[1.19] '<s>Uta tvaḥ paśyan na dadarśa vācam uta tvaḥ śṛṇvan na śṛṇoty enām</s>' (ṚV X.71.4) — 'And one, though seeing, has not seen speech; and one, though hearing, does not hear her.' '<s>Uto tv asmai tanvam vi sasre jāyeva patya uśatī suvāsāḥ</s>' (ṚV X.71.4) — 'And to one [other], she has revealed her body, like a well-dressed wife, desiring her husband.' One [person], though seeing, does not see speech; and though hearing, does not hear her — this half-verse speaks of one who is not learned. And to one [other], she has disclosed her body — she reveals her own self. [The hymn] speaks of the illumination of meaning through this speech, using the supreme comparison: like a wife desiring her husband, well-dressed at the time of her season — well-dressed means beautifully clothed, desiring [him]. Just as in the season he sees her, he hears her — thus is the praise of one who knows the meaning. The following [verse] is for further explanation: '<s>Uta tvam sakhye sthirapītam āhur na enam hinvanty api vājineṣu</s>' (ṚV X.71.5) — 'And one they call firmly fixed in friendship; they do not urge him even in contests.' '<s>Adhenvā carati māyayā eṣa vācam śuśruvām aphalām apuṣpām</s>' (ṚV X.71.5) — 'He wanders with a barren [cow], with an illusion; the speech he has heard is without fruit, without flower.'

body.translated_text: [1.20] And one they call firmly established in the friendship of speech — one who delights in it, who has drunk its meaning deeply; or [it means one dwelling] in the delightful friendship of the gods, as in a [permanent] abode. One whom [others with] knowledge of speech cannot surpass, even those who are powerful in the things to be known by speech. For this one wanders with a barren [cow] — with speech that is a mere semblance (<s>māyā</s>). Speech does not yield to him the desired [fruits] at the stations of gods and humans — he who has heard speech that is without fruit, without flower. Or: speech is fruitless and flowerless for him. Or: [it is speech that is only] slightly flowered and fruited. [<s>Yāska</s>] declares that the fruit and flower of speech is [its] meaning. The fruit and flower pertaining to sacrifice are the deities; or [they pertain to] the spiritual domain (<s>adhyātma</s>). The <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) were those who had directly perceived <s>dharma</s> (the sacred truths). They transmitted the <s>mantras</s> to later generations who had not directly perceived <s>dharma</s>, through instruction. The later [generations], growing weary of [mere] instruction, compiled this text for the purpose of grasping the reflection (<s>bilma</s>) — that is, the elucidation — and also the <s>Vedas</s> and the <s>Vedāṅgas</s> (auxiliary sciences of the Veda). <s>Bilma</s> means <s>bhilma</s>, that is, illumination (<s>bhāsana</s>). These are the roots of similar function; <s>dhātu</s> (root) is from <s>dadhāti</s> (to place/support). These are the names of this entity. This is the designation of these many meanings. 'This is <s>Naighaṇṭuka</s> (belonging to the glossary); this pertains principally to the names of deities' — thus [it is explained]. That which occurs in a <s>mantra</s> [addressed to] a different deity — that is <s>Naighaṇṭuka</s>. '<s>Aśvam na tvā vāravantam</s>' (ṚV I.27.1; SV I.17; II.984) — 'Like a horse with a mane (<s>vāla</s>).' The manes serve the purpose of warding off flies; <s>daṃśa</s> (fly) is from <s>daśati</s> (to bite). '<s>Mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ</s>' (ṚV I.154.2; X.180.2) — 'Terrible like a wild beast, going fiercely, dwelling on mountains.' <s>Mṛga</s> (beast) is from <s>mṛṣṭi</s> (root of going, motion). <s>Bhīma</s> (terrible) — one fears (<s>bibhyati</s>) him. <s>Bhīṣma</s> (dreadful) is also from this very [root]. <s>Kucara</s> — one whose going (<s>carati</s>) is fierce (<s>kutsita</s>). But if it is a designation of a deity — where does he not go? <s>Giriṣṭhā</s> — one who dwells on the mountain. <s>Giri</s> (mountain) is <s>parvata</s> — it is 'emitted forth' (<s>samudgīrṇa</s>). <s>Parvata</s> — having joints (<s>parvan</s>); and <s>parvan</s> is from <s>pṛṇāti</s> (to fill) or <s>prīṇāti</s> (to please). The half-month is a <s>parvan</s> — [because] they please the gods during it. That [etymology] is from the primary [meaning]; the other [use] is from similarity with the compound. Or one who dwells in the cloud — <s>megha</s> (cloud) is also [called] <s>giri</s>, from this very [root]. Those names which are of the principal hymns of praise of the deities — that is called <s>daivata</s> (pertaining to deities). That we shall explain further on. The <s>Naighaṇṭuka</s> [words], which are <s>Naigama</s> (Vedic) [usages] — [they occur] here and there.

[2.1] Now, etymology (<s>nirvacana</s>). In those words where accent (<s>svara</s>) and grammatical formation (<s>saṃskāra</s>) are adequate [to explain the word], accompanied by a regional phonetic modification — one should etymologize them accordingly. But when the meaning is not accompanied [by transparent formation], or when the phonetic modification is not regional, one should investigate based on the meaning, by some similarity of usage (<s>vṛtti-sāmānya</s>). When there is no such similarity [of usage] either, one should etymologize from the similarity of syllables or phonemes; but one should never fail to etymologize. One should not be too attached to the grammatical form, for usages have [their own] domains. One should adapt the case-endings as required by the meaning. [In forms like] '<s>prattam</s>' (given) and '<s>avattam</s>' (cut) — only the root-initial [portion] remains [after phonetic changes]. And also, in the places where the root <s>as</s> (to be) is [conjugated], there is elision of the initial: '<s>staḥ</s>' (the two are), '<s>santi</s>' (they are). And also, final elision occurs: '<s>gatvā</s>' (having gone), '<s>gatam</s>' (gone). And also, medial elision occurs: '<s>jagmatuḥ</s>' (the two went), '<s>jagmuḥ</s>' (they went). And also, medial modification occurs: '<s>rājā</s>' (king), '<s>daṇḍī</s>' (staff-bearer). And also, phoneme-elision occurs: '<s>tattvā yāmi</s>.' And also, two-phoneme elision: '<s>tṛca</s>.' And also, initial transposition occurs: '<s>jyotiḥ</s>' (light), '<s>ghanaḥ</s>' (dense), '<s>binduḥ</s>' (drop), '<s>vāṭyaḥ</s>.' And also, initial-and-final transposition occurs: '<s>stokā</s>' (drop), '<s>rajjuḥ</s>' (rope), '<s>sikatāḥ</s>' (sand), '<s>tarkuḥ</s>' (spindle). And also, final corruption occurs:

body.translated_text: [2.2] '<s>Oghaḥ</s>' (flood), '<s>meghaḥ</s>' (cloud), '<s>nādhaḥ</s>' (protector), '<s>gādhaḥ</s>' (fordable depth), '<s>vadhūḥ</s>' (bride), '<s>madhu</s>' (honey). And also, insertion of a phoneme: '<s>āsthad</s>,' '<s>dvāraḥ</s>' (door), '<s>bharūjaḥ</s>.' Now, where between a vowel and the immediately following semivowel there is a root within — they prescribe that this is the place for [analyzing] words with two bases (<s>dviprakṛti</s>). When one [etymological derivation] is established but not fully adequate, one should try to supplement it with the other. Among these too, some are of partial derivation — such as '<s>ūtiḥ</s>' (protection), '<s>mṛduḥ</s>' (soft), '<s>pṛthuḥ</s>' (broad), '<s>pṛṣataḥ</s>' (spotted), '<s>kuṇārum</s>.' And also, [words] from colloquial roots may be explained as Vedic [forms]: '<s>damūnāḥ</s>' (generous), '<s>kṣetrasādhāḥ</s>' (conquering territories). And also, [words] from Vedic [roots may be explained through] colloquial [forms]: '<s>uṣṇam</s>' (hot), '<s>ghṛtam</s>' (ghee). And also, primary [uninflected] forms are used in some [dialects], modified [forms] in others. The root <s>śavati</s> (to go) is used only among the <s>Kambojas</s>. <s>Kambojas</s> — 'blanket-enjoyers' or 'beauty-enjoyers.' <s>Kambala</s> (blanket) is beautiful (<s>kamanīya</s>). Its modified form is used among the <s>Āryas</s> — '<s>śava</s>' (corpse). <s>Dāti</s> in the sense of 'cutting' [is used] among the easterners; '<s>dātra</s>' (sickle) [is used] among the northerners. Thus one should etymologize single words. But in <s>taddhita</s> (secondary derivation) compounds, whether of one or many members, one should analyze the prior and subsequent [parts] separately and etymologize [each]. '<s>Daṇḍya puruṣaḥ</s>' — a man deserving punishment; '<s>daṇḍa-puruṣaḥ</s>' — a man who deserves a stick, or one who is constituted by [the authority of] the stick. <s>Daṇḍa</s> (stick) is from <s>dadāti</s> (to give), from the action of holding; [as in the] non-derogatory [usage] '<s>akūro dadate maṇim</s>' (the uncruel one takes a jewel). [Or] from <s>damana</s> (taming) — so says <s>Aupamanyava</s>; [as in the expression] 'he draws his stick' — in a context of reproach. <s>Kakṣyā</s> (girth) — the rope of a horse that follows the flank (<s>kakṣa</s>). <s>Kakṣa</s> (flank) is from <s>gāhati</s> (to plunge); <s>ksa</s> is a name-forming [suffix], or from <s>khyāti</s> (to be known) with a meaningless reduplication — 'what is to be known (<s>khyāna</s>) in it'; or from <s>kaṣati</s> (to rub). By analogy, the human <s>kakṣa</s> (armpit) — from the similarity to the [horse's] shoulder-root.

body.translated_text: [2.3] '<s>Rājñaḥ puruṣaḥ</s>' (the king's man) — '<s>rāja-puruṣaḥ</s>' (king-man). <s>Rājā</s> (king) is from <s>rājati</s> (to shine). <s>Puruṣa</s> (person) — one who sits in the city (<s>puri ṣādaḥ</s>), or one who lies in the city (<s>puri śayaḥ</s>), or from <s>pūrayati</s> (to fill). He fills within — this is said with reference to the inner person (<s>antara-puruṣa</s>). '<s>Yasmāt param na aparam asti kiñcid yasmān na aṇīyo na jyāyo asti kaścit</s>' (TA 10.10.3; MU 10.4) — 'Than whom there is nothing higher, nothing lower; than whom there is nothing smaller, nothing greater.' '<s>Vṛkṣa iva stabdho divi tiṣṭhaty ekas tena idam pūrṇam puruṣeṇa sarvam</s>' (TA 10.10.3; MU 10.4; NU 21.9) — 'Standing firm like a tree in heaven, by that <s>Puruṣa</s> all this is filled' — this Vedic passage also exists [as testimony]. <s>Viścakadra</s> — <s>vi</s> [is a prefix]; <s>cakadra</s>: <s>śva</s> is used in the sense of 'going' in common speech; <s>drāti</s> — a deprecatory form of 'going'; <s>kadrāti</s> — a deprecatory form of <s>drāti</s>; <s>cakadrāti</s> — of the form <s>kadrāti</s>, with a meaningless reduplication; one in whom this exists is <s>viścakadra</s>. <s>Kalyāṇa-varṇa-rūpaḥ</s> — one whose form (<s>rūpa</s>) is like that of a beautiful complexion. <s>Kalyāṇa</s> (auspicious) means beautiful (<s>kamanīya</s>). <s>Varṇa</s> (color, complexion) is from <s>vṛṇoti</s> (to choose). <s>Rūpa</s> (form) is from <s>rocati</s> (to please). Thus one should etymologize <s>taddhita</s> compounds. One should not etymologize single words for one who is not a grammarian, nor for one who has not approached [as a student], nor for one who does not know 'this' [i.e., the subject matter]. For one who is ignorant invariably harbors resentment toward knowledge. But one should etymologize for a student who has [properly] approached, or for one who is competent to understand, or for one who is endowed with intellect, or for one who is devoted to austerity.

2.4: 'Knowledge (<s>Vidyā</s>) indeed came to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [saying]: "Protect me, I am your treasure, your treasure I am. Do not tell me to one who is envious, dishonest, or crooked — [if you do not], I shall be powerful thus. He who pierces both ears with truth, causing no pain, granting immortality — him one should regard as father and mother; one should not betray him in anything whatsoever. Those learned ones who, having been taught, do not honor the teacher in speech, mind, or action — just as they are not worthy of eating at the teacher's [table], so that learning does not nourish them. To whomever [you find] pure, attentive, intelligent, endowed with <s>brahmacarya</s> (studentship), who would not betray you in anything whatsoever — to him tell me, O <s>Brahman</s>, as a guardian of treasure."' <s>Nidhi</s> (treasure) and <s>śevadhi</s> (treasure) [are synonyms].

body.translated_text: 2.5: Now we shall proceed in order. '<s>Go</s>' (cow) is a name for the earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>), because it has gone far (<s>dūram gatā</s>), and because beings move (<s>gacchanti</s>) upon it. Or [it is derived] from <s>gāti</s> (going), with the <s>au</s> suffix as the name-forming element. Moreover, the name '<s>paśu</s>' (animal/cattle) also occurs here, from this same [root]. Moreover, Vedic usages occur in derivative senses, as with verbal derivatives. 'With cows they bring the intoxicating [<s>Soma</s>]' — [here 'cows' means] milk (<s>payas</s>). <s>Matsara</s> (intoxicating) is <s>Soma</s>, from <s>mandati</s> (to gladden), related to satisfaction. <s>Matsara</s> is also a name for greed — wealth becomes 'intoxicated' by it. <s>Payas</s> (milk) is from <s>pibati</s> (to drink) or <s>pyāyati</s> (to swell). <s>Kṣīra</s> (milk) is from <s>kṣarati</s> (to flow) or <s>ghasa</s> (to consume), with <s>īra</s> as the suffix, as in <s>uśīra</s>. 'Milking the stalk, they sit upon the cow' — this refers to the <s>Soma</s>-pressing ceremony. The <s>aṃśu</s> (stalk) has eight syllables when combined with <s>śam</s>; and <s>śam</s> is said to be for well-being. <s>Carma</s> (hide) is from <s>carati</s> (to move) or because it is peeled off. Moreover, [under 'cow':] hide and sinew. 'Bound with cows, enter' — this is praise of the chariot. Moreover, sinew and tendons: 'Bound with cows, she flies, released' — this is praise of the arrow. The bowstring (<s>jyā</s>) is also called '<s>go</s>' (cow). If it is derived from cow [material], it is a <s>taddhita</s> derivative; if not from cow, [it is because] it propels (<s>gamayati</s>) the arrows.

body.translated_text: 2.6: 'On each tree is fixed the bellowing cow; thence the birds fly forth, man-eating.' 'On each tree' means 'on each bow.' A tree (<s>vṛkṣa</s>) is from <s>vraścana</s> (cutting), or because it stands (<s>tiṣṭhati</s>) having covered (<s>vṛtvā</s>) the earth (<s>kṣām</s>). <s>Kṣā</s> (earth) is from <s>kṣīyati</s> (to dwell), with the sense of habitation. 'The cow fixed [on the bow] bellows' — it makes sound. <s>Mīmayati</s> denotes making sound. 'Thence the birds fly forth to devour men.' <s>Vi</s> (bird) is a name for birds, from <s>veti</s> (to go), with the sense of movement. Moreover, the name '<s>iṣu</s>' (arrow) also occurs here, from this same [root]. The sun (<s>Āditya</s>) is also called '<s>go</s>' (cow). 'And yonder cow above' — [meaning] the shining one with joints, according to <s>Aupamanyava</s>. Moreover, one of its rays shines toward the moon. This should be considered: its luminosity comes from the sun. There is also the Vedic passage: '<s>Suṣumnā</s> is a ray of the sun; the moon is a <s>Gandharva</s>.' It too is called '<s>go</s>' (cow). Here it is said, 'they found the cows' — we shall explain that further on. All rays too are called '<s>go</s>' (cows).

2.7: 'We desire to go to those abodes of yours where the many-horned cows, untiring, [dwell]. There that supreme abode of the wide-striding Bull shines forth abundantly.' Those abodes of yours we desire for going, where the cows are 'many-horned' (<s>bhūri-śṛṅga</s>), that is, having many horns. <s>Bhūri</s> is a name for 'many,' from the root meaning 'to prevail.' <s>Śṛṅga</s> (horn) is from <s>śrayati</s> (to rest upon), or <s>śṛṇāti</s> (to break), or <s>śamnāti</s> (to pacify), or 'risen up for shelter,' or 'protruding from the head.' <s>Ayāsa</s> means 'untiring' (<s>ayana</s>, going). There, that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the great-strider, placed in the highest realm, shines forth abundantly. <s>Pāda</s> (foot) is from <s>padyate</s> (to go); from that placing, [comes] <s>pada</s> (step/abode). The foot of an animal is the primary [meaning]; the fractional foot [i.e. quarter] is [derived from it]. From the similarity to fractional parts, the other [meanings of] <s>pada</s> [arise]. Thus for other beings too, ambiguities exist. If they share the same action, they share the same etymology; if the actions differ, the etymologies differ and should be explained according to their meaning. Thus these twenty-one names for earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) have been enumerated. Among them, <s>nirṛti</s> is from <s>niramana</s> (going out) + <s>ṛcchati</s> (to go); [meaning] misfortune — that is the other [sense]. It is ambiguous with [a name for] earth; the distinction between the two is as follows.

2.8: 'He who made it does not know it; he who saw it, it vanishes from him. Enclosed within the mother's womb, having many offspring, he entered <s>Nirṛti</s> (destruction).' [Meaning:] 'Having many offspring, he falls into distress' — thus say the wandering mendicants (<s>parivrājakā</s>). 'It is the action of rain' — thus say the etymologists (<s>Nairuktāḥ</s>). 'He who made it' — <s>karoti</s> and <s>kirati</s> (to make and to scatter) are ambiguous in the context of rain. 'He does not know it' — [this refers to] the intermediate [state]. He indeed knows it — the intermediate one who has seen [it] — the sun, deposited in the mother's womb — the mother being the atmosphere (<s>antarikṣa</s>); beings are created from it; the womb is the atmosphere, the great region — enclosed by wind (<s>Vāyu</s>); this other womb too is enveloped by the same. With many offspring, it reaches the earth through the action of rain. <s>Śākapūṇi</s> conceived [the thought]: 'I know all the deities.' A deity of dual gender appeared before him. He did not recognize it. He asked it: 'I wish to know you.' It taught him this verse: 'This is my deity.'

2.9: 'This one resounds, by which the cow, set in motion, bellows forth a bellow, resting upon the cloud at the point of destruction. She, by her actions, did not make [herself] mortal; becoming lightning, she pushed back the covering.' This one makes sound, by which the cow (<s>go</s>), having proceeded forth, bellows a bellow — makes sound — or [bellows] like <s>māyu</s> (bellowing), referring to the sun. This is the intermediate speech (<s>vāc</s>), resting upon the cloud (<s>dhvaṃsana</s> = that which scatters). She, by her actions, humbles the mortal from below; becoming lightning, she pushes back the covering (<s>vavri</s>). <s>Vavri</s> is a name for form/covering, from <s>vṛṇoti</s> (to cover). Having covered the earth with rain, she takes it back again.

2.10: The following fifteen are names for gold (<s>hiraṇya</s>). Why [is it called] <s>hiraṇya</s>? Because it is carried away (<s>hriyate</s>) when being stretched; or because it is carried (<s>hriyate</s>) from person to person; or because it is a source of pleasant delight (<s>hitaramaṇa</s>); or because it delights the heart (<s>hṛdayaramaṇa</s>); or it may be from <s>hary</s> meaning 'to desire.' The following sixteen are names for the atmosphere (<s>antarikṣa</s>). Why [is it called] <s>antarikṣa</s>? Because it is between the two ends (<s>antarā kṣa-antam</s>), or 'between these two [heaven and earth]'; or because it is imperishable (<s>akṣaya</s>) within the bodies. Therein, the word <s>samudra</s> (ocean) is confused with the earthly ocean. Why [is it called] <s>samudra</s>? Because waters flow forth from it (<s>samuddravanti</s>); or because waters flow together into it (<s>samabhidravanti</s>); or because beings rejoice in it (<s>sammodante</s>); or because it has gathered waters (<s>samudaka</s>); or because it raises up (<s>samunatti</s>). [Here follows] the distinction between the two [the celestial and terrestrial oceans]. Regarding that, they relate a historical account (<s>itihāsa</s>): <s>Devāpi</s>, son of <s>Ārṣṭiṣeṇa</s>, and <s>Śāntanu</s> the <s>Kauravya</s> were brothers. <s>Śantanu</s>, being the younger, was consecrated [as king], while <s>Devāpi</s> undertook <s>tapas</s> (austerities). Thereafter, during <s>Śāntanu's</s> reign, the god did not rain for twelve years. The <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> told him: 'You have committed <s>adharma</s> by being consecrated while bypassing your elder brother; therefore the god does not rain for you.' <s>Śantanu</s> wished to entrust <s>Devāpi</s> with the kingdom. <s>Devāpi</s> said to him: 'Let me be your <s>purohita</s> (chief priest) and let me perform sacrifices for you.' This is his hymn desiring rain (<s>varṣakāma-sūkta</s>). This [verse] belongs to him:

2.11: "<s>Ārṣṭiṣeṇa</s>, the <s>ṛṣi</s>, sat down for the <s>Hotra</s> (invocation); <s>Devāpi</s>, knowing the goodwill of the gods, released the divine waters of rain from the upper to the lower ocean." <s>Ārṣṭiṣeṇa</s> means 'son of <s>Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa</s>,' or 'of one whose army is sent forth.' <s>Senā</s> (army) — it is powerful. Or having the same movement; <s>putra</s> (son) protects greatly (<s>puru trāyate</s>), or from falling (<s>niparaṇāt</s>) he saves (<s>trāyate</s>) from <s>naraka</s> (hell). 'The <s>ṛṣi</s> sat down for the <s>Hotra</s>' — <s>ṛṣi</s> is from seeing (<s>darśanāt</s>); he saw the <s>stomas</s> (hymns of praise) — [this is the view] of <s>Aupamanyava</s>. It is traditionally known: 'When <s>Brahman</s>, the self-existent, flowed toward them as they were performing <s>tapas</s>, they became <s>ṛṣis</s>; that is the <s>ṛṣi</s>-nature of the <s>ṛṣis</s>.' <s>Devāpi</s> — the attainment (<s>āpti</s>) of the gods, through praise and through offering — knowing <s>devasumati</s>, the auspicious intention of the gods; <s>cikitvān</s> means 'possessed of awareness.' He [released the waters] from the upper to the lower ocean. The upper [ocean] is higher; the lower is below. '[The water] does not flow downward' — upward movement is prohibited. The further explanation of the upper [ocean follows].

2.12: "When <s>Devāpi</s>, the <s>purohita</s> (chief priest) of <s>Śantanu</s>, chosen for the <s>Hotra</s> (invocation), compassionately performed the ritual; granting the rain-seeking [prayer] heard by the gods, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> gave him speech." <s>Śantanu</s> [is so called because] 'may well-being (<s>śam</s>) extend to [his] body (<s>tanu</s>),' or 'may well-being extend to him.' <s>Purohita</s> (chief priest) — they place him in front (<s>pura enam dadhati</s>). He was chosen for the <s>Hotra</s> and, being compassionate, he meditated. <s>Devaśruta</s> — the gods hear him. <s>Vṛṣṭivanim</s> — one who requests rain. <s>Rarāṇaḥ</s> — gift-giving is practiced. <s>Bṛhaspati</s> was the <s>Brahman</s> [priest]; he gave him speech. <s>Bṛhat</s> has been explained above.

2.13: The following are names shared [between <s>Āditya</s> and <s>Dyaus</s>] — of heaven and of the sun. But those that belong to [each] principally, we shall explain subsequently. Why [is he called] <s>Āditya</s>? He takes up (<s>ādatte</s>) essences; he takes up the splendor of lights; or 'he is aflame with splendor'; or 'he is the son of <s>Aditi</s>.' But this [meaning of 'son of <s>Aditi</s>'] has limited usage in the <s>ṛc</s>-tradition in the <s>sūkta</s>-assignment — '<s>Sūryam Āditeyam</s>,' the son of <s>Aditi</s>. Similarly, the praises of other deities also have explanations through <s>Āditya</s> — for example, those of <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, and <s>Aṃśa</s>. And also of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> [together]: '<s>Ādityā</s>, lords of gifts' — lords of giving. And also of <s>Mitra</s> alone: 'O friend (<s>Mitra</s>), may the mortal who worships you, O <s>Āditya</s>, with [due] observance, be liberal' — thus there is also a Vedic passage. And also of <s>Varuṇa</s> alone: 'So may we [abide] in your observance, O <s>Āditya</s>.' <s>Vrata</s> (observance) is a name for action; it restrains (<s>vārayati</s>) the action of withdrawal — from the existing [root]. This other <s>vrata</s> too [is derived] from the same [root] <s>vṛ</s> (to choose). Food (<s>anna</s>) is also called <s>vrata</s> because it covers (<s>āvṛṇoti</s>) the body.

2.14: <s>Svar</s> (heaven) is [a name of] <s>Āditya</s> — [meaning] well-going (<s>su araṇaḥ</s>); or well-moving (<s>su īraṇaḥ</s>); or having well-extracted essences (<s>su ṛtaḥ rasān</s>); or of well-attained splendor of lights; or 'well-attained through splendor.' By this, <s>Dyaus</s> (heaven) is also explained. <s>Pṛśni</s> (spotted/variegated) is [a name of] <s>Āditya</s> — 'he touches its colors' say the <s>Nairuktas</s> (etymologists); he who touches essences; he who touches the splendor of lights; or 'touched by splendor.' [And] <s>Dyaus</s> — she is touched by lights and by the meritorious. <s>Nāka</s> (firmament) is [a name of] <s>Āditya</s> — the leader of essences, the leader of the splendor of lights, the guide. And <s>Dyaus</s> — <s>ka</s> (<s>kam</s>) is a name for happiness; that [happiness] is denied [for the unrighteous] — 'Not for the one who has not gone to that world is <s>nāka</s> in any way.' Not for the one who has gone to that world is <s>nāka</s> [either, unless deserving] — for only the meritorious go there. <s>Gau</s> (ray, cow) is [a name of] <s>Āditya</s> — he makes the essences go (<s>gamayati</s>); they move in the atmosphere. And <s>Dyaus</s> — because the earth has gone far up to it, and because lights move in it. <s>Viṣṭap</s> (abode) is [a name of] <s>Āditya</s> — he has pervaded (<s>āviṣṭaḥ</s>) essences; he has pervaded the splendor of lights; or 'he has been pervaded by splendor.' And <s>Dyaus</s> — she has been pervaded by lights and by the meritorious. <s>Nabhas</s> (sky, cloud) is [a name of] <s>Āditya</s> — the leader of essences, the leader of the splendor of lights, the guide; or alternatively it may be <s>bhana</s> (shining) reversed; or 'it does not shine' (<s>na bhāti</s>). By this, <s>Dyaus</s> is also explained.

2.15: The following fifteen are names for rays (<s>raśmi</s>). <s>Raśmi</s> is from <s>yam</s> (to control). Among those, the first five are shared with horse-reins (<s>aśva-raśmi</s>). The following eight are names for directions (<s>diś</s>). Why [are they called] <s>diś</s>? From <s>diś</s> meaning 'to point out,' or alternatively from reaching (<s>abhyaśanāt</s>). Among those, the word <s>kāṣṭhā</s> (limit, goal) is also a name for more than one entity. The <s>kāṣṭhās</s> are the directions — because they have gone (<s>krāntvā</s>) and stand (<s>sthitā</s>). The <s>kāṣṭhās</s> are the intermediate directions — because they have gone across each other and stand. <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) is also called <s>kāṣṭhā</s> — because he has gone and stands. The end of a racecourse is also called <s>kāṣṭhā</s> — because [the runner] has gone and stands. Waters too are called <s>kāṣṭhās</s> — because they have gone and stand — this applies to stationary things.

2.16: "In the midst of the <s>kāṣṭhās</s> (directions/goals) that do not stand still, that do not settle, the body is placed. The waters move about, [revealing] the secret of <s>Vṛtra</s>; the enemy of <s>Indra</s> lay in the long darkness." '[Those] that do not stand still' — of the non-stationary <s>kāṣṭhās</s> that do not settle, in their midst 'the body is placed' — [this body is] the cloud (<s>megha</s>). <s>Śarīra</s> (body) is from <s>śṝ</s> (to injure, break) or from <s>śam</s> (to be calm). '[The waters] move about' — the waters know, perceive the secret (<s>ninya</s>), the essential nature (<s>nirṇāma</s>), of <s>Vṛtra</s>. <s>Dīrgha</s> (long) is from <s>drāgh</s> (to stretch). <s>Tamas</s> (darkness) is from <s>tan</s> (to extend). <s>Āśayat</s> is from <s>āśī</s> (to lie, recline). <s>Indraśatru</s> (enemy of <s>Indra</s>) — <s>Indra</s> is his pacifier (<s>śamayitā</s>) or destroyer (<s>śātayitā</s>); therefore [he is] <s>indraśatru</s>. So, who is <s>Vṛtra</s>? The <s>Nairuktas</s> (etymologists) say [he is] the cloud (<s>megha</s>); the <s>Aitihāsikas</s> (historians) say [he is] a <s>Tvāṣṭra Asura</s> (a demon created by <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>). From the mixing of waters and light, the action of rain is born, and in that context, descriptions of battle appear by way of metaphor. But the Vedic passages and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> statements indeed describe it as serpent-like. Having grown in body, he blocked the streams; when he was slain, the waters flowed forth. This <s>ṛc</s> (verse) declares that.

[Nirukta 2.17:] "The wives of the <s>dāsa</s> stood guarded by the serpent (<s>ahi</s>); the waters were held back, like cows by a <s>Paṇi</s>. The opening of the waters that had been sealed — having slain <s>Vṛtra</s>, he opened that." '<s>Dāsapatnīḥ</s>' — those whose lord (<s>adhipati</s>) is the <s>dāsa</s>. '<s>Dāsa</s>' is from the root '<s>das</s>' (to destroy) — 'he assigns servile tasks.' '<s>Ahigopāḥ atiṣṭhan</s>' — stood guarded by the serpent. '<s>Ahi</s>' (serpent) is from '<s>ay</s>' (to go) — 'it goes in the atmosphere'; this other serpent (<s>ahi</s>) also [derives] from the same [root], with the prefix dropped — '<s>āhanti</s>' (it strikes). "The waters were held back, like cows, by the serpent (<s>ahi</s>)." '<s>Paṇi</s>' is a merchant (<s>vanij</s>); '<s>paṇi</s>' from '<s>paṇ</s>' (to bargain); '<s>vanij</s>' — he washes the merchandise (<s>panya</s>). "The opening (<s>bila</s>) of the waters that had been sealed" — '<s>bila</s>' is '<s>bhara</s>' (support), from the root '<s>bhṛ</s>' (to bear). "Having slain <s>Vṛtra</s>, he opened that" — '<s>Vṛtra</s>' is from '<s>vṛ</s>' (to cover), or '<s>vṛt</s>' (to turn), or '<s>vṛdh</s>' (to grow). Because he covered [the waters], that is the '<s>vṛtratva</s>' (Vṛtra-nature) of <s>Vṛtra</s> — thus it is known. Because he turned, that is the <s>vṛtratva</s> of <s>Vṛtra</s> — thus it is known. Because he grew, that is the <s>vṛtratva</s> of <s>Vṛtra</s> — thus it is known.

[Nirukta 2.18:] The subsequent names of Night (<s>rātri</s>) are twenty-three. Why is it called '<s>rātri</s>'? Because it causes beings that roam at night to be active (<s>praramayati</s>), causes others to rest (<s>uparamayati</s>), makes them stationary (<s>dhruvīkaroti</s>); or it may be from the root '<s>rā</s>' (to give), from the act of giving — dews (<s>avaśyāya</s>) are given forth in it. The subsequent names of Dawn (<s>usas</s>) are sixteen. Why is it called '<s>usas</s>'? It is truly from '<s>ucchati</s>' (it shines, rises). It is the later time after night; this [dawn] belongs to that [night].

[Nirukta 2.19:] "This best light of lights has come; the brilliant sign has been born, the all-pervading one. As the one who has given birth [yields] to the begetter (<s>Savitṛ</s>) for begetting, so Night has yielded her place to Dawn." "This best light of lights" — has come; 'the brilliant sign' — the widely spread knowledge; was born, the most manifest. "As the one who has given birth, to <s>Savitṛ</s>" — for the purpose of begetting, Night [yields] to the Sun's [rising]; thus Night has yielded (<s>aricat</s>) her place (<s>yoni</s>) to Dawn. '<s>Yoni</s>' (womb, place) for a woman; the embryo is united with her. This [Dawn] is the subsequent one of that [Night].

[Nirukta 2.20:] "Having a bright calf, the bright one has come with her white [companion]; the dark one has yielded her dwelling places. Kindred, immortal, following one another, Day and Night move, changing their colors." '<s>Ruśadvatsā</s>' — having the sun as her calf; '<s>ruśat</s>' is a color-name, from the root '<s>ruc</s>' (to shine). He calls the sun her calf, because of association or because [the sun] draws her essence. "The bright, white one has come" — '<s>śvetyā</s>' from '<s>śvet</s>' (to be white); she has yielded the dark one's dwelling places — the dark-colored Night. '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' (dark) from '<s>kṛṣ</s>' (to drag) — an inferior color. Then he praises both together: 'of the same bond' (<s>samānabandhū</s>) — of the same binding, immortal (<s>amṛte</s>) — of undying nature, 'following each other' (<s>anūcī</s>) — meaning looking at each other. "Day and Night move" — they are the two 'days' (<s>dyāvau</s>), from '<s>dyut</s>' (to shine). Or: 'the days move,' they move together with her. '<s>Āmināne</s>' — exchanging, making each other's nature their own. The subsequent names of Day (<s>ahar</s>) are twelve. Why is it called '<s>ahar</s>'? Because actions are brought (<s>upāharanti</s>) in it. Its occurrence is found in the verse pertaining to <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.

[Nirukta 2.21:] "The dark day and the white day — the two atmospheric regions revolve with their distinguishing activities. <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, being born like a king, <s>Agni</s> has dispelled the darkness with his light." 'The dark day' is Night; 'and the white, bright day'; the two atmospheric regions (<s>rajasī</s>) revolve with their activities that are to be known (<s>veditavyābhiḥ</s>). '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>, being born' — the rising <s>Āditya</s> (sun), king of all lights, like <s>Agni</s>, has dispelled the darkness with light. The subsequent names of Cloud (<s>megha</s>) are thirty. Why is it called '<s>megha</s>'? Because it discharges (<s>mehati</s>). '<s>Upara</s>' and '<s>upala</s>' — these are shared with mountain-names. '<s>Upara</s>/<s>upala</s>' can mean cloud — because the cloud-masses rest (<s>uparamante</s>) in it, or because they have rested. The [following verse] pertains to them.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 2.22:] "In the creation of the gods, the first ones stood; from the cutting-region, the upper ones rose. Three heat the earth as companions; two carry the rainfall (<s>purīṣa</s>) abundantly." 'In the creation (<s>nirmāṇe</s>) of the gods, the first stood' — the middle groups of gods. '<s>Prathama</s>' (first) is a word for 'chief' (<s>mukhya</s>); it means foremost. '<s>Kṛṇtatram</s>' (the cutting-region) is the atmosphere — the rending of clouds. Through the rending of clouds, water is born. 'Three heat the earth as companions' — <s>Parjanya</s> (rain), <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), and <s>Āditya</s> (sun) ripen the plants through cold, heat, and rain; as '<s>anūpāḥ</s>' (companions) they sprinkle the worlds, each with its own activity. The other '<s>anūpa</s>' also [derives] from the same [root] — '<s>anu-upyate</s>' (is sprinkled) with water; or from the root '<s>āp</s>' (to obtain), '<s>anvāp</s>' — as the word '<s>prāk</s>' [becomes '<s>prācīnam</s>']. Its form would be '<s>anūpa</s>' as '<s>prācīnam</s>' (eastward). 'Two carry <s>bṛbūka</s> (rainfall) abundantly' — <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Āditya</s> [carry] water. '<s>Bṛbūka</s>' is a name for water, from '<s>brū</s>' (to speak), the action of sound, or from '<s>bhraṃś</s>' (to fall). '<s>Purīṣa</s>' from '<s>pṛ</s>' (to fill) or '<s>pūr</s>' (to fill up).

[Nirukta 2.23:] The subsequent names of Speech (<s>vāc</s>) are fifty-seven. Why is it called '<s>vāc</s>'? From the root '<s>vac</s>' (to speak). Among those [names], '<s>Sarasvatī</s>' — of this [word], there are Vedic citations both as a river and as a deity. That which pertains to the deity, we shall explain later. Now this pertains to the river.

[Nirukta 2.24:] "She, with her drying powers, broke the peaks of mountains with her surging, mighty waves, like [a plant breaking through with] a lotus stalk. With well-fashioned praises and devotions, let us attend upon <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the slayer of distant shores." '<s>Śuṣmaiḥ</s>' — with drying powers; '<s>śuṣma</s>' is a name for strength, from the root '<s>śoṣ</s>' (to dry). '<s>Bisa</s>' (lotus stalk) from the root '<s>biṣ</s>' (to split), from the action of splitting or of growing. '<s>Sānu</s>' (peak) is that which is elevated (<s>samucchrita</s>), or raised up (<s>samunnunna</s>). 'With great waves (<s>ūrmibhiḥ</s>).' '<s>Pārāvataghnīm</s>' — the destroyer of the far (<s>pāra</s>) and near (<s>avāra</s>) shores, for the sake of descent; 'with beautiful praises (<s>supravṛktibhiḥ</s>), let us worship <s>Sarasvatī</s> the river with our works.' The subsequent names of Water (<s>udaka</s>) are one hundred and one. Why is it called '<s>udaka</s>'? From the root '<s>und</s>' (to wet). The subsequent names of River (<s>nadī</s>) are thirty-seven. Why '<s>nadī</s>'? Because these are 'resounding' (<s>nadanāḥ</s>), having sound. The <s>Naighaṇṭuka</s> (glossary) entries for them are mostly presented in a remarkable manner, chiefly. Regarding that, they narrate this history: The sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was the <s>purohita</s> (priest) of king <s>Sudās Paijavana</s>. '<s>Viśvāmitra</s>' means 'friend of all' (<s>sarvamitra</s>), 'all that is connected.' '<s>Sudās</s>' means 'giver of good things' (<s>kalyāṇadāna</s>). '<s>Paijavana</s>' — son of <s>Pijavana</s>; '<s>Pijavana</s>' means either 'one whose speed is to be competed with' or 'one whose movement is unmixed.' He (<s>Sudās</s>), having seized [the territory], came to the confluence of <s>Vipāṭ</s> (Beas) and <s>Śutudrī</s> (Sutlej); the others followed. That <s>Viśvāmitra</s> praised the rivers, [saying] 'become fordable' — [this applies] to both the dual and plural [forms]; that which is in the dual, we shall explain later; now this is the plural [form]:

[Nirukta 2.25:] "Be pleased with my <s>Soma</s>-worthy speech, O rivers flowing with truth; pause for a moment with your currents. With a great hymn, directed toward the <s>Sindhu</s>, the son of <s>Kuśika</s> calls you, seeking help." '<s>Uparamadhvam</s>' — pause; 'my speech, <s>Soma</s>-worthy' — leading to <s>Soma</s>. '<s>Ṛtāvarīḥ</s>' — possessing <s>ṛta</s> (truth/water). '<s>Ṛta</s>' is a name for water; it recurs (<s>praty ṛtam bhavati</s>). '<s>Muhūrtam</s>' — with currents (<s>evaiḥ</s>), courses (<s>ayanaiḥ</s>), or flows (<s>avanaiḥ</s>). '<s>Muhūrta</s>' is a 'repeated season' (<s>muhur ṛtu</s>); '<s>ṛtu</s>' from the root '<s>ṛ</s>' (to go), the action of going; '<s>muhūrta</s>' — a time that is as if bewildered (<s>mūḍha</s>), i.e. frequently recurring. And '<s>abhīkṣṇam</s>' (frequently) is '<s>abhikṣaṇam</s>'; '<s>kṣaṇa</s>' (moment) from the root '<s>kṣaṇ</s>' (to consume) — 'time that destroys.' '<s>Kāla</s>' (time) from the root '<s>kal</s>' (to move), the action of going. 'I invoke the <s>Sindhu</s> with a great, immense hymn (<s>manīṣā</s>)' — the movement of the mind (<s>manasa īṣā</s>) — or with praise and wisdom — for the sake of help, [being] the son of <s>Kuśika</s>. '<s>Kuśika</s>' was a king, from the root '<s>kruś</s>' (to cry out), the action of making sound; or from '<s>kraṃś</s>' (to make known), the action of making manifest — 'one who makes worthy things cry out.' The rivers replied —

[2.26] '<s>Indro asmān aradad vajrabāhur apāhan vṛtram paridhim nadīnām / devo anayat savitā supānis tasya vayam prasave yāma ūrvīḥ</s>' — '<s>Indra</s> dug for us, [he who is] thunderbolt-armed; he struck down <s>Vṛtra</s>, the barrier of the rivers; the divine <s>Savitṛ</s> of beautiful hands led [us]; in his impulsion, we go to the wide [spaces].' <s>Indra</s> dug for us, [being] thunderbolt-armed; <s>radati</s> (digs) is a root meaning to dig. 'He struck down <s>Vṛtra</s>, the barrier of the rivers' — this has been explained. 'The divine <s>Savitṛ</s> of beautiful hands' — <s>supāṇi</s> means having beautiful hands. <s>Pāṇi</s> (hand) is from <s>panāyati</s> (to worship), from the action of worship — having grasped their hands, they worship the gods. 'In his impulsion, we go to the wide [spaces]' — <s>urvī</s> (wide) is from <s>ūrṇoti</s> (to cover) or <s>vṛṇoti</s> (to encompass) — so says <s>Aurṇavābha</s>. Having refused, they finally listened.

[2.27] '<s>Ā te kāraḥ śṛṇavāmā vacāṃsi yayātha dūrād anasā rathena / ni te naṃsai pīpyānā iva yoṣā maryāyā iva kanyā śaśvacai te</s>' — 'Let us hear the praises and words of you who have come from afar by cart and chariot. I bow down to you like a woman suckling [her child], like a maiden [bowing] to her suitor — forever to you.' We wish to hear your praiseworthy words. Come from afar by both cart and chariot. We bow down to you like a woman nursing her son, or like a maiden bowing for the embrace of her suitor. The following [section lists] twenty-six names for horse. Of these, the eight following have multiple [etymologies]. Why is [a horse called] <s>aśva</s>? Because it traverses (<s>aśnute</s>) the road, or because it is a great eater (<s>mahāśana</s>). Among these, <s>dadhikrā</s> — this means 'holding forth and striding' (<s>dadhat krāmati</s>), or 'holding forth and neighing' (<s>dadhat krandati</s>), or 'holding forth and acting' (<s>dadhad ākārī bhavati</s>). Its Vedic usages occur both in the horse-sense and in the deity-sense. The deity-related [usages] we shall explain later; now the horse-related [ones].

[2.28] '<s>Uta sya vājī kṣipaṇim turaṇyati grīvāyām baddho apikakṣa āsani / kratum dadhikrā anu saṃtavītvat pathām aṅkāṃsy anvāpanīphanat</s>' — And that prize-winner (<s>vājī</s>) — possessing speed — swiftly traverses the road toward the whip-strike, bound at the neck. <s>Grīvā</s> (neck) is from <s>girati</s> (to swallow), or from <s>gṛṇāti</s> (to praise), or from <s>gṛhṇāti</s> (to grasp). '<s>Apikakṣa āsani</s>' — this has been explained. <s>Dadhikrā</s> followed the action or the intelligence — <s>saṃtavītvat</s> — extended [it]. [This is] a Vedic usage with the prior form from the root <s>tan</s> (to extend). 'The bends of the roads' — the curves of the roads; <s>panthāḥ</s> (path) is from <s>patati</s> (to fall), or <s>padyate</s> (to step), or <s>panthati</s>. <s>Aṅka</s> (bend) is from <s>añcati</s> (to curve). <s>Āpanīphanat</s> is an intensive (<s>carkarīta</s>) form from <s>phanati</s> (to leap/spring). The following ten are said to be terms for implements [of the horse], for the purpose of understanding their contextual associations. The following eleven roots have meanings of 'to blaze.' Just as many following names are names for 'blazing.'

[3.1] The following twenty-six are names for action (<s>karma</s>). Why [is action called] <s>karma</s>? Because it is done (<s>kriyate</s>). The following fifteen are names for offspring (<s>apatya</s>). Why [is offspring called] <s>apatya</s>? Because it falls away (<s>apatatat bhavati</s>), or 'it does not fall (<s>na anena patati</s>)' [i.e., the lineage does not fall because of it]. [Following the pattern of citing] a Ṛg Vedic verse relating to the meaning, just as [we did for] the offspring of a parent —

[3.2] '<s>Parisadyam hy aranasya rekno nityasya rāyaḥ patayaḥ syāma / na śeṣo agner anyajātam asty acetānasya mā patho vi dukṣaḥ</s>' — 'The wealth of a stranger is to be avoided, not to be approached. May we be lords of our hereditary wealth. There is no offspring of fire born from another. [O <s>Agni</s>,] of the mindless one, do not corrupt the paths.' <s>Araṇa</s> (stranger) means one who is without merit (<s>apārṇa</s>). <s>Rekṇa</s> is a name for wealth — it is left over (<s>ricyate</s>) by the one who departs. 'May we be lords of hereditary wealth' — as of ancestral property. 'There is no offspring of fire born from another.' <s>Śeṣa</s> is a name for offspring — it remains (<s>śiṣyate</s>) when one departs; it belongs to one who is mindless, that is, heedless. 'Do not corrupt our paths' — the following [verse is] for further explanation.

[3.3] '<s>Na hi grabhāya araṇaḥ suśevo anyaudaryo manasā mantavā u / adhā cid okaḥ punar it sa ety ā no vājī abhīsāl etu navyaḥ</s>' — 'A stranger, however pleasant, should not be taken [as an heir]; one born from another womb should not even be thought of in mind. Yet that one returns to his [own] home. Let a prize-winner come to us — a newly born one, as a chariot-contender.' An outsider (<s>araṇa</s>), even the most comfortable, should not be adopted; one born from another womb should not even be thought of [with the thought] 'this is my son.' For he returns to his [natal] home, from where he came. <s>Okas</s> is a name for dwelling. 'Let a prize-winner (<s>vājī</s>) — one possessing speed, overcoming rivals, newly born — come to us' — that is, a [natural] son. And this [next verse] they cite regarding the inheritance-right of a daughter.

body.translated_text: [3.4] '<s>Śāsad vahnir duhitur naptyam gād vidvān ṛtasya dīdhitim saparyan / pitā yatra duhituḥ sekam ṛñjant sam śagmyena manasā dadhanve</s>' — 'The husband (<s>vahnī</s>) commands the daughter's grandson to go forth; the knower worships the illumination of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order). Where the father bestows the seed upon the daughter, they unite with harmonious mind.' The husband commands for the purpose of continuing the lineage — [i.e.,] the transformation of the daughter into a son. <s>Duhitā</s> (daughter) — '<s>durhitā</s>' (badly placed), or 'placed far away' (<s>dūre hitā</s>), or from <s>dogdhi</s> (to milk). <s>Naptṛ</s> means the daughter's son (<s>dauhitra</s>) or grandson (<s>pautra</s>). The knower — worshipping the rite of procreation, [that is,] of the seed born from limb to limb, born from the heart, the arrangement of the <s>ṛta</s> (truth) with respect to the mother. Without distinction, sons born in a couple are heirs. This is stated by a verse and a <s>śloka</s>: 'From limb to limb you are born; from the heart you are generated. You are indeed the self named son; live a hundred autumns.' And: 'The inheritance of children is by right, without distinction; of [male-female] couples, beginning with the sending forth — so said <s>Manu Svāyambhuva</s>.' [But] the daughter does not [inherit] — [say] some. Therefore, 'a man is an heir; a woman is not an heir' — thus it is known. Therefore, 'they cast away a daughter when born, but not a son.' For women, gift, sale, and release [into another family] exist — not for men. But for men also [there is sale], say some — from the evidence [in the story] of <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>. 'The [case of] one without brothers' is another [consideration]. 'These [women] go forth, kinswomen, all wearing red garments; they stand like [women] without brothers, their path destroyed.' Women without brothers stand [alone] for continuing the lineage and for offering the funeral cake — their path destroyed. The simile [of being] without brothers [represents] the inability [of such women to establish the lineage]. The following [verse is] for further explanation.

[3.5] '<s>Abhrātā iva puṃsa eti pratīcī gartārug iva sanaye dhanānām / jāyeva patya uśatī suvāsā uṣā hasrā iva nirinīte apsaḥ</s>' — 'Like a woman without brothers, she goes toward the man; like one ascending the assembly-seat for the acquisition of wealth; like a well-dressed wife desiring her husband; <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), as if laughing, reveals her splendors.' Like a woman without brothers, she goes toward the men — toward the ancestors — facing [them] for the purpose of continuing the lineage and offering the funeral cake. Not [like] one going to a husband. Like one ascending the assembly-seat (<s>garta</s>) — the place of assembly — for the purpose of acquiring wealth; one who participates in the gift-giving [assembly]. <s>Garta</s> is an assembly-seat, from <s>gṛṇāti</s> (to speak) — one makes a truthful declaration. There, a woman without a son ascends [it]; there they strike her with dice, and she obtains the inheritance. <s>Garta</s> is also used for a funeral mound, from <s>purati</s> (to fill) — it is heaped up. <s>Śmaśāna</s> (cremation ground) is <s>śmaśamana</s> — the calming of <s>śman</s> (body); body (<s>śarīra</s>) is from <s>śṛṇāti</s> (to break) or <s>śamnāti</s> (to calm). <s>Śmaśru</s> (beard) — hair (<s>loman</s>) that resides on the <s>śman</s> (body). <s>Loman</s> (hair) is from <s>lunāti</s> (to cut) or <s>līyate</s> (to cling). 'One should not expose what is of the subterranean [fire]; if one were to expose what is subterranean, the sacrificer, dwelling in the pit, would die' — this Vedic passage also exists. <s>Garta</s> is also used for a chariot, from <s>gṛṇāti</s> in the sense of praise — the most praised vehicle. '<s>Ā rohatho varuṇa mitra gartam</s>' — this Vedic passage also exists. Like a wife desiring her husband, beautifully dressed at the time of her season; <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), as if laughing, reveals her teeth — that is, her forms. These are four similes. 'One should not marry a woman without brothers, for her offspring belongs to [her father's family]' — this is the direct prohibition against marrying a brotherless woman. [Also explained is] the father's relationship to the son-status [of a daughter's child]: where the father bestows the seed upon an unmarried daughter — he unites, he forms a self through union, with [harmonious] mind. And they cite this [verse] regarding the prohibition of inheritance for a co-wife; [some say] 'the eldest [share goes] to the <s>putrikā</s> (appointed daughter)' — so say some.

3.6: 'He did not assign the inheritance of his body to a sister; he made [the wife] the repository of the womb of the acquirer. When the mothers bore the fire-bearer [son], one becomes the maker of good deeds, another enjoys [the inheritance].' <s>Jāmi</s> means sister; or others beget offspring (<s>jā</s>) in her; or it may be from <s>jamati</s> (to go), [since] she mostly goes away [from the family]. The son (<s>tānva</s>, 'born of the body') distributed the inheritance; he made her [the wife] the receptacle of the womb for the acquirer (<s>sanitu</s>, the husband, lit. 'hand-grasper'). When the mother bore a fire-bearer [i.e. son] and a non-fire-bearer [i.e. daughter], one of them — the male — becomes the perpetuator of the lineage, the other is the heir; having given her a portion, the sister is given to another [in marriage].

3.7: The following are twenty-five names for 'human' (<s>manuṣya</s>). Why [are they called] <s>manuṣya</s>? Because having thought (<s>matvā</s>), they perform actions; or because they were created by the thinking one; <s>manasyati</s> again [means] 'being thoughtful' in the sense of possessing mind; or [they are] the offspring of <s>Manu</s>, or of <s>Manus</s>. Among these, the Vedic usages of '<s>pañca janāḥ</s>' (five peoples) occur.
