body.translated_text: 3.8: 'May I now first attain that supreme speech by which the gods overcame the <s>Asura</s>s. O eaters of food and performers of sacrifice, O five peoples, enjoy my oblation.' May I now attain that supreme speech by which we gods may overcome the <s>Asura</s>s. <s>Asura</s>s — because of being in states of <s>asuratā</s> (demonhood); or because they are cast (<s>asta</s>) from their stations. Or alternatively, <s>asu</s> is a name for breath (<s>prāṇa</s>); it dwells (<s>astaḥ</s>) in the body; those possessing it are <s>Asura</s>s. From <s>su</s> (the auspicious), he created the gods — that is the godhood of the <s>Sura</s>s; from <s>asu</s>, he created the <s>Asura</s>s — that is the demonhood of the <s>Asura</s>s, so it is known. '<s>Ūrjāda uta yajñiyāsaḥ</s>' — eaters of food and fit for sacrifice. <s>Ūrj</s> is a name for food, from <s>ūrjayati</s> (to strengthen); or [it means] cooked and well-prepared. 'O five peoples, enjoy my oblation.' <s>Gandharva</s>s, <s>Pitṛ</s>s, gods, <s>Asura</s>s, and <s>Rākṣasa</s>s — according to some. The four <s>varṇa</s>s with <s>Niṣāda</s> as the fifth — according to <s>Aupamanyava</s>. Why <s>Niṣāda</s>? Because he sits down (<s>nisadana</s>); or because evil has settled (<s>nisanna</s>) in him — according to the etymologists. 'With the people born of the five' — with the people of the five tribes. The number five is combined alike in feminine, masculine, and neuter. The following are twelve names for 'arm' (<s>bāhu</s>). Why <s>bāhu</s>? Because actions are impelled (<s>prabādhate</s>) by them. The following are twenty-two names for 'finger' (<s>aṅguli</s>). Why <s>aṅguli</s>? Because they go first (<s>agra-gāminī</s>), or because they drip first, or because they act first, or because they move first, or because they mark (<s>aṅkanā</s>), or because they anoint (<s>añcanā</s>), or indeed from the act of anointing (<s>abhyañcana</s>) itself. Regarding them, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 3.9: 'From the ten earth-protectors, from the ten girths, from the ten ties, from the ten yokings, from the ten reins — honor the ageless ones — from the ten yokes and ten yoked bearers.' The <s>avanī</s>s (earth-protectors/straps) are bindings; they protect (<s>avanti</s>) the actions. The <s>kakṣyā</s>s (girths) make the actions manifest. Ties (<s>yoktra</s>) and yokings (<s>yojana</s>) have been explained. The reins (<s>abhīśu</s>) reach out to (<s>abhyaśnuvate</s>) the actions. 'From the ten yokes and ten yoked bearers' — <s>dhūr</s> (yoke-pole) is from <s>dhūrvati</s> (to strike), with the sense of killing; this other <s>dhūr</s> also [derives] from the same [root]; [alternatively, it] bears the burden (<s>vaha</s>), or from <s>dhārayati</s> (to support). The following eighteen roots have the sense of shining (<s>kānti-karman</s>). The following are twenty-eight names for 'food' (<s>anna</s>). Why <s>anna</s>? Because it is bent toward (<s>ānata</s>) beings, or from <s>atti</s> (to eat). The following ten roots have the sense of eating. The following are twenty-eight names for 'strength' (<s>bala</s>). Why <s>bala</s>? Because strength is bearing (<s>bhara</s>), from <s>bibharti</s> (to bear). The following are also twenty-eight names for 'wealth' (<s>dhana</s>). Why <s>dhana</s>? From <s>hinoti</s> (to impel). The following are nine names for 'cow' (<s>go</s>). The following ten roots have the sense of being angry. The following are eleven names for 'anger' (<s>krodha</s>). The following two hundred and twenty-two roots have the sense of motion (<s>gati-karman</s>). The following are twenty-six names for 'speed' (<s>kṣipra</s>). Why <s>kṣipra</s>? Because the distance is contracted (<s>saṃkṣipta</s>). The following are eleven names for 'nearness' (<s>antika</s>). Why <s>antika</s>? Because it is brought near (<s>ānīta</s>). The following are forty-six names for 'battle' (<s>saṃgrāma</s>). Why <s>saṃgrāma</s>? From coming together (<s>saṃgamana</s>), or from resounding together (<s>saṃgaraṇa</s>), or because two villages (<s>grāma</s>) meet. Among these, the Vedic usages of '<s>khala</s>' occur:

3.10: 'Alone I am supreme over this one; alone I have prevailed over two — what then can three do to me? Like [a winnower] on a threshing-floor, I strike down many enemies. Why do the foes without <s>Indra</s> revile me?' I overpower this one alone; I am alone; overpowering rivals, I prevail — what can two, what can three do to me? One (<s>eka</s>) — from going (<s>itā</s>), the first number; two (<s>dvau</s>) — a swifter number; three (<s>trayas</s>) — the most crossed-over number; four (<s>catvāraḥ</s>) — the most moving number; eight (<s>aṣṭau</s>) — from <s>aśnoti</s> (to reach); nine (<s>nava</s>) — either 'not to be praised' or 'not attained'; ten (<s>daśa</s>) — from <s>dasta</s> (bitten), or [meaning] 'seen in purpose.' Twenty is twice-ten; a hundred is ten-tens; a thousand (<s>sahasra</s>) is enduring; <s>ayuta</s>, <s>niyuta</s>, <s>prayuta</s> — each multiplied [from the previous]. <s>Ambuda</s> (cloud) is <s>megha</s>; water (<s>ambu</s>) is given (<s>da</s>) by it — [hence] <s>ambuda</s>; or it shines possessing water; or it possesses water — just as it becomes great and abundant when raining, so [by analogy] is <s>arbuda</s> [a large number]. 'Like on a threshing-floor, I strike down many enemies.' Like on a threshing-floor (<s>khala</s>), I strike down enemies abundantly; <s>khala</s> is a name for battle, from <s>khalati</s> (to stumble) or <s>skhalati</s> (to slip). This other <s>khala</s> (threshing-floor) also [derives] from the same [root]; [because grain] is piled upon it. 'Why do the foes without <s>Indra</s> revile me?' — those who have not known <s>Indra</s>; for I am <s>Indra</s>; or 'the others are without <s>Indra</s> [i.e. powerless].' The following ten roots have the sense of pervading. Among them, two names: <s>ākṣāṇa</s> (reaching) [and] <s>āśnuvāna</s> (attaining), <s>āpāna</s> (obtaining) [and] <s>āpnuvāna</s> (reaching). The following thirty-three roots have the sense of killing. Among them, <s>viyāta</s> — either 'he stretches out' or 'stretch out!' '<s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>, you are invoked' — the breaker; <s>khanda</s> from <s>khaṇḍayati</s> (to break). <s>Taḍit</s> (lightning) has a combined sense of nearness and striking, from <s>tāḍayati</s> (to strike).

3.11: 'Through you, O well-nourishing <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>, we humans would obtain desirable wealth; those who are our lightning-bolts from afar, those who are our enemies — crush those breathless ones.' Through you, O well-nurturing <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>, we would obtain desirable goods for humans, and those who are our lightning-strikes from afar and those who are our enemies nearby — those who are non-giving in action or non-giving in knowledge. Crush those breathless ones — <s>apra</s> is the derived form; the name comes from <s>āpnoti</s> (to obtain). Lightning (<s>taḷit</s>) is what <s>vidyut</s> is, says <s>Śākapūni</s>; for it strikes down and is visible from afar. But actually the word <s>antika</s> (near) is what is intended here. 'Even being far, you shine forth like lightning' — even being far, you appear as if near. The following eighteen are names of the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>). Why <s>vajra</s>? Because it averts (<s>varjayati</s>). Among them, <s>Kutsa</s> — this is from the root <s>kṛṇtati</s> (to cut). The <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Kutsa</s> is the maker of <s>stoma</s>s (hymns of praise), according to <s>Aupamanyava</s>. Here too his action is that of slaying — '<s>Indra</s>, his friend, slew <s>Śuṣṇa</s>.' The following four roots denote actions of sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>). The following four are names of the sovereign (<s>īśvara</s>). Among them, <s>ina</s> — either 'he has obtained sovereignty' or 'sovereignty has been obtained by him.'

3.12: 'Where the well-winged ones unceasingly sing to their share of immortality at the assembly — the lord, the guardian of the entire world — he, the wise one, has entered the simple one here.' Where the well-winged ones (<s>suparṇāḥ</s>), those of good flight — the rays of the sun — unceasingly sing to or approach their share of immortality, that is, of water, through knowledge at the assembly. The lord (<s>īśvara</s>), the guardian of all beings, is <s>Āditya</s> (the sun). 'He, the wise one, has entered the simple one here' — the wise one (<s>dhīra</s>) is the intelligent one; the simple one (<s>pāka</s>) is that which is to be ripened; the one of ripened knowledge is <s>Āditya</s> — this is the esoteric (<s>upaniṣad</s>) explanation, which pertains to the cosmic interpretation (<s>adhidaivatam</s>). Now the personal interpretation (<s>adhyātmam</s>): where the well-winged ones, the senses with their good movements, unceasingly sing to or approach their share of immortality, that is, of knowledge, through awareness. The lord, the guardian of all the senses, is the <s>Ātman</s> (Self). 'He, the wise one, has entered the simple one here' — the wise one is the intelligent one; the simple one is that which is to be ripened; the one of ripened knowledge is the <s>Ātman</s> — thus he describes the course of the Self.

body.translated_text: 3.13: The following twelve are names of 'many' (<s>bahu</s>). Why <s>bahu</s>? Because it prevails (<s>prabhavati</s>). The following eleven are names of 'short' (<s>hrasva</s>). <s>Hrasva</s> is from <s>hrasati</s> (to diminish). The following twenty-five are names of 'great' (<s>mahat</s>). Why <s>mahat</s>? It surpasses (<s>jahāti</s>) others by its measure, says <s>Śākapūni</s>; or it is worthy of reverence (<s>mahanīya</s>). Among them, <s>vavakṣitha</s> and <s>vivakṣasa</s> — these are from either <s>vakti</s> (to speak) or <s>vahati</s> (to carry), with reduplication. The following twenty-two are names of 'house' (<s>gṛha</s>). Why <s>gṛhāḥ</s>? Because they seize (<s>gṛhṇanti</s>). The following ten roots denote the action of tending (<s>paricaraṇa</s>). The following twenty are names of 'happiness' (<s>sukha</s>). Why <s>sukha</s>? It is good (<s>su</s>) for the senses (<s>kha</s>); <s>kha</s> in turn is from <s>khanati</s> (to dig). The following sixteen are names of 'form' (<s>rūpa</s>). <s>Rūpa</s> is from <s>rocati</s> (to shine). The following ten are names of 'praiseworthy' (<s>praśasya</s>). The following eleven are names of 'wisdom' (<s>prajñā</s>). The following six are names of 'truth' (<s>satya</s>). Why <s>satya</s>? It has its origin (<s>tāyate</s>) in the real (<s>sat</s>); or it has its origin from that. The following [eight] words denote the action of seeing (<s>paśyati</s>). The following roots beginning with <s>cāyati</s> and names are mixed. The following nine words are for the complete collection of all words. Now, from here [we treat] similes (<s>upamā</s>). That which resembles that which it is not — that is a simile, says <s>Gārgya</s>; that is their function [i.e., the meaning of similes]. One compares the lesser or the less well-known with a greater quality or the most well-known. And also, the greater with the lesser.

3.14: 'Like body-abandoning thieves, the two forest-goers [are controlled] by ten cords.' <s>Tanūtyaj</s> means body-abandoners; <s>vanargū</s> means forest-goers — the two fire-churning arms are compared to thieves. <s>Taskara</s> (thief) — he is one who does that (<s>tat-kara</s>) which is evil, say the etymologists (<s>Nairuktāḥ</s>); or it may be from <s>tanoti</s> (to extend), meaning one who acts continuously, or one who acts by day and night. [Controlled] by ten cords (<s>raśanābhiḥ daśabhiḥ</s>). <s>Abhyadhītām</s> means <s>abhyadhātām</s> (they controlled). The greater quality is intended here in the comparison.

3.15: 'Where at night, where by day, O <s>Aśvins</s>, where do you arrive, where do you dwell? Who takes you to bed — as a widow her brother-in-law, as a maiden her man, in the assembly?' Where are you at night, where by day? Where do you arrive, where do you dwell? Who takes you to bed, as a widow her brother-in-law (<s>devara</s>)? Why <s>devara</s>? He is called the second husband (<s>dvitīya vara</s>). A widow (<s>vidhavā</s>) is one who has a disposer, or from <s>vidhavana</s> (wandering), or from <s>vidhāvana</s> (running about), says <s>Carmaśiras</s>; or, <s>dhava</s> is a name for a man — from separation (<s>viyoga</s>) from him, she is <s>vidhavā</s>. <s>Devara</s> — one whose action is shining (<s>dīpyati</s>). <s>Marya</s> — a human, one subject to death (<s>maraṇa-dharmā</s>). <s>Yoṣā</s> is from <s>yauti</s> (to unite); she acts in the common dwelling (<s>saha-sthāna</s>). Now, the particles (<s>nipāta</s>s) have been explained earlier. <s>Yathā</s> (as/like) is a simile of action. 'As the wind, as the forest, as the ocean moves.' 'Blazing like fire.' 'The essence of disease perishes, like before the seizer of the living.' <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is from either <s>atati</s> (to go) or <s>āpti</s> (to pervade); or it would be like <s>āpta</s> (attained) — all-pervading in extent. Like the <s>Maruts</s> who are fires, shining, bright-chested, glittering, with golden breast-plates.

3.16: 'One should be afraid even of one who gives four [dice], up to the point of placing down; one should not desire bad speech.' One who holds four dice — just as one would fear a gambler, so one should fear bad speech; one should never desire to speak ill. <s>Ā</s> is a prefixed particle (<s>upasarga</s>), explained earlier. Moreover, it is also seen in the sense of simile. '<s>Jāra</s> — to the woman's fortune' — like a lover to a woman's fortune; the sun (<s>Āditya</s>) is here called <s>jāra</s>, the ager of the night. He himself is also speech. This Vedic citation also occurs: 'May the sister's <s>jāra</s> (lover) hear us.' He calls the dawn (<s>Uṣas</s>) his sister, because of association or because of extracting essence. But rather, a human lover is what is intended here; <s>bhaga</s> (fortune) would then refer to the woman; it is from <s>bhajati</s> (to share, to enjoy). <s>Meṣa</s> is a simile of being (<s>bhūta-upamā</s>): 'like a ram, the one who leads forth.' <s>Meṣa</s> (ram) is from <s>miṣati</s> (to blink); likewise <s>paśu</s> (animal) is from <s>paśyati</s> (to see). <s>Agni</s> is a simile of form (<s>rūpa-upamā</s>). 'Of golden form, he of golden appearance — <s>Apām Napāt</s> (Son of Waters) seated, is of golden color.' His form is like that of gold. And <s>thā</s> [is used as a simile particle]: 'like the ancient, like the former, like all, like this.' Like the ancient, like the former, like all, like this. This one is closer to that, that one is more distant from this; <s>amuthā</s> (thus) has been explained as 'like that.' <s>Vat</s> (like) is a fixed simile (<s>siddhā-upamā</s>): 'like a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, like a <s>Vṛṣala</s>' — meaning 'as if a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, as if a <s>Vṛṣala</s>.' <s>Vṛṣala</s> — one of manly character (<s>vṛṣa-śīla</s>); or one having the character of a bull (<s>vṛṣā-śīla</s>).

3.17: "Like <s>Priyamedha</s>, like <s>Atri</s>, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, like <s>Virūpa</s>, like <s>Aṅgiras</s>, O thou of great observance — hear the call of <s>Praskanva</s>." <s>Priyamedha</s> — one whose <s>medhā</s> (intellect, sacrifice) is dear. Just as [you favored] these <s>ṛṣis</s>, so hear the call of <s>Praskanva</s>. <s>Praskanva</s> is the son of <s>Kanva</s>; he is of <s>Kanva</s> origin, as [explained] before. <s>Bhṛgu</s> was born in the flame (<s>arcis</s>). <s>Bhṛgu</s> — [so called because] he was being roasted (<s>bhṛjyamānaḥ</s>) but not in the body. <s>Aṅgiras</s> [was born] in the embers (<s>aṅgāras</s>). <s>Aṅgāras</s> (embers) are so called from marking (<s>aṅkanāḥ</s>) or anointing (<s>añcanāḥ</s>). 'He reaches the third right here,' they said; therefore <s>Atri</s> — as if 'not three' (<s>na trayaḥ</s>). <s>Vaikhānasa</s> is from digging (<s>vikhananāt</s>); <s>Bhāradvāja</s> is from bearing (<s>bharaṇāt</s>); <s>Virūpa</s> means of various forms (<s>nānā rūpaḥ</s>); <s>Mahivrata</s> means having a great observance (<s>mahā vrataḥ</s>).

3.18: Now, they speak of <s>luptopamā</s> (elliptical comparisons) and <s>arthopamā</s> (comparisons of meaning). '<s>Siṃha</s>' (lion) and '<s>vyāghra</s>' (tiger) are used in praise; '<s>śvā</s>' (dog) and '<s>kāla</s>' (crow) are used in censure. '<s>Kāka</s>' (crow) is an onomatopoeia — this is frequent among birds. <s>Aupamanyava</s> says there is no onomatopoeia [here]; <s>kāka</s> means one that makes a harsh sound. <s>Tittiri</s> (partridge) is from crossing (<s>taraṇāt</s>); or 'spotted as much as a sesame seed' (<s>tilamātracitra</s>). <s>Kapi</s> (monkey) — like one that is worn out (<s>jīrṇaḥ</s>); or like one that moves swiftly; or slightly tawny; or 'it produces a beautiful sound' (<s>kamanīyaṃ śabdaṃ piñjayati</s>). <s>Śvā</s> (dog) — a swift goer (<s>āśu yāyī</s>); or from <s>śav</s> meaning 'to go'; or from <s>śvas</s> (to breathe). <s>Siṃha</s> (lion) — from enduring (<s>sahanāt</s>); or it may be from <s>hiṃs</s> (to injure) in reverse; or from <s>han</s> (to strike) with the prefix <s>sam</s> — 'he gathers and strikes' (<s>saṃhāya hanti</s>). <s>Vyāghra</s> (tiger) — from fierce odor (<s>vyāghrāṇāt</s>); or 'he opens wide and strikes' (<s>vyādāya hanti</s>).

body.translated_text: 3.19: The following forty-four are verbal roots denoting the action of praising (<s>arcati-karman</s>). The following twenty-four are names for one who is wise (<s>medhāvin</s>). Why [is one called] <s>medhāvī</s>? Because he possesses <s>medhā</s> (intellect); <s>medhā</s> is that in which understanding (<s>mati</s>) is placed (<s>dhīyate</s>). The following thirteen are names for a praiser (<s>stotṛ</s>). <s>Stotā</s> (praiser) is from praising (<s>stavanāt</s>). The following fifteen are names for sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>). Why [is it called] <s>yajña</s>? <s>Yaj</s> is a well-known action of worship, say the <s>Nairuktas</s> (etymologists); or it involves requesting (<s>yācna</s>); or it involves exaltation (<s>yajr unnas</s>); or 'many black antelope skins' says <s>Aupamanyava</s>; or 'the <s>Yajus</s> formulas lead him.' The following eight are names for a priest (<s>ṛtvij</s>). Why [is one called] <s>ṛtvij</s>? [He is] a mover; 'he is a praiser of <s>ṛc</s>' says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>; or 'he is a sacrificer at the proper season' (<s>ṛtuyājī</s>). The following seventeen are verbal roots denoting the action of requesting (<s>yācnā</s>). The following ten are verbal roots denoting the action of giving (<s>dāna</s>). The following four are verbal roots denoting the action of inviting (<s>adhyeṣaṇā</s>). There are two actions of sleeping (<s>svapiti</s>), <s>svapiti</s> being [a root that] exists. The following fourteen are names for a well (<s>kūpa</s>). Why [is it called] <s>kūpa</s>? Because it involves boiling (<s>kupāna</s>) or from <s>kup</s> (to be agitated). The following fourteen are names for a thief (<s>stena</s>). Why [is one called] <s>stena</s>? 'Sinful concealment (<s>saṃstyāna</s>) is in him,' say the <s>Nairuktas</s>. The following six are names for what is removed or hidden (<s>nirṇīta-antarhita</s>). Why [is it called] <s>nirṇīta</s>? Because it has been cleansed (<s>nirṇiktam</s>). The following five are names for what is distant (<s>dūra</s>). Why [is it called] <s>dūra</s>? Because it has run (<s>drutam</s>); or because it is hard to reach (<s>durayam</s>). The following six are names for what is old (<s>purāṇa</s>). Why [is it called] <s>purāṇa</s>? Because it was formerly new (<s>purā navam</s>). The following six are names for what is new (<s>nava</s>). Why [is it called] <s>nava</s>? Because it has been brought (<s>ānītam</s>).

body.translated_text: 3.20: The following are names that occur in pairs. '<s>Pravit</s>' and '<s>abhīka</s>' [are names] of what is near — '<s>prapitve</s>' means 'on arriving'; '<s>abhīke</s>' means 'anointed, made manifest.' 'Come quickly to us at our reaching, at our arriving.' 'He who creates space even in close encounter' — these too are Vedic passages. '<s>Dabhra</s>' and '<s>arbhaka</s>' [are names] for what is small. <s>Dabhra</s> is from <s>dabhr</s>; <s>sudambha</s> means 'very small.' <s>Arbhaka</s> means 'diminished' (<s>avahṛtam</s>). 'Come close, touch me; do not consider me insignificant.' 'Homage to the great ones, homage to the small ones' — these too are Vedic passages. '<s>Tiras</s>' and '<s>sataḥ</s>' [are names] for what has arrived. <s>Tiras</s> means 'crossed over' (<s>tīrṇam</s>); <s>sataḥ</s> means 'gone together' (<s>saṃsṛtam</s>). 'You two have gone around even across the difficult path, O invincible ones.' 'Like [one breaking] vessels, he goes against the <s>Rakṣas</s>' — these too are Vedic passages. '<s>Tva</s>' and '<s>nema</s>' [are names] for a half. <s>Tva</s> means 'fallen away' (<s>apatataḥ</s>); <s>nema</s> means 'carried away' (<s>apanītaḥ</s>). <s>Ardha</s> (half) is from <s>hṛ</s> (to take) in reverse; or may be from <s>dhṛ</s> (to hold) — it has been raised up; or from <s>ṛgh</s> — the most elevated division. 'He drinks according to his portion and praises according to his portion.' 'Neither gods nor <s>Asuras</s>' — these too are Vedic passages. '<s>Ṛkṣāḥ</s>' and '<s>stṛbhiḥ</s>' [are names] for constellations (<s>nakṣatras</s>). <s>Nakṣatra</s> is from <s>nakṣ</s> (to reach), a root of motion; and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> says: 'these are not dominions (<s>kṣatrāṇi</s>).' <s>Ṛkṣāḥ</s> appear as if raised aloft. 'Those <s>ṛkṣāḥ</s> (bears/constellations) placed on high.' 'Beholding the sky as if with stars' — these too are Vedic passages. '<s>Vaṃrī</s>' and '<s>upajihvikā</s>' [are names] for ants — <s>vaṃrī</s> is from vomiting (<s>vamanāt</s>); <s>sīmikā</s> is from flowing (<s>syamanāt</s>); <s>upajihvikā</s> from licking underneath (<s>upajighraḥ</s>). 'With ants they [consume] the son not given up by the unwed.' 'When the <s>upajihvikā</s> eats, when the ant creeps beyond' — these too are Vedic passages. '<s>Ūrdara</s>' and '<s>kṛdara</s>' [are names] for a receptacle. <s>Ūrdara</s> means raised up (<s>udīrṇam</s>), or 'split open for nourishment' (<s>ūrje dīrṇam</s>). 'Him, like an <s>ūrdara</s>, he fills by driving' — this too is a Vedic passage. 'He fills him like an <s>ūrdara</s> by driving.' <s>Kṛdara</s> means 'having a made opening' (<s>kṛtadaram</s>). 'The kindled one, anointing, [fills] the <s>kṛdara</s> of hymns' — this too is a Vedic passage.

body.translated_text: 3.21: <s>Rambha</s> and <s>Pinākam</s> are [names] for a staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>). <s>Rambha</s> — they take hold of (<s>ārabhante</s>) it. 'Like the aged seizing a <s>rambha</s> (support), he took hold of you' — this too is a Vedic passage. 'We take hold of you as the aged [take hold of] a staff.' <s>Pinākam</s> — one strikes with it (<s>pratipinasti</s>). 'Clad in hide, <s>Pināka</s> in hand, with bow unstrung' — this too is a Vedic passage. <s>Menā</s> and <s>Gnā</s> are [names] for women (<s>strī</s>). <s>Strī</s> is from <s>tyāy</s> meaning 'to be bashful, modest.' <s>Menā</s> — they honor them (<s>mānayanti</s>). <s>Gnā</s> — they go to them (<s>gacchanti</s>). 'You made even the unwomanly ones into ones having wives.' '<s>Gnās</s> produced works and extended them' — these too are Vedic passages. <s>Śepa</s> and <s>Vaitasa</s> are [names] for the male organ. <s>Śepa</s> is from <s>śap</s> (to curse) or from the action of touching (<s>spṛśati karmaṇaḥ</s>). <s>Vaitasa</s> means extending a <s>vitasti</s> (span). 'Into whom, desiring, we thrust the <s>śepa</s>.' 'Three times a day you would cut me with the <s>vaitasa</s>' — these too are Vedic passages. <s>Ayā</s> and <s>enā</s> are [words] of instruction. '<s>Ayā</s> — with this <s>samidh</s> (fuel-stick) we worship you, O <s>Agni</s>' — [here it is used] in the feminine. '<s>Enā</s> — with this, your <s>Agni</s>' — [here it is] neuter. '<s>Enā</s> — with this, wipe your body, O husband' — [here it is] masculine. <s>Sisaktu</s> and <s>sacata</s> [denote] one who serves. 'May he who is swift serve us' — may he who is swift attend to us. 'Follow us with well-being' — attend to us with well-being. <s>Svasti</s> (well-being) is a name for what is imperishable; <s>asti</s> is honored — 'well (<s>su</s>) it exists (<s>asti</s>).' <s>Bhyasate</s> and <s>rejate</s> [denote] fear and trembling. 'Before whose fury the two worlds trembled.' 'The earth trembles before the splendor of <s>Agni</s>' — these too are Vedic passages. The following twenty-four are names for heaven and earth (<s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>); this [verse] belongs to them.

[3.22] '<s>Katarā pūrvā katarā aparā ayoḥ kathā jāte kaviḥ ko viveda / viśvam ātmanā bibhṛto yad dha nāma vi vartete ahanī cakriyā iva</s>' — 'Which of these two is the earlier, which the later? How were they born? Who — what wise one — knows? They bear everything by themselves; the two days revolve, as if yoked to a wheel.' Which is the earlier, which the later of these two? How were they born, wise one? Who knows them? Everything is borne by them through their own nature; whatever [is] their activity — the two days, that is, day and night, revolve like [wheels] yoked [to an axle]. Thus [the hymn] declares the greatness of Heaven and Earth.

[4.1] 'One meaning, many words' — this has been stated. Now, those which are of many meanings but single words — those we shall enumerate hereafter, as well as Vedic usages of unclear grammatical formation. Thus: <s>aola</s>/<s>adola</s> — <s>otu</s> means 'weaves' (<s>ācalsate</s>). <s>Jahā</s> means 'he struck' (<s>jaghāna</s>).

[4.2] '<s>Ko nu maryā amithitaḥ sakhā sakhāyam abravīt / jahā ko asmad īśate</s>' — 'What man, unimpaired, as a friend, has spoken to his friend? He has struck [him] — who among us rules?' <s>Maryā</s> is a name for 'man' (<s>manuṣya</s>), or it may be a designation of 'boundary' (<s>maryādā</s>). <s>Maryādā</s> — taken (<s>ādīyate</s>) by men; or <s>maryādā</s> is the division between <s>marya</s> and <s>ādi</s>. <s>Methati</s> is a root meaning 'to abuse.' 'He struck the innocent one — who then fears me? Who flees from us?' <s>Nidhā</s> means it becomes a snare (<s>pāśyā</s>) — that which is bound. <s>Pāśyā</s> is a collection of bonds. <s>Pāśa</s> (bond) is from <s>pāśayati</s> (to bind), from releasing (<s>vipāśana</s>).

body.translated_text: [4.3] '<s>Vayaḥ suparṇā upa sedur indram priyamedhā ṛṣayo nādhamānāḥ / apa dhvāntam ūrṇuhi pūrdhi cakṣuḥ mumugdhy asmān nidhayā iva baddhān</s>' — 'Like birds of fair wing, the sages of dear wisdom approached <s>Indra</s>, imploring: Remove the darkness, fill [our] sight, release us who are bound as if by bonds.' <s>Vayaḥ</s> is the plural of <s>vi</s> (bird). <s>Suparṇāḥ</s> means 'of beautiful flight,' [comparable to] the rays of the sun. They approached <s>Indra</s>, imploring. 'Remove the darkness, [fill our] sight!' <s>Cakṣus</s> (eye, sight) is from <s>khyāti</s> (to see) or from <s>caṣṭe</s> (to behold). '<s>Pūrdhi</s>' — 'fill!' or 'give!' 'Release us who are bound as if by bonds.' '<s>Pārśvataḥ śroṇitaḥ śitāmataḥ</s>' — from the side, from the hip, from the shoulder-joint. <s>Pārśva</s> (side) — the body-part consisting of ribs (<s>parśu</s>). <s>Parśu</s> (rib) is from <s>spṛśati</s> (to touch) — it touches the region of the back. <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> (back) is from <s>spṛśati</s> — it is touched by the limbs. <s>Aṅga</s> (limb) is from <s>aṅgana</s> (going) or from <s>añcana</s> (bending). <s>Śroṇi</s> (hip) is from <s>śroṇati</s>, a root meaning 'to go and shake' — the hip appears to shake as one walks. <s>Śitāma</s> — the arm (<s>dos</s>); <s>dos</s> is from <s>dravati</s> (to run). '[Or] the womb (<s>yoni</s>) is <s>śitāma</s>' — so says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>, meaning 'it becomes slackened.' '<s>Śyāma</s> (dark) from [the spot] of the liver' — so says <s>Taiṭīki</s>. <s>Śyāma</s> is from <s>śyāyati</s> (to darken). <s>Yakṛt</s> (liver) — how and in what manner it is made. '<s>Śiti</s> (white) from the flesh and fat' — so says <s>Gālava</s>. <s>Śiti</s> is from <s>śyati</s> (to cut). <s>Māṃsa</s> (flesh) is from <s>mānana</s> (measuring) or <s>mānasa</s> (mind) — the mind settles in it. <s>Medas</s> (fat) is from <s>medyati</s> (to grow fat).

[4.4] '<s>Yad indra citra mehanā asti tvā dātam adrivaḥ / rādhas tan no vidad vasa ubhayā hastyā bhara</s>' — 'O <s>Indra</s>, whatever wonderful and enriching [wealth] there is — that is to be given by you, O wielder of the stone. Bestow that wealth upon us with both hands.' 'O <s>Indra</s>, whatever wonderful, delightful, enriching wealth there is' — or alternatively, three middle words [mean] 'what is not here for me.' 'That is to be given by you to us, O <s>Adrivan</s> (wielder of the stone).' <s>Adri</s> (stone) — he tears with it; or it may be from the root <s>ad</s> (to eat) — they are 'soma-eaters,' it is known. <s>Rādhas</s> is a name for wealth — they prosper (<s>radhnuvanti</s>) through it. 'Bestow upon us that wealth, with both hands.' <s>Ubhau</s> (both) — both are held together (<s>samubdhau</s>). <s>Damūnas</s> — one whose mind is on taming (<s>dama-manas</s>), or one whose mind is on giving (<s>dāna-manas</s>), or one of subdued mind (<s>dānta-manas</s>); or <s>dama</s> is a name for 'house,' and [<s>damūnas</s> means] one whose mind (<s>manas</s>) is on that. <s>Manas</s> (mind) is from <s>manoti</s> (to think).

[4.5] '<s>Jutso damūnā atithir duroṇa imam no yajñam upa yāhi vidvān / viśvā agner abhiyujo vihatya śatrūyatām ābharā bhojanāni</s>' — 'O swift one, domestic, guest of the house — come to this our sacrifice, O knower; having overcome all hostilities of <s>Agni</s>, bring food from [the abode of] the enemy.' <s>Atithi</s> (guest) — one who has passed by (<s>abhyatita</s>) the houses; or one who goes (<s>abhyeti</s>) to other families on [particular] lunar days (<s>tithi</s>); or [one who is] received by others. <s>Duroṇa</s> (house) is a name for dwelling — they are hard to satisfy (<s>duravā</s>, <s>dustarpāḥ</s>). 'Come to this our sacrifice, O knower, having overcome all hostilities of <s>Agni</s>, bring food from the enemy.' 'Having struck down the forces of other enemies, bring from [their] dwellings food or wealth.' <s>Mūṣa</s> means mouse (<s>mūṣikā</s>). <s>Mūṣikā</s> (mouse) is from <s>muṣṇāti</s> (to steal). <s>Mūṣa</s> is also from this very [root].

[4.6] '<s>Sam mā tapanty abhitaḥ sapatnīr iva parśavaḥ / mūṣo na śiśnā vyadanti mā adhyaḥ stotāram te śatakrato vittam me asya rodasī</s>' — 'They burn me on all sides, like co-wives — these ribs; like mice they bite at the threads — at the sexual organ.' These ribs burn me on all sides like co-wives; like mice, they bite at the unwashed threads. Or it may be a designation of one's own member — 'the sexual organs bite.' 'The desires burn me; [O <s>Indra</s>,] know your praiser, O <s>Śatakratu</s> (Hundred-powered One). May Heaven and Earth know this of me.' <s>Trita</s> (the third), cast into a well, produced this hymn. There, [one finds] mixed [passages of] <s>Brahma</s>-lore mixed with narrative (<s>itihāsa</s>), mixed with Ṛg verses, and mixed with <s>gāthā</s>-verses. <s>Trita</s> was the most penetrating in intelligence. Or else it may be intended in a numerical sense — <s>Ekata</s>, <s>Dvita</s>, <s>Trita</s> — the three came into being.

[4.7] '<s>Isireṇa te manasā sutasya bhakṣīmahi pitryasya iva rāyaḥ / soma rājan pra na āyūṃṣi tārīḥ ahāni iva sūryo vāsarāni</s>' — 'With a vigorous mind, may we partake of the pressed [soma], as of ancestral wealth. O <s>Soma</s>-king, prolong our lifespans, as the sun [prolongs] the days.' With a vigorous — or passionate, or ardent — mind, may we partake of the pressed [<s>Soma</s>], as of ancestral wealth. Prolong also our lifespans, O <s>Soma</s>-king. 'As the sun [prolongs] the days' — <s>vāsarāṇi</s> means comings and goings (<s>vesarāṇi</s>), or illuminations (<s>vivāsanāni</s>), or journeys (<s>gamanāni</s>). <s>Kurutanā</s> — the [suffixes] <s>tanā</s> etc. are meaningless additions: <s>kartana</s>, <s>hantana</s>, <s>yātnā</s>. <s>Jathara</s> (belly, womb) is the stomach (<s>udara</s>) — what is eaten (<s>jagdha</s>) is held (<s>dhriyate</s>) or placed (<s>dhīyate</s>) in it.

[4.8] '<s>Marutvān indra vṛṣabhaḥ raṇāya pibā somam anusvadham madāya / ā siñcasva jaṭhare madhva ūrmim tvam rājā asi pradivaḥ sutānām</s>' — 'O <s>Indra</s>, accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>, O bull, for the battle, drink the <s>Soma</s> with food, for exhilaration. Pour into your belly the wave of honey; you are the king of pressed [offerings] since ancient days.' <s>Marutvān Indra</s> — <s>Indra</s> accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>, possessing them. <s>Vṛṣabha</s> (bull) — the showerer of waters. <s>Raṇāya</s> — for the delightful battle. Drink the <s>Soma</s>; <s>anusvadham</s> — with food. <s>Madāya</s> — for exhilaration, for victory. Pour into [your] belly the wave of honey. <s>Madhu</s> (honey) is a figurative term for <s>Soma</s>, from <s>mādyati</s> (to be intoxicated). This other [substance called] <s>madhu</s> (honey) is also from this very [root]. You are the king of pressed [<s>Soma</s> offerings] even in former days.
[4.9] <s>Titau</s> — a sieve (<s>paripavana</s>); like something woven (<s>tatavat</s>), or like something sewn (<s>tunnavat</s>), or 'pierced to the size of a sesame seed' (<s>tilamātra tunnam</s>).

4.10: "Like flour with a sieve, purifying, where the wise ones fashioned speech with the mind; there friends recognize friendships, their auspicious <s>lakṣmī</s> (mark/fortune) is placed upon speech." Purifying like flour with a winnowing instrument. <s>Saktu</s> (flour) is a word of difficult derivation from the root <s>sac</s> (to follow), or it may be from <s>kas</s> (to shine) inverted, meaning 'that which is spread out.' Where the wise ones drew forth speech with the mind — the wise (<s>dhīra</s>) are those possessed of insight, possessed of meditation — there friends recognize friendships; their auspicious <s>lakṣmī</s> is placed upon speech. <s>Bhadra</s> (auspicious) has been explained under <s>bhaga</s> — it means 'that which bestows upon beings,' or 'that which delights while being present,' or 'that which is like a vessel.' <s>Lakṣmī</s> may be from <s>lābha</s> (gain), or from <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (mark), or from <s>lapsyanā</s> (obtaining), or from <s>lāñchana</s> (sign), or from the root <s>las</s> (to shine), or from the root <s>lag</s> (to cling) expressing the action of desiring, or from the root <s>lag</s> expressing the action of embracing, or from the root <s>latt</s> expressing the action of disrepute. <s>Śipra</s> — we shall explain this further on.

4.11: "That is the divinity of <s>Sūrya</s>, that is his greatness — what was spread out in the midst of actions, he gathered together; when he yoked the tawny ones from their station, then night spreads a garment for him." That is the divine nature of <s>Sūrya</s>, that is his greatness — that which was spread out in the midst of actions being performed is gathered together; when he yoked the tawny ones — the rays of <s>Āditya</s>, or the tawny horses — then night spreads a garment for him, removing the day from all. There is also a Vedic citation on this: "Again she wove together what was spread out, the weaving one; she sat down together."

4.12: "With <s>Indra</s> indeed you will be seen together, having joined with the fearless one, O <s>Mandū</s>, of equal splendor." You will be seen together with <s>Indra</s>, having come together with the fearless host. <s>Mandū</s> means 'the two who are joyful' — you two are so — or it may be 'with that joy.' 'Of equal splendor' — this has been explained by this very expression.

4.13: "With stirred ends, with united middles, bold, celestial racers — like swans in a line they strive, when the horses have reached the celestial course." 'With stirred ends' (<s>īrmāntāḥ</s>) means with well-stirred ends, or with broad ends. 'With united middles' (<s>silikamadhyamāḥ</s>) means with joined middles, or 'having the head as their middle' — moreover, <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) is the head, because all beings rest upon him, and he stands in their midst; this other [the bodily head] too is a head, because from it the sense organs are dependent. Bold, celestial racers — <s>śūra</s> (bold) is from the root <s>śav</s> (to go) expressing the action of motion; <s>divya</s> (celestial) means born in heaven; <s>atya</s> (racers) means those who stretch forth. Like swans in a line they strive — <s>haṃsa</s> (swan) is from the root <s>han</s> (to strike), meaning they strike the path; <s>śreniśa</s> means 'in a line,' from <s>śri</s> (to resort to), meaning they are ranged together. When the horses have reached the celestial course — when they have attained the celestial path, the race. There is a praise of <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) through the horse — 'the horse sprang from <s>Āditya</s>.' There is also a Vedic citation: "From the hero the <s>Vasus</s> drew forth the horse."

4.14: "While being desired, O <s>Agni</s>, when you went to the forests, your mothers, the waters — that return of yours is not to be forgotten, that you, being far away, came to be here." Being desired (<s>kāyamāna</s>) means being observed, or being longed for. You went to the forests, your mothers, the waters, subsiding. That return of yours, O <s>Agni</s>, is not to be disregarded — that being far away, you come to be here, being born again. "They lead <s>Lodha</s> (the greedy one), thinking him a beast" — they lead the greedy sage, thinking him a beast. "The bright one of purifying flame" — <s>pāvaka</s> means blazing; or it means 'lying along,' or 'consuming.'

4.15: "Like two maidens on a swelling, on a new wooden stand, young — the two tawny ones shine in the courses." <s>Kanīnaka</s> means 'maiden' (<s>kanyakā</s>). A maiden (<s>kanyā</s>) is one who is desirable, or 'where is she to be led,' or 'she was brought with desire,' or it may be from the root <s>kan</s> (to be pleased) expressing the action of loveliness. <s>Śākapūṇi</s> says: the words denoting the location of the two maidens are locative singulars. 'On a pierced wooden-footed [stand]' — <s>dāru</s> (wood) is from the root <s>dṛ</s> (to split); from that same root comes <s>dru</s> (tree). 'New' means newly born; 'young' means not yet grown; just as those two shine on their locations, so the two tawny ones shine in the courses. There is a joint praise of <s>Babhru</s> (the two tawny horses). The <s>ṛṣi</s> says, enumerating: 'from this and from this.' "Well-clad, upon the fording place" — <s>suvās</s> means 'having a quick current'; <s>tugva</s> is a ford, meaning 'they come to it quickly.' "Will the <s>Maruts</s> turn back to us? Will the <s>Maruts</s> bend back to us?" — <s>nasanta</s> will be explained further on. "Those intoxications of yours, O striking one, that move through the air — with those impel <s>Indra</s> to give wealth" — those intoxications of yours that are full of striking, full of deception — with those impel <s>Indra</s> to give wealth.

4.16: "She was seen like the breast of <s>Śundhyu</s> (the sun); like <s>Nodhas</s>, she revealed dear things; rousing the sleeping one like one consuming food, she came eternally, the one who returns again." She was seen — <s>Śundhyu</s> (the purifier) is a name of <s>Āditya</s> (the sun), from purification; the breast is the radiance that has risen from him. This other breast too [the bodily chest] is elevated upon the body from this same [principle]. A bird is also called <s>śundhyu</s>, from purification, because it lives in water; the waters too are called <s>śundhyu</s>, from purification. <s>Nodhas</s> is a sage who upholds new things; just as he reveals desired things through praise, so <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn) reveals her forms. <s>Admasad</s> — <s>adma</s> means food; she is 'one who consumes food' or 'one who procures food.' Rousing the sleeping one, she came eternally, of those who return again — awakening the one who sleeps, she came perpetually, of those who come again. "They, bearing axes, are strikers" — [this means] 'having power' or 'having arrows' or 'having the nature of sages.' <s>Vāsī</s> (axe) is a name for speech — <s>Satya</s> says it is because it commands. "Let us two praise together, O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, answer me; let us make a pleasing offering-conveyance for <s>Indra</s>." They consider this to be a praise of conveyance, a praise proclaimed at the pressing; but it is indeed recited as belonging to <s>Indra</s>. <s>Paritkamya</s> — we shall explain this further on.

4.17: <s>Suvita</s> means 'well-gone' (<s>sugate</s>), in regard to progeny, or beyond. There is also a Vedic citation: "Do not place me in a good path" [i.e., do not consign me to the path of the dead]. The root <s>day</s> has multiple meanings. "Being compassionate to the old with the new, may we be [blessed]" — this is the action of compassion (<s>upadayā-karman</s>). "He who alone distributes wealth" — this is the action of giving or the action of dividing. "The terrible one of ill passage destroys the forests" — this is the action of destruction. "These pressed <s>Indu</s> juices, going forth at dawn — O <s>Aśvins</s>, being of one mind, drink them." "For this very one, the crow, intending to praise, awakened me at evening, being compassionate" — <s>dayamāna</s> means 'being compassionate.' <s>Nū cit</s> is a particle [meaning] 'of old and new,' and <s>nū ca</s> and <s>ca</s>. "Today and of old, that same action of the rivers." Today and of old — that same action of the rivers. "Of old and now, the abode of riches." Today and of old, the abode of riches. <s>Rayi</s> (wealth) is a name for property, from the root <s>rā</s> (to give) expressing the action of giving.

[Nirukta 4.18:] "May we know of that your giving, O boundless one (<s>akūpāra</s>)." 'May we know of that your boundless (<s>akuparana</s>) giving.' The sun (<s>Āditya</s>) is also called '<s>akūpāra</s>' — '<s>akūpāra</s>' means 'one whose further shore is far' (<s>dūrapāra</s>). The ocean (<s>samudra</s>) is also called '<s>akūpāra</s>' — '<s>akūpāra</s>' means 'one whose shore is vast' (<s>mahāpāra</s>). The tortoise (<s>kacchapa</s>) is also called '<s>akūpāra</s>' — '<s>akūpāra</s>' means 'it does not go (<s>ṛcchati</s>) to a well (<s>kūpa</s>).' '<s>Kacchapa</s>' (tortoise): it protects (<s>pāti</s>) the marshy bank (<s>kaccha</s>), or it protects with the marshy bank, or it drinks (<s>pibati</s>) with the marshy bank. '<s>Kaccha</s>' is '<s>khaccha</s>', '<s>khacchada</s>' (that which covers). This other '<s>nadīkaccha</s>' (river-bank) also [derives] from the same — '<s>ka</s>' is water, it is covered (<s>chādyate</s>) by that. "He sharpens (<s>śiśīte</s>) his two horns (<s>śṛṅge</s>) for the destruction (<s>vinikṣe</s>) of the <s>rakṣas</s> (demon)." He whets his two horns for the purpose of destroying the demon. '<s>Rakṣas</s>' (demon): that from which one must be protected (<s>rakṣitavya</s>); or 'it injures (<s>kṣanoti</s>) in secret (<s>rahasi</s>)'; or 'it wanders (<s>nakṣata</s>) at night (<s>rātri</s>).' "<s>Agni</s>, swiftly-moving (<s>sutuka</s>), with swift horses." [This means] swift-moving (<s>sutukana</s>) with swift-moving [horses]; or well-offspring (<s>suprajā</s>) with well-offspring [horses]. "May the auspicious paths (<s>suprāyaṇā</s>) spread out in this sacrifice" — [meaning] those of good passage.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 4.19:] "May the gods be ever near us for our increase, unwasting guardians day by day." May the gods always be for our growth, unwasting, unfailing, and guardians day after day. <s>Cyavana</s> is a sage (<s>ṛṣi</s>); he 'sets in motion' (<s>cyāvayitā</s>) the <s>stomas</s> (hymns of praise). The word '<s>cyavāna</s>' also occurs in Vedic citations of his [name]. "You two fashioned <s>Cyavāna</s>, old like a chariot, back to youth for journeying." 'You two fashioned <s>Cyavāna</s>, old, ancient, like a chariot, back to youth for wandering; a youth sets in motion activities.' '<s>Takṣati</s>' (to fashion) is an action of making. '<s>Rajas</s>' from the root '<s>raj</s>' (to shine/color): light is called '<s>rajas</s>'; water is called '<s>rajas</s>'; worlds are called '<s>rajāṃsi</s>'; blood and the two days (day and night) are called '<s>rajasī</s>.' "The brilliant thunderbolts traverse the <s>rajāṃsi</s> (atmospheric regions)" — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Hara</s>' from the root '<s>hṛ</s>' (to take/carry): light is called '<s>hara</s>'; water is called '<s>hara</s>'; worlds are called '<s>harāṃsi</s>'; blood and the two days are called '<s>harasī</s>.' "Mix (<s>śṛṇīhi</s>) the <s>haras</s> (offering) with <s>haras</s> for <s>Agni</s>" — this is also a Vedic citation. "<s>Juhure vicitayantaḥ</s>" — they offered (<s>juhvire</s>), reflecting (<s>vicetayamānāḥ</s>). '<s>Vyanta</s>' — this [root '<s>vi</s>'] has multiple meanings. "Treading the path of the god with homage" — [here '<s>vi</s>'] has the meaning of 'seeing.' "Eat, O hero, the <s>puroḷāśa</s> (sacrificial cake)" — [here '<s>vi</s>'] has the meaning of 'eating.' "Eat and drink the milk of the cow (<s>usriyā</s>)." '<s>Usriyā</s>' is a name for cow — the enjoyments flowing from her are abundant; also [called] '<s>usrā</s>.' "You, O <s>Indra</s>, with hymns at the pressing, the well-leading ones, desiring wealth, praised with cows" — 'praising' with cows, 'they lauded.' "Come, pour the golden (<s>hari</s>) [Soma] in the lap of the wooden [vessel]; fashion it with stone chisels (<s>vāśī</s>)." Pour the golden [Soma] in the lap of the tree, the wooden [vessel]. '<s>Hari</s>' is <s>Soma</s>, of golden color; this other '<s>hari</s>' also [derives] from the same [root]. 'Fashion with stone chisels' — with stone-made [tools]; or 'with voices' (<s>vācbhiḥ</s>). "May he, the bold one, of the hostile creature, the uneven — may the phallus-worshippers (<s>śiśnadevāḥ</s>) not approach our <s>ṛta</s> (truth/sacrifice)." May he prevail, [against] the hostile, uneven creature; may not the <s>śiśnadevāḥ</s> — those without <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) — [approach]. '<s>Śiśna</s>' (phallus) from '<s>śnath</s>' (to pierce). May they not approach our truth, or our sacrifice.

[Nirukta 4.20:] "Come indeed! Those unsurpassed ages shall come where kindred shall do the deed of the unrelated. Offer your arm to the bull; seek another husband besides me, O fortunate one." Those future ages shall come, where kinsfolk (<s>jāmayaḥ</s>) shall perform acts of the unrelated (<s>ajāmi</s>). '<s>Jāmi</s>' (kinship) is a name for 'excess'; it is the offspring of one who is childish or of a different kind. 'Offer your arm to the bull; seek another husband besides me, O fortunate one' — this has been explained.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 4.21:] "Heaven is my father, the begetter; my bond (<s>nābhi</s>) is here; my mother is this great earth. Between the two outstretched <s>camvos</s> (pressing vessels) is the womb; there the father placed the daughter's embryo." Heaven (<s>dyaus</s>) is my father — the protector or the begetter. '<s>Nābhi</s>' (navel) — here is my bond. My mother is this great earth. '<s>Bandhu</s>' (kinsman) from association (<s>sambandha</s>). '<s>Nābhi</s>' (navel) from binding (<s>samnahana</s>) — 'embryos are born bound at the navel' they say; for this very reason, relatives are called '<s>sanābhi</s>' (sharing a navel) and '<s>sambandhu</s>' (of the same bond). '<s>Jñāti</s>' (relative) from mutual recognition (<s>saṃjñāna</s>). 'Between the two outstretched <s>camvos</s> is the womb.' '<s>Uttāna</s>' — stretched out, or stretched upward. There the father places the daughter's embryo — <s>Parjanya</s> [places his] in the earth. '<s>Śamyu</s>' means 'the giver of happiness' (<s>sukhayuḥ</s>). "Then may he bestow upon us freedom from harm (<s>rapas</s>)." '<s>Rapas</s>' and '<s>ripra</s>' are names for evil. And [<s>śamyu</s> means] 'the pacifier of diseases' and 'the averter of fears.' Furthermore, '<s>Śamyu</s>' is also said [to be] a descendant of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. "We invoke that happiness (<s>śam</s>) — a path for the sacrifice, a path for the lord of sacrifice" — this is also a Vedic citation. A passage for the sacrifice, a passage for the lord of the sacrifice.
[Nirukta 4.22:] <s>Aditi</s> — the unbroken (<s>adīnā</s>), the mother of the gods.

[Nirukta 4.23:] "<s>Aditi</s> is heaven, <s>Aditi</s> is the atmosphere, <s>Aditi</s> is the mother, she is the father, she is the son. All the gods are <s>Aditi</s>, the five peoples, <s>Aditi</s> is what has been born, <s>Aditi</s> is what is to be born." — thus he describes the pervading manifestation (<s>vibhūti</s>) of <s>Aditi</s>; or, [the meaning is:] 'these are unbroken (<s>adīnāni</s>).' "Whom the <s>Bhṛgus</s> set in motion (<s>erire</s>)" — '<s>erire</s>' is from the root '<s>īr</s>' (to move), with reduplicated intensive form.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 4.24:] "And the peoples cry out after him in battles, like [after] a cloth-thief (<s>vastramathi</s>), like a robber (<s>tāyu</s>); stooping like a weary hawk, [he darts] toward fame and toward the cattle-herd (<s>yūtha</s>)." And they cry out after him — like one who churns/steals cloth (<s>vastramāthin</s>), a cloth-thief. '<s>Vastra</s>' (cloth) from '<s>vas</s>' (to clothe). '<s>Tāyu</s>' is a name for thief (<s>stena</s>) — 'wrongdoing is fixed upon him' say the etymologists (<s>Nairuktas</s>); or it may be from the root '<s>tay</s>' (to extend/go). 'The peoples cry out (<s>anukrośanti</s>) in battles (<s>saṃgrāmeṣu</s>).' '<s>Bhara</s>' (battle) is a name for battle, from '<s>bhṛ</s>' (to bear) or '<s>hṛ</s>' (to seize). '<s>Nīcāyamāna</s>' — moving low, stooping. '<s>Nīcaiḥ</s>' — low, compact; '<s>uccaiḥ</s>' — high, heaped up. Like a weary (<s>jasta</s>) hawk (<s>śyena</s>). '<s>Śyena</s>' (hawk): it goes to what is praiseworthy (<s>śaṃsanīya</s>). 'Toward fame (<s>śravas</s>), and toward the cattle-rich herd (<s>yūtha</s>).' Fame, and the cattle-rich herd — or, praises and herds, or wealth and herds. '<s>Yūtha</s>' (herd) from '<s>yu</s>' (to join) — it is joined together (<s>samāyuta</s>). "Kindling him, the devout one (<s>svādhī</s>) praises him" — he sings. '<s>Mandī</s>' from the root '<s>mand</s>' (to praise), the action of praising. "Utter to <s>Mandi</s> a food-laden speech" — speak to <s>Mandi</s> a food-laden word. '<s>Gau</s>' (cow) has been explained.

body.translated_text: 4.25: 'Here the rays of the cow [sun] found the hidden name of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, thus in the house of the moon.' Here the rays of the sun (<s>go</s>) discovered their own name — hidden (<s>apīcya</s>): gone away, diminished, concealed, or disappeared — there in the house of the moon. <s>Gātu</s> (path/song) has been explained. 'Making a path for people at dawn' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Daṃsas</s> (wondrous deeds) — they make deeds wondrous. 'For <s>Kutsa</s>, the hymn and the wondrous deeds' — this Vedic usage also occurs. 'He was strong; distress does not reach him.' He was strong; distress (<s>aṃhati</s>) does not reach him. <s>Aṃhati</s>, <s>aṃhas</s>, and <s>ahmu</s> are from <s>han</s> (to strike), with the substitute consonant reversed. 'O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, drive away the enemy.' O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, you who drive away, O god, the hostile one; <s>pīyati</s> has the sense of harming. <s>Viyutī</s> — heaven and earth, because of their separation (<s>viyavana</s>). 'Of the same measure, separated, far, at the end.' <s>Samāna</s> (equal) — it has the measure of equal honor. <s>Mātrā</s> (measure) is from <s>māna</s> (measuring). <s>Dūra</s> (far) has been explained. <s>Anta</s> (end) is from <s>atati</s> (to go/wander). <s>Ṛdhak</s> is an expression for separateness; but it is also seen in the sense of 'prospering' (<s>ṛdhnoti</s>). 'By prospering, by prospering, the strongest laborer.' 'Prospering he milked; prospering, the strongest laborer' — thus also. <s>Asyā</s> and <s>asya</s> — <s>udātta</s> (high accent) in the first reference, <s>anudātta</s> (low accent) in the subsequent reference. The more emphatic meaning takes <s>udātta</s>; the lesser meaning takes <s>anudātta</s>. 'For this one, come near for our winning, not angry, the generous one, <s>Ajāśva</s>, seeking fame, <s>Ajāśva</s>.' For her, come near for our winning, licking, not angry. <s>Rarivān</s> (generous) — <s>rāti</s> (giving) reduplicated. <s>Ajāśva</s> refers to <s>Pūṣan</s>; <s>Ajāśva</s> — with goats (<s>ajā</s>) [instead of horses], unborn ones. Now the <s>anudātta</s> [usage]: 'Long-lived is the husband of this one; may he live a hundred autumns.' May her husband, who has long life, live a hundred autumns (<s>śarad</s>). <s>Śarad</s> (autumn) — in it the herbs become ripe (<s>śṛta</s>); or the waters become fallen (<s>śīrṇa</s>). <s>Asya</s> and <s>asyā</s> — this has been explained by the above.

4.26: 'Of this desirable, grey-haired invoker, his middle brother is the devourer. The third brother, with ghee-smeared back — here I beheld the lord of the settlement with seven sons.' Of this desirable (<s>vāma</s>, worthy of being desired), grey-haired (<s>palita</s>, protector), invoker (<s>hotṛ</s>, one to be invoked) — his middle brother is the devourer (<s>aśana</s>). <s>Bhrātṛ</s> (brother) is from <s>bharati</s> (to bear), or from <s>harati</s> (to take) — he takes a share; or he is to be maintained (<s>bhartavya</s>). The third brother is the one with ghee-smeared back — this is <s>Agni</s> (fire). There I beheld the lord of all (<s>viśpati</s>), the protector or sustainer of all, with seven sons — [meaning] the seventh son, or the one with winged offspring. <s>Sapta</s> (seven) — the number that has crept along; or the seven rays of the sun, they say.

body.translated_text: 4.27: 'Seven yoke the one-wheeled chariot; one horse with seven names draws it. The wheel with three naves, ageless, unobstructed — upon it all these beings stand.' Seven yoke the chariot that moves as one (<s>eka-cakra</s>, single-wheeled). <s>Cakra</s> (wheel) is from <s>cakati</s> (to be satisfied), or <s>carati</s> (to move), or <s>krāmati</s> (to stride). One horse with seven names draws it — the sun (<s>Āditya</s>); seven rays bring essences (<s>rasa</s>) to it; or seven <s>ṛṣi</s>s praise it. This other name [for the sun] is also from this same bringing together (<s>abhisamnāma</s>). The second half-verse has the year (<s>saṃvatsara</s>) as its principal subject. The three-naved wheel — the year has three seasons: summer (<s>grīṣma</s>), rains (<s>varṣā</s>), and winter (<s>hemanta</s>). <s>Saṃvatsara</s> (year) — beings dwell together (<s>saṃvasanti</s>) in it. <s>Grīṣma</s> (summer) — in it essences are consumed (<s>grasyante</s>). <s>Varṣā</s> (rainy season) — <s>Parjanya</s> (rain-god) rains (<s>varṣati</s>) during them. <s>Hemanta</s> (winter) — possessing snow (<s>hima</s>); <s>hima</s> (snow) is from <s>han</s> (to strike) or <s>nihoti</s> (to pour down). Ageless (<s>ajara</s>) — having the nature of not aging; unobstructed (<s>anarva</s>) — not opposed by another. Upon which all these beings rest — he praises the year with all its measures. 'Revolving in the five-spoked wheel' — by the fivefold division of seasons. 'Five are the seasons of the year' — so the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> says, combining winter (<s>hemanta</s>) and cool season (<s>śiśira</s>). 'They say six spokes are fixed' — by the sixfold division of seasons. The spokes are fixed to the nave. Six again is from <s>sahati</s> (to endure). 'The twelve-fellied that does not grow old'; 'twelve fellies, one wheel' — these refer to the months. <s>Māsa</s> (month) is from <s>māna</s> (measuring). <s>Pradhi</s> (felly) is that which is attached (<s>prahita</s>). 'In it together [are placed] three hundred and sixty, like pegs, immovable.' 'Three hundred and sixty are the day-and-nights of the year' — so the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> says, in summary. 'Seven hundred and twenty stand.' 'Seven hundred and twenty are the day-and-nights of the year' — so the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> says, by division [of day and night separately].

body.translated_text: 5.1: 'He found the bathed [cloud] in the course of the rivers' — the bathed cloud (<s>megha</s>). 'Most excellent for you of invocations, the hymn of praise is a messenger, invoking, O men.' The best conveyor of invocations, the hymn of praise (<s>stoma</s>) is the messenger, invoking, O men. <s>Nara</s> (men) — they dance (<s>nṛtyanti</s>) in their actions. <s>Dūta</s> (messenger) is from <s>javati</s> (to be swift), or <s>dravati</s> (to run), or <s>vārayati</s> (to ward off). 'You are the messenger of the gods among mortals' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Vāvaśāna</s> (lowing/desiring) — from <s>vasti</s> (to dwell) or <s>vāśyati</s> (to bellow). 'Lowing for the seven ruddy sisters' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Vārya</s> (desirable) — from <s>vṛṇoti</s> (to choose); also the most excellent. 'That desirable thing we choose, the greatest, to be protected.' That desirable thing we choose, the greatest, to be guarded; you are the guardians — [it means] 'for you.' <s>Andhas</s> is a name for food; it is to be contemplated upon. 'With ladles, pour the intoxicating food.' Pour with ladles (<s>amatra</s>) the intoxicating food (<s>andhas</s>). <s>Amatra</s> (ladle/vessel) — in it (<s>amā</s>) they eat; or <s>amā</s> means 'unfinished' [i.e. simple/raw]. <s>Pātra</s> (cup) is from <s>pāna</s> (drinking). Darkness (<s>tamas</s>) is also called <s>andhas</s> — in it there is no contemplation, no sight; they say '<s>andhaṃtama</s>' (blinding darkness). This other <s>andha</s> (blind) also [derives] from the same. 'The sighted one sees; the blind one does not perceive' — this Vedic usage also occurs.

5.2: 'Not clinging, with abundant streams, rich in water' — not sticking together, or not repelling each other, with abundant streams, having water. <s>Vanusyati</s> has the sense of attacking; its grammatical form is unclear. 'May we attack, may he attack' — this Vedic usage also occurs. 'He who attacks the long-extended sacrifice — may we conquer him, the evil-minded one, in battles.' He who seeks to destroy the long-extended sacrifice — may we conquer him in battles, the <s>dūdhya</s>, the evil-minded one, the one of wicked thought. <s>Pāpa</s> (evil) — among those who fall (<s>pāt</s>) and drink (<s>peya</s>), the falling one falls downward only; or it may be from <s>pāpatyati</s> (to fall). <s>Tarusyati</s> also has the same sense [of attacking]. '<s>Indra</s> as ally, may we conquer <s>Vṛtra</s>' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Bhandanā</s> is from <s>bhandati</s>, with the sense of praising. 'The much-loved sage praises with his powers' — this Vedic usage also occurs. 'She raises up the offspring-bearing one with praise' — thus also. 'Go quickly by another [path], O maddened slayer!' Go by another [path], O slayer in intoxication, quickly — speaking as though striking; from uncouth speech it becomes like a striking — therefore it should be <s>āhana</s> (striker). <s>Ṛṣi</s> is a name for one who roars (<s>nada</s>), from <s>nadati</s> (to bellow/praise). 'The desire for the bellowing, restrained one came upon me' — the desire came upon the bellowing, restrained one — of the celibate student (<s>brahmacārin</s>) whose procreation is restrained — they say this is the lamentation of a sage's daughter.

5.3: "Neither the heaven and earth, nor the desert, nor the atmosphere, nor the mountains — <s>Soma</s> is <s>akṣāḥ</s> (dice/imperishable)." 5.3: From the root <s>aśnoti</s> (to pervade), according to some. 5.3: "In the marshy land, possessing cows, <s>Soma</s> is <s>akṣāḥ</s> with cows; <s>Soma</s> is <s>akṣāḥ</s> with milked ones." "The <s>lopāśa</s> (jackal) pursues the lion; the fish pursues." 5.3: <s>kṣiyati</s> (dwells) is the earlier Vedic citation; <s>kṣarati</s> (flows) is the later citation, according to some. 5.3: In the marshy land, possessing cows — when he dwells with cows, then <s>Soma</s> flows from the milked ones. 5.3: All citations have the sense of <s>kṣiyati</s> (dwells), according to <s>Śākapūṇi</s>. 5.3: <s>Śvātram</s> is a name meaning swift; it means rapid movement. 5.3: "That which flies and that which is stationary, the moving and that which is swift — <s>Agni</s> <s>Jātavedas</s> made it." 5.3: That which flies and that which is stationary, the movable and the immovable — all that the swift <s>Agni</s> <s>Jātavedas</s> made. 5.3: <s>Ūti</s> (aid) is from <s>avanāt</s> (protecting). 5.3: "We yoke you to the chariot for aid" — thus there is also a Vedic citation. 5.3: <s>Hāsamāna</s> (laughing) we shall explain further on. 5.3: "The ant approaches <s>Indra</s> with its feet." 5.3: With feet, or with bonds, or with touches. 5.3: "He found the hare glowing like a ripe fruit." 5.3: This sleeping one, the intermediate light of impermanent appearance — he found it as if blazing. 5.3: "And in two ways his being, and by his own nature he is <s>Śambhu</s> (auspicious)." 5.3: His dual existence is in the middle and the highest stations. 5.3: <s>Śambhu</s> means one whose existence is pleasant. 5.3: "Like a wild animal, the <s>vrātyas</s> (orders/commands) hunt" — they hunt him like a wild animal, the <s>vrātyas</s> being the ritual commands.

5.4: <s>Varāha</s> (boar) refers to a cloud, because it has the best nourishment (<s>vara-āhāra</s>). 5.4: "You brought the best nourishment" — thus also says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. 5.4: "Piercing the <s>varāha</s> (boar/cloud) beyond the mountain, he cast it" — thus there is also a Vedic citation. This other <s>varāha</s> (the animal boar) is also from the same root. 5.4: It uproots roots; or it uproots the best root again and again. 5.4: "<s>Indra</s>, the <s>varāha</s> (boar), the <s>emuṣa</s> (seizer)" — thus there is also a Vedic citation. The <s>Aṅgirasas</s> are also called <s>varāhas</s>. 5.4: "<s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> with bull-like <s>varāhas</s>." 5.4: Moreover, these intermediate divine hosts are called <s>varāhūn</s>. 5.4: "Seeing the golden-wheeled, iron-tusked, rushing <s>varāhas</s>." 5.4: <s>Svasarāṇi</s> means days — they move by themselves; or <s>Svar</s> is the sun, and he drives them. 5.4: "Like rays, the days" — thus there is also a Vedic citation. 5.4: <s>Śaryā</s> means fingers. 5.4: <s>Śaryā</s> also means arrows, being made of reeds. 5.4: <s>Śara</s> (reed/arrow) is from the root <s>śṛṇāti</s> (to break). 5.4: "Bearing with arrows in his hands" — thus there is also a Vedic citation. 5.4: <s>Arka</s> means a deity, because they worship (<s>arcanti</s>) him; <s>arka</s> means a hymn, because they praise with it; <s>arka</s> means food, because it nourishes beings; <s>arka</s> means the Calotropis plant, which is bitter when plucked.

body.translated_text: 5.5: "The <s>Gāyatrī</s> singers sing you, the worshippers worship <s>Arka</s> (the hymn); the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, O <s>Śatakratu</s> (Indra of a hundred sacrifices), have raised you up like a bamboo pole (<s>vaṃśa</s>)." 5.5: The <s>Gāyatrī</s> singers sing you, the worshippers fully praise your hymn, the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, O <s>Śatakratu</s>, have raised you up like a <s>vaṃśa</s>. 5.5: <s>Vaṃśa</s> (bamboo) dwells in the forest (<s>vana-śaya</s>); or it is heard from the act of entreating (<s>vananāt</s>). 5.5: <s>Pavī</s> is the rim of a chariot wheel, because it purifies (<s>vipunāti</s>) the ground. 5.5: "And with the rim of their chariots they split the rock with force." "The <s>Maruts</s> pierced him with razor-sharp rims" — thus there are also two Vedic citations. 5.5: <s>Vakṣas</s> (chest) has already been explained. 5.5: <s>Dhanvan</s> (desert/atmosphere) is the atmosphere — waters flow (<s>dhanvanti</s>) from it. 5.5: "He shone beyond the atmosphere" — thus there is also a Vedic citation. 5.5: <s>Sina</s> is food; it binds (<s>sināti</s>) beings. 5.5: "With which you bring food to friends" — thus there is also a Vedic citation. 5.5: <s>Itthā</s> (thus) and <s>amuthā</s> (in that way) have already been explained by this. 5.5: <s>Sacā</s> means "together" in meaning. 5.5: "Together with the <s>Vasus</s>" — together with the <s>Vasus</s>. 5.5: <s>Cid</s> is an unemphatic particle (<s>nipāta</s>), unaccented, already explained previously; however, as a noun meaning "animal" (<s>paśu</s>), it is accented here. 5.5: "<s>Cid</s>, you are of mind" — enjoyments are heaped in you, or you make aware. 5.5: <s>Ā</s> is a prefix (<s>upasarga</s>) already explained previously; but it is also seen in the sense of "upon" (<s>adhi</s>). 5.5: "Waters in the cloud" — waters are in the cloud, 5.5: that is, waters upon the cloud. 5.5: <s>Dyumna</s> is from the root <s>dyut</s> (to shine) — it means glory, or food. 5.5: "Bestow upon us splendor and treasures." 5.5: Bestow upon us both splendor and treasures.

5.6: <s>Pavitra</s> (purifier) is from the root <s>punāti</s> (to purify). A <s>mantra</s> (sacred formula) is called <s>pavitra</s>. 5.6: "By which purifier the gods always purify themselves" — thus there is also a Vedic citation. 5.6: Rays of light are called <s>pavitra</s>. 5.6: "Having a hundred purifiers, delighting by their own nature" — 5.6: meaning having abundant waters. 5.6: <s>Agni</s> is called <s>pavitra</s>, <s>Vāyu</s> is called <s>pavitra</s>, <s>Soma</s> is called <s>pavitra</s>, <s>Sūrya</s> is called <s>pavitra</s>, <s>Indra</s> is called <s>pavitra</s>. 5.6: "<s>Agni</s> is the purifier — may he purify me; 5.6: <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Indra</s> — 5.6: may their purifiers purify you" — thus there is also a Vedic citation. 5.6: <s>Toda</s> (goad) is from the root <s>tudyati</s> (to strike/goad).

5.7: "Greatly, O <s>Agni</s>, the liberal worshipper calls upon you alone; 5.7: in the shelter of the goad, of the great one." The liberal giver calls upon you greatly; <s>ari</s> (enemy) is from <s>ṛcchati</s> (to go against), and <s>īśvara</s> (lord) is also <s>ari</s>, from the same root. 5.7: Seeing that oblations intended for other deities are poured into <s>Agni</s>, he spoke thus. 5.7: In the shelter of the goad, of the great one — 5.7: that is, in the shelter of the goader, of the great one. 5.7: <s>Svañcāḥ</s> means well-moving (<s>su-añcana</s>). 5.7: "Offering oblations, with ghee on his back, well-moving" — thus there is also a Vedic citation. 5.7: <s>Śipivisṭa</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> — these are the two names of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. 5.7: The first part has a pejorative meaning, according to <s>Aupamanyava</s>.

5.8: "What is it, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, that is to be proclaimed by you? For you have declared: 'I am <s>Śipivisṭa</s>.' 5.8: Do not hide this form from us — that you assumed another form in battle." 5.8: What is it, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, that is unproclaimed — that is, worthy of being proclaimed — when you tell us 'I am covered like a <s>śepa</s> (membrane),' meaning one whose rays are unmanifest? 5.8: Or rather, praise is the intended meaning of the name: what is it, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, that is well-proclaimed — that is, worthy of proclaiming — when you declare 'I am <s>Śipivisṭa</s>,' meaning one whose rays are manifest? 5.8: <s>Śipi</s> here refers to rays; he is pervaded (<s>āviṣṭa</s>) by them. 5.8: "Do not hide this form from us." 5.8: <s>Varpas</s> is a word meaning form; it is from the root <s>vṛṇoti</s> (to cover/choose). 5.8: "That you assume another form in battle" — in combat, with gathered rays. 5.8: The following verse is for further etymological explanation of this.

5.9: "I, the noble one, today proclaim that name of yours, O <s>Śipivisṭa</s>, knowing the ways; 5.9: I praise you, the mighty one, mightier than the mighty, dwelling in the far reaches of this realm." 5.9: Today I proclaim that name of yours, O <s>Śipivisṭa</s>: I am <s>arya</s> (noble), the lord of hymns of praise; or, you are <s>arya</s> (noble). I praise you, the mighty, mightier than the mighty — <s>tavasa</s> (mighty) is the name of the great one — he rises; dwelling in the far distance of this realm, in the far-reaching space. 5.9: 5.9: <s>Āghṛṇi</s> means one who has come to feel compassion (<s>āgata-hṛṇi</s>). 5.9: "O compassionate one, let us be together" — O you who have attained compassion, let us serve together. 5.9: <s>Pṛthu-jrayāḥ</s> means having broad speed (<s>pṛthu-java</s>). 5.9: "The broad-speeding one destroyed the life of the <s>Dasyu</s>." 5.9: He caused the life of the <s>Dasyu</s> to be destroyed.

5.10: "Men produce the praiseworthy <s>Agni</s> from the <s>araṇī</s> fire-sticks by means of their fingers (<s>dīdhiti</s>), 5.10: by the movement of their hands — the far-seeing one, the lord of the house, the <s>Atharyu</s> (fire-priest)." 5.10: <s>Dīdhiti</s> (fingers/rays) here means fingers; they are employed in rituals. The <s>araṇī</s> fire-sticks are those that are mutually fitted together, or <s>Agni</s> is born from their friction (<s>samaraṇāt</s>). <s>Hasta-cyutī</s> means the movement set forth from the hands. They produced the praiseworthy one, the far-seeing one, the lord of the house, the one who extends.

[Nirukta 5.11:] "With a single quaff (<s>pratidhā</s>) he drank three hundred lakes (<s>sarāṃsi</s>) at once — <s>Indra</s>, the <s>kānukā</s> of <s>Soma</s>." With a single draught (<s>pratidhāna</s>) he drank together — 'together' is the meaning. '<s>Indra</s>, the <s>kānukā</s> of <s>Soma</s>' — [<s>kānukā</s> means] '<s>kāntaka</s>' (desirable ones), or '<s>krāntaka</s>' (traversed ones), or '<s>kṛtaka</s>' (made ones); or '<s>Indra</s> is the beloved (<s>kānta</s>) of <s>Soma</s>'; or 'struck (<s>hata</s>) in the eye (<s>kana</s>),' i.e. '<s>kānti hata</s>' (struck in beauty). Regarding that, the ritualists (<s>yājñikāḥ</s>) declare: there are thirty <s>uktha</s>-vessels at the midday pressing (<s>mādhyandina savana</s>), dedicated to a single deity; at that time, they drink them with a single draught — these are here called '<s>sarāṃsi</s>' (lakes). [But] the etymologists (<s>Nairuktas</s>) say: thirty are the day-and-nights of the dark fortnight (<s>aparapakṣa</s>), thirty of the bright fortnight (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>); the waters that come to the moon as rays — those they drink in the dark fortnight. Thus there is also a Vedic citation: "The imperishable ones drink [from] that imperishable abode." They fill him up in the bright fortnight; thus there is also a Vedic citation: "As the gods fill up the <s>Soma</s> stalk." '<s>Adhrigu</s>' is a <s>mantra</s> [word] — because it refers to a cow (<s>gavi</s>); or a command (<s>praśāsana</s>) may be intended, since it contains the word [<s>go</s>]: "O <s>Adhrigo</s>, be at rest; well-rested, be at rest; be at rest, O <s>Adhrigu</s>." <s>Agni</s> is also called '<s>adhrigu</s>.' "For you, O <s>Adhrigo</s>, the mighty ones (<s>śacīvaḥ</s>) drip." [<s>Adhrigu</s> means] 'having unrestrained movement' (<s>adhṛta-gamana-karmavan</s>). <s>Indra</s> is also called '<s>adhrigu</s>.' "I [am] an <s>adhrigu</s> for <s>Indra</s>" — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Āṅgūṣa</s>' means a hymn of praise (<s>stoma</s>), a proclamation (<s>āghoṣa</s>). "With this <s>āṅgūṣa</s>, may we be with <s>Indra</s>" — with this hymn, may we be with <s>Indra</s>.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 5.12:] "<s>Āpāntamanyu</s> (of aroused fury), <s>tṛpalaprabharman</s> (of swift blows), <s>dhuni</s> (roaring), <s>śimīvān</s> (active), <s>śarumān</s> (armed with arrows), <s>ṛjīṣī</s> (possessing the leavings of Soma) — <s>Soma</s> [has pervaded] all forests (<s>vanāni</s>) through his power (<s>atasā</s>); no counterparts have overpowered <s>Indra</s>." '<s>Āpātitamanyu</s>' — one of aroused anger; '<s>tṛpra-prahārī</s>' — of swift blows, or '<s>kṣipra-prahārī</s>' (of quick blows), or '<s>sṛpra-prahārī</s>' (of creeping blows) — [applied to] <s>Soma</s> or <s>Indra</s>. '<s>Dhuni</s>' from '<s>dhū</s>' (to shake). '<s>Śimī</s>' is a name for action, from '<s>śam</s>' (to pacify) or '<s>śak</s>' (to be able). '<s>Ṛjīṣī</s>' — [applied to] <s>Soma</s>: what overflows when <s>Soma</s> is being purified, that is '<s>ṛjīṣa</s>' (the residue), the 'extracted' (<s>apārjita</s>); hence <s>Soma</s> is '<s>ṛjīṣī</s>.' But there is also a Vedic citation pertaining to <s>Indra</s>: "<s>Ṛjīṣī</s>, the thunderbolt-bearer." The share of his two bay horses (<s>harī</s>), and the parched grains (<s>dhānā</s>). '<s>Dhānā</s>' (parched grain) is roasted (<s>bhrāṣṭra</s>) [grain]; or [grains] placed as fruit. "Let your two <s>Harī</s> (bay horses) smell the parched grains near the <s>ṛjīṣa</s> (Soma residue)" — this is also a Vedic citation. With the initial reduplication (<s>abhyāsa</s>) affixed, [the word] takes an augment (<s>upadhā</s>). '<s>Babhasti</s>' is [the root with] the meaning of 'eating.' <s>Soma</s> [has pervaded] all forests (<s>atasa</s>, <s>vana</s>). No counterparts (<s>pratimānāni</s>) have overpowered <s>Indra</s> — those by which they try to measure him, those do not overpower him; they perish without even reaching him. [This verse is] primarily about <s>Indra</s>, say some etymologists; primarily about <s>Soma</s>; or about both, says another [view]. '<s>Śmaśā</s>' — [either] '<s>śu aśnute</s>' (quickly reaches) or '<s>śma aśnute</s>' (it reaches). "<s>Śmaśā</s> obstructed the waters" — it obstructed the waters — <s>śmaśā</s>.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 5.13:] <s>Urvaśī</s> is an <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymph): she reaches widely (<s>uru abhyaśnute</s>), or she reaches with [her] thighs (<s>ūrubhyām aśnute</s>), or great (<s>uru</s>) is her desire (<s>vaśa</s>). '<s>Apsaras</s>' — one who moves in water (<s>ap-sāriṇī</s>). Or '<s>apsas</s>' is a name for form (<s>rūpa</s>). [From the root] '<s>apsāt</s>' (to adorn/extend) — it becomes '<s>apsānīya</s>,' meaning 'worth beholding' or 'pervading.' '<s>Spasta</s>' (clear) — 'one who is beautiful to see,' says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>. [Regarding] '<s>apsas</s>' as inedible [i.e. 'form'] — '<s>apso nāma</s>' means 'pervading,' says <s>Vyāpin</s>. '<s>Tadrā</s>' — she becomes beautiful of form. 'That is eaten by her' or 'that is given to her.' From seeing her, the semen of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> fell. The following <s>ṛc</s> (verse) is the one that refers to this.

[Nirukta 5.14:] "And you are the son of <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s>, O <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, born from the mind of the desiring (<s>vaśyā</s>) <s>Brahman</s>. The drop (<s>drapsa</s>) that fell — all the gods placed you by divine power in the lotus (<s>puṣkara</s>)." (ṚV 7.33.11) You are indeed the son of <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s>, O <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>; desiring, O <s>Brahman</s>, born from the mind. 'The drop (<s>drapsa</s>) that fell by divine power' — '<s>drapsa</s>' is 'collected' (<s>sambhṛta</s>); it is 'worth seeing' (<s>psānīya</s>). 'All the gods placed you in the <s>puṣkara</s> (lotus).' '<s>Puṣkara</s>' is the atmosphere — it nourishes (<s>poṣati</s>) beings; or '<s>puṣkara</s>' is water; or '<s>puṣkara</s>' means 'worthy of worship' (<s>pūjākara</s>, <s>pūjayitavya</s>). This other '<s>puṣkara</s>' (lotus flower) also [derives] from the same — '<s>puṣkara</s>' is '<s>vapuṣkara</s>' (form-making), or a flower (<s>puṣpa</s>) from '<s>puṣ</s>' (to nourish). '<s>Vayuna</s>' from '<s>vi</s>' (to go/know) — beauty (<s>kānti</s>) or wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>).
