body.translated_text: [Nirukta 5.15:] "He indeed spread the darkness devoid of light (<s>avayuna</s>); he made it luminous (<s>vayunavat</s>) with the sun." He spread the darkness, the unknowing (<s>aprajñāna</s>); he made it full of knowledge (<s>prajñānavat</s>) with the sun. (ṚV 6.21.3) '<s>Vājapastya</s>' means '<s>vāja-patana</s>' (falling/dwelling of food/prize). "May we attain the <s>vājapastya</s>" (ṚV 9.98.12) — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Vājagandhya</s>' — the latter part is '<s>gadhyati</s>' (to grasp). "May we reach the <s>vājagandhya</s>" (ṚV 9.98.12) — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Gadhya</s>' from '<s>gṛhṇāti</s>' (to grasp). "Like a prize (<s>vāja</s>) to be seized (<s>gadhya</s>), desiring to separate" (ṚV 4.16.11) — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Gadhyati</s>' is an action of mixing. "Engaged, surrounded" (ṚV 1.126.6) — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Kaurayāṇa</s>' means 'of accomplished journey' (<s>kṛtayāna</s>). "<s>Pākasthāman</s>, the <s>Kaurayāṇa</s>" (ṚV 8.3.21) — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Taurayāṇa</s>' means 'of swift journey' (<s>tūrṇayāna</s>). "O <s>Taurayāṇa</s>, come to the sacrifice, together with the <s>Maruts</s> as friends, O <s>Indra</s>, in accord" — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Ahrayāṇa</s>' means 'of shameless journey' (<s>ahrītayāna</s>). "Perform the <s>anuṣṭubh</s>, O <s>Ahrayāṇa</s>" (ṚV 4.4.14) — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Harayāṇa</s>' means 'of carrying journey' (<s>haramāṇayāna</s>). "Silver, the <s>Harayāṇa</s>" (ṚV 8.25.22) — this is also a Vedic citation. "He who is set in motion (<s>ārita</s>) in work after work, steadfast" — [he is] directed toward hymns (<s>stomān</s>). '<s>Vrandī</s>' from '<s>vrand</s>' (to become soft), the action of softening.

[Nirukta 5.16:] "When you strike down upon the head of <s>Śvasana</s> (the hissing one), and [upon] <s>Śuṣṇa</s>, the <s>vrandī</s> (soft one), roaring over the forests." (ṚV 1.54.5) You strike down upon the head of <s>Śvasana</s>, the noisy one — of <s>Śuṣṇa</s>, or the sun [which is] a desiccator — roaring over the forests, or with the weapon. "They softened (<s>avradanta</s>) the hardened (<s>vīḷita</s>)" (ṚV 2.24.3) — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Vīḍayati</s>' and '<s>vrīḍayati</s>' and '<s>vrīḍayati</s>' — [the first two] have the meaning of 'making firm' (<s>saṃstambha</s>) and are connected with the preceding [word]. '<s>Niṣṣapī</s>' is a lustful woman — one whose bonds (<s>pasa</s>) have gone out. '<s>Pasa</s>' (bond) from '<s>sap</s>' (to touch), the action of touching. "May you not, like a <s>niṣṣapī</s>, destroy us, O wealthy one" (ṚV 1.104.5) — as she destroys wealth, may you not thus destroy us. '<s>Tūrṇāśa</s>' means water that reaches swiftly (<s>tūrṇam aśnute</s>). "Like <s>tūrṇāśa</s> from a mountain" (ṚV 8.32.4) — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Kṣumpa</s>' is a mushroom (<s>ahicchatra</s>) — because it trembles (<s>kṣubhyate</s>).

[Nirukta 5.17:] "When will <s>Indra</s> kick the mortal who does not worship, like a <s>kṣumpa</s> (mushroom) with his foot? When will he hear our songs?" (ṚV 1.84.8) When will he kick with his foot the mortal who does not propitiate, like a mushroom (<s>kṣumpa</s>)? When will <s>Indra</s> indeed hear our songs? '<s>Aṅga</s>' is a word for 'swiftness' — it is 'bent' (<s>añcita</s>), i.e. 'marked' (<s>aṅkita</s>). '<s>Nicumpuṇa</s>' is <s>Soma</s> — '<s>nicāntapṛṇa</s>' (one who satisfies by tasting), he pleases by tasting (<s>nicamana</s>).

5.18: 'These pressed [<s>Soma</s> juices], accompanied by wives [waters], desiring, go to the drinking; the goer to the waters is <s>nicumpuṇa</s>.' These pressed <s>Soma</s> juices, accompanied by waters, desiring, go for drinking (<s>vīti</s>); the goer to the waters is <s>nicumpuṇa</s>. The ocean is also called <s>nicumpuṇa</s> — it is filled by sinking down (<s>nicamana</s>). The <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding sacrificial bath) is also called <s>nicumpuṇa</s> — in it they sound softly, or they place [offerings] down low. 'The <s>avabhṛtha</s> is <s>nicumpuṇa</s>' — this Vedic usage also occurs. [The forms] <s>nicumpuṇa</s> and <s>nicuṅkuṇa</s> [are variants]. <s>Padi</s> (goer) is from <s>gam</s> (to go) — because it goes (<s>padyate</s>).

5.19: 'He becomes rich in cattle, rich in gold, rich in horses; great prosperity <s>Indra</s> bestows on him who, with food, like a child [loosening] a foot-chain, releases the guest who comes at dawn.' He becomes rich in cattle, rich in gold, rich in horses, and <s>Indra</s> bestows great prosperity on him who, with food, [honors] the guest coming at dawn; like a child [loosening] a foot-chain, he releases [the guest]. A child (<s>kumāra</s>) is <s>mukṣījā</s> — from loosening (<s>mocana</s>), and lying down (<s>sayana</s>), and stretching (<s>tatana</s>). <s>Pādu</s> (foot-chain) is from <s>padyati</s> (to go/step). 'He reveals the light, he hides the moisture; that foot-covering of his is not released, like a garment.' The sun (<s>Āditya</s>) reveals the light; he hides the moisture (<s>busa</s>). <s>Busa</s> is a name for water, from <s>bravīti</s> (to speak/sound) or <s>bhraṃśati</s> (to fall) — because when raining he causes water to fall, and with his rays he takes it back again.
5.20: <s>Vṛka</s> (wolf) is the moon — either because its light is uncovered (<s>vivṛta-jyotiṣka</s>), or altered (<s>vikṛta-jyotiṣka</s>), or striding (<s>vikrānta-jyotiṣka</s>).

body.translated_text: 5.21: 'The ruddy wolf, maker of months, saw one going on the path. Rising after observation, like a carpenter suffering from back disease — know this of me, O heaven and earth!' The ruddy (<s>aruṇa</s>, illuminating) one, the maker of months and half-months, is the moon. The wolf (<s>vṛka</s>) saw one going on the path — the host of constellations (<s>nakṣatra-gaṇa</s>). He rises after observing whichever [constellation] he is about to conjoin with — the moon. Like a carpenter suffering from back ailment. 'May heaven and earth know this of me.' The sun is also called <s>vṛka</s> (wolf) — because it seizes (<s>āvṛṅkte</s>). 'The quail called out to the <s>Aśvin</s>s — when you freed her from the wolf's [mouth]' — [this is the story of] <s>Uraṇamathi</s>. <s>Uraṇa</s> (ram) — it is woolly (<s>ūrṇāvat</s>); <s>ūrṇā</s> (wool) is from <s>vṛṇoti</s> (to cover) or <s>ūrṇoti</s> (to cover). An old she-animal (<s>vṛddha-vāśinī</s>) is also called <s>vṛkī</s>. 'He who gave a hundred rams to the she-wolf — <s>Ṛjrāśva</s>, whose father made him blind' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Joṣavāka</s> is a word of unknown derivation; it is something to be enjoyed (<s>joṣayitavya</s>).

5.22: 'O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, he who praises you at the <s>Soma</s> pressings, O promoters of truth — when he speaks pleasingly (<s>joṣavākam</s>), O gods with generous oblations, you do not [merely] laugh at him.' O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, at the <s>Soma</s> pressings, he who praises you — of his [offering] you partake; but this one who speaks merely pleasant words, a chatterer, O gods with generous oblations — of his you do not partake. <s>Kṛtti</s> (hide/glory) is from <s>kṛntati</s> (to cut); or [it means] fame, or food. 'Great as a hide is your shelter, O <s>Indra</s>' — exceedingly great is your shelter in the atmosphere, O <s>Indra</s>, like a hide. This other <s>kṛtti</s> (hide/garment) also [derives] from the same; made of thread, or used in the sense of comparison. 'Wearing a hide, come; bearing the <s>Pināka</s> [bow], approach' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Śvaghnī</s> (gambler, lit. 'dog-killer') — he destroys (<s>hanti</s>) his own [wealth]; or he returns to his own [stake]. 'Like a gambler, he sorts out the winning throw in the game.' The gambler (<s>kitava</s>) — an onomatopoeia of 'what do you have?' (<s>kim tava asti</s>); or one who has made [a throw], a name for a blessing [i.e. lucky throw]. <s>Sama</s> (all/every) — it is a pronoun denoting totality, with <s>anudātta</s> [accent].

body.translated_text: 5.23: 'May not the distress of the evil-minded one who hates from all sides strike us, as a wave [strikes] a ship.' May not the distress (<s>aṃhati</s>) of the evil-minded (<s>durdhī</s>, of wicked thought), the one who hates from all sides (<s>paridveṣas</s>), strike us, as a wave (<s>ūrmi</s>) [strikes] a ship (<s>nāu</s>). <s>Ūrmi</s> (wave) is from <s>ūrṇoti</s> (to cover). <s>Nau</s> (ship) — it is to be propelled (<s>praṇottavyā</s>); or from <s>namati</s> (to bend). Then how can it be a noun with <s>anudātta</s> base? This should be examined. 'And in the same, sharpen [your gift] for us, O <s>Vasu</s>' — this is in the locative case (seventh). <s>Śiśīti</s> has the sense of giving. 'Protect us from the malicious one' — this is in the ablative case (fifth). <s>Uruṣyati</s> has the sense of protecting. Moreover, [<s>sama</s>] also [occurs] in the nominative plural: 'May the others perish in the same [place].'

5.24: 'With oblation, the lover of the waters protects; the filler, O men, the father of the created, the seer.' With oblation, the cherisher of the waters protects; <s>papuri</s> means 'he fills' — these are the Vedic usages, or 'he pleases' — these are the Vedic usages. The father of the created action, the observer — the sun (<s>Āditya</s>). <s>Śamba</s> is a name for the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>), from <s>śamayati</s> (to pacify) or <s>śātayati</s> (to destroy). 'The fierce one who [wields] the thunderbolt, O much-invoked one, with that [weapon]' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Kupaya</s>s are things that are <s>kapūya</s> (foul-smelling). <s>Kapūya</s> — it purifies (<s>punāti</s>); [but here] the purification is blameworthy — it is foul-purifying.

5.25: 'Separately went the first god-invokers; they performed glorious deeds hard to rival. Those who could not board the sacrificial ship — they settled down here like arms, [mere] trembling ones.' They went separately — <s>pṛthak</s> from <s>prathati</s> (to spread); the first god-invokers who invoked the gods. They performed famous deeds, glorious and hard to imitate by others. Those who were able to board the sacrificial ship — but those who were unable to board the sacrificial ship, they settled down here itself; or they settled into debt; or they settled in this very world. <s>Īrma</s> is a name for the arm — it is 'more agitated' [i.e. more active]. 'All these stations you quickly appropriate for yourself; O son of strength, establish whatever you hold.' All these stations you quickly appropriate; O son of strength, establish [what you hold] yourself. <s>Aṃsatra</s> — protection (<s>trāṇa</s>) from distress (<s>aṃhas</s>); or a bow; or armor (<s>kavaca</s>). <s>Kavaca</s> (armor) — it is bent (<s>ku-añcita</s>), or decorated (<s>kāñcita</s>), or 'bent upon the body (<s>kāya</s>).'

5.26: 'Please the horses; may you win well; make the chariot a safe conveyance. Fill the wooden trough for libation, the stone-wheeled well, the sheath-like armor — pour forth, O men!' Please the horses; may your winning be fortunate; make the chariot a safe conveyance. <s>Droṇāhāva</s> — <s>droṇa</s> is made of wood (<s>druma</s>); <s>āhāva</s> is from inviting (<s>āhvāna</s>); <s>āvaha</s> from conveying (<s>āvahana</s>). <s>Avata</s> (well) — from <s>avāti</s> (to dig); it is large. <s>Aśmacakra</s> — a wheel for eating (<s>aśana-cakra</s>), or a wheel for throwing (<s>asana-cakra</s>). <s>Aṃsatra-kośa</s> — may your armors be like sheaths. <s>Kośa</s> (sheath) is from <s>kuṣṇāti</s> (to tear) — it is torn open. This other <s>kośa</s> (treasury) also [derives] from the same — it becomes great through the measure of accumulated wealth. 'Pour forth, O men' (<s>nṛpāṇa</s>, 'man-drinking') — he compares the battle to the act of drawing from a well. <s>Kākuda</s> (palate) — they say it is <s>tālu</s> (palate). <s>Jihvā</s> (tongue) — placed upon it, the tongue pushes out sounds while making a cooing noise (<s>kokūyamānā</s>); or from <s>kokūyati</s> (to coo), with the sense of making sound. <s>Jihvā</s> is [literally] <s>johuvā</s> [the caller]. <s>Tālu</s> (palate) — from <s>tarati</s> (to cross), the most crossed [i.e. highest] limb; or from <s>latati</s> (to hang), with the sense of hanging down, reversed — just as <s>tala</s> (surface) [relates to] <s>lata</s> (to hang) without reversal.

[Nirukta 5.27:] "You are a good god (<s>sudeva</s>), O <s>Varuṇa</s>, whose seven rivers flow toward the peak (<s>kākuda</s>) like a wave through a hollow [reed]." You are a <s>sudeva</s> — a god of good qualities, or a god of desirable nature — O <s>Varuṇa</s>, whose seven rivers — '<s>sindhu</s>' (river) is from '<s>sravaṇa</s>' (flowing) — whose seven streams flow toward your peak (<s>kākuda</s>); '<s>sūrmi</s>' means a beautiful wave, a stream, like through a hollow (<s>suṣira</s>) [reed]. '<s>Bīriṭa</s>' is '<s>tairīki</s>' — the atmosphere; thus he says: the first [part of the word] is from '<s>vay</s>' (to weave/go), the latter from '<s>ir</s>' (to move) — 'birds (<s>vayāṃsi</s>) move (<s>iranti</s>) in it,' or 'lights (<s>bhāṃsi</s>) [move in it].' And they cite this in the following Ṛg verse; a Vedic citation also occurs.

[Nirukta 5.28:] "The sacred grass (<s>barhis</s>) of beautiful passage turns toward them; like lords of the settlement, <s>Bīriṭa</s> [the two] come. At the invocation of the peoples, at dawn's first call, <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s> with the <s>Niyuts</s> [come] for well-being." The sacred grass of good passage (<s>suprāyaṇa</s>) turns toward them; the two come as protectors of all or as sustainers of all. '<s>Bīriṭa</s>' is the atmosphere, or '<s>bhiyas</s>' (fear), or '<s>bhāsas</s>' (light), [being] an extension (<s>tati</s>). Or alternatively, it may be used in the sense of comparison — like two universal lords, like two kings, in the assembly (<s>bīriṭa</s>) of people, at the separation of night, at the first invocation, <s>Vāyu</s> with the <s>Niyuts</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s> [come] for safe passage. '<s>Niyutvān</s>' — the <s>Niyuts</s> are his horses. '<s>Niyuta</s>' is from '<s>niyamana</s>' (restraining) or '<s>niyojana</s>' (yoking). '<s>Acchā abhi ā āptum</s>' (to reach toward) — so says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>. '<s>Parīm sīm</s>' — these have been explained. '<s>Enam</s>', '<s>enām</s>', '<s>asyā</s>', '<s>asya</s>' — these have been explained by the above. '<s>Sṛṇi</s>' is a goad (<s>aṅkuśa</s>), from '<s>saraṇa</s>' (going); '<s>aṅkuśa</s>' is from '<s>añcati</s>' (to bend), or it means 'bent' (<s>ākucita</s>). "May the nearest come from the goad to the ripe [grain]" — this Vedic citation also occurs — 'may the nearest come from the goad; may the ripe grain come' — that is, 'may it arrive.'

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 6.1:] "You, O <s>Agni</s>, [are born] from the days; you, the swift-shining one; you from the waters; you from the stone. You from the forests, you from the herbs — you, O lord of men, are born pure." You, O <s>Agni</s>, [are born] from the days — from the <s>ahas</s> (days). You, the <s>āśuśukṣaṇi</s> — '<s>āśu</s>' and '<s>śu</s>' are both names meaning 'swift.' '<s>Kṣaṇi</s>' is the latter [part], from '<s>kṣaṇoti</s>' (to wound/destroy) — 'he who swiftly wounds with flame,' or 'he who swiftly conquers.' '<s>Śuk</s>' is from '<s>śocati</s>' (to blaze). Or the nominative is used in the sense of the ablative — thus the sentence construction [makes sense]: the prefix '<s>ā</s>' is placed before, denoting the desired [action] — 'the one who desires to blaze swiftly.' '<s>Śuci</s>' (pure) is from '<s>śocati</s>' (to blaze), expressing the action of burning. This other [meaning of] '<s>śuci</s>' (pure/clean) also [derives] from the same [root] — 'evil (<s>pāpaka</s>) has been expelled (<s>niṣṣikta</s>) from it,' say the etymologists (<s>Nairuktas</s>). '<s>Indra</s> created safety from all the directions' — '<s>āśā</s>' (directions) are from '<s>āsadana</s>' (sitting/reaching); '<s>upadiśas</s>' (sub-directions) are from '<s>abhyaśana</s>' (reaching). '<s>Kāśi</s>' means a fist, from '<s>prakāśana</s>' (illuminating); '<s>muṣṭi</s>' (fist) is from '<s>mocana</s>' (releasing), '<s>moṣaṇa</s>' (stealing), or '<s>mohana</s>' (bewildering). "Even these two worlds of yours, O <s>Indra</s>, [are] boundless — when you grasp them, O <s>Maghavan</s>, your fist is great." Even these two worlds — '<s>rodasī</s>' means heaven and earth (<s>dyāvāpṛthivī</s>), from '<s>virodhana</s>' (obstructing); '<s>rodhas</s>' means a bank (<s>kūla</s>) — it blocks the current. A bank is from '<s>rujati</s>' (to break); conversely, a clod (<s>loṣṭa</s>) [derives] without reversal — [these are] boundless, far-shored. When you grasp them, O <s>Maghavan</s>, your fist (<s>kāśi</s>) is great. "O <s>Indra</s>, having made [him] handless, crush the roaring [cloud] (<s>kuṇāru</s>)." O <s>Indra</s>, having made him handless, crush completely the resounding cloud.

[Nirukta 6.2:] "The cloud (<s>alātṛṇa</s>), <s>Vala</s>, the pen of the cow — before the slayer, trembling, he opened up; he made the paths easy for passage; he drove out the cows. He impelled the waters/voices, flowing, toward the much-invoked one." '<s>Alātṛṇa</s>' — '<s>alam ātardana</s>' (that which pierces greatly) — is the cloud (<s>megha</s>). '<s>Vala</s>' is from '<s>vṛṇoti</s>' (to cover/obstruct). '<s>Vraja</s>' — it moves (<s>vrajati</s>) in the atmosphere — is the pen of the cow, of this intermediate speech (<s>mādhyamikā vāk</s>). Before the striking, trembling, he opened up. He made the paths easy for passage; he drove out the cows — he made easily traversable paths for the exit of the cattle. He impelled the waters, or the voices — '<s>vāṇī</s>' (voices) from '<s>vahana</s>' (carrying), or speech from '<s>vadana</s>' (speaking) — flowing toward the much-invoked (<s>puruhūta</s>) [<s>Indra</s>]; water is [that which is] invoked by many. '<s>Dhamati</s>' is a root expressing the action of motion.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 6.3:] "Pull out the <s>rakṣas</s> (demon) with its root, O <s>Indra</s>; cut the middle; shatter the top. Up to what distance have you made them scattered? Put the burning weapon upon the hater of <s>Brahman</s>." Pull out the demon with its root, O <s>Indra</s>. '<s>Mūla</s>' (root) is from '<s>mocana</s>' (releasing), '<s>moṣaṇa</s>' (stealing), or '<s>mohana</s>' (bewildering). Cut the middle; shatter the front (<s>agra</s>). '<s>Agra</s>' means 'that which has come' (<s>āgata</s>) — [reaching] up to what extent of distance. '<s>Salalūka</s>' means 'one who has been plundered' (<s>saṃlubdha</s>) — [that is,] wicked, say the etymologists; or '<s>sararūka</s>' it may be, from the reduplicated root '<s>sṛ</s>' (to go). '<s>Tapuṣi</s>' is from '<s>tapati</s>' (to burn); '<s>heti</s>' (weapon) is from '<s>han</s>' (to strike). "That same sleeping one, what comfort of sleep [he enjoys]" — '<s>katpaya</s>' means pleasant sleep (<s>sukha-payas</s>), or 'whose water/nourishment is pleasant.' '<s>Visruhas</s>' are the waters, from flowing apart (<s>visravaṇa</s>). "Like branches they grew, the seven streams" — this Vedic citation also occurs. '<s>Vīrudhas</s>' are herbs (<s>oṣadhī</s>), from growing forth (<s>virohaṇa</s>). "The <s>vīrudhas</s> (herbs), the all-pervading ones" — this Vedic citation also occurs. '<s>Nakṣad ābham</s>' — reaching what can be reached, attaining what can be attained, through the act of reaching — [meaning] it overpowers. "Reaching the one that can be reached, the crosser, dwelling on the mountain" — this Vedic citation also occurs. '<s>Askṛdhoyu</s>' — one whose life is undiminished; '<s>kṛdhvati</s>' is a name meaning 'runner' — [it refers to] what is diminished. "He who is undiminished in life, ageless, dwelling in light" — this Vedic citation also occurs. '<s>Niśṛmbhā</s>' — those who release (<s>niśrathya</s>) and carry.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 6.4:] "Let the goats carry <s>Pūṣan</s> on the chariot — those who release and bear [him], bearing the glory of the people." Let the goats carry <s>Pūṣan</s> on the chariot — those who release and bear, bearing the glory born of the people (<s>jana-śrī</s>, 'born-glory'). '<s>Bṛbaduktha</s>' means 'of great praise' (<s>mahaduktha</s>) — his hymn is to be spoken — or '<s>bṛbaduktha</s>' [itself]. "We invoke the one of great praise" — this Vedic citation also occurs. '<s>Ṛdūdara</s>' refers to <s>Soma</s> — '<s>mṛdūdara</s>' (of soft belly), or 'soft in bellies.' "May I be in the companionship of the soft-bellied one" — this Vedic citation also occurs. '<s>Ṛdūpe</s>' — we shall explain this further on. '<s>Pulukāma</s>' means '<s>purukāma</s>' (much-desiring). "For the mortal is much-desiring" — this Vedic citation also occurs. '<s>Asinvatī</s>' [is formed] from '<s>asaṅkhā</s>' (numberless), with the last two [sounds altered]. "<s>Asinvatī</s>, devouring, eating much" — these Vedic citations also occur. '<s>Kapanā</s>' are '<s>kampanā</s>' (trembling ones) — they are worms (<s>krimaya</s>). "Do not destroy the tree like worms, O <s>Vedhas</s>" — this Vedic citation also occurs. '<s>Bhāṛjīka</s>' means 'of well-known radiance' (<s>prasiddha-bhā</s>). "Smoke-bannered, kindled, <s>Bhāṛjīka</s>" — this Vedic citation also occurs. '<s>Rūjānā</s>' are rivers — they break (<s>rujanti</s>) their banks. "The well-born ones desired to crush the enemy of <s>Indra</s>" — this Vedic citation also occurs. '<s>Jūrṇi</s>' is from '<s>javati</s>' (to be swift), or '<s>dravati</s>' (to run), or '<s>dūnoti</s>' (to consume). "The hurled <s>jūrṇi</s> shall not carry" — this Vedic citation also occurs. "The <s>ghraṃsa</s> (heat/food) went around you two" — the food that went around you two — '<s>ghraṃsa</s>' means day-food (<s>ahara-vana</s>), i.e. food [obtained during the] day.

[Nirukta 6.5:] '<s>Upalaprakṣiṇī</s>' — one who grinds upon stones, or one who casts stones. <s>Indra</s> asked the sages: 'By what does one live in famine?' One of them replied: "Dung, a female <s>Śākinī</s> (ewe/goat), cows, a net, a flowing [stream], a forest, the ocean, a mountain, a king — these are the nine livelihoods in famine." Thus that <s>nigada</s> (recitation/verse) has been explained.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 6.6:] "I am a poet (<s>kāru</s>), my father is a physician (<s>bhiṣaj</s>), my mother a grinder of corn with stones (<s>upalaprakṣiṇī</s>). With diverse occupations, desiring wealth, we follow [our callings] like cows [following a path]. O <s>Indra</s>, flow around for <s>Indra</s>." (ṚV 9.112.3) 'I am a <s>kāru</s> (poet)' — a maker of hymns (<s>stoma</s>). 'My father (<s>tata</s>) is a physician.' '<s>Tata</s>' is a name for 'offspring/lineage' (<s>saṃtāna</s>) — [applied to] either father or son. '<s>Upalaprakṣiṇī</s>' — a flour-maker (<s>saktukārikā</s>). '<s>Nanā</s>' from the root '<s>nam</s>' (to bow) — [meaning] mother or daughter. 'Of diverse occupations (<s>nānādhiyaḥ</s>), desiring wealth (<s>vasūyavaḥ</s>), we have followed [our callings] like cows [follow] the world.' '<s>Indrāya indro pari srava</s>' — this is an entreaty. "Seated, he destroys the upright one" — [means] 'in the lap (<s>upastha</s>).' '<s>Prakalavid</s>' is a merchant (<s>vaṇij</s>) — he knows both the portions (<s>kalā</s>) and the sub-portions (<s>prakalā</s>). "The enemies, the <s>prakalavin</s> (skilled merchants), measuring" — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Abhyardhayajvan</s>' — one who sacrifices abundantly (<s>abhyardhayan yajati</s>). "<s>Pūṣan</s> follows the <s>abhyardhayajvan</s>" — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Īkṣa</s>' — 'you rule' (<s>īśiṣe</s>). "You see indeed, O king, both [sides] of wealth" — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Kṣoṇa</s>' — 'of the dwelling' (<s>kṣayaṇa</s>). "Of the great dwelling, O <s>Aśvins</s>, for <s>Kaṇva</s>" — this is also a Vedic citation.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 6.7:] "<s>Asme</s> — your kinsman." [<s>Asme</s>] means 'we' (<s>vayam</s>). "Come to us (<s>asme</s>), O <s>Nāsatyas</s>, in accord" — [<s>asme</s>] means 'to us' (<s>asmān</s>). "Among us (<s>asme</s>), with equal, manly [companions], O bull" — [<s>asme</s>] means 'with us' (<s>asmābhiḥ</s>). "Bestow upon us (<s>asme</s>), O bountiful one, the <s>ṛjīṣin</s> (Soma residue)" — [<s>asme</s>] means 'for us' (<s>asmabhyam</s>). "May hatred go far away from us (<s>asme</s>)" — [<s>asme</s>] means 'from us' (<s>asmat</s>). "Desire has spread among us (<s>asme</s>) like a flame" — [<s>asme</s>] means 'of us' (<s>asmākam</s>). "Bestow wealth in us (<s>asme</s>), O <s>Vasus</s>" — [<s>asme</s>] means 'in us' (<s>asmāsu</s>). '<s>Pātha</s>' is the atmosphere (<s>antarikṣa</s>) — '<s>patha</s>' (path) has been explained. "Like a hawk flying, he follows the <s>pātha</s> (atmosphere)" — this is also a Vedic citation. Water is also called '<s>pātha</s>' — from 'drinking' (<s>pāna</s>). "He beholds the <s>pātha</s> (water) of the rivers" — this is also a Vedic citation. Food is also called '<s>pātha</s>' — from 'drinking' (<s>pāna</s>) as well. "Bring the <s>pātha</s> (offering) of the gods, O wise one" — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Savīmani</s>' — 'in the impelling' (<s>prasave</s>). "In the <s>savīmani</s> (impulse) of god <s>Savitṛ</s>" — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Saprathāḥ</s>' — 'broad in all directions' (<s>sarvataḥ pṛthu</s>). "You, O <s>Agni</s>, are <s>saprathāḥ</s> (widely extended)" — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Vidathāni</s>' — 'acts of knowing' (<s>vedanāni</s>). "Stimulating the <s>vidathāni</s> (assemblies of knowledge)" — this is also a Vedic citation.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 6.8:] "As [all beings] resort to the sun, all partake of <s>Indra</s>'s wealth. Born, being born in power — we have contemplated [our] share." (ṚV 8.99.3) Having resorted to the sun, they attend upon [him]. Or the comparison may be: they attend upon <s>Indra</s> as [they attend upon] the sun. All of <s>Indra</s>'s wealth being distributed — as he distributes wealth to those born and to those yet to be born — we have contemplated that share with might (<s>ojas</s>), with strength. '<s>Ojas</s>' (might) from '<s>oj</s>' (to be strong) or '<s>ubj</s>' (to force). '<s>Āśīr</s>' (mixture/blessing) from '<s>āśray</s>' (to resort to) or '<s>āśrap</s>' (to boil/cook). And this other '<s>āśīr</s>' (benediction) is from '<s>āśās</s>' (to wish/bless). "For <s>Indra</s>, the cows [give] the <s>āśīr</s> (mixed offering)" — this is also a Vedic citation. "May that be my true <s>āśīr</s> (blessing) among the gods" — this is also a Vedic citation. "When the mortal has partaken of your enjoyment, then you are the greatest devourer, the kindler of plants" — when the mortal has reached your enjoyment, [you are] the greatest swallower, the kindler of plants. '<s>Jigarti</s>' — an action of 'swallowing' (<s>girati</s>), or 'praising' (<s>gṛṇāti</s>), or 'seizing' (<s>gṛhṇāti</s>). "O wise ones, we are deluded (<s>mūḍha</s>); you are undeluded; we do not know your greatness, O <s>Agni</s>, but you know [it]." Deluded are we; undeluded are you; we do not know the greatness, O <s>Agni</s>, but you know [it]. '<s>Śaśamāna</s>' — 'one who praises' (<s>śaṃsamāna</s>). "He who serves you both with sacrifices, praising" — this is also a Vedic citation. "The god, by means of divine compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>)" — the god, by compassion directed toward the gods. '<s>Kṛp</s>' (compassion/pity) from '<s>kṛp</s>' (to lament) or '<s>kḷp</s>' (to be fit).

[Nirukta 6.9:] "I have heard that you two are more generous than the brother-in-law (<s>vijāmātur</s>) or the wife's brother (<s>syāla</s>). Therefore, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, with <s>Soma</s> offerings, I produce for you both a new hymn." (ṚV 1.109.2) I have heard that you two are the most generous, more so than the <s>vijāmātar</s> (bridegroom's kinsman) — a well-obtained, well-found kinsman by marriage. '<s>Vijāmātar</s>' — they call a perpetually giving man a 'bought husband' (<s>krītāpati</s>) — as if a well-obtained bridegroom (<s>vara</s>) is intended. '<s>Jāmātar</s>' (son-in-law): '<s>jā</s>' is offspring (<s>apatya</s>); he is its maker (<s>nirmātā</s>). 'Or even more so than the <s>syāla</s> (brother-in-law).' '<s>Syāla</s>' — 'one who is near through connection' say the etymologists of relationships (<s>naidāna</s>). Or '<s>syāla</s>' — '<s>lājā</s> (parched grain) without husband.' '<s>Lājā</s>' (parched grain) from '<s>lāj</s>' (to fry/parch). '<s>Sya</s>' is a winnowing basket (<s>śūrpa</s>), from '<s>sya</s>' (to blow/winnow); '<s>śūrpa</s>' (winnowing basket) is an instrument for grain-cleaning, or from '<s>śṝ</s>' (to crush). Then, with the offering of <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, I produce for you both a new, very new hymn. '<s>Omāsa</s>' — we shall explain later.

[Nirukta 6.10:] "Make the <s>Soma</s>-presser illustrious (<s>svaraṇa</s>), O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>, like <s>Kakṣīvān</s>, who is the son of <s>Uśij</s>." (ṚV 1.18.1) Make the <s>Soma</s>-presser — the one who presses [<s>Soma</s>] — resplendent; make [him] like <s>Kakṣīvān</s>, who is the son of <s>Uśij</s>, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>. '<s>Kakṣīvān</s>' — 'possessing a girdle' (<s>kakṣyāvān</s>). '<s>Auśija</s>' — son of <s>Uśij</s>. '<s>Uśij</s>' from '<s>vaś</s>' (to desire), the action of desiring (<s>kāntikarman</s>). However, this human <s>Kakṣa</s> may indeed be intended — 'make me, the <s>Soma</s>-presser, illustrious, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>.'

[Nirukta 6.11:] "O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Soma</s>, [hurl] against the evil-praiser the burning [bolt]; let the cauldron [of fire], like a vessel of yours, be scorching. For the hater of prayer, the devourer of flesh, the terrible-eyed — inflict upon the <s>kimīdin</s> (sorcerer) inescapable hatred." (ṚV 7.104.2) O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Soma</s>, against the praiser of evil (<s>aghaśaṃsa</s>). '<s>Agha</s>' (evil) from '<s>han</s>' (to strike), with the prefix dropped — '<s>āhanti</s>' (it strikes). '<s>Tapus</s>' (burning) from '<s>tap</s>' (to heat). '<s>Caru</s>' (cauldron) is an earthen vessel, from '<s>car</s>' (to move) — waters boil up (<s>samuccaranti</s>) from it. For the hater of prayer (<s>brahmadviṣ</s>), the enemy of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; the devourer of raw flesh (<s>kravyāda</s>); the terrible-eyed (<s>ghoracakṣas</s>) — of terrible appearance. '<s>Kravya</s>' (raw flesh) — 'it is born from cutting' (<s>vikṛttāt jāyate</s>), say the etymologists. 'Inflict inescapable (<s>anavāya</s>) hatred' — 'inseparable,' meaning 'that which others cannot separate (<s>vyaveyuḥ</s>)'; or 'free from hatred [toward us].' '<s>Kimīdin</s>' (sorcerer) — 'one who goes about [saying] "what now?" (<s>kim idānīm</s>),' or 'one who goes about [saying] "what is this? what is this?"' — a spy (<s>piśuna</s>). '<s>Piśuna</s>' (spy) from '<s>piṃś</s>' (to adorn/deceive) — 'he fabricates' (<s>vipiṃśati</s>).

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 6.12:] "Spread your splendor (<s>pājas</s>) like a net (<s>prasiti</s>) over the earth; advance like a king with his retinue, with an elephant. Angered, pursue along [your] fierce advance; shoot the demons (<s>rakṣas</s>) with the most burning [arrows]." (ṚV 4.4.1) Spread your '<s>pājas</s>' (splendor) — '<s>pājas</s>' from '<s>pāl</s>' (to protect) — like a net (<s>prasiti</s>) over the earth. '<s>Prasiti</s>' (net/noose) from '<s>prasay</s>' (to bind) — a thread, or a net. Advance like a king with his retinue — with followers, with his own troop; or with a fearless elephant (<s>hastin</s>). Angered (<s>drūṇāna</s>) along the fierce advance. Shoot the demons with the most burning [arrows] — the most heated (<s>taptatama</s>), the most sated (<s>tṛptatama</s>), or the most crushing (<s>prapiṣṭhatama</s>). "The evil-named disease (<s>amīvā</s>), a worm (<s>kṛmi</s>), lies in your womb" — '<s>amīvā</s>' has been explained through '<s>abhyammana</s>' (affliction). '<s>Durṇāman</s>' is a worm — of evil name (<s>pāpanāman</s>). '<s>Kṛmi</s>' (worm): it fattens (<s>medyati</s>) on flesh (<s>kravya</s>); or from '<s>kram</s>' (to walk), the action of creeping; or from '<s>kām</s>' (to desire). "Crossing over all difficulties (<s>duritāni</s>)" — crossing over all difficult passages. '<s>Apvā</s>' — when one is pierced by it, one sinks (<s>upavīyate</s>) — whether disease or fear. "Go to the <s>apvā</s> (destruction)" — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Amati</s>' — sickly (<s>amāmayī</s>); '<s>mati</s>' — self-possessed (<s>ātmamayī</s>). "Whose lofty <s>amati</s> (radiance) blazed forth with vitality" — this is also a Vedic citation. '<s>Śruṣṭī</s>' is a name for 'quickness' (<s>kṣipra</s>) — 'quickly' (<s>āśu</s>), 'swiftly' (<s>aṣṭī</s>).

6.13: 'Worship them at the sacrifice, O <s>Agni</s>, the desiring ones, <s>Śruṣṭī</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, the <s>Nāsatyas</s>, <s>Purandhī</s>.' Worship them at the sacrifice (<s>adhvara</s>), the desiring ones who long for the ritual, O <s>Agni</s> — <s>Śruṣṭī</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, and the two <s>Nāsatyas</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>. <s>Aurṇavābha</s> says the <s>Nāsatyas</s> are indeed 'the two truthful ones' (<s>satyau</s>). <s>Āgrāyaṇa</s> says they are 'the two leaders of truth.' Or they were born from the nose (<s>nāsikā</s>). <s>Purandhi</s> means 'of abundant thought' (<s>bahudhī</s>). Then who is <s>Purandhi</s>? <s>Bhaga</s> — one explanation is that it is a prior reference to him; another says <s>Indra</s> — he is the most active in deeds and the greatest destroyer of citadels (<s>pur</s>); yet another says <s>Varuṇa</s> — one praises him with wisdom. 'This wondrous power (<s>māyā</s>) of his, the poet's' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Ruśat</s> is a color-word, from the root <s>ruc</s> (to shine) or <s>jval</s> (to blaze). 'The blazing radiance (<s>pājas</s>) of the kindled [fire] was seen' — this Vedic usage also occurs.

body.translated_text: 6.14: 'For you have kinship, O destroyers of foes, O gods, and you have friendship.' For you have common birth, O gods who shatter enemies (<s>riśādas</s>), and you have friendship (<s>āpya</s>). <s>Āpya</s> (friendship) is from <s>āpnoti</s> (to obtain/reach). <s>Sudatra</s> means 'of beautiful gifts' (<s>kalyāṇa-dāna</s>). '<s>Tvaṣṭā</s>, the beautiful-giver, may he distribute wealth' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Suvidatra</s> means 'of beautiful knowledge' (<s>kalyāṇa-vidyā</s>). 'O <s>Agni</s>, come hither with those of beautiful knowledge' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Ānuṣak</s> — the name means 'attached in sequence' (<s>ānupūrvya</s>). 'They spread the sacred grass (<s>barhis</s>) in sequence' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Turvaṇi</s> means 'swift-conveyor' (<s>tūrṇa-vani</s>). 'He, the swift-conveyor, in great dustless heroism' — this Vedic usage also occurs. A god becomes <s>nirvaṇa</s> (delighted) — they please (<s>vanayanti</s>) him with hymns (<s>gīr</s>). 'The great [hymn], delightful to <s>Girvaṇas</s> (he who delights in hymns)' — this Vedic usage also occurs.

6.15: 'In the undriven [space] and the driven, in the atmosphere, settled — those who created these beings.' The unimpelled [<s>Maruts</s>], in the well-impelled, wind-driven, belonging to the middle divine host — satisfying the earth with moisture and creating beings — they are worshipped: this is the answer referring back to the preceding [verse]. '<s>Amyak</s> is that spear (<s>ṛṣṭi</s>) of yours, O <s>Indra</s>' — [<s>amyak</s> means] either 'anointed' (<s>amāktā</s>) or 'smeared' (<s>abhyaktā</s>). 'Of what sort it was established, that he found by active work' — of what sort it was placed, that he discovered through diligent effort (<s>apasyā</s>). 'Like a father, [the dawn] has been roused by sacrifices as a cow-[herder]' — like a cow, the father-[like dawn] has been awakened by sacrifices.

body.translated_text: 6.16: 'Seeking forth, the delighting ones arose; all became <s>Agni</s>-led prizes.' They went forth delighting, [or] all became [victorious] — either by being foremost in going, or foremost in swallowing, or foremost in accomplishing. Or one may take <s>agra</s> (foremost) here as a meaningless prefix. '<s>Indra</s>, truly partake of these offered oblations; bestow your favor, and cook the <s>Soma</s>.' O <s>Indra</s>, partake of these offered oblations; bestow food (<s>canas</s>). <s>Cana</s> is a name for food. <s>Pacati</s> (to cook) is a nominal [form]. 'Seize that which is cooked from the fat' — this Vedic usage also occurs. Or it may be a dual of the essence of fat (<s>medas</s>) and the sacrificial animal (<s>paśu</s>), where a singular meaning is well-known but a dual form occurs. 'Cook the sacrificial cake (<s>puroḷāś</s>), O <s>Agni</s>' — just so. <s>Śurudh</s> means the waters; they confine (<s>saṃrundhanti</s>) the brightness (<s>śuc</s>). 'For the waters (<s>śurudh</s>) of cosmic order (<s>ṛta</s>) are many' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Amina</s> means one of unmeasured measure, i.e. great, or immeasurable. '<s>Amina</s> in his powers' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Jajjhatī</s>s are the waters that make sound. 'The <s>Maruts</s>, like roaring ones' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Apratiṣkuta</s> means unobstructed (<s>apratiṣkṛta</s>), or unstumbling (<s>apratiskhaliata</s>). 'For us, the unobstructed one' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Śāśadāna</s> means 'being overpowered' (<s>śāśādyamāna</s>). 'He surpassed his own thought, being overpowered' — this Vedic usage also occurs.

body.translated_text: 6.17: <s>Sṛpra</s> (flowing) is from <s>sarpaṇa</s> (crawling/flowing); this other <s>sṛpra</s> (ghee or oil) also [derives] from the same — either <s>sarpis</s> (ghee) or <s>taila</s> (oil). 'Of flowing streams and active arms' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Karasna</s> means the two arms (<s>bāhū</s>) — they are the most active executors (<s>prasnātārau</s>) of actions. <s>Suśipra</s> — this is explained by the same [derivation]. 'In the contest, O beautiful-jawed one (<s>suśipra</s>), with <s>Soma</s>' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Śipre</s> (jaws) are the two jaws (<s>hanū</s>), or the two nostrils (<s>nāṣike</s>). <s>Hanu</s> (jaw) is from <s>han</s> (to strike); <s>nāsikā</s> (nostril) is from <s>nas</s> (to breathe). 'Open wide your jaws, release the milch-cows (<s>dhenā</s>)' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Dhenā</s> (speech/milch-cow) is from <s>dadhāti</s> (to place/nourish). <s>Raṃsu</s> (ray) is from <s>ramaṇa</s> (delighting). 'He shone with brilliant radiance among the rays' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Dvibarhā</s> means one exalted (<s>parivṛḍha</s>) in two stations — in the middle station and in the highest station. 'And the twofold-great, the immeasurable, with his powers' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Akra</s> (swift) is from <s>ākramaṇa</s> (striding). 'Like a swift tawny one in the encounter of the great' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Urāṇa</s> means 'making wide' (<s>uru kurvāṇa</s>). 'You go as a messenger from heaven, O wide-maker' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Stiyā</s>s are the waters, from <s>styāyana</s> (congealing). 'Bull of the rivers, bull of the standing waters' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Stipā</s> (protector of the standing waters) — he protects (<s>pālayati</s>) those who approach (<s>upasthita</s>). 'May he be our protector of the waters and guardian of our bodies' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Jabāru</s> — one who rises swiftly (<s>javamāna-rohi</s>), or one who rises consumingly (<s>jaramāṇa-rohi</s>), or one who rises devouringly (<s>garamāṇa-rohi</s>). 'The <s>jabāru</s> [frog] mounted at the front' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Jarūtha</s> is <s>garūtha</s> (praise), from <s>gṛṇāti</s> (to praise). 'You slay the <s>jarūtha</s> [demon], for wealth and for <s>purandhi</s> (abundance)' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Kuliśa</s> is a name for the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>) — it shatters (<s>śātayati</s>) riverbanks (<s>kūla</s>). 'As if [branches] from shoulders cut by the thunderbolt (<s>kuliśa</s>), the serpent (<s>ahi</s>) lies touching the earth.' The <s>skandha</s> (branch/shoulder) of a tree is what is attached to it; this other <s>skandha</s> (shoulder of the body) also [derives] from the same — what is attached to the body. The serpent (<s>ahi</s>) lies as a clinging companion of the earth. <s>Tuñja</s> is from <s>tuñjati</s> (to push/give), in the sense of giving.

6.18: 'At each giving, at each giving, the highest praises of <s>Indra</s> the thunderbolt-wielder — I cannot find the completion of his praise.' At each act of giving, the highest praises of <s>Indra</s> the thunderbolt-wielder — I cannot find through those [praises] the completion of his eulogy. <s>Barhaṇā</s> means 'all-expanding' (<s>paribarhaṇā</s>). 'The loud-famed <s>Asura</s>, made all-expansive' — this Vedic usage also occurs.

6.19: 'He who presses <s>Soma</s> for him on a hot day or at the udder[-like vessel] becomes radiant indeed. The able one (<s>Śakra</s>) drives away the unrighteous one who has extended [his line]; the body-adorner, the bountiful one (<s>Maghavā</s>), who has foul-smelling friends.' <s>Ghraṃsa</s> is a name for the day — in it, the juices (<s>rasa</s>) are consumed (<s>grasyante</s>). <s>Ūdha</s> (udder) — it is raised up higher (<s>uddhatataram</s>), or swollen (<s>uponnaddham</s>). Due to the similarity of oozing and giving forth, the night is also called <s>ūdha</s>. He who presses <s>Soma</s> for him on a day or also at night becomes radiant (<s>dyotanavān</s>). <s>Śakra</s> (the able one, i.e. <s>Indra</s>) drives away — he repels the one who has extended the thread of <s>dharma</s> [but] has fallen away, the would-be adorner, the non-sacrificer; <s>tanūśubhra</s> means 'one who would make the body <s>Soma</s>-bright'; <s>Maghavā</s> (the bountiful one) — he whose friends (<s>sakhāya</s>) are <s>kapūya</s> (foul-smelling). 'He pierced the firm [fortifications] of <s>Ilābila</s> [the demon] who lay [hidden]; <s>Indra</s> broke apart the horned <s>Śuṣṇa</s>.' He pierced through the firm [defenses] of him who lay in a cave (<s>bila</s>); he broke apart the horned <s>Śuṣṇa</s>, [that is] <s>Indra</s> [did].

6.20: 'Hurl forth for him, hastening swiftly, the thunderbolt at <s>Vṛtra</s>, O sovereign lord! Split open the joints of the cloud as [one splits] a cow's [joints], that the waters may flow.' Hurl for him, swiftly, hastening, the thunderbolt at <s>Vṛtra</s>, O sovereign. <s>Kiyedhāḥ</s> — 'in some measure,' or 'striding in a certain manner.' Split open the joints of the cloud, like those of a cow, so that the waters may go forth for flowing. <s>Bhṛmi</s> (whirling) is from <s>bhrāmyati</s> (to whirl). 'You are <s>bhṛmi</s>, sage-maker among mortals' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Viṣpita</s> (pervaded/reached) means 'widely reached.' 'May he carry us across this [difficulty] that has been widely reached' — this Vedic usage also occurs.

body.translated_text: 6.21: 'That wondrous, much-desired [gift], gathered by oneself — may <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> release it for our prosperity, for wealth; for us, the kinsman desiring us.' That great, quickly-attained [gift], gathered by oneself — may <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> release it for the prosperity of wealth; <s>asmayuḥ</s> means 'desiring us.' <s>Rāspi</s> (giver) — from <s>rapati</s> (to murmur) or <s>rasati</s> (to cry out). 'Of the <s>rāspi</s>, of this one' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Ṛñjati</s> has the sense of adorning (<s>prasādhana</s>). 'Adorn for yourselves food at the dawns' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Ṛju</s> (straight) is also [derived] from this. 'O <s>Varuṇa</s>, leading us straight' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Pratadvasū</s> means 'having attained wealth.' 'O <s>Indra</s>, urge forth the two fallow horses that have attained wealth' — this Vedic usage also occurs.

body.translated_text: 6.22: 'Impel our sacrifice for worship of the gods; impel the prayer for the winning of wealth. At the joining of truth, release your udders; may the waters be obedient and bountiful for us.' Impel our sacrifice for the worship of the gods. Impel the prayer for the obtaining of wealth. At the joining of <s>ṛta</s> (truth) — at the joining of the sacrifice, or the sacrificial [context]. <s>Śakaṛa</s> — it is <s>śakṛt</s>-like (dung-like); or it goes slowly (<s>śanakais takati</s>); or it goes with sound (<s>śabdena takati</s>). 'May the waters be obedient and bountiful for us' — may the waters be pleasant for us. '<s>Coṣkūyamāna</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, [granting] much that is desirable' — giving, O <s>Indra</s>, much that is to be desired. 'Increasing, the king of both [worlds], <s>Indra</s> moves restlessly among the human tribes' — he displaces the non-pressers of <s>Soma</s> who are increasing, and favors the pressers; king of both the celestial and terrestrial [realms]; <s>coṣkūyamāna</s> is from <s>coṣkūyati</s>, in the intensive form. <s>Sumat</s> — the meaning is 'by itself.' 'May the thought well-conceived by meditation come to me' — may the thought that is conceived in my mind come to me through sacrifice — this is a mantra from the horse sacrifice (<s>Aśvamedha</s>). <s>Diviṣṭi</s> — quests for heaven (<s>diva-eṣaṇa</s>). 'Great is the gift of a hundred horses of <s>Kuruṅga</s> at the quests for heaven.' <s>Sthūra</s> (great) — it becomes great to the extent of being fully attained; [or] <s>aṇu</s> (small) following <s>sthavīyāṃsa</s> (greater) as a prefix with the name-forming element dropped, as at present. <s>Kuruṅga</s> was a king — from going through the <s>Kuru</s> [land] or going through the <s>kula</s> (family). <s>Kuru</s> is from <s>kṛntati</s> (to cut). <s>Krūra</s> (cruel) is also [derived] from this. <s>Kula</s> (family) is from <s>kuṣṇāti</s> (to tear) — it is torn open. <s>Dūta</s> (messenger) has been explained. <s>Jinvati</s> has the sense of pleasing. 'The rains please the earth; the fires please the sky' — this Vedic usage also occurs.

body.translated_text: 6.23: <s>Amatra</s> (immeasurable) — it becomes great, of immeasurable measure; or 'not measured against' (<s>abhyamita</s>). 'The great, immeasurable one, you seize upon in the [cattle] enclosure' — this Vedic usage also occurs. 'The wielder of the thunderbolt is praised, equal to the <s>ṛc</s>' — the wielder of the thunderbolt is praised, equal to the hymn. <s>Anarśarāti</s> (ungrudging giver) — one whose giving is not contemptible; <s>aślīla</s> means evil; <s>aśrimat</s> means uneven. 'Praise the ungrudging giver of wealth' — this Vedic usage also occurs. <s>Anarva</s> (unobstructed) — not opposed by another. '<s>Bṛhaspati</s>, the unobstructed bull, sweet-tongued — increase him with new hymns of praise.' The unobstructed one, not opposed by another; the bull; sweet-tongued (<s>mandrajihva</s>) — whose tongue gladdens, or whose tongue delights. Increase <s>Bṛhaspati</s> with new hymns worthy of praise. <s>Asāmi</s> (unsuppressed) — <s>sāmi</s> means 'suppressed,' from <s>syati</s> (to bind). 'You bear unsuppressed strength, O generous ones.' You bear unrestricted strength, O ones of noble giving.

6.24: 'Let me not anger you by constantly begging for <s>Soma</s> with my song, [you who are] like a fierce wild animal angered at the pressing. Who would not beseech the sovereign lord?' Let me not anger you, always begging for <s>Soma</s> through pouring out, with my song, my hymn of praise — [you who are] like a fierce wild animal angered at the pressings. Who would not beseech the sovereign lord? <s>Galdā</s> (throat) — the veins (<s>dhamanī</s>) that are in the throat; the flowing (<s>galana</s>) is placed in them. 'May the drops enter you, through the <s>galdā</s>, through the veins' — this has various case endings; the meaning here is 'the flowing of the veins.'

6.25: 'We are not wicked, nor destitute, nor lacking in brilliance.' We do not consider ourselves evil, nor poor, nor devoid of splendor. 'We possess <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship), study (<s>adhyayana</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), and the practice of giving (<s>dānakarma</s>)' — so declared the sage. <s>Bakura</s> — shining (<s>bhāskara</s>), terrifying (<s>bhayaṃkara</s>), or 'shining, it runs.'

6.26: 'The <s>Aśvin</s>s, sowing barley with a plow, milking food for humankind, the wondrous ones, blowing away the <s>Dasyu</s> with the <s>bakura</s>, made broad light for the <s>Ārya</s>.' The <s>Aśvin</s>s, as if sowing barley with a plow (<s>vṛka</s>). <s>Vṛka</s> (plow) is [so called] from cutting (<s>vikartana</s>). <s>Lāṅgala</s> (plow) is from <s>laṅgati</s> (to go/limp), or [because it has a part] like a tail (<s>lāṅgūla</s>). <s>Lāṅgūla</s> (tail) is from <s>lagati</s> (to attach), <s>laṅgati</s> (to limp), or <s>lambati</s> (to hang). Milking food for humankind, the two splendid ones, blowing away the <s>Dasyu</s> with the <s>bakura</s> — with light, or with water. <s>Ārya</s> — son of a lord. <s>Bekanāṭā</s>s are indeed usurers — those who make double, or those who give double, or those who desire double. '<s>Indra</s> [overcomes] all the usurers who see the days, and the <s>Paṇi</s>s by his power' — <s>Indra</s> overcomes all the usurers who see the sun, who see these days and not beyond — or he overcomes [them] by action, and the <s>Paṇi</s>s (merchants) as well.

6.27: 'Come running to us while we yet live, O <s>Āditya</s>s, before the slaying! Where are you, O ones who hear invocations?' Come running to us while we live, O <s>Āditya</s>s, before the killing! Where are you, O hearers of invocations? They relate this as a sage's [verse] of fish that have fallen into a net. <s>Matsya</s> (fish) — they swim (<s>madhā</s>) in water; or they become intoxicated (<s>mādyante</s>) with one another for the purpose of eating. <s>Aṃhura</s> (distressed) — one having distress; <s>aṃhūraṇa</s> is also [a form] of this. 'Making wide room from narrow distress' — this Vedic usage also occurs. 'The wise ones fashioned seven boundaries; one who transgresses even one of them becomes distressed.' The wise ones indeed made seven boundaries; one who approaches even one [transgression] becomes distressed. [The seven are:] theft, approaching another's wife, killing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, killing an embryo, drinking liquor, repeated commission of sinful acts, and speaking falsehood in [serious] transgressions. <s>Bata</s> is an exclamatory particle [expressing] sorrow and compassion.

6.28: 'O weakling (<s>bata</s>), you are weak (<s>batā asi</s>), O <s>Yama</s>, we cannot fathom your mind and heart; another woman will surely embrace you, as a girth [embraces] one yoked, as a creeper [embraces] a tree.' (<s>ṚV</s> 10.10.13) <s>Bata</s> means 'one who has gone beyond strength' (<s>balātīta</s>), i.e., weak (<s>durbala</s>). 'O <s>Yama</s>, we cannot understand your mind and heart; another woman will surely embrace you, as a girth [embraces] one yoked, as a creeper (<s>libujā</s>) [embraces] a tree.' <s>Libujā</s> is a creeping plant (<s>vratatī</s>) — it clings (<s>līyate</s>), they explain (<s>vibhajanti</s>). <s>Vratatī</s> is derived from choosing (<s>varaṇa</s>), lying (<s>sayana</s>), and extending (<s>tatana</s>). <s>Vātāpya</s> means water — the wind (<s>vāta</s>) nourishes (<s>āpyāyayati</s>) it. 'Purifying the <s>vātāpya</s>, all-gladdening' — this is also a Vedic citation (<s>nigama</s>). 'Like [a tree] in a forest, O <s>Vāyu</s>, it was placed, desiring.' [This means] like a forest, O <s>Vāyu</s>, 'the son of <s>Vi</s>' — or 'desiring.' <s>Śākalya</s> analyzed it as <s>ve</s> and <s>ya</s>. But if taken thus, the verb would have been <s>udātta</s>-accented, and the meaning would have been well-obtained. <s>Ratharyati</s> — the meaning is established: 'one desiring to obtain a chariot,' or 'he desires a chariot.' 'This god desires a chariot (<s>ratharyati</s>)' — this is also a Vedic citation.

6.29: 'Fill her like a cow, the nourishment that cannot be crossed over (<s>asakrām</s>).' [<s>Asakrām</s> means] uncrossable (<s>asaṃkramaṇī</s>). <s>Ādhava</s> is derived from pressing (<s>ādhavana</s>). 'The accomplishment of thoughts and the <s>ādhava</s> of the wise' — this is also a Vedic citation. <s>Anavabravaḥ</s> means one whose speech is not cast down (<s>anavakṣiptavacanaḥ</s>). 'The victory-maker, like <s>Indra</s>, of unsubdued speech (<s>ānavabrava</s>)' — this is also a Vedic citation.

body.translated_text: 6.30: 'O niggardly one (<s>arāyi</s>), O one-eyed one (<s>kāṇe</s>), O deformed one (<s>vikare</s>), go to the mountain, O <s>Sadānvā</s>! With the creatures of <s>Śirimbiṭha</s>, we drive you away.' (<s>ṚV</s> 10.155.1) [<s>Arāyi</s> means] non-giver (<s>adāyinī</s>). O one-eyed one, O deformed one. <s>Aupamanyava</s> says <s>kāṇa</s> means one of impaired vision (<s>vikrāntadarśana</s>). Or it may be derived from the root <s>kaṇ</s> meaning 'becoming small' (<s>aṇūbhāvakarman</s>). <s>Kaṇati</s> is used in the sense of becoming minute — one 'becomes minute' (<s>anukaṇati</s>). From diminution of measure, [one gets] <s>kaṇa</s>; from diminution of sight, <s>kāṇa</s>. <s>Vikara</s> means one of distorted gait, says <s>Aupamanyava</s>. Or it may be from the root <s>kṛ</s> in reversed form — one who is deformed (<s>vikurita</s>). 'Go to the mountain, O <s>Sadānvā</s>' — [<s>Sadānvā</s> is] one who makes sounds constantly (<s>śabdakārikā</s>). 'With the creatures of <s>Śirimbiṛha</s>' — <s>Śirimbiṛha</s> is a cloud (<s>megha</s>): it breaks apart (<s>śīryate</s>) in the sky (<s>biṛha</s>). <s>Biṛha</s> is the atmosphere (<s>antarikṣa</s>); <s>biṛha</s> has been explained through <s>bīriṛa</s>. 'With its creatures' would mean 'with its waters' — 'with those we drive you away.' Alternatively, <s>Śirimbiṭha</s> is [a sage named] <s>Bhāradvāja</s>. <s>Kālakarṇa</s>, endowed [with him], dispelled the adverse fortune (<s>lakṣmī</s>) — 'with his creatures' would mean 'with his deeds' — 'with those we drive you away.' <s>Cātayati</s> means 'to destroy.' <s>Parāśara</s> was born from <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> who was aged (<s>sthavira</s>) and worn out (<s>parāśīrṇa</s>). 'May <s>Parāśara</s> [live] a hundred years, O <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>' — this is also a Vedic citation. <s>Indra</s> too is called <s>Parāśara</s>, the destroyer of sorcerers (<s>yātu</s>). '<s>Indra</s> became the <s>Parāśara</s> of sorcerers' — this is also a Vedic citation. <s>Krivirdatī</s> means one with cutting teeth (<s>vikartanadantī</s>). 'Where your thunderbolt strikes, O <s>Krivirdatī</s>' — this is also a Vedic citation. <s>Karūlatī</s> means one with broken teeth (<s>kṛttadatī</s>). Or perhaps, having seen some god with broken teeth, one spoke thus.

body.translated_text: 6.31: 'May god <s>Aryaman</s> give you desirable thing after desirable thing from afar; [may] <s>Pūṣan</s> [give] desirable things, <s>Bhaga</s> [give] desirable things, [may] the god <s>Karūḷatī</s> [give desirable things].' (<s>ṚV</s> 4.30.24) <s>Vāma</s> means desirable (<s>vananīya</s>). <s>Āduri</s> is derived from giving regard (<s>ādaraṇa</s>). Now, who is <s>Karūḷatī</s>? <s>Bhaga</s> was mentioned before; the back-reference (<s>anvādeśa</s>) to him is one [interpretation], and <s>Pūṣan</s> is another — he is the toothless one (<s>sodantaka</s>). '<s>Pūṣan</s> is toothless (<s>adantaka</s>)' — thus the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> also [states]. 'Give to our people, O <s>Indra</s>, [those of] soft speech (<s>mṛdhravāca</s>).' [This means:] O <s>Indra</s>, make our generous-minded people soft-spoken. 'He considers me as if I were without men (<s>avīrā</s>),' — [this means] this child considers me as if I were weak, wanting to wound (<s>saṃśiśariṣu</s>). <s>Idamyu</s> means 'desiring this.' And moreover, it is used in that sense: '<s>Indra</s> desiring wealth (<s>vasūyu</s>)' — the meaning there is 'possessing wealth' (<s>vasumān</s>). 'Desiring horses, desiring cattle, desiring chariots, desiring wealth, O <s>Indra</s>' — this is also a Vedic citation.

body.translated_text: 6.32: 'What do your cows do among the <s>Kīkaṭas</s>? They do not yield milk quickly, nor do they heat the cauldron. Bring to us the wealth of <s>Pramaganda</s>; O <s>Maghavan</s>, subdue for us <s>Naicāśākha</s>.' (<s>ṚV</s> 3.53.14) What do your cows do among the <s>Kīkaṭas</s>? <s>Kīkaṭa</s> is the name of a region, a non-<s>Ārya</s> settlement. <s>Kīkaṭāḥ</s> means 'what have they done?' (<s>kiṃkṛtāḥ</s>) — or it expresses the desire 'what actions [are possible]?' They do not yield milk quickly, nor do they heat the cauldron (<s>gharma</s>), [meaning] the dwelling (<s>harmya</s>). Bring to us the riches of <s>Pramaganda</s>. <s>Maganda</s> is a usurer (<s>kusīdī</s>). <s>Māṅgada</s> gives [thinking] 'he will come back to me.' His descendant is <s>Pramaganda</s>, of exceedingly usurious lineage; or <s>Pramadaka</s>, one who believes 'only this world exists, not the other' — one who is heedless. Or [it means] a eunuch (<s>paṇḍaka</s>). <s>Paṇḍaka</s>, [also called] <s>paṇḍaga</s>, or <s>prārdaka</s> — he crushes (<s>prārdayati</s>) the testicles (<s>āṇḍau</s>). The testicle (<s>āṇḍa</s>) humiliates what is situated there, like an axle-pin (<s>āṇī</s>). <s>Āṇī</s> is derived from <s>araṇa</s> (fitting). <s>Naicāśākha</s> means one with low branches (<s>nīcaiḥśākha</s>). <s>Śākhā</s> (branch) is derived from <s>śaknoti</s> (to be able). <s>Āṇi</s> is from <s>araṇa</s>. 'O <s>Maghavan</s>, subdue (<s>randhaya</s>) him for us' — <s>radhyati</s> means to come under control. <s>Bunda</s> is an arrow — [derived as] <s>bunda</s>, or <s>bhinda</s> (piercer), or <s>bhayada</s> (fear-giver), or 'shining forth (<s>bhāsamāna</s>) it runs (<s>dravati</s>).'

6.33: 'Your bow, of great thrust (<s>tuvikṣa</s>), is well-made, easy to handle (<s>sūmaya</s>); the <s>bunda</s> (arrow) is a good implement, golden. Both your arms are delightful, well-adorned — even against hard targets, they increase in force.' (<s>ṚV</s> 8.77.11) <s>Tuvikṣa</s> means 'of much thrust' (<s>bahuvikṣepa</s>) or 'of great thrust' (<s>mahāvikṣepa</s>). Your well-made, easy-to-handle bow is an instrument of accomplishment. Your golden arrow (<s>bunda</s>) — both your arms are delightful (<s>raṇya</s>), charming (<s>ramaṇīya</s>), or fit for battle (<s>sāṃgrāmya</s>). <s>Ṛdūpe</s> — striking at [vital] points (<s>ardanapātinau</s>) or reaching [their target] (<s>gamanapātinau</s>); piercing vital spots (<s>marman</s>) or reaching their mark (<s>gamanavedhinau</s>).

6.34: 'He pierced forth from the mountains, holding [the cloud] whose ripe offering is food — <s>Indra</s> [released] the <s>bunda</s> (drop), well-extended.' (<s>ṚV</s> 8.77.6) He pierced forth from the mountains, holding the cloud whose ripe offering is food (<s>odana</s>), the water-giver (<s>udakadāna</s>). <s>Indra</s> [released] the well-extended drop (<s>bunda</s>). <s>Vṛnda</s> (multitude) has been explained through <s>bunda</s>, and [likewise] <s>Vṛndāraka</s>.

6.35: 'This one who is the <s>hotṛ</s> (invoker) — indeed, in the domain of <s>Yama</s>, he carries together what the gods enjoy. Day after day he is born, month after month — thus the gods established the oblation-bearer.' (<s>ṚV</s> 10.52.3) This one who is the <s>hotṛ</s> (performer), in the domain of <s>Yama</s> he carries food (<s>anna</s>) that the gods partake of. Day after day he is born, month after month — or fortnight after fortnight — then the gods placed the oblation-bearer. <s>Ulba</s> (membrane) is derived from <s>ūrṇoti</s> (to cover) or <s>vṛṇoti</s> (to enclose). 'Great was that membrane (<s>ulba</s>), thick it was' — this is also a Vedic citation. <s>Ṛbīsa</s> means [a place] where light has departed (<s>apagatabhāsa</s>), where light has been taken away (<s>apahṛtabhāsa</s>), where light is concealed (<s>antarhitabhāsa</s>), or where light is gone (<s>gatabhāsa</s>).

6.36: 'With frost (<s>hima</s>) you warded off the fire, the summer heat (<s>ghraṃsa</s>); you bestowed upon him nourishment (<s>ūrja</s>) rich in sustenance. O <s>Aśvins</s>, you lifted up <s>Atri</s>, brought low into the <s>ṛbīsa</s> (abyss), together with all his company, to safety.' (<s>ṚV</s> 1.116.8) With water (<s>udaka</s>), at the end of summer, you warded off the fire, the heat (<s>ghraṃsa</s>) of the day; you bestowed food-yielding nourishment (<s>ūrja</s>) upon him, upon <s>Aṅgaya</s> — this <s>ṛbīsa</s> [means] the fire within the earth, within plants, trees, and waters — you lifted him up, together with all his company (<s>sarvagaṇa</s>), meaning 'of all names' (<s>sarvanāman</s>). <s>Gaṇa</s> is derived from counting (<s>gaṇana</s>), and [likewise] <s>guṇa</s>. When it rains, plants spring up and living beings [thrive] on earth — that is the form of the <s>Aśvins</s>; with that [form] one praises them.

[Nirukta 7.1:] [Now the section on deities (<s>Daivata Kāṇḍa</s>). <s>Om</s>. Now, hereafter, [we discuss] the deities.] Those which are the names of the principal deities of the hymns of praise — that is called '<s>daivata</s>' (relating to deity). This is the investigation of deity (<s>devatā-upaparīkṣā</s>). When a sage (<s>ṛṣi</s>), desiring prosperity from a particular deity, employs a hymn of praise — that <s>mantra</s> has that deity as its presiding deity. [This praise is of four kinds: by name, by connections (<s>bandhu</s>), by action, and by form — 'Praise is through name, form, action, and connections,' as stated.] These <s>ṛc</s>-verses are of three kinds: those composed in the indirect mode (<s>parokṣa-kṛtā</s>), those composed in the direct mode (<s>pratyakṣa-kṛtā</s>), and those relating to the self (<s>ādhyātmikī</s>). Among these, the indirectly composed ones are employed with all the case-inflections of the noun and with third-person forms of the verb.

[Nirukta 7.2:] [Examples of indirect (third-person) hymns:] "<s>Indra</s> rules over heaven, <s>Indra</s> over the earth." "The singers [praise] <s>Indra</s>, the great one." "By <s>Indra</s>, these <s>Tṛtsu</s>s, trembling." "Sing the <s>Sāman</s> to <s>Indra</s>." "Without <s>Indra</s>, no abode is purified." "Let me now proclaim the heroic deeds of <s>Indra</s>." "In <s>Indra</s>, desires have come to rest." Now, the directly composed ones employ the second person — 'you' (<s>tvam</s>) and the related pronouns: "You, O <s>Indra</s>, [are] above strength." "Strike down our enemies, O <s>Indra</s>." Moreover, in the directly composed [verses], the praisers [themselves] may be expressed [in the direct mode], while the objects of praise [remain] in the indirect mode: "Do not recite anything else." "O <s>Kanvas</s>, sing forth." "Come forward, O <s>Kuśikas</s>, be alert." Now, the self-referential (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) ones employ the first person — 'I' (<s>aham</s>) and the related pronouns — such as [the hymn where] <s>Indra</s> [speaks as] <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, the <s>Lava</s>-hymn, and the <s>Vāk Āmbhṛṇī</s> [hymn].

[Nirukta 7.3:] The indirectly and directly composed <s>mantras</s> are the most numerous; the self-referential ones are few. Moreover, sometimes there is praise alone, without a benediction — as in "Let me now proclaim the heroic deeds of <s>Indra</s>" and the hymn of that type. [Yet a benediction should be supplied, because praise is employed for the purpose of obtaining a blessing.] And sometimes there is a benediction alone, without praise: "May I be of good sight with my eyes, of good radiance with my face, of good hearing with my ears." This [type] is abundant in the <s>Ādhvaryu</s> [<s>Veda</s>, i.e., <s>Yajurveda</s>] and in the sacrificial <s>mantras</s>. [Yet even there praise should be supplied, for a deity that has not been praised does not fulfill the benediction.] Moreover, there are oaths and imprecations: "May I die today if I am a sorcerer." "Then let him be separated from ten heroes." Moreover, sometimes there is a desire to narrate some state of being: "There was no death, nor immortality then." "Darkness was concealed by darkness in the beginning." Moreover, sometimes there is lamentation arising from some condition: "May the good god (<s>sudeva</s>) today fall down, never to return." "I do not know whether I am this" [— thus this self-reproachful lamentation is called '<s>paridevanā</s>' (bewailing)]. Moreover, sometimes there is censure and commendation: "He who eats alone becomes entirely sinful." "The dwelling of the generous one (<s>Bhoja</s>) is like a lotus-pond." Likewise in the Dice Hymn (<s>Akṣa-sūkta</s>), there is censure of gambling and commendation of agriculture. Thus, with various high and low intentions, the sages' visions of the <s>mantras</s> come about.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 7.4:] Now, those <s>mantras</s> whose deity is not indicated — regarding them is the investigation of deity. Whatever deity a sacrifice or a sacrificial subsidiary belongs to, that becomes [its] deity. [For the rule is that in <s>mantras</s> of doubtful deity, the deity is determined by the ritual context.] Now, in contexts outside the sacrifice, 'they belong to <s>Prajāpati</s>' — so say the ritualists (<s>Yājñikas</s>); 'they are <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> (human-praising)' — so say the etymologists (<s>Nairuktas</s>). ['<s>Yajña</s>' — so says <s>Kātthakya</s>; '<s>Agni</s>' — so says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>.' By the word '<s>yajña</s>', <s>Viṣṇu</s> is meant, for it is known that '<s>Viṣṇu</s> indeed is the sacrifice.' 'For <s>Agni</s> has the greatest share among the deities'; therefore a <s>mantra</s> whose deity-marker is not manifest should be attributed to <s>Agni</s>, since <s>Agni</s> encompasses all deities — for it is known that '<s>Agni</s> indeed is all the deities' and 'in him all the deities dwell.'] Or alternatively, the deity may be the one desired (<s>kāma-devatā</s>). [For the deity should be assigned according to one's wish.] Or the presiding deity [of the ritual section] — for there is a widespread practice in the world: '<s>Devadeva</s>' (god of gods) [is applied] to a guest, [meaning] 'having a guest as deity,' 'having ancestors as deity.' [Whatever remains from such classification belongs commonly to gods, ancestors, and humans.] The <s>mantra</s> has the sacrifice or a deity as [its presiding entity]. Moreover, non-deities too are praised as if they were deities — such as the horse and others, up to the herbs — and there are also the eight pairs [of deities]. One should not think that the attributes of the deities are adventitious; this is directly observable. Due to the greatness of the deity, one self (<s>eka ātmā</s>) is praised in many ways; the other gods become limbs of the one self. Furthermore, they say that the sages praise [the deities] through the natural states (<s>prakṛti-bhūmi</s>) of beings, and because of the pronominal nature of [the term] '<s>prakṛti</s>' (nature). They are born of one another; they share one another's natures; they are born of action; they are born of the self. The self itself becomes their chariot, the self their horses, the self their weapons, the self their arrows — the self is everything of each god.

7.5: There are only three deities — so say the etymologists (<s>Nairuktāḥ</s>): <s>Agni</s>, whose station is the earth; <s>Vāyu</s> or <s>Indra</s>, whose station is the atmosphere; and <s>Sūrya</s>, whose station is the sky. Due to the greatness of each of them, each one has many names. Or, due to the differentiation of functions — just as one and the same [priest] is called <s>Hotṛ</s>, <s>Adhvaryu</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Udgātṛ</s>. Or they may indeed be separate [deities], for the hymns of praise are separate, and so are the designations. As to the [argument] that 'due to differentiation of functions,' even many [priests] may divide and perform the functions. In that regard, the unity of abode and the unity of enjoyment should be considered. Just as on the earth, humans, animals, and gods [share] unity of abode and of enjoyment. Just as [earth is nourished] by <s>Parjanya</s> (rain) and by <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Āditya</s> (wind and sun), and the enjoyment of the other world is by <s>Agni</s> — in this, [the system is] like a human kingdom.

7.6: Now, the consideration of the form of the deities. Some say they should be human-formed, for the hymns of praise are addressed as though to sentient beings, and so are the designations. [Another reason:] moreover, they are praised with human-like limbs: 'Great are your arms, O <s>Indra</s>, of the mighty one'; 'When you grasp, O <s>Maghavan</s>, what could resist you?' Moreover, with human-like material associations: 'Come, O <s>Indra</s>, with your two bay horses'; 'Beautiful is the wife in your house, at the [<s>Soma</s>-]drinking.' Moreover, with human-like actions: 'Eat, O <s>Indra</s>, and drink of the pressed [<s>Soma</s>]'; 'O you of attentive ear, hear the invocation!'

7.7: Others say they should be non-human-formed. For what is seen is non-human-formed, such as fire (<s>Agni</s>), wind (<s>Vāyu</s>), the sun (<s>Āditya</s>), earth (<s>Pṛthivī</s>), and the moon (<s>Candramā</s>). As to the [argument] that 'the hymns are addressed as though to sentient beings' — even non-sentient things are thus praised, from the dice onward to the herbs. As to the [argument] that 'they are praised with human-like limbs' — this occurs even for non-sentient things: 'They cry aloud with green-colored [stones]' — this is a praise of the pressing-stones. As to the [argument] about 'human-like material associations' — this too is of the same kind: 'The river yoked the comfortable chariot of the <s>Aśvin</s>s' — this is a praise of the river. As to the [argument] about 'human-like actions' — this too is of the same kind: 'Even before the <s>Hotṛ</s>, they tasted the oblation' — this is again a praise of the pressing-stones. Or perhaps they are of both kinds. Or perhaps, being truly non-human-formed, these [human attributes] may be their action-selves, just as a sacrifice [represents] the sacrificer — and this is the teaching of the traditional narratives.

7.8: 'There are only three deities' — this was stated earlier. We shall now explain the classification of their associations. [When the deity of a verse or mantra is not clearly identified, it is determined by association or companionship — for this purpose the classification of associations is stated.] Now these are the associations of <s>Agni</s>: this [earthly] world, the morning pressing, spring, <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter], the <s>Trivṛt</s> <s>Stoma</s>, the <s>Rathantara</s> <s>Sāman</s>, and whatever groups of gods are enumerated in the first position. <s>Agnāyī</s>, <s>Pṛthivī</s>, <s>Iḍā</s> — these are the female [deities associated with <s>Agni</s>]. Now his function is the conveying of oblations and the inviting of deities; whatever pertains to the domain of seeing [i.e., the visible/earthly domain] — that is the action of <s>Agni</s> itself. [By association, even without the word <s>Agni</s>, the mantra is <s>Āgneya</s>.] Now the deities praised alongside him [are:] <s>Indra</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Parjanya</s>, the seasons, and the offering to <s>Agni-Viṣṇu</s>. But no <s>ṛc</s> praising [<s>Agni</s>] jointly is found in the decades. Moreover, there is an offering to <s>Agni-Pūṣan</s>, but no joint praise; for that they cite this verse as a separate-praise verse.

7.9: 'May <s>Pūṣan</s>, the knowing one, move you from here — he whose cattle are not lost, the protector of the world. May he hand you over to these fathers; may <s>Agni</s> [hand you] to the gods who know well.' May <s>Pūṣan</s> move you from here, the knowing one — he whose cattle are not lost, the protector of the world — for he is the protector of all beings, the sun (<s>Āditya</s>). 'May he hand you over to these fathers' — the third quarter [of the verse] is ambiguous. <s>Pūṣan</s> in the first [part] is followed by his pronominal reference (<s>anvādeśa</s>) — that is one [interpretation]; <s>Agni</s> in the last [part] is followed by his direct naming (<s>prakīrtanā</s>) — that is the other. '<s>Agni</s> [hands over] to the gods who know well' — <s>suvidatra</s> is wealth, from <s>vindati</s> (to find) with one prefix [<s>su</s>]; or from <s>dadāti</s> (to give) with two prefixes [<s>su</s> and <s>vi</s>].

7.10: Now these are the associations of <s>Indra</s>: the atmospheric world, the midday pressing, summer, <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [meter], the fifteen-fold <s>Stoma</s>, the <s>Bṛhat</s> <s>Sāman</s>, and whatever groups of gods are enumerated in the middle position, and whatever female [deities]. Now his function is the distribution of essence (<s>rasa</s>) and the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>. Whatever display of strength [there is] — that is the action of <s>Indra</s> itself. Now the deities praised alongside him [are:] <s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>, <s>Parvata</s>, <s>Kutsa</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>. Moreover, <s>Mitra</s> is praised alongside <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s> alongside <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Soma</s> [alongside <s>Rudra</s>], <s>Agni</s> alongside <s>Pūṣan</s>, and <s>Vāta</s> alongside <s>Parjanya</s>.

7.11: Now these are the associations of <s>Āditya</s> (the sun): the yonder [celestial] world, the third pressing, the rainy season, <s>Jagatī</s> [meter], the seventeen-fold <s>Stoma</s>, the <s>Vairūpa</s> <s>Sāman</s>, and whatever groups of gods are enumerated in the highest position, beginning with the <s>Āditya</s>s, and whatever female [deities]. Now his function is the absorption of essence (<s>rasa</s>) [by evaporation] and the sustaining of essence through his rays; whatever is sent forth — that is the action of <s>Āditya</s> itself. The joint praises are with the moon, <s>Vāyu</s>, and the year. Among these same classifications of stations, one should assign the remaining associations of season, meter, <s>Stoma</s>, and <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [<s>Sāman</s>]. Autumn, <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, twenty-one-fold <s>Stoma</s>, <s>Vairāja</s> <s>Sāman</s> — these are the earth-based associations. Winter, <s>Paṅkti</s>, <s>Trinava</s> <s>Stoma</s>, <s>Śākvara</s> <s>Sāman</s> — these are the atmosphere-based associations. The cool season (<s>śiśira</s>), <s>Atichandas</s>, thirty-three-fold <s>Stoma</s>, <s>Raivata</s> <s>Sāman</s> — these are the sky-based associations.

body.translated_text: 7.12: <s>Mantra</s> (sacred formula) is from <s>manana</s> (thinking/contemplation). <s>Chandas</s> (meter/hymn) is from <s>chādana</s> (covering/protecting). <s>Stoma</s> (hymn of praise) is from <s>stavana</s> (praising). <s>Yajus</s> (sacrificial formula) is from <s>yajati</s> (to sacrifice). <s>Sāman</s> (chant) — it is measured together with the <s>ṛc</s>; or from <s>asyati</s> (to throw); or 'equal to the <s>ṛc</s>' they consider — so say the <s>Naidāna</s>s (ritualists). <s>Gāyatrī</s> is from <s>gāyati</s> (to sing), with the sense of praising; or 'moving in three' [i.e., three-footed], reversed; 'it sprang from the mouth of the singer' — so says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. <s>Uṣṇik</s> — it is well-bathed (<s>utsnātā</s>); or from <s>snihyati</s> (to be affectionate), with the sense of shining; or it is 'turbaned' (<s>uṣṇīṣinī</s>), used comparatively. <s>Uṣṇīṣa</s> (turban) is from <s>snāyati</s> (to wrap). <s>Kakubh</s> — it is peaked (<s>kakubhinī</s>). <s>Kakubh</s> and <s>kubja</s> (hunchback) are from <s>kujati</s> (to make sound) or <s>ubjati</s> (to press). <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> — from following-praise (<s>anustobhana</s>); 'it follows the three-footed <s>Gāyatrī</s> with a fourth foot by praising' — so says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. <s>Bṛhatī</s> (the great) — from encompassing (<s>paribarhaṇa</s>). <s>Paṅkti</s> — it is five-footed. <s>Triṣṭubh</s> — it praises with the last foot. But what would be its 'three'? It is the most-crossed meter; the three-fold <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt), and that [meter] is its praiser. 'Because it praised thrice, therefore it is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; you are <s>Triṣṭubh</s>' — so it is known.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 7.13:] '<s>Jagatī</s>' is the most mobile (<s>gatatama</s>) meter; or [named from] the gait of aquatic creatures (<s>jalacara</s>). The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> also says: "moving about (<s>jalgalyamāna</s>), he emitted." '<s>Virāṭ</s>' — from '<s>virāj</s>' (to shine forth), or '<s>virādh</s>' (to oppose), or '<s>viprāp</s>' (to overfill). From shining forth — [a verse with] complete syllable-count; from opposing — [with] deficient syllables; from overfilling — [with] excess syllables. 'Having a waist like an ant (<s>pipīlikamadhyā</s>)' — this is a simile. '<s>Pipīlikā</s>' (ant) from '<s>pel</s>' (to go), the action of going. Thus these deities have been enumerated. Most [deities] receive a whole hymn (<s>sūktabhāj</s>), an oblation (<s>havisbhāj</s>), or a verse (<s>ṛcbhāj</s>); some receive [only] an incidental mention (<s>nipātabhāj</s>). [The incidental mention (<s>nipāta</s>) is of two kinds: in the common praise together with other deities, and as a glossarial term (<s>naighaṇṭukatva</s>). Regarding the common praise — for example: '<s>Vidhātṛ</s>' (<s>Dhātṛ</s>) has been explained; its incidental occurrence is in a verse with many deities: "of King <s>Soma</s>" — in that [hymn], <s>Vidhātṛ</s> is praised in common along with <s>Soma</s> and others. As a glossarial term — for example: '<s>Pṛthivī</s>' (Earth) has been explained; her incidental occurrence is in a verse addressed to <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>: "O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, on the highest earth" — here <s>Pṛthivī</s> is not praised in common with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>; rather, she is used merely as a descriptive locative for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> alone.] [Another type of incidental mention is to be considered: namely, the absolutely glossarial deity-designation and the not-absolutely-glossarial.] Moreover, joining [the deity's name] with characteristic epithets (<s>abhidhāna</s>), [the poet] directs the oblation: 'for <s>Indra</s> the <s>Vṛtra</s>-slayer, for <s>Indra</s> the <s>Vṛtra</s>-conqueror, for <s>Indra</s> the releaser from distress.' Some enumerate these too [as deity-names]; but they are more numerous than the enumerated [canonical names]; however, whatever has become a conventional epithet (<s>saṃvijñāna</s>) that constitutes primary praise — that is enumerated. Moreover, the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) also praises the deities by their deeds: '<s>Vṛtrahā</s>' (Vṛtra-slayer), '<s>Purandara</s>' (fortress-destroyer). Some enumerate these too; but they are more numerous than the enumerated [names]; such [an epithet] serves merely as an indicator (<s>vyañjana</s>) of that [proper] name — just as [one says] 'give rice to the hungry <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, ointment to the bathed one, water to the thirsty one.'

[Nirukta 7.14:] Now hereafter we shall enumerate [the deities]. <s>Agni</s> occupies the station (<s>sthāna</s>) of earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>); him we shall explain first. Why [is he called] '<s>Agni</s>'? He is the leader (<s>agranī</s>) — he is led foremost (<s>agram</s>) in sacrifices; he leads (<s>nayati</s>) the limbs [of the sacrifice], bending down. He is '<s>aknopana</s>' (unwetting), says <s>Sthaulāṣṭhīvi</s> — he does not moisten (<s>knopayati</s>), does not make oily (<s>snehayati</s>). [The word '<s>Agni</s>'] is born from three verbal roots, says <s>Śākapūṇi</s> — from '<s>i</s>' (to go), from '<s>aj/añj</s>' (to anoint), and from '<s>dah</s>' (to burn), or from '<s>nī</s>' (to lead). He indeed takes the '<s>a</s>'-sound from '<s>i</s>' (going), the '<s>g</s>'-sound from '<s>añj</s>' (anointing) or '<s>dah</s>' (burning); '<s>nī</s>' (leading) is the final [element]. The [following verse] pertains to him.
