body.translated_text: [Nirukta 7.15:] "I praise <s>Agni</s>, the <s>purohita</s> (priest placed in front), the divine <s>ṛtvij</s> (officiant) of the sacrifice, the <s>hotṛ</s> (invoker), the most bountiful bestower of treasures." I praise (<s>īḷe</s>) <s>Agni</s> — I beseech <s>Agni</s>. '<s>Īḷ</s>' is an action of supplication (<s>adhyeṣaṇā</s>) or worship (<s>pūjā</s>). '<s>Purohita</s>' (placed in front) and '<s>yajña</s>' (sacrifice) have been explained. '<s>Deva</s>' (god) — from '<s>dā</s>' (to give), or '<s>pā</s>' (to nourish), or '<s>dyut</s>' (to shine), or because he occupies the station of heaven (<s>dyu</s>). That which is a '<s>deva</s>' — that is the '<s>devatā</s>' (deity). '<s>Hotṛ</s>' (invoker) — one who calls (<s>hvātṛ</s>). '<s>Hotṛ</s>' is from '<s>hu</s>' (to offer), says <s>Aurṇavābha</s>. '<s>Ratnadhātama</s>' — the greatest bestower of '<s>ratna</s>' (delightful wealth), the most generous giver of treasures. The [following verse] pertains to him.

[Nirukta 7.16:] "<s>Agni</s>, praiseworthy by the ancient <s>ṛṣis</s> and by the new ones too — may he bring the gods here." <s>Agni</s>, who is to be worshipped (praised) by the ancient <s>ṛṣis</s> and by us, the more recent ones — may he bring the gods here. One should not think 'this alone is <s>Agni</s>' — for the following two celestial lights (<s>jyotiṣī</s>) are also called <s>Agni</s>. Then [comes] the middle one [the atmospheric fire].

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 7.17:] "The streams of ghee (<s>ghṛta</s>) approached <s>Agni</s> like women (<s>yoṣāḥ</s>) of one mind, beautiful, smiling. The firewood (<s>samidh</s>) attains [him]; delighting in them, <s>Jātavedas</s> exults." They bowed down (<s>abhinamanta</s>), like women of one mind (<s>samanasaḥ</s>). '<s>Samana</s>' — from '<s>saman</s>' (harmony) or from '<s>sammāna</s>' (respect). 'Beautiful, smiling toward <s>Agni</s>' — this is a simile. 'The streams of <s>ghṛta</s>' — the streams of water. 'The firewood attains [him]' — '<s>nasati</s>' is an action of reaching (<s>āpnoti</s>) or bowing (<s>namati</s>). 'Delighting in them, he exults (<s>haryati</s>), <s>Jātavedas</s>.' '<s>Haryati</s>' is an action of 'desiring' (<s>prepsā</s>) — 'he exults' (<s>viharyati</s>). "From the ocean the honeyed wave arose" — they consider this to refer to <s>Āditya</s> (the sun). The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> also says: "for he rises from the ocean, from the waters." And there is also a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passage]: "<s>Agni</s> is all the deities." The following [verses] are for further etymological explanation.

[Nirukta 7.18:] "They call him <s>Indra</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Agni</s>; and he is the divine, beautiful-winged <s>Garutmān</s>. The wise speak of the one Being (<s>ekam sat</s>) in many ways — they call him <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Mātariśvan</s>." (ṚV 1.164.46) This very <s>Agni</s>, the great <s>Ātman</s> — the one <s>Ātman</s> — the wise (<s>medhāvins</s>) speak of in many ways: [they call him] <s>Indra</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and the divine <s>Garutmān</s>. '<s>Divya</s>' (divine) — born in heaven (<s>divija</s>). '<s>Garutmān</s>' — 'possessing a throat' (<s>garaṇavān</s>), 'heavy-souled' (<s>guru-ātmā</s>), or 'great-souled' (<s>mahā-ātmā</s>). He who receives a [whole] hymn (<s>sūkta</s>), to whom an oblation (<s>havis</s>) is offered — that is this very <s>Agni</s>. The following two celestial lights partake of this name incidentally (<s>nipāta</s>).

[Nirukta 7.19:] Why [is he called] '<s>Jātavedas</s>'? He knows (<s>veda</s>) [all] created beings (<s>jāta</s>); or all created beings know (<s>viduḥ</s>) him; or he is found (<s>vidyate</s>) in every being that is born (<s>jāte jāte</s>); or he is one whose wealth (<s>vitta</s>) is born, whose riches are born; or '<s>jātavidya</s>' — one whose knowledge (<s>prajñāna</s>) is born [innately]. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> says: "Because, being born, he found (<s>avindata</s>) the cattle — therefore [he has] the <s>jātavedas</s>-nature (<s>jātavedastva</s>) of <s>Jātavedas</s>." And [the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> also says]: "Therefore, in all seasons, cattle approach <s>Agni</s>." The [following verse] pertains to him.

[Nirukta 7.20:] "Send forth now <s>Jātavedas</s>, [swift] like a prize-winning horse. May he come to sit upon this our sacred grass (<s>barhis</s>)." Send forth <s>Jātavedas</s>, who encompasses [all] by his deeds. Or the comparison may be: [send him forth] like a horse — [like] <s>Jātavedas</s>. May he come to sit upon this our sacred grass. This one <s>Gāyatrī</s> triplet of <s>Jātavedas</s> is found in the decades (<s>daśatayī</s>). Whatever is addressed to <s>Agni</s> is used in place of [hymns to] <s>Jātavedas</s>. One should not think that this alone is <s>Agni</s> — the following two celestial lights are also called <s>Jātavedas</s>. Then [comes] the middle one. "The streams [of ghee] approached like women of one mind" — that has been explained earlier. And regarding the sun (<s>Āditya</s>): "That <s>Jātavedas</s> rises" — that we shall explain later. He who receives a hymn, to whom an oblation is offered — that is this very <s>Agni</s>, <s>Jātavedas</s>. The following two celestial lights partake of this name incidentally.

[Nirukta 7.21:] Why [is he called] '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>'? He leads (<s>nayati</s>) all men (<s>viśvān narān</s>); or all men lead him. Or it may simply be '<s>viśvānara</s>' — [the fire that] recurs (<s>pratyṛta</s>) in all beings; [the patronymic] of that [<s>viśvānara</s>] is '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>.' The [following verse] pertains to him.

[Nirukta 7.22:] "May we be in the good grace of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>; for he is the king, the glory over the worlds. Born from here, he surveys all this; <s>Vaiśvānara</s> strives with the sun." Born from here, he surveys, looks over, all this. <s>Vaiśvānara</s> strives together with the sun. The king who is to be resorted to (<s>abhiśrayanīya</s>) by all beings — may we be in the good grace (<s>kalyāṇī mati</s>) of that <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. Then who is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>? 'The middle one [the atmospheric fire],' say the teachers; for he praises him by the act of raining.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 7.23:] "Let me now proclaim the greatness of the bull, whom the peoples attend as the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>. <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>, having struck the <s>Dasyu</s>, shook down the waters and broke open <s>Śambara</s>." I proclaim that greatness, that majesty, of the bull — the one who showers waters. Whom the peoples — the men who are to be satisfied — attend as the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, the destroyer of the cloud, serving him, desiring rain. '<s>Dasyu</s>' is from '<s>dasyati</s>' (to destroy), with the sense of destruction — essences flow into him (<s>upadasyanty asmin rasāḥ</s>), or he makes activities flow. That one <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s> struck down; he shook loose the waters and the logs (<s>kāṣṭhā</s>); he broke open <s>Śambara</s>, the cloud. 'But that [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>] is <s>Āditya</s> (the sun)' — so say the earlier ritualists (<s>Yājñikas</s>). By the ascent through these worlds, the ascent through the <s>savanas</s> (pressings) is taught. From the ascent, a descent is intended [in the ritual]. Imitating that [cosmic pattern], the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest begins the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> recitation (<s>śastra</s>) with the <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> hymn. He too should not cling to the <s>Stotriya</s> [portion], for it belongs to <s>Agni</s>. From there come the deities of the intermediate station — <s>Rudra</s> and the <s>Maruts</s>. Then he recites the <s>Stotriya</s> for <s>Agni</s> in this [earthly] station, right here. Moreover, the <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> offering is on twelve potsherds, for this [fire] has twelvefold activity. 'That <s>Āditya</s> (sun) yonder is <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>' — [so the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> says]. Moreover, the <s>Nivit</s> invocation is solar-<s>Vaiśvānara</s>: 'He who shines upon heaven and earth.' For he illuminates both heaven and earth. Moreover, the Chāndogya hymn is solar-<s>Vaiśvānara</s>: 'His back shone in heaven.' For he indeed shone with his back in heaven. Moreover, the <s>Haviṣpāntīya</s> hymn is solar-<s>Vaiśvānara</s>. 'This very [terrestrial] <s>Agni</s> is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>' — so says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>. '<s>Viśvānarau</s>' — these latter two are the [celestial] lights. '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' is this [fire] because it is born from both of them. But how is this [fire] born from those two? When the lightning strikes a shelter, as long as it is not taken up [by fuel], it remains of intermediate nature — having water as its kindling and body as its pacification. When taken up [in fuel], this [fire] comes into being — having water as its pacification [origin] and body as its radiance. And from <s>Āditya</s> (the sun): having first obtained the rays going northward toward the sun, one polishes a copper [vessel] or a crystal, and holding it at a focus where dry cow-dung is placed without touching, that [dung] catches fire — and that too is this very same [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>]. Moreover, it is said: '<s>Vaiśvānara</s> strives with the sun.' But one self does not strive with itself; one strives with another. Thus when one kindles this [fire], from there the rays of that [sun] become manifest; from here the flames of this [fire rise]. Having observed the meeting of those two lights, [the sage] thus declared it. Now, those hymns or portions belonging to the highest station — whether <s>Sāvitra</s> (of <s>Savitṛ</s>), or <s>Saurya</s> (of <s>Sūrya</s>), or <s>Pauṣṇa</s> (of <s>Pūṣan</s>), or <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> (of <s>Viṣṇu</s>), [or <s>Vaiśvadevya</s>] — among these, <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> expressions would have appeared. And they praise him with the actions of <s>Āditya</s>: 'You rise,' 'You set,' 'You revolve.' But <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> expressions occur only in hymns of <s>Agni</s>. And they praise him with the actions of fire: 'You carry,' 'You cook,' 'He burns.' As for the objection that 'he praises him with the actions of rain,' this also applies to [terrestrial fire]: 'The same water rises up and falls down in days. The rains enliven the earth; the fires enliven the sky.' Thus that recited verse (<s>nigada</s>) has been explained.

[Nirukta 7.24:] "The dark passage of <s>Āditya</s> — the tawny, fair-winged ones, clad in water, fly up to heaven. They return from the seat of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order); then with ghee the earth is moistened." The dark passage is the night of <s>Āditya</s> (the sun). The tawny, fair-winged ones — the carrying rays of the sun. When they turn back from above toward here, together from the station of water, from <s>Āditya</s> — then with ghee, that is, with water, the earth is moistened. '<s>Ghṛta</s>' (ghee) is a name for water, from '<s>jigharti</s>' (to sprinkle), expressing the action of sprinkling. Moreover, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passage] states: '<s>Agni</s> indeed sets rain in motion from here; becoming like a cloud-cover (<s>dhāmacchad</s>), he rains; the <s>Maruts</s> guide the released rain.' 'When the <s>Āditya</s> (sun) turns downward with his rays, then it rains.' This is the meaning of 'from the ascent, a descent is intended.' This comes from the teaching of tradition (<s>āmnāya</s>). [The statement 'from the ascent, a descent' is merely a laudatory expression.] As for 'the <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> [offering] is on twelve potsherds' — the number of potsherds is not fixed, for there exist solar offerings of one potsherd and of five potsherds. As for 'moreover, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passage] states' — the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> contain manifold interpretive statements — '<s>Pṛthivī</s> (Earth) is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>,' 'the year (<s>Saṃvatsara</s>) is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>,' 'the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.' [Such '<s>bhakti</s>' (attribution) is an attribution of qualities.] As for 'the <s>Nivit</s> invocation is solar-<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' — that too belongs to this very [terrestrial fire]: 'He who shines for the human settlements' — for this [fire] indeed shines for human settlements. As for 'the <s>Haviṣpāntīya</s> hymn is solar-<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' — that too belongs to this very [fire]. '<s>Jamadagni</s>, the oblation-invoked one' — the <s>Jamadagnis</s> are those whose fires are kindled, or whose fires blaze; by those [fires] he is invoked. As for 'the <s>Haviṣpāntīya</s> hymn is solar-<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' — that too belongs to this very [fire].

[Nirukta 7.25-26:] "The drinkable oblation, ageless, knowing heaven, offered in the sky-touching [fire], pleasing to <s>Agni</s> — for his sustaining, for his bringing into being, for his upholding, the gods spread this [<s>Agni</s>] with food, for all these purposes." The oblation that is drinkable, ageless, knowing the sun, offered in the sky-touching [fire], pleasing to <s>Agni</s> — for his bearing, his bringing into being, and his sustaining — for all these purposes, the gods spread this <s>Agni</s> with food. Moreover, he says: [7.26] "In the lap of the waters, the great ones grasped him — the settlements attended their king, the praiseworthy one. The messenger brought <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s> from <s>Vivasvat</s>, <s>Mātariśvan</s> [brought him] from afar." In the lap of the waters — in the abode, in the great atmospheric world — seated, or [they are called] great ones. The intermediate hosts of gods grasped [him]; like the settlements [attending] a king, they attended the praiseworthy one — '<s>ṛgmiya</s>' means either 'possessing hymns,' or 'worthy of praise,' or 'worthy of worship.' The messenger of the gods brought him from <s>Vivasvat</s>, from <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) — <s>Vivasvān</s> means 'possessing illumination' — sent forth [by him], or from this <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s> who came from afar — he names <s>Mātariśvan</s> as the bringer. <s>Mātariśvan</s> is <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) — he breathes in the mother, the atmosphere (<s>mātari antarikṣe śvasiti</s>), or 'he goes swiftly in the mother' (<s>mātari āśvanati</s>). And with these two [fire and sun], he praises all things.

[Nirukta 7.27:] 'The head of the two worlds (<s>bhuvas</s>) becomes <s>Agni</s> at night; from that, <s>Sūrya</s> is born, rising in the morning. This is indeed the skillful design (<s>māyā</s>) of the sacrificial ones — that he, the knower, swiftly moves through his works.' (<s>ṚV</s> 1.143.3) <s>Mūrdhā</s> (head) — [so called because] form (<s>mūrta</s>) is placed (<s>dhīyate</s>) in it; <s>mūrdhā</s>, he who is [the head] of all beings, becomes [<s>Agni</s>] at night. From that, <s>Sūrya</s> is born, rising in the morning — he is the same one. They consider this to be the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) of the sacrificial gods, those who accomplish the sacrifice. [The meaning of] 'works' (<s>apas</s>) — he who, knowing, moves swiftly through all stations. The following [verse] is for further etymological explanation (<s>nirvacana</s>) of that.

[Nirukta 7.28:] 'By praise (<s>stoma</s>), indeed, the gods in heaven generated <s>Agni</s>; with their powers (<s>śakti</s>), they filled heaven and earth. They made him threefold on the earth; he ripens herbs of all forms.' (<s>ṚV</s> 1.143.4) By praise, indeed, the gods in heaven generated <s>Agni</s>; with powers, with ritual acts, they made the filling of heaven and earth; they made him for threefold existence — on earth, in the atmosphere, and in heaven — so says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>. 'That which is his third [form] in heaven, that is the <s>Āditya</s> (sun)' — thus states the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Having made that [identification with] <s>Agni</s>, he praises. Then with this [verse] he praises, having made [the identification with] <s>Āditya</s>.

[Nirukta 7.29:] 'When the sacrificial gods placed him in heaven as <s>Sūrya</s>, the son of <s>Aditi</s>; when the two wandering ones became a pair — then they beheld all the worlds.' (<s>ṚV</s> 1.143.5) When the sacrificial [gods], all the gods in heaven, placed him as <s>Sūrya</s>, the son of <s>Aditi</s> (<s>āditya</s>). When the two wandering ones became a pair — always moving together, <s>Uṣas</s> (dawn) and <s>Āditya</s> (the sun). <s>Mithuna</s> (pair) — why? <s>Minoti</s> means the act of casting (<s>śrayati</s>); <s>thu</s> is a name-forming suffix, or the <s>stha</s>-element [is present]; or the latter part is from <s>nayati</s> (to lead) or <s>vanir</s> (to desire) — the two who, mutually dependent, lead or desire each other. The human pair also — from this same [etymology] — the two who embrace (<s>methantau</s>), mutually desiring each other. Then with this [verse] he praises, having made [the identification with] <s>Agni</s>.

[Nirukta 7.30:] 'Where the nearer and the farther one dispute — which of the two among us knows the sacrifice better? Companions rejoicing together have attained success — they partake of the sacrifice; who will proclaim this?' (<s>ṚV</s> 1.143.6) Where the two divine <s>hotṛ</s>s (invokers) dispute — this <s>Agni</s> here and that middle one [in the atmosphere]. Which of the two knows more in the sacrifice — they are able [to accomplish] that, those priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) of common renown who rejoice together; among those who partake of the sacrifice, who would not wish to proclaim this? The following [verse] is for further etymological explanation (<s>nirvacana</s>) of that.

[Nirukta 7.31:] 'As much as the measure of dawn's likeness — [during that time] <s>Mātariśvan</s> dwells like a fair-winged bird. For that long he places [the offering], coming to the sacrifice; the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> priest, the lower <s>hotṛ</s>, sits down.' (<s>ṚV</s> 1.143.7) As much as the measure (<s>mātra</s>) of dawn's countenance (<s>pratyakta</s>), meaning its appearance (<s>pratidarśana</s>). There is a usage of a simile (<s>upamāna</s>) in the sense of the thing compared — as in the expression 'place it just like this.' The fair-winged (<s>suparṇi</s>) [nights] — the nights of good flight — during which <s>Mātariśvan</s> (the light-bearer) dwells; for that long he places [offerings], coming to the sacrifice. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> priest, the <s>hotṛ</s> of this swift <s>Agni</s>, sits down. However, the <s>hotṛ</s>'s recitation (<s>hotṛ-japa</s>) without fire belongs to [the rite of] <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. 'O god <s>Savitṛ</s>, they choose you, this <s>Agni</s>, for the <s>hotra</s> office, together with <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the father' — thus [the formula]. This indeed refers to <s>Agni</s> as <s>Savitṛ</s>, the impeller of all, whether the middle or the highest father. But the one to whom the hymn is dedicated, for whom the oblation is prepared — that very one is <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>. Indeed, these latter two luminaries (<s>jyotiṣī</s>) share this name as a mere designation (<s>nipāta</s>).

[Nirukta 8.1:] Why [is <s>Agni</s> called] <s>Draviṇodas</s> (giver of wealth)? Wealth (<s>dhana</s>) is called <s>draviṇa</s>, because people run (<s>abhidravanti</s>) toward it. Or <s>draviṇa</s> means strength (<s>bala</s>), because with it people rush forward (<s>abhidravanti</s>). The giver (<s>dātṛ</s>) of that is <s>Draviṇodas</s>. This [verse] belongs to that [epithet].

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 8.2:] '<s>Draviṇodas</s> — seizers of wealth, with hands [extended] at the <s>adhvara</s> (sacrifice); they praise the god at the sacrifices.' (<s>ṚV</s> 1.15.9) <s>Draviṇodas</s> — you who [are such]. <s>Draviṇasas</s> means 'wealth-acquiring' (<s>draviṇa-sādin</s>), or 'wealth-possessing' (<s>draviṇa-sānin</s>), or 'therefore let <s>Draviṇas</s> drink.' At sacrifices they praise the god — they beseech, they extol, they magnify, they worship. Now, who is <s>Draviṇodas</s>? <s>Indra</s>, says <s>Krauṣṭuki</s>. He is the greatest giver of both strength and wealth, and all exercise of strength belongs to him. 'Born of might, I deem him thus' — so it says. Moreover, <s>Agni</s> too is called <s>Drāviṇodasa</s>. But he (<s>Agni</s>) is born from him (<s>Indra</s>). 'He who generated <s>Agni</s> between two stones' — this is also a Vedic citation. Moreover, in the seasonal offerings (<s>ṛtu-yāja</s>), the <s>Drāviṇodasa</s> invocations occur. Of those, the drinking from the vessel again belongs to <s>Indra</s>. Moreover, he praises him with the <s>Soma</s> drink. And moreover it says: 'Let <s>Draviṇodas</s> drink of the <s>Drāviṇodasa</s> [offerings].' This very <s>Agni</s> is <s>Draviṇodas</s> — so says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>. For in the hymns dedicated to <s>Agni</s> alone do the <s>Drāviṇodasa</s> invocations occur. 'The gods upheld <s>Agni</s>, the giver of wealth (<s>Draviṇodā</s>)' — this is also a Vedic citation. As for the [argument] that he is the greatest giver of both strength and wealth — sovereignty exists in all deities. As for [the citation] 'born of might, I deem him thus' — this <s>Agni</s> too is born by being churned with force (<s>ojas</s>, strength). Therefore he is called son of strength (<s>sahasaḥ putra</s>), offspring of strength (<s>sahasaḥ sūnu</s>), child of strength (<s>sahaso yahu</s>). As for [the argument] that <s>Agni</s> is called <s>Drāviṇodasa</s> — [in that context] the priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) are called <s>Draviṇodas</s>. They are the givers of the oblation, and they generate him (<s>Agni</s>). 'The son of the <s>ṛṣi</s>s, this sovereign' — this is also a Vedic citation. As for [the argument] that the drinking from the vessel again belongs to <s>Indra</s> — that is merely a conventional attribution (<s>bhakti-mātra</s>), just as 'belonging to <s>Vāyu</s>' is [said] of all <s>Soma</s> vessels. As for [the argument] that he praises him with the <s>Soma</s> drink — this also applies to <s>Agni</s>. '<s>Soma</s>, drink, delighting, with the <s>Gaṇāśri</s> chants' — this is also a Vedic citation. As for [the argument] 'let <s>Draviṇodas</s> drink of the <s>Drāviṇodasa</s> [offerings]' — that too belongs to this very [<s>Agni</s>].

[Nirukta 8.3:] 'May your draft-animals by which you travel prosper, unharmed; strengthen yourself, O <s>Vanaspati</s> (lord of the forest). Living long, O bold one, O reverend one, drink <s>Soma</s> from the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>'s [station], by the seasons.' (<s>ṚV</s> 1.13.11) May your bearers (<s>vahni</s>), the carriers by which you travel, prosper unharmed. Be firm, be strong! Living long, O bold one, O reverend one, [drink] from the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>'s station (<s>dhiṣṇya</s>). <s>Dhiṣṇya</s> means <s>dhiṣaṇya</s> or <s>dhiṣaṇā</s> — the [sacrificial] seat. <s>Dhiṣaṇā</s> means speech (<s>vāc</s>), from <s>dhiṣ</s> in the sense of 'placing' (<s>dadhāti</s>). Or it means 'intellect-acquiring' (<s>dhī-sādinī</s>), or 'intellect-possessing' (<s>dhī-sāninī</s>). He calls him <s>Vanaspati</s> (lord of the forest), for he is the drinker (<s>pātṛ</s>) or protector (<s>pālayitṛ</s>) of the forests (<s>vana</s>). <s>Vana</s> is derived from <s>vanoti</s> (to desire, to serve). Drink by the seasons (<s>ṛtu</s>), [that is,] by the [proper] times (<s>kāla</s>).

[Nirukta 8.4:] Now, next, [regarding] the <s>Āprī</s> [verses]. Why <s>Āprī</s>? From <s>āpnoti</s> (to obtain), or from <s>prīṇāti</s> (to please). 'With the <s>Āprī</s> verses, he pleases (<s>āprīṇāti</s>)' — thus the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [states]. Among those [verses], <s>idhma</s> (firewood) comes first. <s>Idhma</s> is derived from kindling (<s>samindhana</s>). This [verse] belongs to that.

body.translated_text: 8.5: 'Kindled today in the house of man, O god, you sacrifice to the gods, O <s>Jātavedas</s>. Bring [them] hither, O friend of great ones, knowing one — you are the messenger, the seer, the wise one.' Kindled today in the house of the human being, O god, you sacrifice to the gods, O <s>Jātavedas</s>; and bring [them], O friend of great ones, the knowing one, the conscious one — you are the messenger, the seer, the one of advanced understanding. 'In the sacrifice, it is the kindling-wood (<s>idhma</s>)' — so says <s>Kātthakya</s>. 'It is <s>Agni</s>' — so says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>. <s>Tanūnapāt</s> is the clarified butter (<s>ājya</s>). <s>Napāt</s> is the name for immediate offspring. It is the most extended [product]. Here 'cow' (<s>go</s>) is called <s>tanū</s> (body). The enjoyments are prepared (<s>tatā</s>) in her. From her, milk (<s>payas</s>) is born. From milk, clarified butter (<s>ājya</s>) is born. '<s>Agni</s>' — so says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>. Here 'waters' (<s>āpas</s>) are called <s>tanū</s> (bodies). They are extended in the atmosphere. From them in turn, trees and plants are born; from plants and trees, this [<s>Agni</s>] is born. Regarding this, the following [verse] occurs:

8.6: 'O <s>Tanūnapāt</s>, anointing with honey the paths of truth to be traversed, make [them] sweet, O fair-tongued one. Fulfill our thoughts with prayers, and the sacrifice; make our rite go to the gods.' O <s>Tanūnapāt</s>, anointing with honey the paths of the sacrifice to be traversed, make [them] sweet, O fair-tongued one. Fulfill our contemplations with prayers and the sacrifice. Make our sacrifice go to the gods. '<s>Narāśaṃsa</s> is the sacrifice' — so says <s>Kātthakya</s>; men (<s>narāḥ</s>) sitting in it praise (<s>śaṃsanti</s>). '<s>Agni</s>' — so says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>; he is praiseworthy by men. Regarding this, the following [verse] occurs:

8.7: 'Let us praise the greatness of <s>Narāśaṃsa</s>, of these [gods], the worshipful one, with sacrifices. The gods who are of good deeds, pure, holders of thought — may they make both kinds of oblations sweet.' Let us praise the greatness of <s>Narāśaṃsa</s>, among these, the worshipful one, with sacrifices; the gods who are of good deeds, pure, sustainers of thought — may they sweeten both kinds of oblations: <s>Soma</s> and the others; or the regular offerings and the occasional ones. <s>Iḍā</s> is from <s>iṭṭi</s> (praising), with the sense of praise; or from <s>indh</s> (to kindle). Regarding this, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 8.8: 'Being invoked, worthy of praise and veneration, come, O <s>Agni</s>, delighting with the <s>Vasu</s>s. You are the great <s>Hotṛ</s> of the gods — worship them, being impelled, most worthy of sacrifice.' Being called upon, worthy of being praised and venerated, come, O <s>Agni</s>, delighting together with the <s>Vasu</s>s. You are the great <s>Hotṛ</s> of the gods. <s>Yahva</s> is a name for 'great.' He both goes (<s>yāta</s>) and is invoked (<s>hūta</s>). Worship them, being impelled, the most worthy of sacrifice. <s>Iṣita</s> means 'sent forth' or 'requested.' <s>Yajīyān</s> means 'most devoted to sacrifice.' <s>Barhis</s> (sacred grass) is from <s>paribarhaṇa</s> (encompassing). Regarding this, the following [verse] occurs:

8.9: 'Let the sacred grass be spread eastward, in the direction of the earth, for the dwelling of this [goddess], at the beginning of the days. Let it be spread wider and broader, a pleasant [seat] for the gods and for <s>Aditi</s>.' Let the sacred grass be spread eastward, in the direction of the earth, for dwelling upon, for this one — the sacred grass [is spread] on the first day. It is spread wider — more scattered or more extended. Broader (<s>varīyas</s>) — more desirable, or more spacious. A pleasant [seat] for the gods and for <s>Aditi</s>. <s>Syona</s> is a name for comfort, from <s>syati</s> (to bind) — they find rest upon it; or it is something to be resorted to. <s>Dvār</s> (door) is from <s>javati</s> (to be swift), or <s>dravati</s> (to run), or <s>vārayati</s> (to bar). Regarding them, the following [verse] occurs:

8.10: 'Wide-spreading, may they open broadly, adorning themselves like wives for their husbands. Divine doors, great ones, pervading all — be easy of access for the gods.' Having width, may they open with spaciousness; like wives [opening] their thighs for their husbands in the rite of union, adorning themselves. The thigh is the most desirable limb. Divine doors, great ones — through them everything goes in the sacrifice. 'House doors' — so says <s>Kātthakya</s>. '<s>Agni</s>' — so says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>. <s>Uṣāsānaktā</s> — dawn (<s>Uṣas</s>) and night (<s>Naktā</s>). <s>Uṣā</s> has been explained. <s>Naktā</s> is a name for night — she anoints (<s>anakti</s>) beings with dew; or <s>naktā</s> means 'of indistinct color.' Regarding these two, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 8.11: 'Let the well-praising one worship nearby; may <s>Uṣāsānaktā</s> (Dawn and Night) sit down in the [sacrificial] seat — the two divine, great, golden-adorned [goddesses] in the heavenly womb, bearing bright, multi-colored beauty.' [Alternatively:] the two who cause pleasant dreams; or the two who cause good sleep; may they sit down; may they sit down upon [the seat]. The two sacrificial, approached [goddesses] in the divine womb. The two great ones. The two golden, the two shining ones. Bearing bright, multi-colored beauty. <s>Śukra</s> (bright) is from <s>śocati</s> (to blaze), with the sense of burning. <s>Peśas</s> is a name for form/color. From <s>piṃśati</s> (to adorn) — it becomes variegated. The two divine <s>Hotṛ</s>s — this <s>Agni</s> here and that intermediate one; regarding these two, the following [verse] occurs:

8.12: 'The two divine <s>Hotṛ</s>s, the first, the eloquent, measuring out the sacrifice for the human being to worship, inspiring the skilled at the assemblies, pointing forth the eastward light in the eastward direction.' The two divine <s>Hotṛ</s>s, the first, the eloquent, fashioning the sacrifice for the human being, for his worship. Inspiring the performers at the sacrificial assemblies, indicating that the sacrifice should be performed in the eastern direction. The three goddesses — the three divine ones; regarding them, the following [verse] occurs:

8.13: 'May <s>Bhāratī</s> come quickly to our sacrifice; <s>Iḍā</s> awakening here as among humans; may the three goddesses sit upon this pleasant sacred grass — <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the skilled ones.' May <s>Bhāratī</s> come quickly to our sacrifice. <s>Bharata</s> is the sun (<s>Āditya</s>); <s>Bhāratī</s> is his radiance. And <s>Iḍā</s>, awakening here as among human beings. May the three goddesses — <s>Sarasvatī</s> and the skilled ones — sit upon this pleasant sacred grass. <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> — 'he quickly attains' according to the etymologists; or from <s>tviṣ</s> (to shine), with the sense of blazing; or from <s>tvakṣ</s> (to fashion), with the sense of making. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

8.14: 'He who fashioned these two, heaven and earth, the mother-pair, and adorned all beings with forms — him, O <s>Hotṛ</s>, impelled, most worthy of sacrifice, worship here today, the divine <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, knowing one.' He who made these two, heaven and earth, the two mothers, and made all beings with forms — him, O <s>Hotṛ</s>, impelled, most worthy of sacrifice, worship here today, the divine <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, as one who knows. '<s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> is the intermediate one [i.e., atmospheric],' they say, and he is enumerated in the middle position. '<s>Agni</s>' — so says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>. Regarding him, the following other [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 8.15: 'Made manifest, the beautiful one grows among them; erect among the crooked, self-glorious, in the lap. Both [heaven and earth] fear him being born, O <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>; facing [him], they delight in the lion.' Made manifest — from making known (<s>āvedana</s>). The beautiful one grows among them. <s>Cāru</s> (beautiful) is from <s>carati</s> (to move). <s>Jihma</s> (crooked) is from <s>jihīti</s> (to be crooked). The erect one is elevated. Self-glorious (<s>svayaśas</s>) — glorious by his own glory; in the lap (<s>upastha</s>) — at the station. Both [heaven and earth] fear him, O <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, being born. Facing [him], they delight in the lion. [The 'both' means] heaven and earth, or day and night, or the two fire-sticks (<s>araṇī</s>). The two facing ones delight in the lion (<s>siṃha</s>), the overpowering one. <s>Vanaspati</s> (lord of the forest/sacrificial post) has been explained. Regarding it, the following [verse] occurs:
8.16: <s>Vanaspati</s> (lord of the forest) has been explained. Regarding it, the following [verse] occurs:

8.17: 'Release [the offering] with self-anointing; offer the food of the gods, the oblations, season by season. May <s>Vanaspati</s>, the divine slaughterer, <s>Agni</s> — may they make the oblation sweet with honey and ghee.' Release the offering with self-anointing, the self anointing the self; the food of the gods, the oblations, at each proper season. <s>Vanaspati</s>, the slaughterer (<s>śamitṛ</s>), and the divine <s>Agni</s> — these three, may they sweeten the oblation with honey and with ghee. Who then is <s>Vanaspati</s>? 'The sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>)' — so says <s>Kātthakya</s>. '<s>Agni</s>' — so says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>. Regarding him, the following other [verse] occurs:

[Nirukta 8.18:] "Those desiring the gods anoint you, O <s>Vanaspati</s>, in the sacrifice, with divine honey. When you stand upright, bestow wealth here; or when your dwelling is in the lap of this mother." Those desiring the gods anoint you, O lord of the forest (<s>Vanaspati</s>), in the sacrifice, with divine honey and with ghee. When you will stand upright, and will give us wealth. Or when your dwelling (<s>kṣaya</s>) is made in the lap (<s>upastha</s>) of this mother — i.e. in her station. [<s>Vanaspati</s> here is] <s>Agni</s>, says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>. The next [verse] pertains to him.

[Nirukta 8.19:] "O <s>Vanaspati</s>, present the oblation to the gods, O golden-leaved one; since ancient times [this has been] your purpose. Having yoked [you] with a rein, turning rightward, convey [the offering] by the straightest paths of <s>ṛta</s> (sacred order)." O <s>Vanaspati</s>, [present] the oblation to the gods, O golden-leaved one — or '<s>ṛta</s>-leaved' (having leaves of truth); or the comparison may be — 'having leaves of golden color.' '<s>Pradivas</s>' — 'since ancient times, this is your purpose which we declare to you.' Convey the sacrifice by the straightest paths — the most seasonal (<s>ṛtutama</s>), the most vigorous (<s>rajasvalatama</s>); or 'the most well-ground' (<s>prapiṣṭatama</s>). The next [verse] pertains to him.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 8.20:] "O <s>Vanaspati</s>, yoked with a rein of excellent form, knowing the lights of knowledge (<s>vayunāni</s>), carry the oblations to the gods, O desirer, and announce the giver to the immortals." O <s>Vanaspati</s>, yoked with a rein — of the most excellent form (<s>surūpatamayā</s>). Knowing the lights of knowledge — understanding the modes of wisdom (<s>prajñānāni prajānan</s>) — carry the oblations to the gods in the sacrifice. And announce the giver to the immortal gods. [Now regarding] the <s>Svāhākṛti</s> (the <s>Svāhā</s>-utterances): '<s>Svāhā</s>' — this means '<s>su āha</s>' (well-spoken); or '<s>svā</s>' (self) '<s>āha</s>' (declares) — 'the self declares'; or '<s>svam prāha</s>' — 'one declares oneself'; or '<s>svāhutam haviḥ juhoti</s>' — 'one offers the well-offered oblation.' The [following verse] pertains to them.

[Nirukta 8.21:] "Being born at once, he measured out the sacrifice; <s>Agni</s> became the forerunner of the gods. May the gods eat the <s>Svāhā</s>-consecrated oblation, by the direction of this invoker (<s>Hotṛ</s>), by the voice of <s>Ṛta</s> (truth)." Being born at that very moment, he fashioned (<s>niramimīta</s>) the sacrifice; <s>Agni</s> became the forerunner (<s>purogāmī</s>) of the gods. By the direction of this invoker, by the voice of <s>Ṛta</s> — by the mouth — may the gods eat the <s>Svāhā</s>-consecrated oblation. Thus these <s>Āprī</s> (propitiatory) deities have been enumerated. Now, to what deities do the <s>prayājas</s> (fore-offerings) and <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings) belong? 'To <s>Agni</s>,' say some.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 8.22:] "Give me a share of the <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s>, single ones, rich in nourishment, of the oblation. And [give me] the ghee of the waters, the essence (<s>puruṣa</s>) of the plants; and may long life be for <s>Agni</s>, O gods." "May your <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s> be single, rich in nourishment — your shares of the oblation. May all the sacrifice be yours, O <s>Agni</s>; may the four directions bow to you." "The <s>prayājas</s> belong to <s>Agni</s>; the <s>anuyājas</s> belong to <s>Agni</s>" — thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. [They belong] to the meters (<s>chandas</s>), says another [view]. "The <s>prayājas</s> belong to the meters; the <s>anuyājas</s> belong to the meters" — thus also says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. [They belong] to the seasons (<s>ṛtu</s>), says another. "The <s>prayājas</s> belong to the seasons; the <s>anuyājas</s> belong to the sacrificial animals" — thus also says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. [They belong] to the vital breaths (<s>prāṇa</s>), says another. "The <s>prayājas</s> belong to the in-breath (<s>prāṇa</s>); the <s>anuyājas</s> belong to the out-breath (<s>apāna</s>)" — thus also says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. But the established view is that they belong to <s>Agni</s>; the others are merely secondary associations. Why then is this said [i.e. the multiple attributions]? "When an oblation has been taken for a [particular] deity, one should meditate on that deity in the mind when about to utter the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call" — thus it is known. These are the eleven <s>Āprī</s> hymns. Among them, the <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> type is this one; the <s>Vādhyaśva</s> and <s>Gārtsamada</s> types do not contain the <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> [verse]. The <s>Maidhātithi</s>, <s>Dairghatamasa</s>, and <s>Praiṣika</s> types contain both. The remaining ones contain the <s>Tanūnapāt</s> [verse].

[Nirukta 9.1:] Now, those earthly beings that receive praise — those we shall enumerate hereafter. Among them, the horse (<s>aśva</s>) comes first. '<s>Aśva</s>' (horse) has been explained. The [following verse] pertains to him.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 9.2:] "The horse is the carrier of comfort, of the chariot; of laughter, the enticers; the frog desires water for rain-breeding — flow around for <s>Indra</s>, O drop." The horse is the carrier (<s>voḍhṛ</s>) — the carrier of comfort, the carrier of the chariot. '<s>Sukha</s>' (comfort) is a name for 'good, auspicious'; what is auspicious is meritorious; it is well-placed (<s>suhita</s>); or 'one goes well (<s>suhitam gamyati</s>) [in it].' [The horse] is the laugher (<s>hasā</s>), or the runner (<s>etā</s>); or the drinker (<s>pātā</s>), or the one who plays (<s>pālalyitā</s>). Or 'it reaches the penis (<s>śepa</s>).' '<s>Vāri</s>' (water) — it wards off (<s>vāryati</s>). '<s>Māna</s>' (man/human) has been explained. The [following verse] pertains to him.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 9.3:] "May <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Āyu</s>, <s>Indra</s> <s>Ṛbhukṣan</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s> not find fault — when we shall proclaim at the assembly the heroic deeds of this divine-born steed." When we shall proclaim at the sacrifice, at the assembly (<s>vidatha</s>), the heroic deeds of this prize-winning (<s>vājin</s>), divine-born steed (<s>sapti</s>, the runner) — may <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Āyu</s> (<s>Vāyu</s>, the course), <s>Indra</s> (of wide abode, or king of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>), and the <s>Maruts</s> not find fault. '<s>Śakuni</s>' (bird): it is able (<s>śaknoti</s>) to lift itself up; or 'it is able to resound (<s>naditu</s>)'; or 'it is able to fly (<s>takitu</s>)'; or 'may the beneficent (<s>śaṃkara</s>) one be [auspicious] from all sides'; or from '<s>śak</s>' (to be able). The [following verse] pertains to him.

[Nirukta 9.4:] "Crying out, proclaiming its birth, it utters its voice like an oarsman [propels] a boat. Be an auspicious bird, O <s>Śakuni</s>! May no overwhelming hostile power find you." It cried out, proclaiming its birth — its sound is its name — it utters its voice, like an oarsman [propels] a boat. Be an auspicious bird, O <s>Śakuni</s> — of good omen (<s>kalyāṇa-maṅgala</s>). '<s>Maṅgala</s>' (auspiciousness) from '<s>nir</s>' (to lead) in the sense of 'praising' (<s>gṛṇāti</s>); or 'it swallows (<s>girati</s>) misfortunes.' '<s>Aṅgala</s>' — having limbs (<s>aṅgavat</s>). 'It sinks (<s>majjayati</s>) the sinful one' — say the etymologists (<s>Nairuktas</s>). Or 'may it come to me.' And may no overwhelming (<s>abhibhūti</s>) power anywhere find you. The <s>kapiñjala</s> (francolin partridge) cried out auspiciously when <s>Gṛtsamada</s>'s purpose arose. The following <s>ṛc</s> (verse) refers to this.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 9.5:] "Speak auspiciously from the right, speak auspiciously from the north, speak auspiciously from the east, speak auspiciously from the west, O <s>Kapiñjala</s>" — that has been explained by its literal text (<s>nigada</s>). '<s>Gṛtsamada</s>' — one who is intoxicated (<s>madana</s>) by '<s>gṛtsa</s>' (wisdom). '<s>Gṛtsa</s>' is a name for 'wise' (<s>medhāvin</s>), from '<s>gṝ</s>' (to praise), the action of praising. '<s>Mandūka</s>' (frog) — '<s>majjūka</s>' (diver), from '<s>majj</s>' (to sink/dive). Or from '<s>mad</s>' (to rejoice), the action of rejoicing; or from '<s>mand</s>' (to be satisfied), the action of satisfaction. '<s>Mandayati</s>' (it gladdens), say the grammarians. Or '<s>manda</s>' is their dwelling (<s>okas</s>).' '<s>Manda</s>' from '<s>mad</s>' (to rejoice) or '<s>mud</s>' (to be glad). The [following verse] pertains to them.

[Nirukta 9.6:] "Having lain for a year, the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> observing vows — the frogs (<s>mandūkāḥ</s>) have raised their voice, animated by <s>Parjanya</s>." Having lain for a year, the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> observing vows, having been silent [all the while]. Or the comparison may be: 'like <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> observing vows.' They raised their voice, the frogs, [their voice being] animated, pleased, by <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god). <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, desiring rain, praised <s>Parjanya</s>. The frogs rejoiced along with him. Having seen the frogs rejoicing, he praised [them]. The following <s>ṛc</s> refers to this.

[Nirukta 9.7:] "Speak forth, O <s>Mandūkī</s> (female frog); call the rain, O <s>Tādurī</s>! Swim in the middle of the lake, stretching out your four limbs" — that has been explained by its literal text. [Now regarding] dice (<s>akṣāḥ</s>): either 'they reach (<s>aśnuvate</s>) them [the players],' or 'they [the players] reach by means of them.' The [following verse] pertains to them.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 9.8:] 'The trembling [dice] of the great one delight me; born in the wind, rolling on the desert plain — like the draught of <s>Soma</s> from <s>Mūjavat</s>, the <s>Vibhīdaka</s> (dice-nut), ever wakeful, has appeared for me.' (<s>ṚV</s> 10.34.1) The trembling fruits of the great <s>Vibhīdaka</s> tree delight me. <s>Pravātejāḥ</s> (born in the wind) means <s>pravanejāḥ</s> (born in blowing). Rolling on the desert plain (<s>iriṇa</s>). <s>Iriṇa</s> means 'without debt' (<s>nirṛṇa</s>), from the root <s>ṛṇā</s> (to owe) — it becomes barren (<s>apārṇa</s>); or 'from which vegetation (<s>oṣadhi</s>) has departed.' Like the draught of <s>Soma</s> from <s>Mūjavat</s>. <s>Maujavata</s> means 'produced on <s>Mūjavat</s>.' <s>Mūjavat</s> is a mountain, [also called] <s>Muñjavat</s>. <s>Muñja</s> grass releases (<s>vimucyate</s>) the inner reed (<s>isīkā</s>). <s>Isīkā</s> is from the root <s>is</s> (to go), denoting motion. This other <s>isīkā</s> (arrow-reed) is also from the same [root]. <s>Vibhīdaka</s> is from <s>vibhedana</s> (splitting). <s>Jāgṛvi</s> (wakeful) is from <s>jāgaraṇa</s> (waking). '[It] has appeared for me' (<s>mahyam acacchadat</s>). He praises them [the dice] with the first [verse] and censures them with the subsequent ones. They declare this to be the hymn (<s>ārṣa</s>) of a seer (<s>ṛṣi</s>) ruined by dice. <s>Grāvāṇaḥ</s> (pressing-stones) [derives] from <s>han</s> (to strike), or from <s>gṛṇāti</s> (to praise), or from <s>gṛhṇāti</s> (to seize). This [verse] belongs to them:

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 9.9:] 'Let these speak forth, let us speak forth; speak a word to the pressing-stones (<s>grāvāṇaḥ</s>), to those that are speaking. When the stones (<s>adrayaḥ</s>), the mountains, swift together, bearing <s>Soma</s>, [raise] their sound and call for <s>Indra</s>.' (<s>ṚV</s> 10.94.1) Let these speak forth. Let us speak forth. Speak a word to the pressing-stones, to those that are speaking. When the stones, the mountains — worthy of respect (<s>adaranīyāḥ</s>), together, swift in action — <s>śloka</s> (sound) is from <s>śṛṇoti</s> (to hear); <s>ghoṣa</s> (call) is from <s>ghuṣyate</s> (to resound). 'You are possessed of <s>Soma</s>' — [this is one meaning]; or 'in the houses of <s>Soma</s>-possessors.' That mantra by which men are praised is called <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> (praise of men). This [verse] belongs to it:

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 9.10:] 'Unfailing praises I bring forth with inspiration — to [the king] dwelling on the <s>Sindhu</s>, who shall come into being. He who measured out a thousand pressings for me — the unhasty king, desiring fame.' (<s>ṚV</s> 8.5.37) Unfailing praises — not foolish, or not small. <s>Bāla</s> (child) subsists on strength (<s>bala</s>), for he must be maintained (<s>bhartavya</s>). Or '<s>ambā</s> (mother) is sufficient (<s>alam</s>) for him.' Or '<s>ambā</s> is his strength (<s>bala</s>).' Or <s>bāla</s> is [derived from] a negation with intervening [sounds]. 'I bring forth with <s>manīṣā</s>' — with the impulse (<s>īṣā</s>) of the mind (<s>manas</s>), [meaning] praise or wisdom. To the king dwelling upon the <s>Sindhu</s>, of the <s>Bhāvayavya</s> [dynasty], who measured out a thousand pressings (<s>savān</s>) for me. The unhasty king — or 'unhurried,' or 'not rushing.' Desiring praise (<s>praśaṃsā</s>).

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 9.11:] Through connection with sacrifice, a king obtains praise. Through connection with a king, [one obtains] implements of war. Among those, the chariot (<s>ratha</s>) comes first. <s>Ratha</s> is from the root <s>raṃh</s> (to go), denoting motion; or it may be from <s>sthira</s> (firm), by metathesis; or 'one who stands (<s>tiṣṭhati</s>) delighting (<s>ramamāṇa</s>) in it'; or from <s>rap</s> (to speak), or from <s>ras</s> (to cry out). This [verse] belongs to it:

[Nirukta 9.12:] 'O <s>Vanaspati</s> (lord of the forest), be firm-limbed; be our ally, granting safe crossing, with good heroes. You are fastened with leather straps — brace yourself! May your rider conquer what is to be conquered.' (<s>ṚV</s> 6.47.26) O <s>Vanaspati</s>, be firm-limbed, be our ally, granting safe crossing, having good heroes (<s>suvīra</s>) — excellent heroes. You are fastened with leather straps; brace yourself (<s>vīḷayasva</s>), meaning 'make firm.' May your rider conquer what is to be conquered. <s>Dundubhi</s> (war-drum) is an onomatopoeia; or 'a tree split [to make it]'; or it may be from the root <s>dundubhyat</s>, denoting a sound-action. This [verse] belongs to it:

[Nirukta 9.13:] 'Inspire the earth and also the sky; let the moving world everywhere heed your [sound]. O <s>Dundubhi</s>, together with <s>Indra</s> and the gods, drive away the enemies far and farther.' (<s>ṚV</s> 6.47.29) Inspire the earth and the sky. Let the stationary and the moving world everywhere heed your sound. O <s>Dundubhi</s>, together with <s>Indra</s> and the gods in unison (<s>sajūḥ</s>), drive away the enemies far and farther. [Next is] the <s>iṣudhi</s> (quiver) — the receptacle (<s>nidhāna</s>) of arrows (<s>iṣu</s>). This [verse] belongs to it:

[Nirukta 9.14:] 'Father of many, having many a son — he makes a rattling sound when they come together. The quiver (<s>iṣudhi</s>), with all its bands and battle-arrays, fastened on the back, conquers when set in motion.' (<s>ṚV</s> 6.75.5) Father of many, having many a son — this is said with reference to the arrows. He seems to laugh, as it were, when opened. Or it is an onomatopoeia. <s>Saṅkāḥ</s> (bands) is from <s>sac</s> (to accompany), or from <s>kir</s> (to scatter) with the prefix <s>sam</s>. 'Fastened on the back, he conquers when set in motion' — this has been explained. <s>Hastaghna</s> (arm-guard) is [so called because] it is struck on the hand (<s>haste hanyate</s>). This [verse] belongs to it:

[Nirukta 9.15:] 'Like a serpent, it encircles the arm with its coils; the arm-guard, warding off the blow of the bowstring. The <s>hastaghna</s>, knowing all courses, may the man protect the man on every side.' (<s>ṚV</s> 6.75.14) Like a serpent, it wraps around the arm with its coils, protecting from the blow of the bowstring — the arm-guard (<s>hastaghna</s>), knowing all signs of direction (<s>vayunāni</s>). <s>Pumān</s> (man) is one who has many thoughts (<s>purumanas</s>), or from <s>puṃs</s> (to nourish). <s>Abhīśu</s> (rein) has been explained. This [verse] belongs to them:

[Nirukta 9.16:] 'Standing in the chariot, he guides the swift horses forward; wherever the skilled charioteer (<s>susārathi</s>) desires [to go]. Revere the might of the reins (<s>abhīśu</s>); the traces follow the mind from behind.' (<s>ṚV</s> 10.73.10) Standing in the chariot, he guides the swift horses which are in front, wherever the skilled charioteer — the one with an excellent charioteer — desires. I honor the might of the reins. The traces (<s>raśmayaḥ</s>), being behind, follow the mind. <s>Dhanus</s> (bow) is from the root <s>dhanv</s> (to run), denoting motion, or denoting striking; arrows (<s>iṣu</s>) fly (<s>dhanvanti</s>) from it. This [verse] belongs to it:

[Nirukta 9.17:] 'With the bow, may we win cattle; with the bow, may we win the contest; with the bow, may we win fierce battles. The bow causes the enemy's displeasure; with the bow, may we conquer all the quarters.' (<s>ṚV</s> 6.75.2) — Thus that [verse] is explained as a <s>nigada</s> (plain recitation). <s>Samadaḥ</s> (battles) — [this is either] <s>samada</s>, from <s>ad</s> (to eat) [with prefix <s>sam</s>], or <s>sammada</s> from <s>mad</s> (to rejoice). <s>Jyā</s> (bowstring) is from <s>ji</s> (to conquer), or from <s>jināti</s> (to deprive), or 'it propels (<s>prajāvayati</s>) the arrows.' This [verse] belongs to it:

[Nirukta 9.18:] 'As if about to speak, she approaches the ear; embracing her dear companion [the arrow]. Like a woman, she makes a sound on the stretched bow — this bowstring, bringing [the arrow] across in battle.' (<s>ṚV</s> 6.75.3) As if about to speak, she approaches the ear, embracing the arrow like a dear companion. Like a woman, she makes a sound — on the stretched bow, this bowstring, bringing across (<s>pārayantī</s>), carrying to the other side, in battle (<s>samana</s>), in combat. <s>Iṣu</s> (arrow) is from the root <s>is</s> (to go), denoting motion, or denoting striking. This [verse] belongs to it:

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 9.19:] 'She wears the plumage of a bird; her tooth is of a deer; fastened with leather straps, she flies when released. Where men run together and scatter apart, there may the arrows (<s>iṣu</s>) grant us shelter.' (<s>ṚV</s> 6.75.11) She wears the plumage of a bird (<s>suparṇa</s>) — this is said with reference to the swift [feathered parts] of arrows. Her tooth is of deer [horn], from <s>mṛgaya</s> (to hunt); 'fastened with leather straps, she flies when released' — this has been explained. Where men run together and scatter apart, there may the arrows grant us shelter (<s>śaraṇa</s>) in battles. [Regarding] the <s>aśvājanī</s> (horse-whip): they call it <s>kaśā</s> (whip). The <s>kaśā</s> reveals (<s>prakāśayati</s>) fear to the horse; or from <s>kṛṣ</s> (to plough/drag), by vowel change. Speech (<s>vāc</s>), in turn, reveals meanings (<s>arthān</s>). [It is also] <s>khaśayā</s> — 'resting in space'; or from <s>kruś</s> (to cry out). This [verse] belongs to the horse-whip:

9.20: 'They strike their ridges; they beat upon their hind-quarters. O <s>Aśvājanī</s> (horse-whip), O wise one, urge the horses in the battles.' They strike their ridges, their haunches, their thighs. <s>Sakthi</s> (thigh) is from <s>sacati</s> (to follow) — the body is attached (<s>āsakta</s>) at it. And it strikes upon the hind-quarters. <s>Jaghana</s> (hind-quarter) is from <s>jaṅghanyati</s> (to strike repeatedly). O <s>Aśvājanī</s>, of advanced understanding, urge the horses in encounters, in skirmishes, in battles. <s>Ulūkhala</s> (mortar) — 'making wide' (<s>uru-kara</s>), or 'with upward cavity' (<s>ūrdhva-kha</s>), or <s>ūrkara</s>. 'Make it wide for me,' it said — that became the mortar. 'And this is <s>urukara</s>; they call it <s>ulūkhala</s> indirectly' — so says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Regarding it, the following [verse] occurs:
9.21: 'Though you are yoked in house after house, O little mortar, speak here most brilliantly, like a drum at a sacrifice.' Thus it has been explained as a <s>nigada</s> (ritual recitation).

9.22: <s>Vṛṣabha</s> (bull) — he rains (<s>varṣati</s>) offspring, or he exceedingly increases semen. That is the bull-action; <s>vṛṣabha</s> is from raining (<s>varṣaṇa</s>). Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

9.23: 'Making him bellow, they came upon him; they made the bull urinate in the middle of the contest. With that, <s>Mudgala</s> won in the battle a prize of hundreds and thousands of cows, well-nourished.' 'Making him bellow, they came upon him' — this has been explained. 'They made the bull urinate in the middle of the contest' — of the driving, of the racing. With that, [he won] that king <s>Sūbharva</s> (well-nourishing). <s>Bharvati</s> has the sense of eating. Or that well-nourished [prize of] a thousand cows — <s>Mudgala</s> won in the battle. <s>Pradhana</s> is a name for battle — in it wealth is scattered about. <s>Drughaṇa</s> — a wooden club (<s>druma-maya ghana</s>). In this regard they narrate the legend (<s>itihāsa</s>): the sage <s>Mudgala Bhārmyaśva</s>, having yoked a bull and a wooden club, engaging in battle, won the race. This <s>ṛc</s> is addressed to that.

body.translated_text: 9.24: 'Behold this companion of the bull, the wooden club lying in the middle of the track. With which <s>Mudgala</s> won hundreds and thousands of cows in the contests of armies.' Behold this companion yoked with the bull, the wooden club lying in the middle of the track. With which <s>Mudgala</s> won hundreds and thousands of cows in the battle-contests. <s>Pṛtanājya</s> is a name for battle — from the driving of armies, or from the conquering [of armies]. <s>Mudgala</s> — possessing beans (<s>mudga</s>); or swallowing (<s>gila</s>) beans; or swallowing intoxication; or swallowing joy. <s>Bhārmyaśva</s> — son of <s>Bhṛmyaśva</s>. <s>Bhṛmyaśva</s> — whose horses whirl (<s>bhṛmi</s>); or from nourishing horses. <s>Pitu</s> is a name for food — from <s>pāti</s> (to protect), or <s>pibati</s> (to drink), or <s>pyāyati</s> (to swell). Regarding it, the following [verse] occurs:

9.25: 'I praise that food, the sustainer of the great, of strength. By whose might <s>Trita</s> shattered the jointless <s>Vṛtra</s>.' I praise that food, the sustainer of greatness and of strength. <s>Taviṣī</s> is a name for strength, from <s>tavati</s> (to grow), with the sense of increasing. By whose [strength], <s>Trita</s>, by power, by might — <s>Trita</s>, stationed in three places, <s>Indra</s> — shattered the jointless <s>Vṛtra</s>. Rivers have been explained. Regarding them, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 9.26: 'O <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Yamunā</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Śutudrī</s>, attend to this hymn of mine, together with <s>Paruṣṇī</s>; O <s>Asikṇī</s>, with <s>Marudvṛdhā</s>, along with <s>Vitastā</s>, O <s>Ārjīkīyā</s>, listen, with <s>Susomā</s>.' O <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Yamunā</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Śutudrī</s>, <s>Paruṣṇī</s> — attend to this hymn of mine; O <s>Asikṇī</s> together with <s>Marudvṛdhā</s>, along with <s>Vitastā</s>, O <s>Ārjīkīyā</s>, listen, together with <s>Susomā</s> — this is the combined meaning. Now the word-by-word etymology: <s>Gaṅgā</s> — from going (<s>gamana</s>). <s>Yamunā</s> — 'she goes youthfully,' or 'she goes to a distant place.' <s>Sarasvatī</s> — <s>saras</s> is a name for water, from <s>sarati</s> (to flow); she who possesses that [water]. <s>Śutudrī</s> — 'flowing rapidly,' 'running swiftly,' or 'she who flows as if pushed quickly.' They call <s>Irāvatī</s> by the name <s>Paruṣṇī</s> — 'jointed,' 'shining,' 'flowing crookedly.' <s>Asikṇī</s> — 'not white,' i.e. dark (<s>asitā</s>). <s>Sita</s> is a name for the color white; its negation is <s>asita</s> (dark). <s>Marudvṛdhā</s> — all rivers [are so called], for the <s>Marut</s>s (storm gods) nourish them. <s>Vitastā</s> — 'unburned' [i.e., undiminished]; or 'greatly increased, of large banks.' <s>Ārjīkīyā</s> — they call it <s>Vipāś</s>; or 'originating in <s>Ṛjīka</s>' or 'flowing straight.' <s>Vipāś</s> — from scattering (<s>vipātana</s>), or from loosening (<s>vipāśana</s>), or from carrying away (<s>viprāpaṇa</s>). The bonds (<s>pāśā</s>) of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, who was about to die, were loosened in it — therefore it is called <s>Vipāś</s>; formerly it was [called] <s>Uruñjirā</s>. <s>Susomā</s> is <s>Sindhu</s> (the Indus), because the rivers flow abundantly into it. <s>Sindhu</s> is from <s>syandana</s> (flowing).

9.27: 'For you are indeed the waters that bring bliss; grant us food; and for great and delightful vision.' For you are indeed the waters that bring happiness; grant us food. And for great and delightful and beautiful vision. <s>Oṣadhi</s>s (herbs) — they suck (<s>dhayanti</s>) the burning element (<s>oṣat</s>); or in the heat (<s>oṣati</s>) they suck; or they suck away the burning (<s>doṣa</s>). Regarding them, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 9.28: 'O herbs, born in ancient times, three ages before the gods — I now contemplate the hundred and seven abodes of the brown ones.' O herbs, born in ancient times, three ages before the gods. I now contemplate this — of the brown ones. Brown-colored, shining, nourishing ones. Hundred and seven abodes. <s>Dhāman</s> (abode) has three [meanings]: stations, names, and births. Here, births are intended. Seven hundred are the vital points (<s>marman</s>) of a person; they place [the herbs] upon them. Night (<s>rātri</s>) has been explained. Regarding it, the following [verse] occurs. <s>Āpas</s> (waters) is from <s>āpnoti</s> (to attain/pervade). Regarding them, the following [verse] occurs:

From the seats of heaven, great one, you extend — the fierce darkness revolves from you.' You have filled, O Night, the earthly realm, with the stations of the intermediate [space]. From the seats of heaven, the great one, you extend — the fierce darkness revolves. <s>Araṇyānī</s> (forest goddess) — the wife of the forest (<s>araṇya</s>). <s>Araṇya</s> (forest) — leafless [land] beyond the village. Or it is a place of delight (<s>aramaṇa</s>). Regarding her, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 9.30: 'O <s>Araṇyānī</s>, O <s>Araṇyānī</s>, you who seem to vanish yonder — why do you not ask for the village? Does not fear seize you?' He addresses her as <s>Araṇyānī</s>. You who, O <s>Araṇyānī</s>, seem to disappear, turning away among the forests. Why do you not ask for the village? Fear does not seem to seize you. The particle <s>iva</s> [here has] the sense of surrounding fear. <s>Śraddhā</s> (faith) is from <s>śraddhāna</s> (believing/trusting). Regarding it, the following [verse] occurs:

9.31: 'With faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) is <s>Agni</s> kindled; with faith the oblation is offered. Faith we declare by our speech to be at the summit of fortune (<s>bhaga</s>).' With faith, <s>Agni</s> is well kindled. With faith, the oblation is well offered. We declare faith by our speech to be at the summit — the chief limb — of one's share of fortune. <s>Pṛthivī</s> (earth) has been explained. Regarding it, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 9.32: 'May the earth be pleasant for us, free from thorns, affording a resting place; grant us broad shelter.' May the earth be pleasant for us, free from thorns, affording a resting place. <s>Ṛkṣara</s> (thorny) — a thorn (<s>kaṇṭaka</s>), from <s>ṛcchati</s> (to go/reach). <s>Kaṇṭaka</s> (thorn) — 'lip-drinker' (<s>kaṇṭapa</s>), or from <s>kṛntati</s> (to cut), or from <s>kaṇṭati</s> (to go), with the sense of motion. It is the most protruding [thing]. Grant us shelter — may they grant shelter, broad in all directions. <s>Apvā</s> has been explained. Regarding it, the following [verse] occurs:

[Nirukta 9.33:] "Confusing their minds, seize their limbs, go forth, O <s>Apvā</s> (destructive force). Advance upon them, burn their hearts with grief; may the enemies be enveloped in blind darkness." Confusing their minds, their intellects — seize their limbs, O <s>Apvā</s>. Go forth. Advance. Burn their hearts with grief; may the enemies be enveloped in blind darkness. '<s>Agnāyī</s>' is the wife (<s>patnī</s>) of <s>Agni</s>. The [following verse] pertains to her.
[Nirukta 9.34:] "Here I invoke <s>Indrāṇī</s>, and <s>Varuṇānī</s> for well-being, and <s>Agnāyī</s> for the <s>Soma</s>-drinking" — that has been explained by its literal text (<s>nigada</s>).

[Nirukta 9.35:] Now hereafter [come] the eight deity-pairs (<s>dvandva</s>). [First:] the mortar and pestle (<s>ulūkhala-musala</s>). '<s>Ulūkhala</s>' (mortar) has been explained. '<s>Musala</s>' (pestle) — 'repeatedly moving' (<s>muhuḥ sara</s>). The [following verse] pertains to them.

[Nirukta 9.36:] "O worshipful ones, best winners of food! For you two are lifted high, like two bay horses eating food." O worshipful ones, the best sharers of food — for they are wielded on high, like two bay horses eating food. '<s>Havirdhāna</s>' (two oblation-receptacles) — the containers of oblations (<s>havisām nidhāna</s>). The [following verse] pertains to them.

[Nirukta 9.37:] "May the sacrificial gods sit in your lap, O harmless ones, here today for the <s>Soma</s>-drinking." May they sit in your lap (<s>upastha</s>), [in your] station — [you who are] 'not to be harmed' (<s>adrogdhavya</s>); the sacrificial gods, those who bring about the sacrifice, here today for the drinking of <s>Soma</s>. Heaven and Earth (<s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>) have been explained. The [following verse] pertains to them.

[Nirukta 9.38:] "May Heaven and Earth today bestow upon us this effective sacrifice that touches the sky, among the gods." May Heaven and Earth today bestow upon us this effective (<s>sādhana</s>) sacrifice, heaven-touching, among the gods. <s>Vipāś</s> and <s>Śutudrī</s> have been explained. The [following verse] pertains to them.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 9.39:] "From the lap of the mountains, eagerly, like two mares released, laughing — like two bright cows, the mothers, licking [their calves], <s>Vipāś</s> and <s>Śutudrī</s> rush with [their] milk." From the station of the mountains — the two eager ones (<s>uśatī</s>), desiring. Like two horses released — or 'two [horses] that have sunk down'; laughing (<s>hāsamānā</s>). '<s>Hāsati</s>' — [used] in the sense of competition; or 'exulting.' Like two bright, beautiful cows, the mothers, licking [each other] — <s>Vipāś</s> and <s>Śutudrī</s> rush with [their] milk. '<s>Ārtnī</s>' (the two bow-ends) — or '<s>artanī</s>'; or '<s>araṇī</s>' (the two fire-churning sticks); or '<s>arisaṇī</s>.' The [following verse] pertains to them.

[Nirukta 9.40:] "Moving together like two women of one mind, like a mother carrying her son in her lap — may they, the two <s>ārtnīs</s>, harmonizing, strike down the enemies, driving away the foes, flashing forth." Moving together like two women of one mind; like a mother carrying her son in her lap, at the station. May they strike down the enemies; the two <s>ārtnīs</s>, harmonizing, driving away the foes. '<s>Śunāsīrau</s>': '<s>Śuna</s>' is <s>Vāyu</s> (wind); '<s>śu</s>' goes in the atmosphere. '<s>Sīra</s>' is <s>Āditya</s> (the sun), from 'moving' (<s>saraṇa</s>). The [following verse] pertains to them.

[Nirukta 9.41:] "O <s>Śunāsīrau</s>, accept this utterance; whatever moisture you have created in heaven, with that sprinkle this [earth]" — that has been explained by its literal text. '<s>Devī joṣṭrī</s>' — two divine female delighters (<s>joṣayitrī</s>). [They are] Heaven and Earth, or Day and Night. '<s>Sasya</s> (crop) and <s>samā</s> (year),' says <s>Kautthakya</s>. The [following] is the directive (<s>sampraisa</s>) pertaining to them.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 9.42:] "O two divine delighters, bearers of wealth — of whom one averts evil hostilities, while the other brings desirable riches to the sacrificer — for the winning and bestowing of wealth, may they accept [the offering]. Sacrifice!" The two divine delighters (<s>joṣayitrī</s>), the two bearers of wealth (<s>vasudhitī</s>) — of whom one averts evils and hostilities; the other brings desirable riches (<s>vasūni</s>) to the sacrificer, for the winning of wealth and for the bestowing of wealth. 'Sacrifice!' is a directive (<s>sampraisa</s>). '<s>Devī ūrjāhutī</s>' — two divine ones invoked with nourishment (<s>ūrjā āhvānīyau</s>). [They are] Heaven and Earth, or Day and Night. '<s>Sasya</s> and <s>samā</s>,' says <s>Kautthakya</s>. The [following] is the directive pertaining to them.

body.translated_text: [Nirukta 9.43:] "O two divine ones invoked with nourishment — may one bring food and nourishment, may the other bring shared eating and shared drinking. May we, bestowing the new upon the old and the old upon the new — may the two <s>Ūrjāhutī</s>, nourishing, bestow that nourishment, for the winning and bestowing of wealth. May they drink. Sacrifice!" The two divine ones invoked with nourishment. One brings food and essence. The other [brings] shared eating and shared drinking. May we, bestowing the new upon the old and the old upon the new — may the two <s>Ūrjāhutī</s>, nourishing, bestow that nourishment, for the winning of wealth and for the bestowing of wealth. '<s>Vītām</s>' — may they drink, or may they desire. 'Sacrifice!' is a directive.

[Nirukta 10.1:] Now hereafter [come] the deities of the middle station (atmosphere). Among them, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) comes first. '<s>Vāyu</s>' from '<s>vā</s>' (to blow) or '<s>vī</s>' (to go), the action of going. '<s>Eter</s> (to go),' says <s>Sthaulāṣṭhīvi</s> — the '<s>va</s>'-sound is meaningless. The [following verse] pertains to him.

[Nirukta 10.2:] "Come, O <s>Vāyu</s>! Beautiful [to behold], these <s>Soma</s> draughts are prepared. Drink of them; hear our call." O <s>Vāyu</s>, come! O beautiful one, these <s>Soma</s> [draughts] are fully prepared, well-prepared. Drink of them; hear our invocation. Whom else among the atmospheric [deities] would one thus address? The next [verse] pertains to him.

[Nirukta 10.3:] "The chariot-horses, having rushed forth with strength toward <s>Indra</s> of the beautiful wheel, dashing along straight, may carry the food; and may the immortal [offering] of <s>Vāyu</s> never run out." Having rushed forth, toward <s>Indra</s> who is becoming strong — the chariot-horses of the beautiful wheel, fit for the chariot, carriers of the chariot, going straight (<s>ṛju-gāminaḥ</s>) — may they carry the food, both new and old. '<s>Śravas</s>' is a name for food — because it is heard of (<s>śrūyate</s>). And may this enjoyment of <s>Vāyu</s> never be exhausted. [This verse is] primarily about <s>Indra</s>, say some; [the mention of <s>Vāyu</s> is] a glossarial element. 'About both equally,' says another [view]. '<s>Varuṇa</s>' — from '<s>vṛ</s>' (to cover). The [following verse] pertains to him. [<s>Varuṇa</s>: in the atmosphere, from the covering of water, he is <s>Vāyu</s> himself.]

[Nirukta 10.4:] "<s>Varuṇa</s> released the downward-opening cloud-vessel (<s>kavandha</s>) into the space between heaven and earth. With it, the king of all the world moistens the earth like rain [moistens] barley." The downward-opening — '<s>Varuṇa</s>' [released] the cloud (<s>megha</s>), the '<s>kavandha</s>.' '<s>Kavana</s>' is water; it is held (<s>dhīyate</s>) in that [cloud]. Water is also called '<s>kavandha</s>.' '<s>Bandhira</s>' — in the sense of containment (<s>nibhṛtatva</s>). He releases water that is not contained, and [fills] both heaven and earth and the atmosphere with its vastness. With that, the king of all the world moistens the earth like rain [moistens] barley. The next [verse] pertains to him.

[Nirukta 10.5:] "Him I praise with the same song and with the thoughts of the fathers, with the praises of <s>Nābhāka</s> — he who, at the rising of the rivers, [is praised as] having seven sisters; he is the middle one. May the others perish at the assembly." Him I praise with the same song — with singing and praising — and with the meditative hymns of the fathers, with the praises of <s>Nābhāka</s>. <s>Nābhāka</s> was a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage); at the rising of these flowing waters, he calls [<s>Varuṇa</s>] 'having seven sisters' — with his words. He is called 'the middle one' (<s>madhyama</s>) — and it is he himself. 'May the others perish at the assembly' — may all the other enemies perish, those who hate us, of evil minds, of evil resolves. '<s>Rudra</s>' — from '<s>ru</s>' (to cry/howl); or 'he who howls (<s>rorūyamāna</s>) and runs (<s>dravati</s>)'; or from '<s>rud</s>' (to weep, to make weep). The <s>Kāṭhaka</s> [<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] says: "Because he wept (<s>arudat</s>), that is the <s>Rudra</s>-nature (<s>rudratva</s>) of <s>Rudra</s>." The <s>Hāridravika</s> [<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] says: "Because he cried (<s>arodīt</s>), that is the <s>rudratva</s> of <s>Rudra</s>." The [following verse] pertains to him.

10.6: 'These hymns to <s>Rudra</s>, firm of bow, swift of arrow, the self-sustaining god, unconquerable, overpowering, the ordainer, of sharp weapons — may <s>Bharata</s> listen to us.' These hymns to <s>Rudra</s>, firm of bow, swift of arrow, the god who possesses food, unconquerable by others, overpowering, the disposer, of sharp weapons — O <s>Bharata</s>, may he listen to us. <s>Tigma</s> (sharp) is from <s>tejas</s> (brilliance), denoting the action of vigour. <s>Āyudha</s> (weapon) is from <s>āyothana</s> (fighting). Regarding him, the following [verse] also occurs:

body.translated_text: 10.7: 'Your missile, released from heaven above, that moves across the earth — may it envelop us. You have a thousand well-spoken remedies — do not harm us in our offspring and descendants.' Your missile (<s>didyut</s>), released from heaven above, from the sky. <s>Didyut</s> (missile/lightning) is from <s>dyati</s> (to shine), or from <s>dyuti</s> (splendour), or from <s>dyotati</s> (to illuminate). It moves across the earth (<s>kṣmā</s>). <s>Kṣmā</s> means the earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>). It moves upon it, or it moves through it, or it moves causing the earth to tremble. May that [missile] envelop us protectively. You have a thousand well-spoken remedies. Do not harm us in our sons and grandsons. <s>Toka</s> (offspring) is from <s>tudyate</s> (to be struck/generated); <s>tanaya</s> (descendant) is from <s>tanoti</s> (to extend). <s>Agni</s> is also called <s>Rudra</s>. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 10.8: 'O awakener through praise, accomplish that for every person worthy of worship — a hymn to <s>Rudra</s>, splendid to behold.' <s>Jarā</s> (praise) is a <s>stuti</s> (eulogy), from <s>jarati</s> (to praise), denoting the action of praising. Know that praise. Or, be one who awakens through it. Accomplish that — do that — for the worship of each and every person. A hymn to <s>Rudra</s>, splendid to behold. [Now regarding <s>Indra</s>:] <s>Indra</s> — he who tears apart nourishment (<s>irā</s>), or who gives nourishment, or who sustains nourishment, or who holds nourishment, or who bears nourishment; or [the name derives from] <s>indu</s> (the moon/Soma drop) that flows, or <s>indu</s> that delights, or he kindles beings. It is known from the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: 'Because they kindled him with the vital breaths, that is the <s>Indra</s>-nature of <s>Indra</s>.' [The name is] from doing this — so says <s>Āgrāyaṇa</s>. From seeing this — so says <s>Aupamanyava</s>. Or from <s>indati</s>, denoting the action of sovereignty. Or: '<s>in</s>' — he who tears apart enemies, or who drives them away, and who honours the worshippers. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.9: 'You tore open the fountainhead, you released the channels; you held back the surging floods. O <s>Indra</s>, when you cleft the great mountain, you released the streams and slew the demon (<s>Dānava</s>).' You tore open the fountain (<s>utsa</s>). <s>Utsa</s> (fountain) is from <s>utsarati</s> (to rise up), or <s>utsadana</s> (to emerge), or <s>utsyandana</s> (to flow forth), or from <s>unatti</s> (to gush). You released its channels. You held back these surging, overflowing, middle-realm floods that were pressing against each other. <s>Ramnati</s> (to hold back) denotes the action of restraining, or the action of releasing. O <s>Indra</s>, when you cleft the great mountain — the cloud — you released its streams and slew the demon (<s>Dānava</s>), named from the action of giving (<s>dāna</s>). Regarding him, the following [verse] also occurs:

body.translated_text: 10.10: 'He who, as soon as born, first among the wise, a god, surrounded all the gods with his power; before whose might the two worlds trembled — he, O people, is <s>Indra</s>.' He who, being born, was the first, wise one, a god, who by his power and action surrounded the gods, encompassed them, protected them — or surpassed them. Before whose strength the heaven and earth were frightened — by the greatness of his might, by the magnitude of his strength. 'He, O people, is <s>Indra</s>' — this is the delight of the seer who has perceived the meaning, conjoined with a narrative. <s>Parjanya</s> (rain-god) — from <s>tṛp</s> (to satisfy), with the first and last [syllables] reversed. He who satisfies beings. Or, the one who conquers fully. Or, the one who generates. Or, the one who procures essences. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.11: 'He strikes down the trees and strikes the demons; the whole world fears his great weapon. Even the guiltless flees from the mighty one, when <s>Parjanya</s>, thundering, strikes down the evildoers.' He strikes down the trees. He strikes down the demons (<s>rakṣas</s>). All beings fear him because of his great weapon (<s>mahāvadha</s>), for great indeed is his weapon. Even the unoffending one flees in fear from the one who performs the action of raining, when <s>Parjanya</s>, thundering, strikes down the evildoers — those who commit sinful deeds. <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Lord of Prayer) — the protector or guardian of the great (<s>bṛhat</s>). Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.12: 'He saw the honey enclosed in rock, like a fish dwelling diminished in the water. He extracted it like a cup from a tree — <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, having broken it open with a roar.' He saw the honey enclosed by a rock-like cloud, like a fish dwelling diminished in the water. He extracted it, like a cup from a tree. <s>Camasa</s> (cup) — why [is it so called]? Because they sip (<s>camanti</s>) from it. <s>Bṛhaspati</s> [extracted it] with a roar — with sound — having broken it open. <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> (Lord of Sacred Speech) — the protector or guardian of <s>Brahman</s> (sacred speech). Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.13: '<s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> with his might pierced through the honey-streaming [cloud] that was rocky and overflowing. All the sun-seeing [rays] drank of that very [stream]; together they abundantly irrigated the fountain of waters.' [He pierced through] the one having rock, having flow, having wind — <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> with his might — with his strength — pierced through that honey-streaming [cloud]. All the rays, having the sun as their seer, drink of that very [stream]. Together they abundantly irrigate the fountain of waters — the one possessing water.

10.14: <s>Kṣetrapati</s> (Lord of the Field) — <s>kṣetra</s> (field) is from <s>kṣiyati</s> (to dwell), denoting the action of dwelling. He is its protector or guardian. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 10.15: 'With the lord of the field, as with a friend, we prosper; may he make our cows and horses thrive — may he be gracious to us in this manner.' With the lord of the field, as with a good friend, we prosper. O one who nourishes cows and horses, bring [them] to us. May he be gracious to us in this manner — through strength or through wealth. <s>Mṛḷati</s> (to be gracious) denotes the action of giving, or the action of honouring. Regarding him, the following [verse] also occurs:

body.translated_text: 10.16: 'O lord of the field, pour forth for us, like a cow [yielding] milk, a honey-laden wave. May the lords of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), like well-purified ghee dripping with honey, be gracious to us.' O lord of the field, pour forth for us a honey-laden wave, like a cow [yielding] milk. [That which is] dripping with honey, like ghee — water well-purified. May the protectors or guardians of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) be gracious to us. <s>Mṛḷayati</s> (to be gracious) denotes the action of compassion, or the action of honouring. Now, when in a common verse there is a common expression, that constitutes repetition (<s>jāmi</s>) — this is one [principle]. For example: 'honey-laden' and 'dripping with honey.' And when in the same verse-quarter there is a common expression, that is also repetition — this is another [principle]. For example: 'of golden form, he of golden appearance.' And however a distinction [is made], that is non-repetition (<s>ajāmi</s>) — this is yet another [principle]. For example: 'like frogs from water, frogs from water.' <s>Vāstospati</s> (Lord of the Dwelling) — <s>vāstu</s> (dwelling) is from <s>vasati</s> (to dwell), denoting the action of dwelling. He is its protector or guardian. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 10.17: 'O <s>Vāstospati</s>, destroyer of disease, entering into all forms — be our auspicious friend.' O <s>Vāstospati</s>, destroyer of mental afflictions, entering into all forms — be our well-pleased friend. <s>Śeva</s> is a name for happiness (<s>sukha</s>). It is from <s>śiṣyati</s> (to leave/remain). The letter 'v' is a name-forming element, a semivowel intervening [between syllables], having a secondary characteristic, with a manifested quality. <s>Śiva</s> (auspicious) is also a [related] form. Whatever form he desires, that deity he becomes. There is also the Vedic passage: '<s>Maghavān</s> (the bountiful one) assumes form after form.' <s>Vācaspati</s> (Lord of Speech) — the protector or guardian of speech (<s>vāc</s>). Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.18: 'Come back, O Lord of Speech, together with the divine mind. O Lord of Wealth, free from illness — place in me my very body.' Thus it has been explained as a <s>nigada</s> (ritual recitation). <s>Apām Napāt</s> (<s>Tanūnaptṛ</s>) has been explained. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.19: 'He who, without kindling, shines within the waters; whom the wise ones praise at the sacrifices — O <s>Apām Napāt</s>, give us honey-bearing waters, by which <s>Indra</s> has grown for heroic deeds.' He who, without kindling, shines, blazes within the waters. Whom the intelligent ones praise at the sacrifices. He, <s>Apām Napāt</s>, give honey-bearing waters for the pressing. By which <s>Indra</s> grows for heroism, for heroic action. <s>Yama</s> — from <s>yacchati</s> (to restrain). Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:
