body.translated_text: 10.20: 'Him who has gone along the great slopes, who has shown the path for the many — the son of <s>Vivasvat</s>, the gathering-place of peoples, King <s>Yama</s> — honor with oblation.' Him who has gone around, who has traveled. <s>Pravata</s> (slope), <s>udvata</s> (ascent), <s>nivata</s> (descent). <s>Avati</s> has the sense of motion (<s>gati</s>). He who shows the path to the many. The son of <s>Vivasvat</s>, the gathering-place of peoples. Honor King <s>Yama</s> with oblation. <s>Duvasyati</s> has the sense of succeeding/honoring. <s>Agni</s> too is called <s>Yama</s>. These verses address him.

body.translated_text: 10.21: 'Like an army released, she establishes fear or strength — the arrow of fierce appearance, unsheathed. <s>Yama</s>, born — honored at birth; lover of maidens, lord of wives. You traverse with her — through the animal offering, and the dwelling with the plant offering — as cows reach their stable, so may we reach that which is kindled, enriched with enjoyments.' Like a released army, she establishes fear or strength. Like the arrow of fierce appearance, unsheathed — of strong appearance, of glorious appearance, of great appearance, or of blazing appearance. '<s>Yama</s>, born, united with <s>Indra</s>' — '<s>Yama</s> [is the name] here, here [born] of the mother' — this Vedic usage also occurs. Born like <s>Yama</s> [i.e. a twin]; <s>Yama</s> who is about to be born; lover of maidens — the one who ages the maiden. Lord of wives — the protector of married women. For they are principally united through the sacrificial connection. 'The third, <s>Agni</s>, is your husband' — this Vedic usage also occurs. You traverse with her — through the animal offering of the wandering [life], and through the plant offering of the dwelling, settled [life]. As cows reach their stable, so may we attain that which is kindled, lit up with enjoyments. <s>Mitra</s> — he measures (<s>pramīti</s>) and protects (<s>trāyate</s>). Or he moves measuring. Or from <s>medayati</s> (to nourish). Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 10.22: '<s>Mitra</s> controls the peoples by speaking; <s>Mitra</s> upholds the earth and the sky. <s>Mitra</s> watches over the peoples without blinking — to <s>Mitra</s> offer the oblation rich in ghee.' <s>Mitra</s> controls the peoples, proclaiming, making sound. <s>Mitra</s> alone upholds the earth and the sky. <s>Mitra</s>, without blinking, watches over the peoples. <s>Kṛṣṭi</s> is a name for humans — they are active in works; or they have stretched-out bodies. 'To <s>Mitra</s> offer the oblation rich in ghee' — this has been explained. <s>Juhoti</s> (to offer) has the sense of giving. <s>Ka</s> — [means] desiring, or striding, or pleasant. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 10.23: '<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (Golden Embryo) arose in the beginning; born, he was the one lord of created beings. He upheld the earth and this sky — to which god shall we offer oblation?' <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — the embryo is golden (<s>hiraṇyamaya</s>); or the one whose embryo is golden. <s>Garbha</s> (embryo) is from <s>gṛbh</s> (to seize), in the sense of grasping. Or it 'swallows' (<s>girati</s>) impurities. For when a woman grasps qualities, and qualities are grasped in her, then the embryo comes to be. He came into being in the beginning. Born, he became the one lord of created beings. He upholds the earth and the sky. 'To which god (<s>ka</s>) shall we offer oblation?' — this has been explained. <s>Vidhati</s> (to worship) has the sense of giving. <s>Sarasvat</s> has been explained. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:
10.24: 'O <s>Sarasvat</s>, your waves, honey-bearing, dripping with ghee — with them be our protector.' Thus it has been explained as a <s>nigada</s> (ritual recitation).

body.translated_text: 10.26: '<s>Viśvakarman</s>, of expansive mind, the encompasser, the establisher, the ordainer, and the supreme seer — their desirable things, delighting together with waters [or food], where they say the seven sages [stars] are beyond which is the one [sun].' <s>Viśvakarman</s> — of expansive mind, all-pervading, both the establisher and the ordainer, and the supreme seer of beings. Their [desirable things] — wished for, or desired, or gone, or attained, or thought, or bent. They delight together with the waters, where these seven sage-stars [are]. Beyond them is the sun. They become one in him — this is the cosmic interpretation (<s>adhidaivata</s>). The personal interpretation (<s>adhyātma</s>): <s>Viśvakarman</s> — of expansive mind, all-pervading, both the establisher and the ordainer, and the supreme revealer of the sense-organs. Their [desirable things] — wished for, or desired, or gone, or attained, or thought, or bent. They delight together with food, where these seven sage-faculties, the sense-organs [are]. Beyond them is the <s>Ātman</s> (Self). They become one in it — thus he describes the course of the Self. In this regard they narrate the legend: <s>Viśvakarman Bhauvana</s> offered all beings in the universal sacrifice (<s>Sarvamedha</s>). This <s>ṛc</s> addresses that: 'He who offered all these beings [as oblations].' The next [verse] is for further explanation.

10.27: 'O <s>Viśvakarman</s>, increasing through oblation, sacrifice to the earth and sky yourself. May the other peoples round about be confounded — may a generous patron be ours here.' O <s>Viśvakarman</s>, increasing through oblation, sacrifice to the earth and sky yourself. May the other peoples — the rivals — round about be confounded. May a generous, renowned patron be ours here. <s>Tārkṣya</s> — <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> has been explained. He dwells (<s>kṣiyati</s>) in the traversed atmosphere. He swiftly protects [or flows to] the goal; or from <s>aśnoti</s> (to attain). Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.28: 'We invoke here that prize-winning stallion, god-impelled, mighty, crossing beyond chariots, of unharmed wheel-rim, army-conquering, swift — <s>Tārkṣya</s>, for our welfare.' That stallion, abundantly food-possessing. <s>Jūti</s> means movement, or affection. God-impelled — god-moved, or god-pleased. The mighty one, the rescuer of chariots, of unharmed rim, army-conquering, swift — for welfare, we invoke <s>Tārkṣya</s> here. Who else would speak of the atmospheric [deity] thus? Regarding him, the following other [verse] occurs:

10.29: 'He who by his might at once stretched out over the five peoples like the sun with its light — his speed wins thousands, wins hundreds; they cannot stop him, like a young maiden, like an arrow of reed.' He who by his might, by his strength, at once stretches out the waters like the sun with its light, over the five human races. His speed wins thousands, wins hundreds. They cannot stop it, like a swift maiden-arrow made of reed. <s>Manyu</s> (wrath) is from <s>manyati</s> (to be wrathful), with the sense of blazing; or of anger; or of striking. Arrows are wrathful from it. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.30: "Mounting the same chariot with you, O <s>Manyu</s>, breaking [the foes], rejoicing, unconquered, accompanied by <s>Maruts</s>, sharpening sharp-arrowed weapons, let the men go forth, having the form of <s>Agni</s>."
10.30: Mounting the same chariot with you, O <s>Manyu</s>, breaking [foes], with names of joy, unconquered, accompanied by <s>Maruts</s>, sharpening their sharp-arrowed weapons, let the men go forth, having the form of <s>Agni</s>, performing the deeds of <s>Agni</s>.
10.30: Or, "armored ones wearing cuirasses."
10.30: <s>Dadhikrā</s> has been explained.
10.30: Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.31: "<s>Dadhikrā</s> with his might extended over the five peoples like <s>Sūrya</s> with his light. The winner of thousands, winner of hundreds, the swift prize-winning steed — may he fill these our words with sweetness."
10.31: <s>Dadhikrā</s> extends with his might, with strength, over the waters — like <s>Sūrya</s> with light — over the five human races.
10.31: The winner of thousands, winner of hundreds, the swift one, the prize-winning, rapid steed — may he fill our words, these utterances, with <s>madhu</s> (sweetness/water).
10.31: <s>Madhu</s> is from the root <s>dham</s>, inverted.
10.31: <s>Savitā</s> is the impeller of everything.
10.31: Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.33: "O <s>Hiraṇyastūpa</s>, O <s>Savitṛ</s>, just as the descendant of <s>Aṅgiras</s> offered, in this contest for food — so I, praising and venerating you for protection, watch over [you] like a portion of <s>Soma</s>."

10.33: so I, praising and venerating you for protection, watch over [you] like a portion of <s>Soma</s>.

body.translated_text:
10.34: "The divine <s>Tvaṣṭā</s>, all-formed, nourished [all]; he generated offspring in manifold ways. All these beings are his; great is the one lordship (<s>asurattva</s>) of the gods."
10.34: The divine <s>Tvaṣṭā</s>, having all forms, nourishes offspring by providing nourishment.
10.34: And he generates them in manifold ways.
10.34: All these beings, these waters, are his.
10.34: And great is his one <s>asurattva</s> (lordship) over the gods — namely, the state of having progeny, or the state of having lineage.
10.34: Or, <s>asur</s> is a name for wisdom — he casts away afflictions, and things of value are stored in it.
10.34: <s>Asurattva</s> has initial elision.

10.35: "May <s>Vāta</s> blow medicines to us, auspicious and delightful for our hearts; may he extend our lifespans."
10.35: May <s>Vāta</s> blow medicines, auspicious and delightful, for our hearts.
10.35: And may he extend our lifespans.
10.35: <s>Agni</s> has been explained.
10.35: Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.36: "You are summoned to this pleasing sacrifice for the drinking of <s>Soma</s>; O <s>Agni</s>, come with the <s>Maruts</s>."
10.36: You are summoned to that pleasing sacrifice for the drinking of <s>Soma</s>.
10.36: O <s>Agni</s>, come together with the <s>Maruts</s>.
10.36: Who else from the middle [region] would one speak of thus?
10.36: Regarding him, this other [verse] also occurs:

10.37: "I release for you the <s>Soma</s>-sweetness for the first drinking; O <s>Agni</s>, come with the <s>Maruts</s>."
10.37: <s>Vena</s> is from the root <s>ven</s>, denoting an action of desire.

10.40: And subject us to the sight of <s>Sūrya</s>.

10.40: With <s>ghṛta</s>, strengthen yourself, your body.

10.40: Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.41: "For many are the nourishments of <s>Ṛta</s>; the thought of <s>Ṛta</s> destroys what is crooked. The fame of <s>Ṛta</s> pierced the deaf one's ears, awakening, shining, of the living being."
10.41: For many are the nourishments of <s>Ṛta</s>.

10.41: The fame of <s>Ṛta</s> pierces even the ears of the deaf.

10.41: Awakening the ears, shining, of <s>āyu</s> — of the living being, of man.
10.41: Or of light, or of water.

10.42: "I would proclaim that for the future, for <s>Indu</s> — like one worthy of invocation, he who, possessing arrows, shakes [our] hymns; the slayer of <s>Rakṣas</s> shakes [our] hymns. He himself shall conquer with weapons those who revile us, [and] evil thought. Let the evil-speaking one flow away, and thereafter let the insignificant one flow away like something small."
10.42: I proclaim that to <s>Indu</s> for the future — like one worthy of invocation, he who, possessing arrows (food/desires), shakes our hymns.
10.42: The slayer of <s>Rakṣas</s> shakes [them] with his strength.
10.42: He himself shall conquer with weapons those who revile us, [and] evil thought.
10.42: Let the evil-speaking one flow away.
10.42: And thereafter let [him] flow away like something small and insignificant.
10.42: In repetition, they consider the meaning to be intensified,
10.42: as in "Oh, what a sight! Oh, what a sight!"
10.42: Such is the style of <s>Paruccepa</s>.
10.42: <s>Paruccepa</s> is a seer — one having a jointed tail, or one who has a tail at every joint.
10.42: Thus these twenty-seven deity names have been enumerated — those sharing hymns and those sharing oblations.
10.42: Among those, these do not share oblations: <s>Vena</s>, <s>Asunīti</s>, <s>Ṛta</s>, <s>Indu</s>.
10.42: <s>Prajāpati</s> is the protector or guardian of creatures.
10.42: Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.43: "O <s>Prajāpati</s>, no other than you has encompassed all these created beings. May that for which, desiring, we offer to you, be ours; may we be lords of wealth."
10.43: O <s>Prajāpati</s>, no other than you has encompassed all these created beings.
10.43: May that for which, desiring, we offer to you, be ours.
10.43: May we be lords of wealth — thus the benediction.
10.43: <s>Ahi</s> (serpent) has been explained.
10.43: Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.44: 'You praise with hymns the serpent born in the waters, sitting at the bottom of the rivers, in the waters.' You praise with hymns the serpent born in the waters, sitting at the bottom of the rivers, in the waters. <s>Budhna</s> (bottom) is the atmosphere; the waters are bound and held in it. This other <s>budhna</s> [meaning foundation] also [derives] from the same — the vital breaths are bound and held in it. The serpent (<s>Ahi</s>) that is <s>Budhnya</s> (of the deep) — <s>budhna</s> is the atmosphere, which is his dwelling. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.45: 'May <s>Ahi Budhnya</s> (serpent of the deep) not place us in anger; may the sacrifice of this truthful one not go astray.' May <s>Ahi Budhnya</s> not place us in anger. May the sacrifice of this lover of truth not fail. <s>Suparṇa</s> (well-winged eagle) has been explained. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 10.46: 'The one <s>Suparṇa</s> (eagle) entered the ocean; he surveys this entire world. With a simple mind I saw him from nearby — the mother licks him, and he licks the mother.' The one eagle, he enters the ocean. He surveys all these beings. With a simple mind I saw him from nearby — this is the joy of the sage who has seen the truth, connected with the narrative (<s>ākhyāna</s>). The mother licks him — this is the intermediate speech (<s>vāc</s>). And he licks the mother. <s>Purūravas</s> — he cries out (<s>rorūyate</s>) abundantly. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

10.47: 'When he was born, the divine women sat beside him; and the self-moving rivers nourished him. When the gods nourished you, O <s>Purūravas</s>, for great delight, for the slaying of the <s>Dasyu</s>s.' The divine women sat beside him when he was born — <s>gnā</s> means waters (from going), or wives of the gods. And the rivers nourished him, self-moving. And when, O <s>Purūravas</s>, the gods, the gods nourished you for great delight, for the delightful battle, and for the slaying of the <s>Dasyu</s>s.

body.translated_text: 11.2: 'Having taken it, the eagle brought the <s>Soma</s>, a thousand pressings and ten thousand at once. There the generous one abandoned the enemies — in the intoxication of <s>Soma</s>, the wise one [overcame] the foolish.' Having taken it, the eagle brought the <s>Soma</s>. A thousand pressings and ten thousand at once — intending a thousand-fold pressing. There, ten thousand are <s>Soma</s> drinks. Or by connection, ten thousand are the gifts (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>). There the generous one abandoned the enemies — or the non-givers. In the intoxication of <s>Soma</s>, the wise one [overcame] the foolish. He is praised both in the <s>Indra</s> hymn and through the drinking of <s>Soma</s>. Therefore they consider [him to be] <s>Indra</s>. The herb <s>Soma</s> is from <s>sunoti</s> (to press), because they press it. Its <s>Naighaṇṭuka</s> (lexicographic) usage is extensive. It is primarily [treated as] something wondrous. We shall cite examples from its <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses].

11.3: 'Flow, O <s>Soma</s>, in the sweetest, most intoxicating stream, pressed for <s>Indra</s> to drink.' Thus it has been explained as a <s>nigada</s> (ritual recitation). Now this other [verse] pertains either to the moon or to this [<s>Soma</s> plant]:

body.translated_text: 11.4: 'One thinks one has drunk <s>Soma</s> when they crush the herb; the <s>Soma</s> that the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s know — no one tastes of that.' One thinks one has drunk <s>Soma</s> when they crush the herb — this refers to the improperly pressed, non-<s>Soma</s>. The <s>Soma</s> that the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s know — no non-sacrificer tastes of that — this is the ritual interpretation (<s>adhiyajña</s>). Now the cosmic interpretation (<s>adhidaivata</s>): one thinks one has drunk <s>Soma</s> when they crush the herb — this refers to the <s>Yajus</s>-pressed non-<s>Soma</s>. The <s>Soma</s> that the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s know — the moon. No non-deity tastes of that. Now this other [verse] pertains either to the moon or to this [<s>Soma</s>]:

body.translated_text: 11.5: 'When the gods drink you, you fill up again. <s>Vāyu</s> is the protector of <s>Soma</s>; the month is the shape of the years.' When the gods drink you, you fill up again — intending the <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> [cups]; [the <s>Soma</s>s that have been filled are called <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s>s in the <s>Śastra</s>s]; or the bright and dark fortnights. <s>Vāyu</s> is the protector of <s>Soma</s> — he calls <s>Vāyu</s> its protector, through association or through carrying away the essence. The month is the shape (<s>ākṛti</s>) of the years — <s>Soma</s> [is distinguished] by particular forms, whether as herb or as moon. The moon (<s>Candramā</s>) — it moves (<s>dramati</s>) shining (<s>cāyan</s>); or it has a shining measure (<s>cāndra māna</s>). <s>Candra</s> (shining) is from <s>candati</s> (to shine), with the sense of radiance. <s>Candana</s> (sandalwood) is also [derived] from this. [Or:] it flows beautifully (<s>cāru dravati</s>). Or it flows long (<s>ciram dravati</s>). Or from <s>cam</s> first; or <s>cāru</s> from <s>ruc</s> (to shine) reversed. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

11.6: 'Ever new, being born, he goes as the banner of the days, at the forefront of the dawns. Coming, he apportions shares to the gods; the moon extends long life.' Ever new, being born — intending the beginning of the bright fortnight. The banner of the days, going at the forefront of the dawns — intending the end of the dark fortnight. The second quarter has the sun as its deity, according to some. Coming, he apportions shares to the gods — intending the fortnightly sacrifice. The moon extends long life. <s>Mṛtyu</s> (death) — 'he causes to die' (<s>mārayati</s>). Or 'he dislodges the dead' — so says <s>Śatabala Ālakṣa Maudgalya</s>. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

11.7: 'Go far away, O Death, by your own path, which is different from the path of the gods. I speak to you who have eyes and ears — do not harm our offspring or our heroes.' (Go far, O Death; go steadily, O Death; go away, O Death; it has been told to you, O Death. He dislodges the dead.) [<s>Mṛtyu</s>] is from <s>mad</s> (to be intoxicated) or <s>mud</s> (to be glad). Regarding them, the following [verse] occurs: ('The fierce, rushing together, of the vigorous ones — O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the drinker of pressed [<s>Soma</s>] rescues you; that which is placed against the mortal — you are angry at the arrow-string of <s>Kṛśānu</s>.')
11.8: Thus it has been explained by recitation. <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (belonging to all men) has been explained. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

11.9: 'Praise forth for the great one, rejoicing in the food, sing to <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the all-pervading. Of <s>Indra</s>, whose easily-invoked might is great, whose fame and manly strength — heaven and earth attend upon him.' Praise forth, you all, a hymn to the great one, the giver of food, rejoicing — or being praised, or resounding — to <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the one all-pervading. Of <s>Indra</s>, whose delight is a greatly easy might, and whose hearable fame is great, and whose manly strength — the strength bowed to by men. Heaven and earth attend upon you. Who else but the atmospheric [deity] would be spoken of thus? Regarding him, the following other [verse] occurs: 'The immortal light shining upward for all people — <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, has risen.'

11.10: He has raised up the immortal light for all people — <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the divine <s>Savitṛ</s>. <s>Dhātṛ</s> (Establisher) — the establisher and ordainer of all. Regarding him, the following [verse] occurs:

11.11: 'May <s>Dhātṛ</s> grant to the worshipper an advanced, imperishable livelihood. May we obtain the gracious thought of the god whose law is truth.' May <s>Dhātṛ</s> grant to the one who has given — an advanced livelihood, undiminished. May we obtain the gracious thought — the unfading thought — of the god whose law is truth. <s>Vidhātṛ</s> and <s>Dhātṛ</s> have been explained. This is his occurrence in a verse addressed to many deities. [The occurrence alongside other deities in a multi-deity verse.]

11.12: 'In the ordinance of King <s>Soma</s>, of <s>Varuṇa</s>, in the favor and shelter of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, in your praise, O <s>Maghavan</s> (bountiful one), O <s>Dhātar</s> (Establisher), O <s>Vidhātar</s> (Disposer), today I have drunk from the <s>kalaśa</s> (vessel).' That is, impelled by these deities, I have drunk from the <s>Soma</s> vessels. Why is it called <s>kalaśa</s>? Because <s>kalās</s> (parts, measures) lie (<s>śerate</s>) in it. Both <s>kali</s> and <s>kalā</s> are from the root <s>kir</s> (to scatter) — they are scattered measures.
11.13: Now, from here [we treat] the deity groups of the middle station (<s>madhyasthāna</s>). Among them, the <s>Maruts</s> come first.

body.translated_text: 11.14: 'Come, O <s>Maruts</s>, with your lightning-bearing, bright-rayed chariots, equipped with spears and with horse-winged [vehicles]; with the most abundant food, fly to us like birds, O ones of wondrous power.' [Commentary:] With lightning-bearing, bright-rayed — <s>svarka</s> means either 'self-moving' (<s>svañcana</s>), or 'self-shining' (<s>svarcana</s>), or 'having their own splendor' (<s>svarcis</s>). Come with [your] chariots. Equipped with spears and horse-winged, that is, horse-swift. And with the most abundant food, fly to us like birds. <s>Sumāyāḥ</s> means either 'of beautiful deeds' or 'of beautiful wisdom.' The <s>Rudrās</s> have been explained [previously]. The following [verse] pertains to them:

11.15: 'Come, O <s>Rudrās</s>, accompanied by <s>Indra</s>, united together, with golden chariots, for our welfare. This hymn from us delights you, like a spring from heaven for one who thirsts for water.' Come, O <s>Rudrās</s>, united with <s>Indra</s>, for welfare, for [sacred] action. This hymn from us also pleases you, like a heavenly spring for one who thirsts for water. <s>Tṛṣṇaj</s> is from <s>tṛṣyati</s> (to thirst); <s>udanyu</s> is from <s>udanyati</s> (to desire water). The <s>Ṛbhus</s> [are so called] either because they shine widely (<s>uru bhānti</s>), or because they shine with <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order), or because they exist through <s>ṛta</s>. The following [verse] pertains to them:

11.16: 'Having accomplished [great deeds], with swiftness, praisers, though mortals, they attained immortality — the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, sons of <s>Sudhanvan</s>, sun-eyed; in a year they were united with [divine] works.' Having performed their works with speed, speakers of wisdom or the wise ones, though being mortals, they attained immortality — the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, sons of <s>Sudhanvan</s>. <s>Sūracakṣas</s> means either 'renowned by the sun' or 'having the wisdom of the sun.' In a year they were united with works, that is, with [sacred] deeds. <s>Ṛbhu</s>, <s>Vibhvan</s>, and <s>Vāja</s> — these three were the sons of <s>Sudhanvan</s> the <s>Āṅgirasa</s>. Among them, numerous Vedic citations occur for the first and the last, but not for the middle one. Thus, by the plural form of <s>Ṛbhu</s> and by the praise of the <s>camasa</s> (cup), there are many hymns in the decades [of the <s>Ṛgveda</s>]. The rays of the sun are also called <s>Ṛbhus</s>. 'That which you slept in the house of <s>Agohya</s> (the Unconcealed one) — that, O <s>Ṛbhus</s>, you do not follow today.' <s>Agohya</s> is the sun (<s>Āditya</s>), the one who cannot be concealed; that which you slept in his house — as long as you were there, you were not here. The <s>Aṅgirasas</s> have been explained [previously]. The following [verse] pertains to them:

11.17: 'Of varied forms, such seers, of profound insight — they, the sons of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, they were born from <s>Agni</s>.' Of many forms, [they are] seers. They are either of profound deeds or of profound wisdom. They are the sons of <s>Aṅgiras</s>. They were born from <s>Agni</s> — thus they are of fiery origin. The <s>Pitṛs</s> (Fathers) have been explained [previously]. The following [verse] pertains to them:

body.translated_text: 11.18: 'May the lower ones arise, may the upper ones arise, may the middle <s>Pitṛs</s> (Fathers), worthy of <s>Soma</s>, arise — those who have gone to the life-breath, free from enemies, knowers of <s>ṛta</s> (truth) — may those Fathers help us at the invocations.' May the lower ones arise, may the upper ones arise, may the middle Fathers, worthy of <s>Soma</s>, partakers of <s>Soma</s>, arise — those who followed the <s>asu</s> (life-breath). <s>Avṛka</s> means without enemies, or knowers of truth, or knowers of sacrifice. May those Fathers come to us at the calls. They say <s>Yama</s> belongs to the middle station; therefore they consider the Fathers to be of the middle station. The <s>Aṅgirasas</s> have been explained. The <s>Pitṛs</s> have been explained. The <s>Bhṛgus</s> have been explained. The <s>Atharvans</s> are those who possess steadfastness (<s>athana</s>). <s>Tharvati</s> is an action of movement (<s>carti karman</s>); <s>a-</s> is its negation [i.e., steadfastness]. The following [verse] is common to them all:

11.19: 'The <s>Aṅgirasas</s> are our Fathers, the <s>Navagvas</s>, the <s>Atharvans</s>, the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, worthy of <s>Soma</s> — may we be in the good will of those worthy of sacrifice, and in their auspicious benevolence.' The <s>Aṅgirasas</s> are our Fathers, the <s>Navagvas</s> — those of nine paths, or those of newly-led paths. The <s>Atharvans</s>, the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, worthy of <s>Soma</s>, partakers of <s>Soma</s>. May we be in their good will, in their auspicious thought, of those worthy of sacrifice. And may we be in their auspicious, delightful, share-worthy, benevolent mind. [These are] the deity group of the middle station, according to the etymologists (<s>Nairuktāḥ</s>). [They are] Fathers, according to tradition (<s>ākhyāna</s>). Moreover, the <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) are also praised [in the Veda]:

11.20: 'Like the expanse of the sun is their light, like the ocean is their profound greatness, like the swiftness of the wind — no other praise is sufficient to reach you.' Thus it is. The <s>Āptyas</s> are from the root <s>āp</s> (to obtain). The following passage concerning them occurs in a verse belonging to <s>Indra</s>:

11.21: 'I would praise the many-formed one, the most <s>Ṛbhu</s>-like, the most unyielding, the <s>Āptya</s>, the most <s>Āptya</s> among the <s>Āptyas</s>. He manifests by his might the seven givers; he surpasses many measures.' [This means:] The one to be praised, of many forms, widely extended, most powerful, the one most to be attained among those to be attained. He who by his might (<s>śavas</s>), by his strength, [subdues] the seven givers — or the seven <s>Dānavas</s> (demons). He surpasses many measures. <s>Sākṣati</s> means 'he attains' — it is a word denoting action.
11.22: Now, from here [we treat] the females of the middle station. Among them, <s>Aditi</s> comes first. <s>Aditi</s> has been explained [previously]. The following [verse] pertains to her:

body.translated_text: 11.23: 'In the birth and ordinance of <s>Dakṣa</s>, O <s>Aditi</s>, you serve the two kings <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>. <s>Aryaman</s>, of unobstructed path, of many chariots; the seven-<s>hotṛ</s> in births of varied forms.' In the birth and rite of <s>Dakṣa</s>, in the work [of sacrifice], you serve the two kings <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>. <s>Vivāsati</s> means service; as in 'she serves the one possessing oblations.' Or it is from the root <s>āś</s> (to pervade). <s>Atūrtapanthā</s> means one whose path is unhurried. <s>Aryaman</s>, the <s>Āditya</s> (solar deity), of many chariots, restrains enemies. The seven-<s>hotṛ</s> — seven rays bring essences (<s>rasa</s>) to him. Or, seven <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) praise him. In births of varied forms, that is, in works, in risings of dissimilar forms. They say the sun (<s>Āditya</s>) is <s>Dakṣa</s>, and he is praised in the midst of the <s>Ādityas</s>. <s>Aditi</s> is the daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s> (<s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s>). How then would it be fitting — they would be of the same birth? Or rather, by the law of the gods, they would be of mutual birth, of mutual origin. <s>Agni</s> is also called <s>Aditi</s>. The following [verse] pertains to him:

11.24: 'To whom you give good wealth, O sinless <s>Aditi</s>, [you who are] all-pervading — whom you impel with auspicious might, may we be [blessed] with offspring-rich bounty.' To whom you give good wealth, sinlessness means freedom from transgression, O <s>Aditi</s>, in all extensions of action. <s>Āgas</s> (sin) is from the prior [form] of the root <s>gam</s> (to go). <s>Enas</s> (guilt) is from the root <s>i</s> (to go). <s>Kilbiṣa</s> (offense) is that which splits (<s>bhid</s>) good action, or which splits one's fame. Whom you impel with auspicious might, with strength, and with offspring-rich bounty, with wealth — may we be here. <s>Saramā</s> is from <s>saraṇa</s> (movement). The following [verse] pertains to her:

body.translated_text: 11.25: 'Desiring what did <s>Saramā</s> come hither? For the path is long, wandering with those who go far. What was your errand to us? What was the night-fever? How did you cross the waters of the <s>Rasā</s>?' Desiring what did <s>Saramā</s> come here? For the path is long. <s>Jaguri</s> (wandering) is from <s>jaṅgamyate</s> (to go about). Attended upon by those going afar. What purpose-placing was there for you among us? What was the <s>paritakman</s> (night-fever)? <s>Paritakmyā</s> is night — <s>takman</s> (fever) goes around it. <s>Takman</s> is a name for heat, from <s>takata</s> (being hot). 'How did you cross the waters of the <s>Rasā</s>?' <s>Rasā</s> is a river, from <s>rasati</s> (to sound), a word denoting sound. Or, 'How [did you cross] those waters, the <s>rasā</s>s (essences)?' The narrative is that the divine dog (<s>deva-śunī</s>), sent by <s>Indra</s>, encountered the <s>Paṇi</s>s, the <s>Asura</s>s. <s>Sarasvatī</s> has been explained. Regarding her, the following [verse] occurs:

11.26: '<s>Sarasvatī</s>, the purifying one, rich in food, abounding in nourishment, may she attend to the sacrifice, she whose wealth is action.' Purifying for us is <s>Sarasvatī</s>. Rich in food, abounding in nourishment. May she attend to the sacrifice — <s>dhiyāvasu</s> means one whose wealth is action. Regarding her, the following other [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 11.27: '<s>Sarasvatī</s> makes manifest the great flood by her beacon; she illumines all thoughts.' <s>Sarasvatī</s> makes known, causes to understand, the great flood — by her beacon, by action, or by wisdom. And she illumines all these forms of knowledge. <s>Vāc</s> (Speech) is employed in the sense of meaning. Therefore they consider her to be the intermediate <s>Vāc</s> (Speech). <s>Vāc</s> has been explained. Regarding her, the following [verse] occurs:

11.28: 'When <s>Vāc</s> (Speech) speaks things incomprehensible, the queen of the gods sat down, delightful; she milked forth nourishment and waters in four [streams] — where has her highest [part] gone?' When <s>Vāc</s> speaks things unknown, incomprehensible, the queen of the gods sat down, delightful, intoxicating; she milked forth nourishment and waters in the four directions. 'Where has her highest [part] gone?' — either that which goes to the earth, or that which the rays of the sun carry away. Regarding her, the following other [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 11.29: 'The gods generated the divine <s>Vāc</s> (Speech); animals of all forms speak her. May she, the cow, the <s>Vāc</s>, well-praised, milking nourishment and delight, come to us.' The gods generated the divine <s>Vāc</s>. Animals of all forms speak her — both those with articulate speech and those with inarticulate speech. May she, delighting, milking food and essence, the cow <s>Vāc</s>, come to us, well-praised. <s>Anumatī</s> and <s>Rākā</s> are wives of the gods, according to the etymologists (<s>Nairuktā</s>s). They are the full moon days, according to the ritualists (<s>Yājñikā</s>s). 'The earlier full moon day is <s>Anumatī</s>, the later one is <s>Rākā</s>' — thus it is known. <s>Anumatī</s> is from <s>anumana</s> (approval, assent). Regarding her, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 11.30-31: 'Approve of us, O <s>Anumatī</s>; grant us happiness. Impel us toward purpose and skill; extend our lifespans.' Approve, O <s>Anumatī</s>. Grant us happiness and food; bestow offspring upon us and increase our life. <s>Rākā</s> is from <s>rāti</s> (to give), with the sense of giving. Regarding her, the following [verse] occurs: '<s>Rākā</s>, easily invoked, well-praised, I call upon; may the fortunate one hear us, may she perceive of her own accord. May she sew with an unbreaking needle; may she give a hero, a hundredfold giver, worthy of praise.' 11.31: <s>Rākā</s>, easily invoked, well-praised, I call upon. May the fortunate one hear us. May she perceive of her own accord. May she sew the work of procreation with a needle that does not break. <s>Sūcī</s> (needle) is from <s>sīvyati</s> (to sew). May she give a hero, a hundredfold giver, worthy of praise — worthy of being spoken of with praise. <s>Sinīvālī</s> and <s>Kuhū</s> are wives of the gods, according to the etymologists (<s>Nairuktā</s>s). They are the new moon days, according to the ritualists (<s>Yājñikā</s>s). 'The earlier new moon day is <s>Sinīvālī</s>, the later one is <s>Kuhū</s>' — thus it is known. <s>Sinīvālī</s>: <s>sina</s> is food; she nourishes (<s>sināti</s>) beings. <s>Vāla</s> is a joint, from <s>vṛṇoti</s> (to cover); in that [joint] she is possessed of food. Or she is possessed of hair (<s>vālinī</s>). Or because in her, due to [the moon's] slenderness, the moon is to be perceived only by its sliver (<s>vāla</s>). Regarding her, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text: 11.32: 'O <s>Sinīvālī</s>, broad-tressed one, you who are the sister of the gods, accept the offering that has been made; O goddess, grant us offspring.' O <s>Sinīvālī</s>, broad-hipped one — <s>stuka</s> is a cluster, from <s>styāyati</s> (to congeal, to mass together); broad in tresses of hair, or broadly praised. You who are the sister of the gods — <s>svasā</s> (sister) is 'good thrower'; or she who sits among her own. Accept the offered oblation. And, O goddess, grant us offspring. <s>Kuhū</s> is from <s>gūhati</s> (to conceal). Or 'where did she go?' Or 'where, being present, is she invoked?' Or 'where does she offer the oblation that has been offered?' Regarding her, the following [verse] occurs:

11.33: 'I invoke <s>Kuhū</s>, of good conduct, of known deeds, easily invoked, at this sacrifice. May she grant us the fame of our forefathers; to you, O goddess, we would offer with oblation.' I invoke <s>Kuhū</s>, of good conduct, of known deeds, easily invoked, at this sacrifice. May she grant us the fame of our forefathers — to you, O goddess, we would offer with oblation. Or the ancestral wealth. Or the ancestral glory. 'To you, O goddess, we would offer with oblation' — this has been explained. <s>Yamī</s> has been explained. Regarding her, the following [verse] occurs:

11.34: 'Surely another [will embrace] you, O <s>Yamī</s>, and another you — as a creeper [embraces] a tree. May you desire his mind, or he yours; make a fair and auspicious compact.' Indeed another [will embrace] you, O <s>Yamī</s>, and another will embrace you, as a creeper [embraces] a tree. Either desire his mind, or he yours. Make a compact by placing [your hearts together], a fair and auspicious one (<s>subhadrā</s>, having good fortune). The narrative is that <s>Yamī</s> desired <s>Yama</s>, and he rejected her.
11.35: <s>Urvaśī</s> has been explained. Regarding her, the following [verse] occurs:

11.36: 'She who, falling like lightning, flashed, bearing my desired watery [gifts] — a manly, well-born one was born from the waters; may <s>Urvaśī</s> extend long life.' She who, falling like lightning, shone forth, bearing my desired watery [gifts] of the atmospheric realm — when this [child] would be born from the waters. <s>Narya</s> means human, beneficial to men, or offspring of men. <s>Sujāta</s> means very well-born. Then <s>Urvaśī</s> extends long life. <s>Pṛthivī</s> (Earth) has been explained. Regarding her, the following [verse] occurs:

11.37: 'Truly, O <s>Pṛthivī</s>, you bear the breaking of the mountains; you set the earth in motion with slopes, with greatness, O great one.' Truly you bear the breaking, splitting, and piercing force of the mountains and clouds, O <s>Pṛthivī</s>. You set in motion the earth with its slopes, with greatness, O great one — or, 'abounding in waters.' <s>Indrāṇī</s> is the wife of <s>Indra</s>. Regarding her, the following [verse] occurs:

11.38: 'Among these women I have heard <s>Indrāṇī</s> is the most fortunate, for never does her husband die of old age — <s>Indra</s> is supreme over all.' Among these women I have heard <s>Indrāṇī</s> is the most fortunate. For not even in the latest age does her husband die of old age. We say this of <s>Indra</s>, who is supreme over all. Regarding her, the following other [verse] occurs:

(11.39) 'I do not rejoice, O <s>Indrāṇī</s>, without the friendship of <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, whose dear oblation, [cooked] in waters, reaches the gods; <s>Indra</s> is above all.' (ṚV 10.86.10)
(11.39) 'I do not rejoice, O <s>Indrāṇī</s>, without the friendship of <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, whose <s>āpya</s> (watery) oblation — cooked in water, or prepared with waters — [being] dear, goes to the gods.'
(11.39) He who is above everything, [that is] <s>Indra</s> — we address him thus.
(11.39) '<s>Gaurī</s>' — [means] 'shining,' 'blazing,' [derived] from the root [denoting] action.
(11.39) This other [word] '<s>gaura</s>' (white) in complexion is also from this very [root].
(11.39) [It means] 'praiseworthy.'
(11.39) Of her, this [verse] is [spoken]:

(11.40) '<s>Gaurī</s> (the radiant one) has created the waters, fashioning [them]; one-footed, two-footed, she has become four-footed, eight-footed, nine-footed, with a thousand syllables, in the highest heaven.' (ṚV 1.164.41)
(11.40) <s>Gaurī</s> has created the waters, fashioning, making [them]. 'One-footed' by the intermediate [region]; 'two-footed' by the intermediate and the sun; 'four-footed' by the [four] directions; 'eight-footed' by the directions and intermediate directions; 'nine-footed' by the directions, intermediate directions, and the sun.
(11.40) 'With a thousand syllables' [means] 'with much water'; in the highest expanse.
(11.40) Of her, this other [verse] is [spoken]:

(11.41) 'From her the oceans flow forth; by that, the four quarters live; from that flows the imperishable — that sustains all.' (ṚV 1.164.42)
(11.41) From her the oceans flow forth.
(11.41) The clouds rain.
(11.41) By that, beings that depend on the directions live.
(11.41) From that flows the imperishable water.
(11.41) All beings subsist on that.
(11.41) '<s>Gaur</s>' (cow/speech) has been explained.
(11.41) Of her, this [verse] is [spoken]:

body.translated_text:
(11.42) 'The cow lowed after the calf that was blinking; she made a lowing sound at [its] head, for [its] mother's [sake]; bellowing at the hot [milk], she lows her lowing-sound; she swells with milks.' (ṚV 10.169.2)
(11.42) The cow lowed after the calf 'blinking' — or 'not blinking,' [meaning] the sun.
(11.42) She made a sound at his head — for contemplation.
(11.42) At the <s>sṛkvāṇa</s> (flowing), the <s>gharma</s> (hot [milk/sun]), bellowing, she lows her lowing-sound; she swells with milks.
(11.42) Or '<s>māyu</s>' [means] the sun.
(11.42) This is the intermediate speech (<s>vāc</s>).
(11.42) 'The <s>gharma</s>-milker' — thus [say] the ritualists.
(11.42) '<s>Dhenu</s>' (milch-cow) [is derived] from <s>dhayati</s> (sucks) or from <s>dhinoti</s> (satisfies).
(11.42) Of that [cow], this [verse] is [spoken]:

body.translated_text:
(11.43) 'I invoke this good-milking cow; the good-handed milk-man milks her; let <s>Savitṛ</s> extract for us the best pressing; the <s>gharma</s> (hot oblation) has been kindled — that I declare well.' (ṚV)
(11.43) 'I invoke this well-milking cow; the good-handed milk-man also milks her.'
(11.43) 'Let <s>Savitṛ</s> press out for us the best pressing.'
(11.43) For this is the best of all pressings — that which is water, or the <s>Yajus</s>-possessing milk.
(11.43) 'The <s>gharma</s> has been kindled — that I declare well.'
(11.43) This is the intermediate speech.
(11.43) 'The <s>gharma</s>-milker' — thus [say] the ritualists.
(11.43) '<s>Aghnyā</s>' (inviolable cow) — she who should not be killed.
(11.43) Or '<s>agha-ghnī</s>' — she who destroys evil.
(11.43) Of that [cow], this [verse] is [spoken]:
'From good pasture, O fortunate one, may you prosper; then may we too be fortunate.'

(11.44) 'Eat grass, O inviolable one, at all times; drink pure water, moving about.' (ṚV 1.164.40)
(11.44) 'Be one who has good pasture, O fortunate one.'
(11.44) 'And now may we too be fortunate.'
(11.44) 'Eat grass, O inviolable one, always; and drink pure water, moving about.'
(11.44) Of her, this other [verse] is [spoken]:

(11.45) 'Lowing, the mistress of goods, of the goods, desiring [her] calf, has come with [her] mind; may she, the inviolable one, yield milk for the <s>Aśvins</s>; may she increase for great good fortune.' (ṚV 4.57.7)
(11.45) Thus she has been explained through direct citation (<s>nigada</s>).
(11.45) '<s>Pathyā Svasti</s>' (Welfare of the Path):
(11.45) The path is the atmosphere — because of dwelling therein.
(11.45) Of her, this [verse] is [spoken]:

(11.46) '<s>Svasti</s> (Welfare) indeed is foremost on the highway, wealthy in riches, she who goes toward desirable things; may she protect us at home, at the place of kindling, and at the place of departure; may she be well-entered, protected by the gods.' (ṚV)
(11.46) '<s>Svasti</s> indeed is foremost on the highway, wealthy — possessing wealth — she who goes toward goods worthy of desire.'
(11.46) 'May she protect us at home, at the place of kindling, and at the place of departure.'
(11.46) 'May she be well-entered.'
(11.46) 'Protected by the gods' — may the divine one protect the gods; or may the gods protect her.
(11.46) '<s>Uṣas</s>' (Dawn) has been explained.
(11.46) Of her, this [verse] is [spoken]:

(11.47) '<s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn) fled from the well-pressed cloud-chariot [= the thundering cloud], frightened, when the bull [= <s>Indra</s>] roared.' (ṚV)
(11.47) '<s>Uṣas</s> fled from the chariot (<s>anas</s>), from the well-pressed cloud, frightened.'
(11.47) '<s>Anas</s>' (chariot) is wind, from [the root] <s>aniti</s> (breathes); or it may be used metaphorically — like a chariot.
(11.47) '<s>Anas</s>' is a chariot; [also] clothing bound upon it.
(11.47) Or it may be from [the root denoting] life-sustaining action.
(11.47) [Beings] subsist on this.
(11.47) A cloud too is '<s>anas</s>' — from this very [root].
(11.47) 'When the bull, the rainer, the intermediate one [= <s>Indra</s>/cloud], roared.'
(11.47) Of her, this other [verse] is [spoken]:

(11.48) 'This, her chariot, lies well-pressed, released from bonds; she [Dawn] has gone forth, impelled from afar.' (ṚV 1.92.7)
(11.48) 'This, her chariot (<s>anas</s>), rests well-pressed, like the other.'
(11.48) '<s>Vipāśī</s>' — freed from bonds.
(11.48) '<s>Uṣas</s> has gone forth, impelled from afar, or come from afar.'
(11.48) '<s>Iḷā</s>' has been explained.
(11.48) Of her, this [verse] is [spoken]:

(11.49) 'May <s>Iḷā</s>, mother of the herd, or <s>Urvaśī</s>, sing praises to us with rivers; or may <s>Urvaśī</s> sing praise in the great heaven, covering over [us] for the bringing forth of <s>Āyu</s> (life).' 'May she furnish us with nourishment and prosperity.' (ṚV 5.41.19)
(11.49) 'May <s>Iḷā</s>, the mother of the herd — mother of all — sing praises to us with rivers; or may <s>Urvaśī</s> sing praise.'
(11.49) 'Or may <s>Urvaśī</s> in the great heaven — in the great sky — singing praise, covering over, for the bringing forth of <s>Āyu</s> (life-force), of man, or of light, or of water — may she furnish us with food and prosperity.'
(11.49) '<s>Rodasī</s>' (Heaven-and-Earth) is the consort of <s>Rudra</s>.
(11.49) Of her, this [verse] is [spoken]:

(11.50) 'We invoke the swift chariot of the <s>Maruts</s>, [the cloud,] for fame; in which <s>Rodasī</s> (Heaven-and-Earth) has taken her place, bearing beautiful [waters], together with the <s>Maruts</s>.' (ṚV 5.56.8)
(11.50) 'The swift (<s>kṣipra</s>) chariot of the <s>Maruts</s> — the cloud — we invoke for that which is worthy of hearing. In which <s>Rodasī</s> has taken her place, bearing delightful waters, together with the <s>Maruts</s> — [that is] <s>Rodasī</s> (the two worlds).'

body.translated_text:
(12.1) Now, henceforth, the deities stationed in heaven.
(12.1) Of these, the <s>Aśvins</s> are the first to come.
(12.1) The <s>Aśvins</s> — because they pervade everything: one with essence (<s>rasa</s>), the other with light.
(12.1) '<s>Aśvins</s> [are so called] because of horses (<s>aśva</s>)' — [says] <s>Aurṇavābha</s>.
(12.1) Then who are the <s>Aśvins</s>?
(12.1) 'Heaven and Earth' — say some.
(12.1) 'Day and Night' — say some.
(12.1) 'Sun and Moon' — say some.
(12.1) 'Two kings who performed meritorious deeds' — say the historians (<s>aitihāsikas</s>).
(12.1) Their time [of worship] is after midnight, following upon the support of [the state of] light becoming [manifest].
(12.1) For the portion of darkness is the middle [night]; the portion of light is the sun.
(12.1) Of those two, this [verse] is [spoken]:

(12.2) 'You two move about in dwelling-places like two birds; when, O <s>Aśvins</s>, did you approach the gods?' (ṚV 1.181.1) — thus she has been explained through direct citation.
(12.2) Of those two, who are of the same time and the same activity, [and who] are mostly praised together, this half-verse [distinguished them] through differentiation:
(12.2) '<s>Vāsātya</s> (son of <s>Vasāti</s>) is one [of them], [the one] called the son of <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn); the other is yours [i.e., of another lineage].'  
(12.2) Of those two, this other [verse] is [spoken]:

(12.3) 'Born here and here, the two are praised together; with a body untouched by evil, and with their own names. One of you is the victorious inspirer of great strength — the intermediate one; the other, fortunate, is called the son of heaven — the sun.' (ṚV 1.181.4)
(12.3) 'Born here and here — the two are praised together, with a body not besmeared by evil, and with their own names. One of you, victorious, the urger of great strength — the intermediate one [= the moon]; the other, fortunate, is called the son of heaven — the sun.'
(12.3) Of those two, this other [verse] is [spoken]:

(12.4) "Awaken in the morning the two who are yoked together (<s>yujā</s>); let the <s>Aśvins</s> come here / for the drinking of this <s>Soma</s>." [Explanation:] Awaken in the morning the two who yoke themselves — the <s>Aśvins</s>. Let them come here for the drinking of this <s>Soma</s>. The following verse also belongs to those two [<s>Aśvins</s>]:

body.translated_text: (12.5) "Worship the <s>Aśvins</s> in the morning; send [them] forth. There is no evening [worship] that is unaccepted by the gods / Or another worships from [a place other than] us — depart! The earlier and earlier sacrificer is more favored." [Explanation:] Worship the <s>Aśvins</s> in the morning; send them forth. There is no evening worship of the gods — that is unaccepted. Or rather, another worships from [a place other than] us — depart! The earlier and earlier sacrificer is the most favored. The time of those two [<s>Aśvins</s>] extends until sunrise; during that [time] other deities are invoked. [The word] <s>uṣas</s> [is derived] from <s>vas</s> [meaning 'to desire'] — [related to] the action of desiring; or from <s>ucchati</s> [meaning 'to shine']. The other [verse] belongs to the middle [portion of the day]. The following verse belongs to her [<s>Uṣas</s>]: "O <s>Uṣas</s>, bring that bright [gift] to us, O you who possess nourishment / by which we may sustain sons and grandsons."

(12.6) O <s>Uṣas</s>, bring that bright, desirable, magnifiable wealth to us, O you who possess food, by which we may sustain sons and grandsons. The following verse also belongs to that [<s>Uṣas</s>]:

body.translated_text: (12.7) "These very <s>Dawns</s> have made their banner; in the eastern half of the sky they have displayed their light / Uncovering [themselves] like bold [warriors bearing] weapons, the ruddy cows come forth — [they are] mothers." [Explanation:] These <s>Dawns</s> have made their banner — their sign. The plural is used for the purpose of honoring a single one. In the eastern half of the atmospheric world, they unite with radiance. 'Uncovering' — like bold [warriors with] weapons. [The prefix] <s>nis</s> stands in the place of <s>sam</s> [here]. "I go to their ransom like a seductress" — this is also a Vedic citation. They come forth — <s>go</s> [means 'cow'] from [the root meaning] 'going.' <s>Aruṣī</s> [means 'ruddy'] from [the root meaning] 'shining.' <s>Mātṛ</s> [means 'mother'] from <s>bhāṣa</s> [speech] — creators. <s>Sūryā</s> is the wife of <s>Sūrya</s>. She is the very one who is most expressly [identified with a particular] time. The following verse belongs to her:

body.translated_text: (12.8) "Mount the well-<s>kiṃśuka</s>-[adorned], <s>śalmali</s>-[wood chariot], all-formed, golden-colored, well-sustained, well-wheeled / O <s>Sūryā</s>, [mount] the immortal's realm; make the bridal procession comfortable for the husband." [Explanation:] Good seat, free from impurity, all-formed. Or perhaps it is used as a simile — 'like <s>kiṃśuka</s>, [like] <s>śalmali</s>.' <s>Kiṃśuka</s> [is derived] from <s>kraṃśati</s> [meaning 'illuminates'] — from the action of illuminating. <s>Śalmali</s> is [so called because it is] well-arrowed or possessing arrows. 'Mount, O <s>Sūryā</s>, the realm of the immortal — of water.' Make the bridal procession comfortable for the husband. "<s>Savitṛ</s> gave <s>Sūryā</s> to <s>Soma</s>, to the king, to <s>Prajāpati</s>" — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text]. <s>Vṛṣākapāyī</s> is the wife of <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>. She is the very one who is most expressly [identified with a particular] time. The following verse belongs to her: "<s>Vṛṣākapāyī</s>, rich, with good sons, with good daughters-in-law / Let <s>Indra</s> eat the bulls; [make] dear, pleasure-giving oblation — <s>Indra</s> is above all."

(12.9) <s>Vṛṣākapāyī</s> — rich, with good sons — [spoken] in the middle [register]; with good daughters-in-law — in the <s>mādhyaṃdina</s> (midday) speech. <s>Snuṣā</s> [means daughter-in-law] — either 'one who attains well' (<s>sādhu sādinī</s>), or 'one who gains well' (<s>sādhu sāninī</s>), or 'she obtains (<s>sanoti</s>) good offspring.' 'Let <s>Indra</s> eat these bulls' — these middle <s>saṃstyāyas</s> (praise-hymns). <s>Ukṣan</s> [means 'bull'] from <s>ukṣati</s> — from the action of growing; or 'they sprinkle with water.' 'Make [it] dear, pleasure-giving, comfort-giving oblation.' He who is <s>Indra</s>, who is above all — we call him <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun). <s>Saraṇyū</s> [is so called] from <s>saraṇa</s> (movement). The following verse belongs to her:

body.translated_text: (12.10) "They hid the immortal one from mortals; having made a <s>Savarṇā</s> (one of like appearance), they gave [her] to <s>Vivasvat</s> / And she bore the <s>Aśvins</s> — that is what happened; and <s>Saraṇyū</s> abandoned the two twins." [Explanation:] They hid the immortal one from mortals. Having made a <s>Savarṇā</s>, they gave [her] to <s>Vivasvat</s>. And she bore the <s>Aśvins</s> — that is what happened; <s>Saraṇyū</s> abandoned the two twins. [The word] 'middle ones' and 'those belonging to the middle' [refer to] speech — so say the etymologists (<s>Nairuktas</s>). [They refer to] <s>Yama</s> and <s>Yamī</s> — so say the historians (<s>Aitihāsikas</s>). Regarding that, they relate the legend: <s>Tvāṣṭrī Saraṇyū</s>, from <s>Vivasvat</s> the <s>Āditya</s>, gave birth to a twin pair — <s>Yama</s> [and <s>Yamī</s>]. She, having substituted another <s>Savarṇā</s> [in her place], and having assumed the form of a mare, fled away. <s>Vivasvat</s> the <s>Āditya</s>, having likewise assumed the form of a horse, followed her and united with her. From that the <s>Aśvins</s> were born. From <s>Savarṇā</s>, <s>Manu</s> [was born]. The following verse refers to that:

(12.11) "<s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> prepares the bridal procession for his daughter — at this, the entire world assembles / The mother of <s>Yama</s>, being led away in marriage, the great wife of <s>Vivasvat</s>, disappeared." [Explanation:] <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> prepares the bridal procession for his daughter — at this, the entire world assembles; and all these beings come together. The mother of <s>Yama</s>, being led away in marriage — the wife of the great <s>Vivasvat</s> — disappeared. Night disappears at the rising of the sun (<s>Āditya</s>).
(12.12) <s>Savitṛ</s> has been explained. His time is when the sky becomes free of darkness [and] filled with rays [of light]. The following verse belongs to him:

body.translated_text: (12.13) "The poet releases all forms; he has produced good for bipeds and quadrupeds / <s>Savitṛ</s> the excellent has illuminated the firmament; he shines following the departure of <s>Uṣas</s>." [Explanation:] This verse belongs to him. He releases all signs — the wise one. <s>Kavi</s> (poet) means 'one who has transcendent vision,' or [is derived] from [the root] <s>ku</s>. He brings forth good for bipeds and quadrupeds. <s>Savitṛ</s> the excellent illuminated the firmament; following the departure of <s>Uṣas</s>, he shines. "The downward-dark one [is] of <s>Savitṛ</s>" — this is known in the <s>Paśu-samāmnāya</s> (animal enumeration). From what similarity? — Darkness exists at that time below — from that similarity. 'The downward-dark one' — dark below — from what similarity? "Having piled the fire, one should not approach a dark [cow]" — "A dark [cow] is approached for pleasure, not for <s>dharma</s>." [It is] of the dark species — from that similarity. "The rooster [is] of <s>Savitṛ</s>" — this is known in the <s>Paśu-samāmnāya</s>. From what similarity? — [It is determined] by going around the announcement of time. <s>Kṛkavāku</s> (rooster) — the first part is an onomatopoeia; the latter from [the root] <s>vac</s> (to speak). <s>Bhaga</s> has been explained. His time is before [the sun's] rising. The following verse belongs to him:

(12.14) "In the morning we would invoke the victorious, mighty <s>Bhaga</s> — the son of <s>Aditi</s>, who is the upholder / Even the poor man thinks of him; even the swift one; even a king says: 'May I have a share (<s>bhaga</s>)!'" [Explanation:] In the morning we would invoke the victorious, mighty <s>Bhaga</s>, son of <s>Aditi</s>, who upholds all. Even the poor man — one who thinks [of him] — the indolent, the destitute. Even the swift one — <s>tura</s> means <s>Yama</s> as a name, or [is derived] from <s>tarati</s> (to cross) or <s>tvarati</s> (to hasten) — <s>Yama</s> whose movement is swift. Even a king says: 'May I consume (<s>bhakṣi</s>) <s>Bhaga</s> (a share)!' "<s>Bhaga</s> is blind, they say — he who is not raised up is not seen. [<s>Śiva</s>] struck out his [<s>Bhaga's</s>] eyes at the <s>Prāśitra</s> [portion]" — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text]. Or it is known [from]: "<s>Bhaga</s> goes to people." He goes to people at sunrise. <s>Sūrya</s> [is so called] from <s>sṛ</s> (to go), or from <s>su</s> (to impel), or from <s>svṝ</s> (to shine). The following verse belongs to him:

(12.15) "They carry up that <s>Jātavedas</s>, the god, with banners / <s>Sūrya</s> — for the sight of all." [Explanation:] They carry up that <s>Jātavedas</s> — the rays [are] the banners — for the seeing of all beings — <s>Sūrya</s>. What else could be described thus other than <s>Āditya</s>? The following verse also belongs to that one:

12.16: 'The wondrous face of the gods has risen — the eye of <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Agni</s>; it has filled heaven, earth, and the atmosphere — <s>Sūrya</s> is the self of the moving and the stationary.'
12.16: The wondrous splendor of the gods has risen — the face.
12.16: The eye of <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Agni</s>.
12.16: It has filled heaven and earth and the atmosphere with its greatness.
12.16: <s>Sūrya</s> is the self of the moving and the stationary.
12.16: Now, since he nourishes with rays (<s>raśmi-poṣam puṣyati</s>), he becomes <s>Pūṣan</s>.
12.16: Regarding him, this [verse] occurs:

12.17: 'One [form] of yours is bright, another sacrificial; the two days of diverse form — you are like the sky; for you control all magical powers, O self-sustaining one; may your generous gift be here for us, O <s>Pūṣan</s>.'
12.17: One of yours is bright, another is red; one is sacrificial, another is fit for sacrifice.
12.17: The two days (day and night) of different forms are your activity.
12.17: And you are like the sky.
12.17: You protect all forms of knowledge, O possessor of food.
12.17: May your gift here be fruitful, O <s>Pūṣan</s>.
12.17: Regarding him, this other [verse] occurs:

12.18: 'The lord of every path, the guardian of speech, fashioned by desire, has approached the <s>arka</s> (sun); may he grant us bright-tipped treasures; <s>Pūṣan</s> accomplishes prayer after prayer.'
12.18: The lord of each path — the overlord — fashioned by speech and desire, he has approached the <s>arka</s> (sun), or has reached the sun.
12.18: May he give us the foremost possessions that lead to heaven.
12.18: And may <s>Pūṣan</s> accomplish each and every rite for us.
12.18: Now, since he pervades (<s>viṣita</s>), he becomes <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
12.18: <s>Viṣṇu</s> [derives] either from <s>viśateḥ</s> (to enter/pervade) or from <s>vyaśnoteḥ</s> (to pervade/reach).
12.18: Regarding him, this [verse] occurs:

12.19: '<s>Viṣṇu</s> strode across this; he placed his foot in three ways, gathered up in his dust.'
12.19: Whatever this [universe] is, <s>Viṣṇu</s> strides across it.
12.19: He places his foot in three ways.
12.19: For the threefold existence — on earth, in the atmosphere, and in heaven — so says <s>Śākapūṇi</s>.
12.19: At the summit, in <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s step, at the head of <s>Gaya</s> — so says <s>Aurṇavābha</s>.
12.19: 'Gathered in his dust' — the step in the atmosphere, the place of increase, is not seen.
12.19: Or perhaps it should be understood in the sense of a simile: his step is not seen, as if gathered in dust.
12.19: <s>Pāṃsu</s> (dust) [derives from]: 'they are produced by feet,' or 'they lie fallen,' or 'they are to be crushed.'

12.20: <s>Viśvānara</s> has been explained.
12.20: Regarding him, this quotation occurs in a verse connected with <s>Indra</s>:

12.21: 'The lord of trees of <s>Viśvānara</s>, of unbending might; with the desires and paths of peoples, I invoke for help the chariots.'
12.21: Of <s>Viśvānara</s>, i.e., of <s>Āditya</s>, of unbending, great power — with the desires, paths, or protections of peoples, i.e., of human beings, and along the path of chariots, I invoke <s>Indra</s> at this sacrifice.
12.21: <s>Varuṇa</s> has been explained.
12.21: Regarding him, this [verse] occurs:

12,22: svargasya.lokasya.api.vodhā/
12,22: tat.sampātī.bhuranyuh/
12,22: anena.pāvaka.khyānena/
12,22: bhuranyantam.janān.anu/
12,22: tvam.varuṇa.paśyati/
12,22: tat.te.vayam.stuma.iti.vākya.śesah/
12,22: api.vā.uttarasyām/
body.translated_text:
12.22: 'With which purifying eye, the swiftly-moving people — O <s>Varuṇa</s>, you see.'
12.22: <s>Bhuraṇyu</s> is a name for 'swift.'
12.22: <s>Bhuraṇyu</s>, the bird, leads through a vast path.
12.22: He is also the guide to the heavenly world.
12.22: That swift-moving one is <s>Sampātī</s>.
12.22: With this purifying vision,
12.22: [you see] the swiftly-moving people.
12.22: O <s>Varuṇa</s>, you see.
12.22: 'We praise you for that' — this is the completion of the sentence.
12.22: Or, in the following [verse]:

12.23: 'With which purifying eye, the swiftly-moving people — O <s>Varuṇa</s>, you see.' 'You traverse heaven and the broad atmosphere, measuring the days by nights, seeing all births, O <s>Sūrya</s>.'
12.23: You traverse heaven and the broad atmosphere — the great realm — and the days, measuring them together with the nights, seeing all that is born, O <s>Sūrya</s>.
12.23: Or, in the preceding [verse]:

body.text:
12,24: ``yenā.pāvaka.cakṣasā.bhuranyantam.janān.anu/
12,24: tvam.varuṇa.paśyasi/''.``.pratyan.devānām.viśaḥ.pratyann.esi.mānusān/
12,24: pratyan.viśvam.svar.dṛśe/''.
12,24: pratyann.idam.sarvam.udesi/
12,24: pratyann.idam.jyotiṣ.ucyate/
12,24: pratyann.idam.sarvam.abhivipaśyasi.iti/
12,24: api.vā.etasyām.eva/
12,24: ``yenā.pāvaka.vakṣasā.bhuranyantam.janān.anu/
12,24: tvam.varuṇa.paśyasi/''.
body.translated_text:
12.24: 'With which purifying eye, the swiftly-moving people — O <s>Varuṇa</s>, you see.' 'Facing the divine beings, facing human beings — facing all, for seeing the light.'
12.24: Facing all this, you rise up.
12.24: Facing this, the light is spoken of.
12.24: Facing this, you behold all.
12.24: Or, in this very [verse]:
12.24: 'With which purifying eye, the swiftly-moving people — O <s>Varuṇa</s>, you see.'

12.25: By that [eye] you behold our people.
12.25: <s>Keśin</s> (the long-haired one):
12.25: <s>Keśāḥ</s> (hairs) are the rays (<s>raśmayaḥ</s>); he who possesses them becomes that [<s>Keśin</s>].
12.25: Or [the word derives] from <s>kāśana</s> (shining) or from <s>prakāśana</s> (illuminating).
12.25: Regarding him, this [verse] occurs:

body.text:
12,26: ``keśy.agnim.keśī.visam.keśī.bibhati.rodasī/
12,26: keśī.viśvam.svar.dṛśe.keśī.idam.jyotir.ucyate/''.
12,26: keśin1.agnim.ca.visaṃś.ca/
12,26: visam.ity.udaka.nāma,.visnāter.vi.pūrvasya.snāteḥ.śuddhi.arthasya/
12,26: vi.pūrvasya.vā.sacateh/
12,26: dyāvā.pṛthivī.au.ca.dhārayati/
12,26: keśī.[viśvam?].idam.sarvam.idam.abhivipaśyati/
12,26: keśī.idam.jyotiṣ.ucyata.ity.ādityam.āha/
12,26: atha.apy.ete.itare.jyotiṣī.keśinī.ucyete/
12,26: dhūmena.agnī.rajasā.ca.madhyamah/
12,26: teṣām.eṣā.sādhāranā.bhavati/
body.translated_text:
12.26: '<s>Keśin</s> bears the fire, <s>Keśin</s> bears the waters, <s>Keśin</s> bears both worlds (heaven and earth); <s>Keśin</s> is all this for seeing the light; <s>Keśin</s> is called this light.'
12.26: <s>Keśin</s> [bears] fire and the waters.
12.26: <s>Viṣa</s> is a name for water, from <s>visnāteḥ</s> with the prefix <s>vi</s>, meaning 'purification,' or from <s>vi</s>-prefixed <s>sacateḥ</s> (to follow/accompany).
12.26: And he sustains heaven and earth.
12.26: <s>Keśin</s> beholds all this.
12.26: '<s>Keśin</s> is called this light' — he speaks of <s>Āditya</s> (the sun).
12.26: Moreover, these other two lights are also called <s>keśin</s>: fire by its smoke, and the middle one (atmosphere/lightning) by its dust.
12.26: Regarding them, this common [verse occurs]:

12.27: 'Three <s>keśins</s> (long-haired ones) look forth according to the seasons; in the year, one of them shaves; one beholds all with his powers; the movement of one is seen, but not the form.'
12.27: Three <s>keśins</s> look forth according to the seasons — at each appointed time they observe.
12.27: 'In the year, one of them shaves' — fire burns the earth.
12.27: One beholds all with his deeds — <s>Āditya</s> (the sun).
12.27: The movement of one is seen, but not the form — of the middle one (lightning/atmospheric fire).
12.27: Not the form of the middle one.
12.27: Now, since he (the sun) goes forth shaking with his rays, he becomes <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> — <s>vṛṣā</s> (powerful one), <s>kampana</s> (shaking)...

12.28: 'Come back, O <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, let us arrange auspicious rites; you who destroy sleep, you go to setting by the path again — <s>Indra</s> is superior to all.'
12.28: Come back, O <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>; let us arrange your well-produced rites.
12.28: Destroyer of sleep — you destroy sleep by the rising of <s>Āditya</s>; and you go to setting by the path again.
12.28: He who is <s>Indra</s>, superior to all — we say this of <s>Āditya</s>.
12.28: <s>Yama</s> has been explained.
12.28: Regarding him, this [verse] occurs:

body.text:
12,29: ``yasmin.vṛkṣe.supalāśe.devaiḥ.sam.pibate.yamah/
12,29: atrā.no.viśpatiḥ.pitā.purānān.anu.venati/''.

body.translated_text:
12.29: 'In which fair-leafed tree <s>Yama</s> drinks with the gods — there our lord of the people, our father, yearns after the ancestors.'
12.29: 'In which fair-leafed tree' — i.e., in a place, or in the cessation of coverings.
12.29: Or perhaps it should be understood as a simile — 'like a fair-leafed tree.'
12.29: <s>Vṛkṣa</s> (tree) [derives] from <s>vraścanāt</s> (cutting).
12.29: <s>Palāśa</s> (leaf) [derives] from <s>palāśanāt</s> (leafing).
12.29: <s>Yama</s> meets with the gods — i.e., <s>Āditya</s> [meets] with the rays.
12.29: There, our protector or guardian of all yearns after the ancestors.
12.29: <s>Aja Ekapād</s> (the one-footed unborn one):
12.29: The moving one [with] one foot; or 'he protects with one foot'; or 'he drinks with one foot.'

body.text:
12,30: ``pāvīravī.tanyatur.ekapādajo.divo.dhartā.sindhur.āpaḥ.samudriyah/
12,30: viśve.devāsaḥ.śṛṇavan.vacāṃsi.me.sarasvatī.saha.dhībhiḥ.purandhyā/''.
12,30: paviḥ.śalyo.bhavati,.yad.vipunāti.kāyam/
12,30: tadvat.pavīram.āyudham/
12,30: tadvān.indraḥ.pavīravān/
12,30: ``atitasthau.pavīravān''.ity.api.nigamo.bhavati/
12,30: tad.devatā.vāc.pāvīravī/
12,30: pāvīravī.ca.divyā.vāc,.tanyatus.tanitrī.vācas.anyasyāh/

body.translated_text:
12.30: '<s>Pāvīravī</s> (the thunderous one), <s>Tanyatu</s> (thunder), <s>Aja Ekapāt</s> (the one-footed unborn), supporter of heaven, <s>Sindhu</s>, the waters, and the ocean — may all the gods hear my words, <s>Sarasvatī</s> together with inspired thoughts and bounty.'
12.30: <s>Pavi</s> (sharp point) is a śalya (piercing weapon), because it purifies (<s>vipunāti</s>) the body.
12.30: Similarly, <s>pavīra</s> is a weapon possessing such [a point].
12.30: <s>Indra</s>, possessing the <s>pavīra</s>, is called <s>pavīravān</s>.
12.30: 'He surpassed [all], the <s>pavīravān</s>' — thus a Vedic citation (<s>nigama</s>) also occurs.
12.30: The deity of that [weapon] is speech (<s>vāc</s>), hence <s>pāvīravī</s>.
12.30: <s>Pāvīravī</s> is the divine speech; <s>tanyatu</s> (thunder) is the thundering of another [kind of] speech.
12.30: And <s>Aja Ekapāt</s>, and the supporter of heaven, and <s>Sindhu</s>, and the waters, and the oceanic [waters], and all the gods — may <s>Sarasvatī</s> together with inspired thoughts and bounty [hear my words].

12.31: 'O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, whether you stand in the highest, the middle, or the lowest [region of] earth — from there, O two bulls, come hither; then drink of the pressed <s>Soma</s>.' Thus that [verse] has been explained in the <s>nigada</s> (ritual formulae) section.
12.31: <s>Samudra</s> (ocean) has been explained.
12.31: Regarding it, this occurrence is found in a <s>Pāvamānī</s> verse:

12.32: 'Those possessing purifying [rays] sit around speech; their ancient father guards their sacred observance. <s>Varuṇa</s> concealed the great ocean; the wise sought to grasp support in the foundations.'
12.32: Those possessing <s>pavitra</s> (purifying rays), that is, the ray-bearing middle divine hosts, surround the middle speech.
12.32: The middle father, their ancient one, guards [their] observance, [their] ritual action.
12.32: <s>Varuṇa</s> hides, conceals the great ocean; then the wise ones are able to undertake the commencement of ritual action in the foundations, that is, in the waters.
12.32: <s>Aja Ekapāt</s> has been explained.
12.32: <s>Pṛthivī</s> has been explained.
12.32: <s>Samudra</s> has been explained.

12.33: 'And may <s>Ahi Budhnya</s> hear us, <s>Aja Ekapāt</s>, <s>Pṛthivī</s>, and <s>Samudra</s>; all the gods who increase truth, being invoked, praised by mantras — may the mantras proclaimed by sages protect us.'
12.33: May also <s>Ahi Budhnya</s> hear us, and <s>Aja Ekapāt</s>, and <s>Pṛthivī</s>, and <s>Samudra</s>, and all the gods who increase truth or who increase sacrifice, being invoked, praised by mantras — may the mantras proclaimed by sages, that is, proclaimed by the wise, protect us.
12.33: <s>Dadhyañc</s> means one upon whom meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) is placed, or one in whom meditation is directed. (12.34)
12.33: <s>Atharvā</s> has been explained.
12.33: <s>Manu</s> [derives] from thinking (<s>manana</s>).
12.33: Regarding them, this occurrence is found in a verse addressed to <s>Indra</s>:

12.34: 'The thought which <s>Atharvā</s>, <s>Manu</s> the father, and <s>Dadhyañc</s> extended — in that, sacred formulas and hymns to <s>Indra</s>, as of old, came together; they praised [in celebration of] sovereign dominion.'
12.34: The thought which <s>Atharvā</s> and <s>Manu</s>, the father of mankind, and <s>Dadhyañc</s> extended — in that, the sacred formulas, the ritual actions, and the hymns to <s>Indra</s>, as of old, came together; [they are] praiseworthy and proximate, [leading to] sovereign dominion.

12.35: Now, from here [we discuss] the celestial divine hosts.
12.35: Among them, the <s>Ādityas</s> are the first to be discussed.
12.35: The <s>Ādityas</s> have been explained.
12.35: Regarding them, the following [verse] occurs:

12.36: 'These songs, dripping with ghee, I offer with the sacrificial ladle to the <s>Ādityas</s>, the eternal kings. May <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, the abundantly-born one, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, and <s>Aṃśa</s> hear us.'
12.36: <s>Ghṛta-snū</s> means dripping with ghee, flowing with ghee, streaming with ghee, or abounding in ghee — [these are] the oblations [offered] to the <s>Ādityas</s>. I long offer with the sacrificial ladle, for long life, or to the eternal kings.
12.36: May [they] hear these our songs — <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Aryaman</s> and <s>Bhaga</s> and the abundantly-born <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Aṃśa</s>.
12.36: <s>Aṃśa</s> has been explained through [the word] <s>aṃśu</s> (ray).
12.36: The seven sages (<s>sapta ṛṣayaḥ</s>) have been explained.
12.36: Regarding them, the following [verse] occurs:

12.37: 'Seven sages are established in the body; seven guard the seat without negligence. Seven waters went to the world of the sleeping one; there the two wakeful, unsleeping gods, the pair dwelling in the sacrificial session, [stand guard].'
12.37: Seven sages are established in the body, [that is,] rays in the sun.
12.37: Seven guard the seat without negligence, [guarding] the year without failing.
12.37: The seven openings — they themselves go to the world of the sleeping one, [that is,] to the set sun.
12.37: There, the two wakeful, unsleeping gods dwelling in the sacrificial session are <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Āditya</s>.
12.37: Thus [is the] theological interpretation (<s>adhidaivatam</s>).
12.37: Now the personal interpretation (<s>adhyātmam</s>):
12.37: Seven sages are established in the body — [the seven senses in the head]...

12.38: 'An inverted bowl with its opening sideways and its bottom upward — in which is placed glory of all forms. There sat the seven sages together, who became the guardians of this great [universe].'
12.38: The bowl with its opening sideways and its binding upward, or its awareness upward.
12.38: In which is placed glory of all forms.
12.38: There sat the seven sages together, [that is,] the rays of the sun, who became the guardians of this great [universe] — thus is the theological interpretation (<s>adhidaivatam</s>).
12.38: Now the personal interpretation (<s>adhyātmam</s>):
12.38: The bowl with its opening sideways and its binding upward, or its awareness upward.
12.38: In which is placed glory of all forms — there sat the seven sages together, [the seven senses in the head]...

12.39: 'May the auspicious favor of the gods be directed toward us; may the gift of the gods come to us. May we attain the friendship of the gods; may the gods extend our lifespan for living.'
12.39: May we [dwell] in the auspicious, noble favor of the gods — [the favor] of those who move rightly, or those who move according to the seasons.
12.39: May the gift of the gods come to us.
12.39: May we attain the friendship of the gods.
12.39: May the gods extend our lifespan for long living.
12.39: <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> means all the gods.
12.39: Regarding them, the following [verse] occurs:

body.translated_text:
12.40: 'O protectors, supporters of peoples, all gods, come hither; [receive from] the sacrificers the pressed <s>Soma</s> of the givers.'
12.40: [<s>Omāsaḥ</s> means] protectors or those deserving protection; supporters of men — all gods, come hither; the givers [offer] the pressed <s>Soma</s> of the givers.
12.40: This indeed is the single <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (belonging to all gods) <s>Gāyatra</s> (in <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter) <s>tṛca</s> (set of three verses) found in the decade [hymns].
12.40: Whatever, however, is addressed to many deities — that is appropriately placed in the section of the <s>Viśve Devas</s>.
12.40: [It should be classified thus] if it has the characteristic of universality — according to <s>Śākapūṇi</s>.
12.40: But this enumeration [of deities] is not exhaustive.
12.40: 'The brown one, the single one' — [this is a set of] ten two-footed [verses] without gender markers.
12.40: [These pertain to] the elemental portion, according to <s>Kāśyapa</s>, [placed in] the <s>Āśvina</s> [section]...
