body.translated_text: 12.41: 'The gods worshipped sacrifice with sacrifice; these were the first laws. Those great ones attained heaven, where the ancient <s>Sādhya</s> gods dwell.' The gods worshipped sacrifice with sacrifice — the gods worshipped <s>Agni</s> with <s>Agni</s>. '<s>Agni</s> was the sacrificial animal; they offered him. With him they sacrificed' — thus the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> states. These were the first <s>dharmas</s> (laws, rites). Those great ones served heaven, where the ancient <s>Sādhya</s> gods dwell — [so called] from <s>sādhana</s> (accomplishment). 'A group of gods dwelling in heaven' — [say] the etymologists (<s>Nairuktā</s>s). 'A former age of gods' — [say] the narrative traditions. Regarding them, the following [verse] occurs:

12.42: 'May the paths to you, O gods, be easy to traverse; you who have come to these <s>savanas</s> (pressings), enjoying them. Having eaten and drunk, O all <s>Vasvas</s>, bestow riches upon us.' May the paths to you be easy to travel and well-routed, O gods, you who come to these <s>savana</s> pressings, enjoying them. Having eaten and drunk, all of you, bestow upon us, [you who are] possessors of wealth, riches. Regarding them, the following other [verse] occurs:

12.43: 'Here on the earth the <s>Vasus</s>, the gods, took delight; in the broad atmosphere they move, shining. Make the paths hither, O swift-moving ones; hear, O messengers, this messenger of ours who has come.' Here on the earth the <s>Vasus</s>, the gods, found pleasure. <s>Jmā</s> is the earth; those dwelling on her, in the broad atmosphere, they move — <s>marjayanta</s> means 'cause to go' — shining, resplendent. Make the paths hither, O swift-moving ones. Hear this messenger of ours who has come — [that is,] <s>Agni</s>. The <s>Vājins</s> (coursers) have been explained. Regarding them, the following [verse] occurs:

12.44: 'May the <s>Vājins</s> (coursers) be auspicious to us at invocations, divine, with measured speed, bright-hymned; crushing the serpent, the wolf, and the demons, may they swiftly drive away our ailments.' May the <s>Vājins</s> be pleasant to us at invocations — <s>devatāti</s> means 'at the sacrifice.' <s>Mita-dravaḥ</s> means 'of measured, well-regulated speed.' <s>Svarkāḥ</s> means either 'well-going,' or 'well-praising,' or 'well-shining.' Crushing the serpent and wolf and demons — swiftly may they drive away from us our ailments. [They are] the divine horses, or the wives of the gods — the wives of the gods. Regarding them, the following [verse] occurs:

12.45: 'May the willing wives of the gods protect us; may they help us for the winning of offspring and food. Those who are of the earth, those who are in the sphere of the waters — may those divine ones, easily invoked, grant us shelter.' May the wives of the gods, being willing, protect us. May they help us for the generation of offspring and for the attainment of food. Those who are of the earth, those who are in the sphere of the waters, in their domain of action — may those divine ones, easily invoked, grant us shelter, refuge. Regarding them, the following other [verse] occurs:

12.46: 'And may the divine wives come: <s>Indrāṇī</s>, <s>Agnāyī</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s> — may she reign! May <s>Rodasī</s> and <s>Varuṇānī</s> hear; may the goddesses come who are the season of women.' And may the divine wives come — the wives of the gods. <s>Indrāṇī</s> is the wife of <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agnāyī</s> is the wife of <s>Agni</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s> is the wife of the <s>Aśvins</s>. <s>Rāṭ</s> is from <s>rājati</s> (to reign, to shine). <s>Rodasī</s> is the wife of <s>Rudra</s>. And <s>Varuṇānī</s> is the wife of <s>Varuṇa</s>. May the goddesses come — may they desire [us]. That is the season, the time, of women — that is the season, the time, of women.

13.1: Now these are called <s>atistuti</s>s (excessive praises). Or perhaps it is just fitting reverence due to the greatness of the deity. He [the poet] first praises <s>Agni</s> [with]: 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, [shine] through the days; you, the swift-shining one' — as in this hymn. '"Not even in the twinkling of an eye does one equal you" — this is [praise] of <s>Varuṇa</s>.' Now the following is [in praise] of <s>Indra</s>:

13.2: 'If, O <s>Indra</s>, the heavens were a hundred and the earths also a hundred, not even a thousand suns, O wielder of the <s>vajra</s>, nor the two heaven-and-earth could match you, O unborn one.' If, O <s>Indra</s>, a hundred heavens and a hundred earths were your measure — not even a thousand [could match you], O wielder of the <s>vajra</s>; not even the suns, not even heaven and earth could attain to you. Now the following is [in praise] of <s>Āditya</s>:

13.3: 'When you two went northward to the house, O <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> and <s>Indra</s>, where is his hairy beast, where has that mischief-maker gone? — <s>Indra</s> is supreme over all.' 'When you two went northward to the house, O <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> and <s>Indra</s>, where is his hairy beast?' — where is that creature of many appetites, that beast? <s>Mṛga</s> (beast) is from <s>mārṣṭi</s> (to go), a verb of motion. 'Where has the mischief-maker gone?' — to what place. He who is <s>Indra</s>, supreme over all — we say this of <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun). Now the following is [in praise] of the rays of <s>Āditya</s>:

13.4: 'For they let loose for creation, they did not regard <s>Indra</s> as a god. Where <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> became intoxicated, the lord, among the creatures — my companion in drink — <s>Indra</s> is supreme over all.' They released [the waters] for the sake of creation, yet they did not honor <s>Indra</s> as a god. Where <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> became intoxicated — the lord (<s>arya</s>), among the creatures, among the nourishments — my companion in drink (<s>matsakhā</s>), my friend in intoxication. Or: 'those who are our companions, together with them.' He who is <s>Indra</s>, supreme over all — we say this of <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun). Now the following is [in praise] of the <s>Aśvins</s>:

body.translated_text: 13.5: 'Like a sickle, the nourishing one and the destroying one — like the son of <s>Nitoṣa</s>, the swift-destroying, the scattering one; like a water-born [pair], eating, intoxicating — these two remove my old age, the undecaying, the death-conquering.' <s>Sṛṇī</s> (sickle) — thus. There are two kinds of sickle: the supporter and the destroyer. Likewise the <s>Aśvins</s> too are supporters. <s>Jarbharī</s> means 'the nourishing one' — that is the meaning. <s>Turpharītū</s> means 'the destroying one.' 'Like the son of <s>Nitoṣa</s>, the swift-destroying, the scattering one.' <s>Naitoṣa</s> means 'the offspring of <s>Nitoṣa</s>.' Like <s>Naitoṣa</s>, the swift-destroying one. 'Like the water-born [pair], eating, intoxicating' — like those born in water, like aquatic [creatures].

13.6: 'The intoxicated one crosses, he runs — the stream of the pressed <s>andhas</s> (Soma plant); the intoxicated one crosses, he runs.' He who praises crosses over all evil — the intoxicated one. He runs, he goes on the upward path. 'The stream of the pressed <s>andhas</s>' — the stream of the pressed <s>Soma</s>, purified by <s>mantras</s>, praised by speech. Now the following is [in praise] of the sacrifice:

body.translated_text: 13.7: 'Four are his horns, three his feet, two his heads, seven his hands. Bound threefold, the bull roars; the great god has entered mortals.' 'Four horns' — these are said to be the <s>Vedas</s>. 'Three his feet' — the three <s>savanas</s> (pressings). 'Two heads' — the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> (opening) and <s>udayanīya</s> (closing) [rites]. 'Seven hands' — the seven meters (<s>chandas</s>). 'Bound threefold' — bound in three ways by <s>mantra</s>, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and <s>kalpa</s>. The bull roars — his roaring is the sequential recitation: with <s>ṛc</s>s they recite, with <s>yajus</s> formulas they sacrifice, with <s>sāmans</s> they sing.

body.translated_text:
13.8: 'Going heavenward, they do not look back; they ascend to heaven, to the two world-halves. Those who, well-knowing, extended the sacrifice that supports all around.'
13.8: Those going to heaven — the sacrificers — do not look back. They who have gone to that very world look [only ahead].
13.8: They ascend to heaven, to the two world-halves.
13.8: Those who, well-knowing, extended the sacrifice that is all-supporting (<s>viśvatodhāra</s>).
13.8: Now there follows one as if spoken about <s>Vāc</s> (Speech):
13.8: 'Four are the measured steps of Speech; those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who are wise know them. Three, hidden in the cave, they do not reveal; the fourth [step] of Speech humans speak.' (13.9)
13.8: Four are the measured steps of <s>Vāc</s>.
13.8: Those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who are intelligent know them.
13.8: Three are hidden in the cave — they do not convey the meaning.
13.8: <s>Guhā</s> (cave) is from <s>gūhati</s> (to hide). <s>Turīya</s> (fourth) is from <s>tvarati</s> (to hasten).
13.8: Which are those four steps?
13.8: '<s>Oṃkāra</s> and the great <s>Vyāhṛtis</s>' — [say] the <s>Ṛṣis</s>.
13.8: 'Nouns, verbs, prefixes, and particles' — [say] the grammarians (<s>Vaiyākaraṇas</s>).
13.8: '<s>Mantra</s>, <s>Kalpa</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, and the fourth is everyday [speech]' — [say] the ritualists (<s>Yājñikas</s>).
13.8: '<s>Ṛcs</s>, <s>Yajus</s> formulas, <s>Sāmans</s>, and the fourth is everyday [speech]' — [say] the etymologists (<s>Nairuktās</s>). (13.9)
13.8: 'The speech of serpents, of birds, of small creeping creatures, and the fourth is everyday [speech]' — [say] some.
13.8: 'In animals, in flutes, in wild beasts, and in the self' — [say] the <s>Ātmapravādas</s> (those who teach about the Self).
13.8: Moreover, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> text states:

13.9: 'That <s>Vāc</s> (Speech), having been created, became fourfold. In these very worlds [reside] three; in animals, the fourth. That which is on the earth is in <s>Agni</s>, is in the <s>Rathantara</s> [<s>Sāman</s>]. That which is in the atmosphere is in <s>Vāyu</s>, is in the <s>Vāmadevya</s> [<s>Sāman</s>]. That which is in heaven is in <s>Āditya</s>, is in the <s>Bṛhatī</s> [<s>Sāman</s>], is in thunder.'

13.10: Now regarding [the fourth part, residing] in animals:
13.10: 'That portion of <s>Vāc</s> which remained over, that they placed in the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. Therefore the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> speak both kinds of speech — that of the gods and that of humans.'
13.10: Now the following concerns the syllable (<s>akṣara</s>):
13.10: '<s>Ṛcs</s> [are established] in the imperishable, in the highest heaven, wherein all the gods are seated — he who does not know that, what will he do with the <s>ṛc</s>? Those who know that, they are assembled here.'
13.10: You point out [something]. What is this <s>akṣara</s> (syllable, the imperishable)?
13.10: 'It is <s>Oṃ</s> — this is <s>Vāc</s>' — [says] <s>Śākapūṇi</s>.
13.10: For the <s>ṛcs</s> are placed in the imperishable, in the highest abode, and in <s>mantras</s> addressed to various deities.
13.10: 'This indeed is that syllable in relation to which the entire threefold knowledge stands' — thus the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> also states.

13.11: '<s>Āditya</s>' — [says] the son of <s>Śākapūṇi</s>.
13.11: This [imperishable] becomes the <s>ṛc</s> because they worship it (<s>arcanti</s>).
13.11: All beings are reflections of the <s>ṛc</s>.
13.11: That which is other than the <s>mantras</s> — that becomes the <s>akṣara</s> (imperishable).
13.11: The rays — here the gods are said to be those who are seated upon it — this is the cosmological interpretation (<s>adhidaivatam</s>).
13.11: Now the individual interpretation (<s>adhyātmam</s>):
13.11: The body is here called the <s>ṛc</s>, because they worship by means of it.
13.11: All the senses are reflections of the <s>ṛc</s>.
13.11: That which is its indestructible quality — that becomes the <s>akṣara</s>.
13.11: The senses are here called gods, those seated within it — [say] the <s>Ātmapravādas</s> (those who teach about the Self).

body.translated_text:
13.12: <s>Akṣara</s> (the imperishable): it does not flow away (<s>na kṣarati</s>), or it does not diminish (<s>na kṣīyate</s>) — it is undecaying (<s>akṣaya</s>).
13.12: Or it is the axle (<s>akṣa</s>) of speech.
13.12: The axle of a vehicle is from <s>añjana</s> (anointing, moving).
13.12: The other [meaning] is from similarity with turning, being of the same root-nature.
13.12: Thus this investigation and reasoning regarding the meaning of the <s>mantras</s> has been carried out — both from scripture (<s>śruti</s>) and from reasoning (<s>tarka</s>).
13.12: The <s>mantras</s> should not be explained in isolation;
13.12: rather, they should be explained according to their context.
13.12: For in these [<s>mantras</s>] there is no direct perception for one who is not a <s>ṛṣi</s> or who lacks <s>tapas</s> (austerity).
13.12: But among successive knowers, increasingly greater knowledge becomes praiseworthy — this has been stated before.
13.12: Or, when the <s>ṛṣis</s> departed, humans said to the gods: 'Who will be our <s>ṛṣi</s>?'
13.12: They gave them this reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) as a <s>ṛṣi</s> — the investigation and reasoning regarding the meaning of the <s>mantras</s>.
13.12: Therefore, whatever a learned one reasons out — that becomes <s>ārṣa</s> (having the authority of the <s>ṛṣis</s>).

body.translated_text:
13.13: 'Those tested in the heart, swift in mind — when the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, companions, sacrifice together — therein some abandon you through their insights; some <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> wander about [in ignorance].'
13.13: Those tested in the heart, swift in the speed of mind — when the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the priests sharing the same recitation, sacrifice together —
13.13: therein some abandon you through insights, through things to be known, through [superior] activities.
13.13: <s>Oha-brahmāṇaḥ</s>: those whose <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge) is reasoning (<s>ūha</s>).
13.13: Or: 'reasoning is their <s>Brahman</s>.'
13.13: This knowledge is the understanding that transcends scripture (<s>śruti</s>).
13.13: Its far shore is to be attained through <s>tapas</s> (austerity).
13.13: This should not be explained by one who desires long life.
13.13: Therefore the remaining passages in the <s>Chandas</s> (Vedic hymns) should be disregarded.
13.13: Now the traditional teaching (<s>āgama</s>): whatever deity he explains, he experiences identification with that very deity — he experiences it.

14.1: The topic of deities and the limbs of sacrifice have been explained.
14.1: Now from here onward we shall explain the path and the course.
14.1: '<s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun) is the <s>Ātman</s> (Self)' — for the performer of rites, the witness is the risen one.
14.1: Moreover, they teach this further.
14.1: This great <s>Ātman</s> is praised by this <s>ṛc</s>:
14.1: 'They call him <s>Indra</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Agni</s>...'
14.1: Then this great <s>Ātman</s>, through desire for self-knowledge, declared himself:
14.1: '<s>Agni</s> am I by birth, <s>Jātavedas</s>' and 'I am the firstborn' — by these two [verses].

14.2: '<s>Agni</s> am I by birth, <s>Jātavedas</s>; ghee is my eye, immortality is my mouth. The threefold light, the measurer of space, the unextinguished warmth — oblation is my name.'
14.2: 'I am the firstborn of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), before the gods, [bearing] the name of immortality. He who gives me — he alone preserves me; I who am food devour the eater of food.'
14.2: He, having known [himself], manifested.
14.2: Thus he declared [to himself]: 'Declare this <s>Ātman</s>, born within, the inner self, close by, to another.'

14.3: 'I saw the protector, never falling, going back and forth on paths. He, clothing himself in those that converge and those that diverge, moves again and again within the worlds.'
14.3: He moves again and again within the worlds.
14.3: Now this great <s>Ātman</s>, characterized by <s>sattva</s> (being, purity) — that is the supreme, that is <s>Brahman</s>, that is truth, that is the waters, that is the unmanifest, that is the intangible, that is the formless, that is the tasteless, that is the odorless, that is the immortal, that is the luminous, that is the stable — the self of all beings.
14.3: This is the primordial nature (<s>bhūtaprakṛti</s>) of beings — [say] some.
14.3: That is the field (<s>kṣetra</s>); from knowing that, having attained the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>), one becomes selfless.
14.3: Now this great <s>Ātman</s> is threefold: <s>sattva</s> (purity), <s>rajas</s> (passion), <s>tamas</s> (darkness).
14.3: <s>Sattva</s>, being pure, stands in the middle; <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> are on either side.
14.3: <s>Rajas</s> means desire and aversion; <s>tamas</s> means the purification of the unknown — it serves to separate the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field) by creating manifestation.
14.3: The great <s>Ātman</s> shines forth, marked by the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>), marked by <s>tamas</s>.
14.3: Marked by the light of knowledge is <s>tamas</s> [overcome].
14.3: Marked by the certainty [derived from] <s>ākāśa</s> (space).

body.translated_text:
14.4: Sound is the quality of space (<s>ākāśa</s>).
14.4: From space [arises] wind (<s>vāyu</s>), having two qualities, [adding] touch.
14.4: From wind [arises] light (<s>jyotis</s>), having three qualities, [adding] form.
14.4: From light [arise] waters (<s>āpas</s>), having four qualities, [adding] taste.
14.4: From waters [arises] earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>), having five qualities, [adding] smell.
14.4: From earth [arise] all classes of beings, stationary and moving.
14.4: This [<s>Brahman</s>] remains awake for a thousand pairs of ages (<s>yuga</s>).
14.4: At their end, wishing to sleep, he withdraws his limbs.
14.4: The classes of beings return to earth;
14.4: waters [return] to light;
14.4: light to wind; wind to space.
14.4: Space [returns] to mind (<s>manas</s>).
14.4: Mind to knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>).
14.4: Knowledge to the great self (<s>mahān ātman</s>).
14.4: The great self to <s>pratibhā</s> (intuitive understanding).
14.4: <s>Pratibhā</s> to <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature).
14.4: She sleeps for a thousand pairs of ages — [that is] the night.
14.4: These two, day and night, revolve ceaselessly.
14.4: That is time; this is the day.
14.4: 'A day lasting a thousand pairs of ages — that is what they know as the day of <s>Brahman</s>;
14.4: and the night ending after a thousand pairs of ages — those people are the knowers of day and night.'
14.4: Thus.

14.5: Another [self] follows that which revolves.
14.5: [He is] understood as the creator (<s>sraṣṭā</s>), the seer (<s>draṣṭā</s>), the distributor (<s>vibhaktā</s>), the transcendent (<s>atimātra</s>), the 'I' (<s>aham</s>).
14.5: In the false perception of this: fire (<s>pāvaka</s>) is among the great elements, subtle; from space [come] the vital breaths from wind; sight and the speakers from fire; moisture from waters; embodiment from earth.
14.5: One should know eight qualities pertaining to earth.
14.5: Three from the mother, three from the father.
14.5: Bones, sinews, and marrow are from the father.
14.5: Skin, flesh, and blood are from the mother.
14.5: Food and drink — [thus] eight.
14.5: This <s>puruṣa</s> (person) is made of everything and is endowed with all knowledge.

body.translated_text:
14.6: If he follows [<s>dharma</s>], he becomes that.
14.6: If he follows <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), he becomes a god (<s>deva</s>).
14.6: If he follows knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), he becomes immortal.
14.6: If he follows desire (<s>kāma</s>), he falls.
14.6: He enters this womb.
14.6: This is the view taught here:
14.6: Phlegm (<s>śleṣman</s>) arises from semen (<s>retas</s>).
14.6: From phlegm, chyle (<s>rasa</s>).
14.6: From chyle, blood; from blood, flesh; from flesh, fat; from fat, sinews; from sinews, bones; from bones, marrow; from marrow, semen.
14.6: This semen, deposited in the womb, [gives rise to] a person.
14.6: With an excess of semen (<s>śukra</s>), a male is born; with an excess of blood (<s>śonita</s>), a female.
14.6: When both are equal, a neuter (<s>napuṃsaka</s>) is born.
14.6: When the semen is split, twins (<s>yama</s>) are born.
14.6: From the union of semen and blood, from the union of mother and father.
14.6: How then is this body formed in the womb?
14.6: It becomes like <s>Soma</s> (fluid).
14.6: After one night, it becomes a <s>kalala</s> (embryonic fluid).
14.6: After five nights, bubbles (<s>budbuda</s>).
14.6: After seven nights, a lump of flesh (<s>peśī</s>).
14.6: After fourteen nights, a rounded mass (<s>arbuda</s>).
14.6: After twenty-five nights, it becomes solid (<s>ghana</s>).
14.6: After one month, it becomes hard (<s>kathina</s>).
14.6: Within two months, the head is formed.
14.6: In three months, the neck and features appear; in four months, the skin appears.
14.6: In the fifth month, nails and hair appear.
14.6: In the sixth, the mouth, nose, eyes,
14.6: and ears are formed.
14.6: In the seventh [month], it becomes capable of movement; in the eighth, the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) becomes determined.
14.6: In the ninth, it becomes complete in all limbs.
14.6: 'I have died and been born again; born, I have died again.
14.6: I have dwelt in thousands of various wombs.
14.6: Various foods have been eaten; various breasts have been drunk from.
14.6: Various mothers have been seen, and fathers and friends likewise.
14.6: Head downward, pressed, the creature, fully conscious,
14.6: should practice <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>, or [contemplate] the <s>puruṣa</s> of twenty-five [principles].' Thus.
14.6: Then in the tenth month, [the child] is born.
14.6: Having been born and touched by the wind, it does not remember birth and death.
14.6: And at the end, good and bad <s>karma</s> — this is the measure of the body.

14.7: One hundred and eight joints.
14.7: The head is formed of eight plates (<s>kapāla</s>).
14.7: Sixteen membranes of fat (<s>vapāpala</s>).
14.7: Nine hundred sinews.
14.7: Seven hundred vital points (<s>marman</s>) of a person.
14.7: Four and a half <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of hairs; the heart has eight plates; the tongue twelve plates; the testicles are eight eagle-shaped.
14.7: Likewise the genitals, rectum, and anus.
14.7: Why [is there] urine and excrement?
14.7: Because [the body] is irrigated by food and drink.
14.7: Those whose actions are not accumulated are born from one another.
14.7: Knowledge and action attend upon him, and prior understanding.
14.7: Immersed in the great darkness of ignorance, overwhelmed by the pairs [of opposites] consisting of old age, death, hunger, thirst, sorrow, anger, greed, delusion, pride, fear, envy, joy, despondency, jealousy, and ill-will — from this, through the directness and swiftness of things, he is liberated.
14.7: From this sinful body [composed] of the great elements, departing in mere moments, passing beyond <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), having made a luminous body (<s>taijasa śarīra</s>), having experienced the fruit appropriate to his <s>karma</s>, upon its exhaustion, he returns again to this world.

14.8: Now, those who, resorting to violence, abandoning knowledge, perform great austerities, or in time perform the rites enjoined by the <s>Veda</s> — they attain smoke.
14.8: From smoke, night; from night, the waning fortnight.
14.8: From the waning fortnight, the southern course [of the sun]; from the southern course, the world of the ancestors (<s>pitṛloka</s>); from the world of the ancestors, the moon; from the moon, wind; from wind, rain; from rain, herbs — having become these, upon its exhaustion, he returns again to this world.

14.9: Now, those who, abandoning violence, resorting to knowledge, perform great austerities, or perform the acts enjoined by knowledge — they attain the flame (<s>arcis</s>); from the flame, the day; from the day, the waxing fortnight; from the waxing fortnight, the northern course [of the sun]; from the northern course, the world of the gods (<s>devaloka</s>); from the world of the gods, the sun (<s>Āditya</s>); from the sun, lightning (<s>vaidyuta</s>); from lightning, the mental [realm] (<s>mānasa</s>).
14.9: Having become a mental person (<s>mānasa puruṣa</s>), they attain the world of <s>Brahman</s>.
14.9: They do not return.
14.9: The rest — mere rods and insects — are those who do not know this.
14.9: Therefore this should be known.
14.9: And further he says:

body.translated_text:
14.10: 'You do not know him who generated these [beings]; something different has come between you.
14.10: Enveloped in mist and chatter, sated with life-sustaining hymns, they wander.'
14.10: They do not know him — the learned who know thus speak of the imperishable lord of sacred speech (<s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>).
14.10: 'Different from you, another, different from these' — something intermediate has come to be.
14.10: Enveloped in mist — in darkness — and chatter, sated with life-sustaining hymns, the breath, the sun — on whatever path they wander.
14.10: The ignorant speak after the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>).
14.10: But indeed the wise are in accord with the knower of the field.
14.10: By his austerity alone does he attain freedom from negligence; then he becomes one who has attained.
14.10: By him one should desire the unbroken [state].
14.10: By him one should desire friendship.
14.10: For he is the best friend — he knows the past, the present, and the future.
14.10: The knower — from what is he born?
14.10: The friend — from what does he befriend?
14.10: He lies together with the elements and sense-faculties.
14.10: The great elements together with the sense-faculties — understanding (<s>prajñā</s>) causes action. Or:
14.10: That which is the foundation of waters [is his support].
14.10: [One whose] character is tranquility, whose self is <s>Brahman</s> — he becomes one with <s>Brahman</s>.
14.10: He remains as a mere witness — bondage is made by knowledge [alone].
14.10: Now we shall enumerate in order the primary designations of the great elements of the self.

body.translated_text:
14.12: '<s>Soma</s> purifies himself — the begetter of thoughts, the begetter of heaven, the begetter of earth, the begetter of <s>Agni</s>, the begetter of <s>Sūrya</s>, the begetter of <s>Indra</s>, and the begetter of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.'
14.12: <s>Soma</s> purifies himself — the begetter of thoughts, the begetter of heaven, the begetter of earth, the begetter of fire, the begetter of the sun, the begetter of <s>Indra</s>, and the begetter of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
14.12: <s>Soma</s> purifies himself.
14.12: <s>Soma</s>, that is, <s>Sūrya</s> (the sun), because of [his] impelling — the begetter of thoughts, [that is,] of the illuminating rays of <s>Āditya</s>.
14.12: Of heaven, [that is,] of the rays of <s>Āditya</s> whose action is illumination.
14.12: Of earth, [that is,] of the rays of <s>Āditya</s> whose action is extension.
14.12: Of fire, [that is,] of the rays of <s>Āditya</s> whose action is movement.
14.12: Of the sun, [that is,] of the rays of <s>Āditya</s> whose action is self-appropriation.
14.12: Of <s>Indra</s>, [that is,] of the rays of <s>Āditya</s> whose action is sovereignty.
14.12: Of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, [that is,] of the rays of <s>Āditya</s> whose action is pervading.
14.12: Thus [is the] theological interpretation (<s>adhidaivatam</s>).
14.12: Now the personal interpretation (<s>adhyātmam</s>):
14.12: <s>Soma</s>, the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), is also [so called] for this very reason — the meaning is that he is the begetter of the senses (<s>indriyāṇām</s>).
14.12: Or alternatively, the <s>Ātman</s> is endowed with all [divine] powers through all [its] manifestations.
14.12: Thus he declares the course of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self).

body.translated_text:
14.13: '<s>Brahman</s> among the gods, the path-finder among the sages, the seer among the inspired, the buffalo among the beasts, the hawk among the vultures, the axe among the forests — <s>Soma</s> passes through the purifier, resounding.'
14.13: <s>Brahman</s> among the gods — thus [is explained].
14.13: For he is the <s>Brahman</s> among the gods, [that is,] the rays of <s>Āditya</s> whose action is playing/shining.
14.13: The path-finder among the sages — thus [is explained].
14.13: For he knows the path of the sages, [that is,] of the rays of <s>Āditya</s> that are poetically inspired.
14.13: The seer among the inspired ones — thus [is explained].
14.13: For he becomes the seer among the inspired, [that is,] the rays of <s>Āditya</s> whose action is pervading.
14.13: The buffalo among the beasts — thus [is explained].
14.13: For he becomes great among the beasts, [that is,] the rays of <s>Āditya</s> whose action is seeking.
14.13: The hawk among the vultures — thus [is explained].
14.13: The hawk is <s>Āditya</s>, from <s>śyāyati</s> (to move), [whose] action is movement.
14.13: The vulture is <s>Āditya</s>, from <s>gṛdhyati</s> (to desire), [whose] action is standing firm, since [all] stand established in him.
14.13: The axe among the forests — thus [is explained].
14.13: For <s>Āditya</s> himself bears the actions among the forests, [that is,] the rays of <s>Āditya</s> whose action is desiring.
14.13: <s>Soma</s> passes through the purifier, resounding — thus [is explained].
14.13: For he passes through the purifier, [that is,] the rays, being praised.
14.13: This very one is all that — the imperishable.
14.13: Thus [is the] theological interpretation (<s>adhidaivatam</s>).
14.13: Now the personal interpretation (<s>adhyātmam</s>):
14.13: <s>Brahman</s> among the gods — thus [is explained].
14.13: This one too is the <s>Brahman</s> among the gods, [that is,] the senses (<s>indriyāṇi</s>) whose action is playing/shining.
14.13: The path-finder among the sages — thus [is explained].
14.13: This one too knows the path of the sages, [that is,] of the senses that are poetically inspired.
14.13: The seer among the inspired ones — thus [is explained].
14.13: This one too becomes the seer among the inspired, [that is,] the senses whose action is pervading.
14.13: The buffalo among the beasts — thus [is explained].
14.13: This one too becomes great among the beasts, [that is,] the senses whose action is seeking.
14.13: The hawk among the vultures — thus [is explained].
14.13: The hawk is the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), from <s>śyāyati</s>, whose action is knowledge.
14.13: The vultures are the senses (<s>indriyāṇi</s>), from <s>gṛdhyati</s>, whose action is knowledge, since [all] stand established in this [Self].
14.13: The axe among the forests — thus [is explained].
14.13: This one too himself bears the actions within the <s>Ātman</s> — among the forests, [that is,] the senses whose action is desiring.
14.13: <s>Soma</s> passes through the purifier, resounding — thus [is explained].
14.13: This one too passes through the purifier, [that is,] the senses.
14.13: Being praised, this very one experiences all that.
14.13: Thus he declares the course of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self).

body.translated_text:
14.14: 'The carrier [of offerings] sends forth three speeches — the contemplation of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), the wisdom of <s>Brahman</s>. The cows go seeking the lord of cows; the thoughts go to <s>Soma</s>, lowing.' (ṚV 10.97.34)
14.14: The carrier (<s>vahni</s>) is <s>Āditya</s> (the sun).
14.14: He sends forth three speeches — the <s>Ṛg</s> [verses], the <s>Yajus</s> [formulas], and the <s>Sāman</s> [chants].
14.14: The actions of <s>Ṛta</s>, that is, of <s>Āditya</s>, are the thoughts of <s>Brahman</s>.
14.14: This very one is all that — the imperishable.
14.14: Thus [is the] theological interpretation (<s>adhidaivatam</s>).
14.14: Now the personal interpretation (<s>adhyātmam</s>):
14.14: The carrier (<s>vahni</s>) is the <s>Ātman</s> (Self).
14.14: He sends forth, impels the three speeches — [those] of knowledge, thought, and intelligence.
14.14: The actions of <s>Ṛta</s>, that is, of the <s>Ātman</s>, are the thoughts of <s>Brahman</s>.
14.14: This very one experiences all that.
14.14: Thus he declares the course of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self).

body.translated_text:
14.15: 'The cows, the milch-cows, go lowing to <s>Soma</s>; the inspired ones go to <s>Soma</s>, seeking with their thoughts. <s>Soma</s>, pressed out, is purified as he is anointed; in <s>Soma</s>, the songs in <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter come together.' (ṚV 9.97.35)
14.15: These very cows, milch-cows, [that is,] rays, desiring and lowing, go to <s>Soma</s>, [that is,] to <s>Āditya</s> (the sun).
14.15: Likewise, the inspired ones, [that is,] the rays, seeking and desiring with thoughts, go to <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Āditya</s>.
14.15: Likewise, <s>Soma</s>, pressed out, is purified as he is anointed.
14.15: The songs and the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [verses] come together in this very one.
14.15: Then in this <s>Āditya</s>, they all become one.
14.15: Thus [is the] theological interpretation (<s>adhidaivatam</s>).
14.15: Now the personal interpretation (<s>adhyātmam</s>):
14.15: These very cows, milch-cows, [that is,] the senses (<s>indriyāṇi</s>), desiring and longing, go to <s>Soma</s>, [that is,] to the <s>Ātman</s> (Self).
14.15: Likewise, the inspired ones, [that is,] the senses, seeking and desiring with thoughts, go to <s>Soma</s>, to the <s>Ātman</s>.
14.15: Likewise, <s>Soma</s>, pressed out, is purified as he is anointed.
14.15: The <s>Ātman</s> and the seven sages come together in this very one.
14.15: These all become one in this <s>Ātman</s> (Self).
14.15: Thus he declares the course of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self).

14.16: "The ocean strode forth in the first ordinance, generating offspring, the king of the world. The bull upon the filter, on the woolen [sieve] at the summit, great <s>Soma</s> grew strong, pressed forth, the drop." (ṚV 9.97.40)
14.16: The ocean — <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) — strode beyond in the supreme separation, generating offspring by the action of raining, the king of the world, the king of all.
14.16: The bull upon the filter, on the woolen [sieve] at the summit, great <s>Soma</s> grew strong, pressed forth, the drop.
14.16: Thus is the theological (<s>adhidaivata</s>) interpretation.
14.16: Now the metaphysical (<s>adhyātma</s>) interpretation:
14.16: The ocean — the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) — strode beyond in the supreme separation, generating offspring by the action of knowledge, the king of the world, the king of all.
14.16: The bull upon the filter, on the woolen [sieve] at the summit, great <s>Soma</s> grew strong, pressed forth, the drop.
14.16: Thus it speaks of the course of the <s>Ātman</s>.

14.17: "<s>Soma</s>, the great buffalo, accomplished a great [deed] — when the embryo of the waters chose the gods. He placed vigor in <s>Indra</s>, the purifying one; the drop (<s>Indu</s>) generated light in <s>Sūrya</s>." (ṚV 9.97.41)
14.17: <s>Soma</s>, the great buffalo, accomplished a great [deed] — when the embryo of the waters chose [the gods].
14.17: He placed the sovereignty of the gods in <s>Indra</s>; the purifying one generated vigor; the drop, <s>Āditya</s>, generated light in <s>Sūrya</s>.
14.17: The drop (<s>Indu</s>) [here represents] the <s>Ātman</s>.

body.translated_text:
14.18: "The agitated one, the subduer, in the gathering of many — the grey one swallowed the young one. Behold the poetic power and greatness of the god: he who died today is the same one [reborn] yesterday." (ṚV 10.55.5)
14.18: <s>Vidhu</s> — one whose nature is to agitate; <s>dadrāṇa</s> — one whose nature is to subdue. The grey <s>Āditya</s> (Sun) swallows the young moon.
14.18: He dies instantly during the day — when the sun rises.
14.18: Thus is the theological (<s>adhidaivata</s>) interpretation.
14.18: Now the metaphysical (<s>adhyātma</s>) interpretation:
14.18: <s>Vidhu</s> — one whose nature is to agitate; <s>dadrāṇa</s> — one whose nature is to subdue. The grey <s>Ātman</s> swallows the great young one.
14.18: He dies at night.
14.18: Night has risen.
14.18: Thus it speaks of the course of the <s>Ātman</s>.

body.translated_text:
14.19: "Of the co-born ones, the seventh is called the single-born; the six are <s>ṛṣis</s> born of the gods. Their desired [things], distributed according to stations, stand firm and tremble, manifold in forms." (ṚV 1.164.15)
14.19: Of the six co-born <s>ṛṣis</s>, <s>Āditya</s> is the seventh.
14.19: Their desired things, or beautiful things, or things traversed, or things gone, or things thought, or things bowed — they rejoice together with the waters.
14.19: Where these seven luminous <s>ṛṣi</s>-lights are — beyond them is <s>Āditya</s>.
14.19: They become one in him.
14.19: Thus is the theological (<s>adhidaivata</s>) interpretation.
14.19: Now the metaphysical (<s>adhyātma</s>) interpretation:
14.19: Of the six co-born senses (<s>indriya</s>), the <s>Ātman</s> is the seventh.
14.19: Their desired things, or beautiful things, or things traversed, or things gone, or things thought, or things bowed — they rejoice together with food.
14.19: Where these seven <s>ṛṣi</s>-like senses are — beyond them is the <s>Ātman</s>.
14.19: They become one in him.
14.19: Thus it speaks of the course of the <s>Ātman</s>.

14.20: "They are women indeed, yet people call them men. He who has eyes sees; the blind one does not discern. The son who is a sage — he understands these [things]. He who knows them would be the father of his father." (ṚV 1.164.16)
14.20: These — the carriers of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — are indeed feminine.
14.20: They — the blind one, who calls that one by the masculine word <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), being without nourishment, seeing, does not discern.
14.20: The son who is a sage — he knows these.
14.20: He who knows these would be the father of his father.
14.20: Thus it speaks of the course of the <s>Ātman</s>.

14.21: "The seven half-embryos, the seed of the world, stand in <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s ordinance, in the directions. They, the wise ones, with thoughts and mind encompass and pervade everything on all sides." (ṚV 1.164.36)
14.21: <s>Āditya</s> swallows these seven rays — the word is elevated from the middle station.
14.21: Those that stand in him — they transform through thoughts and mind.
14.21: The encompassing ones encompass all actions through the action of raining.
14.21: Thus is the theological (<s>adhidaivata</s>) interpretation.
14.21: Now the metaphysical (<s>adhyātma</s>) interpretation:
14.21: The <s>Ātman</s> swallows these seven senses — the word is elevated from the middle station.
14.21: Those that stand in him — they transform through thoughts and mind.
14.21: The encompassing ones encompass all the senses through the action of knowledge.
14.21: Thus it speaks of the course of the <s>Ātman</s>.

14.22: "I do not know whether I am this. Mysterious, bound up, I wander with my mind. When the firstborn of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) came to me, then I obtained a share of this speech." (ṚV 1.164.37)
14.22: I do not know whether I am this.
14.22: Mysterious, fully bound, I wander with my mind.
14.22: For indeed, the unknowing — intelligence, nourishment, offspring — they do not reveal. This is <s>Āditya</s>; this is the <s>Ātman</s>.

14.23: "Going backward and forward, seized by his own nature, the immortal shares a common origin with the mortal. The two go constantly in opposite directions — people perceive one but do not perceive the other." (ṚV 1.164.38)
14.23: He moves backward and forward, seized by his own nature — the immortal <s>Āditya</s> together with the mortal moon.
14.23: The two go constantly, going everywhere, or going in many directions.
14.23: One sees <s>Āditya</s> but not the moon.
14.23: Thus is the theological (<s>adhidaivata</s>) interpretation.
14.23: Now the metaphysical (<s>adhyātma</s>) interpretation:
14.23: He moves backward and forward, seized by his own nature — the immortal <s>Ātman</s> together with the mortal mind.
14.23: The two go constantly, going everywhere, or going in many directions.
14.23: One sees the <s>Ātman</s> but not the mind.
14.23: Thus it speaks of the course of the <s>Ātman</s>.

body.translated_text:
14.24: "That was the greatest among beings, from which was born the fierce one of blazing might. As soon as born, he drives away the enemies; all the allies rejoice in him." (ṚV 10.120.1)
14.24: That becomes the greatest among beings, among the worlds — <s>Āditya</s>, from which was born the fierce one of blazing might, of radiant might.
14.24: As soon as born, he drives away the enemies.
14.24: <s>Niriṇāti</s> denotes an action of delight or an action of shining. All the allies rejoice in him.
14.24: Thus is the theological (<s>adhidaivata</s>) interpretation.
14.24: Now the metaphysical (<s>adhyātma</s>) interpretation:
14.24: That becomes the greatest among beings, among the worlds — the <s>Avyakta</s> (Unmanifest), from which is born the fierce one of blazing might, of the might of knowledge.
14.24: As soon as born, he drives away the enemies.
14.24: <s>Niriṇāti</s> denotes an action of delight or an action of shining.
14.24: All the allies rejoice in him.
14.24: Thus it speaks of the course of the <s>Ātman</s>.

14.25: "Who today yokes at the pole the cattle of <s>Ṛta</s> — active, wrathful, hard to suppress? Who would string arrows in the hearts, delightful? He who fulfills their maintenance — he shall live." (ṚV 1.84.16)
14.25: Who — <s>Āditya</s> — yokes at the pole the cattle, the rays — active, radiant, hard to suppress? They empty and discharge arrows, delightful, pleasure-bringing.
14.25: He who knows this accumulated [wisdom] — how does he live?
14.25: Thus is the theological (<s>adhidaivata</s>) interpretation.
14.25: Now the metaphysical (<s>adhyātma</s>) interpretation:
14.25: Who — the <s>Ātman</s> — yokes at the pole the cattle, the senses — active, radiant, hard to suppress? They empty and discharge arrows, delightful, pleasure-bringing.
14.25: He who knows these accumulated [senses] — he lives long.
14.25: Thus it speaks of the course of the <s>Ātman</s>.

14.26: "Who goes? Who gives? Who fears? Who thinks <s>Indra</s> exists? Who speaks for offspring, for prosperity, for wealth, for the body, for the people?" (ṚV 1.84.17)
14.26: Who indeed goes? Who gives? Who fears? Who thinks <s>Indra</s> exists?
14.26: Who [speaks] for offspring, for progeny, and for great delight — for the pleasing, for the beautiful?

14.27: 'Who worships <s>Agni</s> with oblation, with ghee, with the sacrificial ladle, as a sacrificer, with the fixed seasons? For whom do the gods convey the swift oblation? Who is the one of good invocations, blessed with gods, who meditates?' (ṚV 1.84.18)
14.27: Who worships <s>Āditya</s> with oblation and with ghee, with the sacrificial ladle, as a sacrificer, with the fixed seasons?
14.27: For whom do the gods convey the swift oblation-offerings?
14.27: Who meditates — the one of good invocations, blessed with gods (<s>sudeva</s>) — possessing excellent deities?
14.27: Thus [is the interpretation] regarding the deity (<s>adhidaivatam</s>).
14.27: Now, regarding the self (<s>adhyātmam</s>):
14.27: Who worships the Self (<s>ātman</s>) with oblation and with ghee, with the sacrificial ladle, as a sacrificer, with the fixed seasons?
14.27: For whom do the gods convey the swift oblation-offerings?
14.27: Who meditates — the one of good invocations, possessed of excellent knowledge (<s>suprajña</s>), having noble understanding?
14.27: Thus he declares the path of the Self (<s>ātmagati</s>).

14.28: 'You indeed, O god most mighty, shall praise the mortal; there is no other protector than you, O bountiful one — O <s>Indra</s>, I speak this word to you.' (ṚV 1.84.19)
14.28: You indeed shall praise the mortal, O god most mighty.
14.28: There is no other than you, O bountiful one (<s>Maghavan</s>) — no other protector, or guardian, or conqueror, or bestower of happiness.
14.28: 'O <s>Indra</s>, I speak this word to you' — [this is] connected with praise (<s>stuti</s>).

body.translated_text:
14.29: 'The swan (<s>Haṃsa</s>) dwelling in purity, the <s>Vasu</s> dwelling in the atmosphere, the priest (<s>Hotṛ</s>) dwelling at the altar, the guest dwelling in the house; dwelling among men, dwelling in the noble, dwelling in truth (<s>ṛta</s>), dwelling in the sky — born from the waters, born from the earth, born from truth, born from the mountain — the great Truth.' (ṚV 4.40.5)
14.29: <s>Haṃsa</s> — thus [it is explained].
14.29: The <s>haṃsas</s> are the rays of the sun.
14.29: The supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>) is the supreme light.
14.29: The earth is pervaded.
14.29: All is pervaded — pervaded by the act of penetration, through repetition, by the orb of <s>Āditya</s>.
14.29: He moves forth — thus [the explanation of] the world; he moves forth.
14.29: Moving like a swan, he advances.
14.29: The <s>haṃsas</s> are the <s>paramahaṃsas</s> (supreme swans/ascetics).
14.29: The supreme Self dwells abundantly and deeply through the rays of the sun.
14.29: Or he dwells in three [realms]; or the ray dwells; or the fire dwells — the golden-seeded <s>Pūṣan</s>...

14.30: 'Two birds, companions joined together, embrace the same tree; one of them eats the sweet <s>pippala</s> (fruit), while the other, not eating, looks on.' (ṚV 1.164.20)
14.30: Two and two are established — well-doers, performers of <s>dharma</s> (duty).
14.30: Evil-doing, sin, and attachment — so they explain.
14.30: 'Two birds, companions joined together' — the individual self (<s>ātman</s>), the base self (<s>durātman</s>), rises up to meet the supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>).
14.30: That is born in the body itself.
14.30: The tree is the body — the tree of protection; it establishes its two wings.
14.30: Of those two, one, having eaten food, while the other, not eating, attains identity of form and identity of world — he who knows thus.
14.30: 'Not eating, the other looks on.'
14.30: Thus he declares the path of the Self (<s>ātmagati</s>).

14.31: 'Come, O <s>Indra</s>, by the praised paths; enjoy this our sacrifice, our appointed share; as one abandons a satisfied maternal uncle's daughter — your share is the <s>vapā</s> (omental fat offering), as from a paternal aunt's daughter.'
14.31: The mighty one (<s>Śakra</s>) shall come — the deities, by the three sacred fords, praised by the three sacred paths to <s>Śakra</s>. Enjoy this our sacrificial share — the shares of <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> — may <s>Indra</s> accept them.
14.31: Satisfied thus, as the share of a maiden connected to an uncle — that deity is in that place, with <s>Śakra</s> as the illustration.

body.translated_text:
14.32: 'The inspired ones [invoke] the inspired one for protection; the mortals [invoke] the god for aid; we call <s>Agni</s> with our hymns.' (ṚV 8.11.6)
14.32: The inspired ones [invoke] the inspired one for protection — they know.
14.32: <s>Veda</s> (knowledge) [derives] from <s>vindateḥ</s> (to find) — that which is to be known.
14.32: By means of <s>vāyu</s> (breath/wind) with a pure body.
14.32: The inspired one (<s>vipra</s>), however — in the lotus of the heart, he should fill the syllable <s>u</s>, joined with the syllable <s>a</s>, reaching to the abode of the syllable <s>m</s>; the inspired one, sprinkled as a drop (<s>bindu</s>) in the vital breaths, blossoming, radiant with the splendor of fire, in the golden lotuses, having an immortal body, established in the state of immortality — the speakers of immortal speech declare this in the mouth of truth (<s>ṛta</s>).
14.32: We call <s>Agni</s> with our hymns.
14.32: One should awaken <s>Agni</s> — '<s>Agni</s> is all the deities.'
14.32: The following [verse is given] for further etymological explanation:

14.33: 'Let us press <s>Soma</s> for <s>Jātavedas</s> (the knower of all births); may the knowing one burn down those who are hostile; may he carry us across all dangers — <s>Agni</s>, like a ship across the river, past all misfortunes.' (ṚV 1.99.1)
14.33: <s>Jātavedas</s> — thus [it is explained].
14.33: All this that is born, moving and unmoving, according to the principle of creation, maintenance, and dissolution — let us press <s>Soma</s> by extraction for the sacrifice — <s>Soma</s>, the king, the immortal; 'for the purpose of sacrifice' — this is said with certainty; he burns and reduces to ashes — <s>Soma</s> gives, such is the meaning.
14.33: May he carry us across all dangers — places difficult to traverse — like a ship across a river; just as a helmsman carries [passengers] across the river by a ship — across the flowing, water-filled, great-banked [river] — <s>Agni</s> carries us past all misfortunes.

14.34: 'This of yours is unlike the other waters — whatever rivers flow to the ocean; the snake sheds its old skin — [so one sheds] sin, going forth head-first.'
14.34: This of yours, unlike the other [waters] — whatever rivers flow, having made the ocean their lord.
14.34: As a snake sheds its old skin,
14.34: [so] they shed sin.
14.34: <s>Āpa</s> (water) [derives] from <s>āpnoteḥ</s> (to reach/pervade).
14.34: Regarding them, this [verse] occurs:

14.35: 'We worship the three-eyed one (<s>Tryambaka</s>), the fragrant one, the increaser of nourishment; like a cucumber from its stalk, may I be freed from death, not from immortality.' (ṚV 7.59.12)
14.35: <s>Tryambaka</s> is <s>Rudra</s>; that <s>Tryambaka</s> we worship — the fragrant one.
14.35: <s>Sugandhi</s> — having a good fragrance.
14.35: The increaser of nourishment — one who causes nourishment.
14.35: As a cucumber-fruit [is freed] from its stalk, from the binding — from death, free me!
14.35: From what? [The answer follows.]
14.35: Of these, the other [verse] follows:

14.36: 'Live a hundred autumns, growing; a hundred winters, a hundred springs; may <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> restore this one with the oblation that grants a hundred years of life.' (ṚV 10.161.4)
14.36: 'Live a hundred autumns, growing' — thus also is the Vedic citation (<s>nigama</s>).
14.36: 'A hundred' means a long life of a hundred [years].
14.36: The <s>Maruts</s> increase him.
14.36: A hundred — he becomes one of a hundred selves, as it were.
14.36: A hundred becomes infinite.
14.36: A hundred becomes sovereignty.
14.36: 'A hundred' means a long life of a hundred [years].

body.translated_text:
14.37: 'May your bounties, may your aids, O <s>Vasu</s>, never fail us at any time; measure out to us all the human riches for the people.' (ṚV 1.84.20)
14.37: May your domains, may yours never at any time leave us.
14.37: All knowledge for the measuring out — for the benefit of humanity.
14.37: This <s>Āditya</s> is this Self (<s>ātman</s>).
14.37: Moreover, they declare this further:
14.37: Moreover, this group of Ṛgvedic verses proclaims this great Self — [the hymn] addressed to <s>Viśvakarman</s>:
14.37: 'Of the gods, we indeed [know] the generations...'
14.37: 'There was neither non-being (<s>asat</s>) nor being (<s>sat</s>) at that time' — and so on.
14.37: This is the inquiry into the Self (<s>ātma-jijñāsā</s>).
14.37: This is the inquiry into all beings (<s>sarva-bhūta-jijñāsā</s>).
14.37: One who knows thus attains the equality, identity of form, and identity of world with <s>Brahman</s>.
14.37: Salutation!
